539254|2026-06.headline: AESL Q1 FY27: Energy Solutions platform delivered about INR 570 crore EBIT on 3,325 MU long-term sales; management frames AESL as a full-scale utility.
539254|2026-06.overview: Management said AESL has moved to a full-scale utility with four operating businesses (transmission, distribution, smart metering, Energy Solutions) and expects consistent quarter-on-quarter reporting. Quarterly capex was close to INR 3,500 crore. Energy Solutions is the new focus: about 5 GW of take-or-pay supply and 3,500 MWh of storage tied up, with long-term offtake being built out. Management said the IntelliSmart acquisition is pending CCI approval. Analysts pressed on the sustainability of Energy Solutions margins, which management tied to whether purchase positions are back-to-back with sales.

segments.commentary: Described as growing at a stable pace; no segment figures were given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the smart meter balance tender pipeline and the IntelliSmart return profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance tenders about 10-11 crore meters, in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana and parts of Andhra and other states. IntelliSmart awaits CCI approval; profitability expected similar to AESL.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Energy Solutions book is tied up and what is the EBITDA sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants most purchase capacity tied on the sales side too, leaving only a few percent liquid, to avoid P&L volatility.

qa_highlights.question: What is the spread on the services and position-taking business?
qa_highlights.answer: Services earn about INR 0.3 per unit this quarter as service revenue; position-taking margins are much higher and contract-specific.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of the Energy Solutions EBIT and volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 570 crore from long-term contracted volume of 3,325 MU; balance from services and trading on about 9,800 MU. About 400-500 MU is back-to-back with C&I customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 profit sustainable given the delayed monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said open positions create year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter variability; target is to close positions on both sides quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Smart meter revenue fell QoQ in presentation: why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said accounting treatment (capex booked as expense and revenue) explains the presentation figures; commissioned meter operating revenue rose from INR 68 crore to about INR 161-166 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Who is party to the 2.5 GW Maharashtra round-the-clock contract?
qa_highlights.answer: LOI was issued to Adani Power, but AESL expects to be a major participant and may buy power from Adani Power to fulfil the solution.

qa_highlights.question: Right-of-way challenges and STU payment mechanism?
qa_highlights.answer: ROW handled at ground level in parallel with state machinery; STU payment mechanism mirrors CTU structure with distribution companies paying STU monthly.

539254|2026-09.headline: AESL Q2 FY27: total income up over 50%, EBITDA up ~67%, PAT up 145% as Energy Solutions earned strong merchant margins; smart meter deployment lagged.
539254|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong quarter, with total income up over 50%, EBITDA up close to 67% and PAT up 145% year on year. Capex deployed in H1 reached about INR7,850 crore, described as an all-time high, with transmission capex guided to about INR14,000 crore for FY27. Energy Solutions revenue was over INR2,000 crore and EBITDA over INR800 crore in the quarter, helped by merchant market conditions that management said will not be repeated at that level. Smart meter installations were slower than expected in H1, which management attributed to consumer resistance and utility-specified installation scopes. Transmission commissioning in H1 was minimal, with ROW issues in Gujarat delaying Halvad and Navinal, and management still targets some FY27 commissioning.

financial_highlights.metric: Energy Solutions H1 long-term sale revenue

segments.name: Distribution (AEML, MUL)
segments.commentary: Mumbai distribution losses fell to 4.29% in H1 FY27 while consumption rose more than 10%, per management.

Transmission commissioning: Khavda Phase 4 one element done; Khavda-Lakadia progressing; Halvad has about 50 locations pending due to ROW; WRSR at final commissioning stage with drone-based stringing; Navinal may slip to next year H1; Mahan Phase 1 this year, Phase 2 in Q1 next year.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Intellismart transaction close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CCI approval is pending and expected soon; all utility approvals are secured, and completion is expected within about one month of CCI approval.

qa_highlights.question: Why was smart meter deployment slow in H1, and how will H2 pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited consumer resistance and utility-specified scopes (Maharashtra HT consumers first, Bihar tagging); with these resolved, pace is expected to rise significantly.

qa_highlights.question: Will Energy Solutions margins fall with the shift to long-term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said long-term PPAs will yield steadier margins of about INR0.80-1.00 per unit versus the currently high merchant margins; volumes to rise to 7,000-8,000 MW over 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10 million smart meter target for FY27 still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 target is about 8-9 million, with 4-4.5 million balance in the next half year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the transmission capitalisation target of about INR15,000 crore being revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Not for now; management is hopeful of completing WRSR, Halvad and Khavda Phase 4 this year and will reassess in the next six months.

qa_highlights.answer: No mandatory thermal component; management said it is exploring long-term thermal capacity from Adani Power or third parties, without locking in quantities.

539289|2026-06.headline: Aurum PropTech Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 70.9% YoY to INR 111.84 crore and PBT turned positive at INR 2.31 crore, with Housing.com acquisition announced.
539289|2026-06.overview: Aurum PropTech reported its third consecutive profitable quarter, with revenue from operations of INR 111.84 crore (up 70.9% YoY but down from INR 123.85 crore QoQ) and PBT of INR 2.31 crore (2.1% margin). Management said PBT margins expanded 1,590 bps and adjusted EBITDA margins 1,320 bps YoY. The quarter also featured the announced acquisition of Housing.com, which management says is loss-making and targeted to reach profitability in four to six quarters; the company guided to a burn of about INR 200 crore annualised at Housing. Management also said the INR 112 crore sale of a building closed during the quarter, contributing INR 52.38 crore of other income from discontinued operations.

Management cited marketplaces valued at 4.5x revenue in India and 10x in another marketplace; says Aurum acquired Housing at about 1.5x revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is there cannibalisation risk between Housing.com organic listings and Aurum Analytica paid lead generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no cannibalisation and views Housing as adding an end-to-end vertical from listings to advertising, lead generation and transactions.

qa_highlights.question: Where will Housing.com market share go over the next two to three years and what tax rate should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to upsell more SKUs within the Housing cohort and extend into transactions; tax structure evaluation is ongoing, with positions to be given in Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unit economics and loss at Housing.com and what are the priority fixes?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities: monetise intent via transactions, increase utilisation of under-used Housing SKUs, ancillary cross-selling, cut top-heavy corporate costs, streamline sales team and marketing spend (Meta, Google). Target four to six quarters to break-even.

qa_highlights.question: What is Housing.com's FY26 loss and burn, and how does it compare with 99acres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Housing's current burn is about INR 200 crore annualised; FY26 numbers still under audit and to be shared later. It argued listing-only models carry losses and the transaction layer is the differentiator.

qa_highlights.question: How will dilution and ecosystem cross-selling be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Deora said the REA stake (24.9% post-deal) brings strategic value; Housing adds the top of the funnel for cross-selling to PropTiger, KuberX and Analytica. No numerical cross-sell metric was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be profitable at company level within two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees potential for company-level profitability as existing businesses are profitable, but will guide after the Housing deal closes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did QoQ revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Shrikant Jagtap said a PropTiger revenue category crystallised on target-slab achievement in Q4 FY26; slabs unlock mainly in the second half, so the drop is seasonal rather than one-time.

Quarter-on-quarter revenue decline (INR 123.85 crore to INR 111.84 crore) and distribution revenue down to INR 55.94 crore from INR 66.87 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can KuberX scale to match Square Yards' mortgage-led revenue?

qa_highlights.answer: Internal breakeven target is 4 to 6 quarters and external target 6 to 8 quarters, with profitability expected before that. Management said a price softening could be turned into an opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What are the integration cost cuts and revenue synergies for Housing.com, and what is the AI spend?

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, which management says it is confident of achieving.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR 12,000 crore, mainly BOP EPC and O&M; FY28 target INR 12,000-15,000 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12.5% including other income, up 0.25-0.3 percentage points.
MDO revenue targets: about INR 500 crore in FY27 (KBP INR 350 crore, Tasra/SAIL INR 150 crore), INR 1,250 crore in FY28, and about INR 2,100-2,200 crore at full capacity in FY29-30.
Blended EBITDA is guided to rise about 0.5% a year to 14% by FY30 and about 14.25% in FY31.
FY27 capex of about INR 400 crore at Power Mech level (washery) and about INR 400 crore at the Tasra SPV, without debt.
capex_capacity: KBP mine (Kurmitar area) began production in November 2025; the client is lifting above contract capacity, and FY26 offtake was about 1.6 million tonnes.
Tasra washery construction should finish by December 2026, with washed coal from Q4 FY27 and Tasra production from mid Q4 FY27. Management says the Tasra ramp-up reaches peak rated capacity in FY29.
Target full capacity: KBP about 5 million tonnes by FY30; SAIL/Tasra about 4 million tonnes by FY29.
Current metro O&M covers about 1,095 operational km in India, expected to reach 2,000 km; Mumbai light rail O&M covers 15 stations.
Annual power commissioning is expected to reach about 8,000 MW a year, which management sees as driving installation, civil and O&M demand.
demand_pricing: Management identified about INR 70,000 crore of opportunities for FY27 across power, non-power, metro O&M and EPC. Its past bidding is about INR 40,000-50,000 crore at a hit ratio of about 15%.
BOP opportunities worth about INR 15,000 crore are being bid for 2-3 projects, with a target of one more BOP win in FY27.
Pricing is the main constraint on BHEL packages; management says BHEL is changing its packaging approach.
Named opportunities: BALCO O&M about INR 1,500 crore, Butibori O&M about INR 700 crore, and NMDC EPC tenders worth about INR 8,000-10,000 crore with Thyssenkrupp as partner.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value remains, with about INR 128 crore of work awaiting certification and INR 90 crore receivable. Management has stopped new water bids.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 10,000 crore order target missed, and is FY27 better?
qa_highlights.answer: The miss was mainly the INR 1,563 crore West Bengal BESS cancellation. Management expects West Bengal to re-tender, and says Bangalore Metro and Monorail (L1 in April) support about INR 10,000 crore; FY27 target is INR 12,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook given water division delays and labour code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 EBITDA of about 12.5%, up 0.25-0.3 points, helped by more O&M and EPC mix. The Labour Code gratuity provision in Q4 was about INR 4.5 crore for the full-year impact.

qa_highlights.question: Do escalation clauses protect margins against commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic contracts carry PVC/escalation clauses that are billed to clients. International business is mainly O&M manpower, so impact is limited; the 1.2-1.5% of international order book is largely O&M.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MDO FY28 cut from INR 1,800-1,900 crore to INR 1,250 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The KBP washery is not ready on the CCL side, so offtake is conservatively put at INR 350 crore in FY27. The SAIL/Tasra ramp from zero to 4 million tonnes in one year is treated as a challenge, so FY28 is INR 750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MDO margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin is about 15% at present, and management expects about 1 percentage point a year, reaching 20%-21% at peak rated capacity around FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Are there labour shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount is above 40,000, with 70-75% in labour roles and about 18,000 in O&M. Management says construction and installation labour is the constraint, but schedules have been met so far.

risks_watch: Order inflow execution: FY26 missed by about 28%, and the FY27 target of INR 12,000 crore depends on BOP wins against BHEL's changed packaging approach and pricing.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value is stalled pending central and state fund release, and certification delays weigh on margins.
MDO ramp-up: KBP and Tasra volumes depend on client offtake, the CCL washery, and the rainy season. The FY27 MDO target (INR 500 crore) is well above the Q4 monthly run-rate once March is excluded.
Commodity and labour inflation: steel, cement and diesel prices have risen. Recovery relies on PVC clauses, and labour availability is a constraint.
Management's 1-point-a-year margin expansion in MDO and blended EBITDA targets rest on O&M and EPC mix shifts.
539302|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and bullish on long-term power and O&M demand, but cautious on near-term order inflow and the water division. Management was explicit about the BESS cancellation and the MDO timing shortfall, and gave specific numbers on most questions. Some answers on segment figures and MDO revenue were revised during the call, which weakens the precision of the guidance.

Of course, on the BOP side, we are going to bid for two- three projects, that's worth INR 15000 crores.
We are confident of achieving that, and even the MDO business ramp -up of production is happening, and we are more focused on the high -margin O&M business.

539334|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 21.1% to Rs 976.6 crore, but Unit 5/6 commissioning is stalled by raw-material price spikes, with FY27 revenue guided to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore.
539334|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 976.6 crore (+21.1%), EBITDA Rs 99.5 crore (10.2% margin) and PAT Rs 70.1 crore (7.1% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was about Rs 218 crore with EBITDA Rs 22.1 crore and PAT Rs 12.9 crore, held back by raw-material availability. Management said it deliberately stopped dispatches in the second week of March 2026 as ammonia and sulphur prices roughly tripled, and new Unit 5 and Unit 6 capacity has not been commissioned. Management lowered its FY27 revenue visibility to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 72,423 MT (+27.9%) for Rs 531.8 crore, with segment revenue up 25.2%. Q4 FY26 sales 13,725 MT (+36% YoY) for Rs 126.4 crore. Management cited H Acid at about Rs 750/kg (from Rs 525-530/kg) and Vinyl Sulphone at about Rs 350/kg (from Rs 240/kg).

segments.name: Fertilisers
segments.commentary: FY26 sales 252,777 MT for Rs 444.8 crore, with segment revenue up 16.5%. Q4 FY26 sales 50,500 MT for Rs 91.8 crore. Management said NBS subsidy was raised on 1 Feb and 1 Apr 2026 but is still not sufficient for current raw-material costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue visibility lowered to Rs 1,250-1,300 crore from the earlier Rs 1,500 crore, assuming about Rs 1,000 crore from existing plants at 65-70% utilisation and Rs 250 crore from Rabi season; no benefit from higher current prices assumed.
Kharif FY27 season expected to contribute no revenue from Unit 5 or Unit 6; start of trial production under evaluation, with management saying it could start within about one month.
Q1 FY27 expected to benefit from liquidating inventory held back in Q4; management said PAT should be about 8-8.5% of revenue and Q1 sales above Rs 250 crore, without firm numbers.
Normal tax rate guided at 22-25% for FY27, with deferred tax expected to rise significantly as Unit 5, Unit 6 and solar capitalise.
Management sees 8-10% margins as achievable, while noting that sulphur may settle at about Rs 70-75/kg rather than the earlier Rs 30-35/kg.
capex_capacity: Total planned capex Rs 512 crore; Rs 189 crore incurred as of 31 March 2026, funded by internal accruals and preferential allotment.

Unit 5 (dyes) and Unit 6 are mechanically ready; Unit 6 about 90-95% complete. Commissioning delayed by electricity issues (resolved in March 2026) and raw-material price spikes; no capitalisation yet.
Solar: 1.1 MW DC commissioned at Hisar, Haryana, taking installed capacity to 10.6 MW DC; 10 MW Nanded plant on track, which would take total to 20.6 MW DC.

Planned Rs 350 crore additional facility at Madhya Bharat Phosphates, Meghnagar (Unit 3). About Rs 140 crore sits in AAA-rated bonds, plus Rs 30 crore preferential allotment to promoter; remaining about Rs 180 crore to come from accruals, with possibly 25-30% term loan.
Plant utilisation currently 65-70% per CFO; Unit 1 sulphuric plant was shut for maintenance in Q4.
demand_pricing: Ammonia rose from Rs 40-42/kg to Rs 100+/kg and sulphur from Rs 30/kg to about Rs 100/kg, according to management.
Sulphur rose a further 20% in May 2026 up to 19 May, per management.
Management said demand is weakening as prices rise and that the market is accepting the higher prices for chemicals, though fertiliser acceptability at current prices is uncertain.

Company stopped SSP dispatches in the second week of March 2026 deliberately to avoid selling at the old cost base; management said FY26 revenue would have crossed Rs 1,000 crore if sales had continued for 15 more days.
Management said the company has not factored in the higher current selling prices in its FY27 outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 320-odd crore capex be funded, and what is the maths?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 174 crore and Rs 155 crore phases were funded internally except a Rs 25 crore HDFC solar term loan, and the new Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat project will use about Rs 170 crore of existing bonds and preferential allotment, with the balance from accruals or a possible 25-30% term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-28 outlook for Unit 5 and 6 after the delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the electricity issue was resolved in March 2026 but raw-material price spikes delayed start-up; FY27 revenue is now visualised at Rs 1,250-1,300 crore, with no Kharif contribution from Units 5 and 6.

qa_highlights.question: Will the inventory benefit flow into Q1 FY27, and can it be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY27 should be better than recent quarters as held-back Q4 inventory is liquidated, but declined to quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue flat YoY in Q4 despite chemical volumes up over 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not answer on the call and said the company would respond through its IR advisor.

qa_highlights.question: What tax rate should be assumed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a normal rate of 22-25% should be used, with deferred tax rising next year as Unit 5, Unit 6 and solar are capitalised; the Q4 deferred tax charge of about Rs 4-4.5 crore related to land recognised as right-of-use assets for the Madhya Bharat project.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 PAT fall short of the 8% margin management had earlier signalled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT would have been Rs 75-80 crore without the deferred tax charge and leasehold-land provisions, which brought it to Rs 70 crore for FY26 (about 7%).

risks_watch: Raw-material cost and supply: ammonia and sulphur prices have roughly tripled and remain volatile; management could not predict when they will ease.
Unit 5 and 6 start-up timing is unresolved; the Kharif season is lost and Rabi FY27 is the next opportunity.
Demand and fertiliser affordability at current prices; management said subsidy support is not yet adequate and noted a 10% government cap.
Q1 FY27 inventory-liquidation benefit is unquantified, and management declined to give numbers; also the Q4 revenue-versus-volume gap is unexplained on the call.
Deferred tax and effective tax rate will rise in FY27 as projects capitalise; a term loan may be used for the Rs 350 crore Madhya Bharat capex.
Governance and disclosure: management relied on the CFO for most figures and its tone on the call was unusually unstructured.
539334|2026-03.management_tone: Management was candid but cautious, emphasising conservatism and a wait-and-see stance on Units 5 and 6 and on FY27 pricing. Its visibility was often hedged ("I can't read too far"), and it repeatedly deferred detailed numbers to the CFO or to later IR follow-up.
key_quotes: So, sir, let the market be matured. Let the market be accepting these new prices, which are almost three times of the raw material prices of our earlier.
Old numbers will never be seen again.
So we will definitely do Rs. 250 crores in that. Rs. 1000 crores and Rs. 250 crores.

539334|2026-06.headline: Shree Pushkar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 280-281 crore and EBITDA rose 9.7% to Rs 31.9 crore, despite volumes falling sharply.
539334|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 10% YoY on higher realisations even though fertiliser volumes fell to 66,527 MT from 76,288 MT and chemical volumes fell to 9,113 MT from 14,837 MT. EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2%, with PAT up about 9% to Rs 22.9 crore. Management said acid plants were run at low load due to high sulphur prices and working-capital strain, and Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 are close to trial operation. Management reiterated an FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, which it said could reach Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, with PAT of around 8.5-9%.

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 142 crore, up 4% YoY, on 66,527 MT volume (down from 76,288 MT). Management said inventory is being held in anticipation of higher prices.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 138 crore, up 17.1% YoY, on 9,113 MT (down from 14,837 MT). Acid plants were put on low load; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, with management saying it could reach Rs 1,300-1,400 crore (Rs 1,350-1,400 crore in one answer), and PAT of around 8.5-9%.
Management expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and better than Q2 FY26 (about 110% higher, per management's reply to an analyst's Rs 250-285 crore comparison).
Unit 6 expected to start trials by end-August or September 2026, giving about 4-5 months of operation in FY27.
Next year (FY28) with a full 12 months of Unit 6 could reach Rs 1,700-1,750 crore, per management's personal view.
Management says peak revenue for all units could reach about Rs 1,700 crore at current prices once Unit 6 is on stream.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of Rs 209 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026 against a total planned Rs 512 crore; about Rs 20 crore spent in Q1 FY27.
Expansions at Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 and Meghnagar are expected to add 450,000 MT per annum of fertiliser capacity and 72,000 MT per annum of chemical capacity.

Unit 5 dyes plant (small vertical, about Rs 37 crore) and 10 MW DC solar project at Nanded are complete or nearing completion; total solar capacity to reach 20.6 MW DC once commissioned. Capitalisation not yet announced.
Acquired about 30,000 sq m of land adjacent to Unit 1 at Lote Parshuram for Rs 9.3 crore in Q1.
Madhya Bharat (Madhya Pradesh) project has Rs 60 crore invested to June; timeline 2028. Plant is about twice Unit 6 capacity and includes an 800 TPD chemical plant for captive NPK integration.
Rs 125 crore in non-lien deposits as of 30 June 2026; capex funded from internal accruals and preferential issue proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are absorbing higher raw material prices, and demand is recovering after a pause during the West Asia conflict.
Sulphur prices have risen to about USD 1,100/t from USD 250-300 earlier, per management; ammonia and sulphur shortages followed Hormuz closure.
K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus per management; company says it is the largest K-acid maker in India and has inquiries for K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone from China.
Dye utilisation has decreased due to the global scenario, per management.
Management says it chose value over volume, with dispatches stopped in mid-March 2026 in expectation of higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 volume weakness mitigating, and is the company on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is optimistic, citing 40 days of data, and expects Q2 to beat Q1; volumes should be met while protecting value.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 not reflect the upside from orders held back from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders retracted in Q4 do not carry over into Q1, and that EBITDA and PAT each rose about 10% YoY, so recovery is visible.

qa_highlights.question: Why were acid plants run at low load?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur requires advance payment while acid is sold on credit, and working-capital stress made the margin unattractive; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company fill existing capacity before expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unit 5 and 6 are nearly complete and that the Madhya Bharat expansion is also underway, citing confidence in the team and available cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is DAP substitution affecting NPK and SSP demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management questioned DAP availability and said that if DAP is cheaper and available, farmers will shift, so product availability is the key variable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter battery-grade phosphoric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the agenda for now; the focus is on stabilising current expansions first.

risks_watch: Volumes are down about 17% in fertiliser and about 39% in chemicals YoY, and management has prioritised pricing over volume.
Unit 6 start-up timing depends on long-term raw material contracts, due by August or September 2026; ammonia and sulphur supply and price remain volatile with Hormuz still closed.
Working-capital strain from advance sulphur payments; acid plants at low load.
Management guidance has moved between Rs 1,250 crore, Rs 1,300-1,400 crore and Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, and its PAT target is 8.5-9% versus a remark of up to about 10%.
Inconsistent figures in the call: revenue of Rs 280.1 crore vs Rs 281.1 crore; EBITDA of Rs 31.9 crore vs Rs 31 crore; PAT growth of 9.4% vs 9%. Verify against the filing.
Capex of Rs 303 crore remains to be spent against the Rs 512 crore plan.

Rs 31.9 crore (11.4% margin); CFO quoted Rs 31 crore

So, I believe Q2 will be even better than Q1.

It was cautious on Unit 5 and 6 start-up, saying it is taking a measured approach, and it declined to confirm the 10% PAT figure, reiterating 8.5-9%.

539336|2026-03.headline: Gujarat Energy FY26 EBITDA rose to INR3,772 crore (from INR3,241 crore) while PAT was flat at INR2,299 crore; the merger became effective 1 May 2026.
539336|2026-03.overview: The GSPC/GSPL merger into Gujarat Gas became effective 1 May 2026, with the company renamed Gujarat Energy from 14 May 2026. Q4 FY26 EBITDA was INR943 crore (vs INR790 crore a year earlier), and CNG volume hit a record 3.6 mmscmd. Morbi ceramic demand ramped sharply to about 8 mmscmd after the Middle East conflict constrained propane and LPG supply. Management said FY26 financials are not like-for-like with FY25 because of the demerger and merger accounting, and gave segment EBITDA for the first time on a call. The board recommended a dividend of INR8.90 per share (about INR835 crore outgo).

financial_highlights.change: vs INR790 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR8.90 per share (445% of face value); outgo about INR835 crore

financial_highlights.metric: CGD EBITDA per SCM (FY26, excluding amalgamation impact)

financial_highlights.value: Gas trading about INR400 crore; CGD about INR450 crore; E&P about INR14 crore; renewables about INR5 crore

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Total trading volume was 10.2 mmscmd in FY26, of which about 5.3 mmscmd was intersegment sales to CGD; net external volume was about 4.9 mmscmd, down about 19% from FY25. Management guided trading margins of 4-6% and said FY26 included a one-off of about INR200 crore linked to a Petronet LNG regasification liability, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

segments.name: City Gas Distribution (CGD)
segments.commentary: Q4 CNG volume was a record 3.6 mmscmd (up 12% YoY) across 839 stations, with 17.68 lakh vehicles. Domestic PNG customers crossed 24.18 lakh; Q4 PNG industrial volume was 4.19 mmscmd, up about 7% QoQ. Morbi volume rose 21% QoQ to an average of 2.02 mmscmd in Q4.

segments.name: Exploration and production (E&P)
segments.commentary: FY26 EBITDA was about INR29 crore, but the segment is loss-making after depreciation. Reserves are stated at 6.71 mmboe. FY27 E&P capex is about INR100 crore for planned drilling.

segments.name: Power (renewables / GSEG and GPPC gas-based plants)
segments.commentary: Plant load factors were about 1% at GPPC and about 6.5% at GSEG. FY26 segment EBITDA was about INR46 crore (renewables, as stated), and the segment reported losses due to forex and impairment items of about INR15 crore and INR23 crore. The company is reviewing options for the 700 MW combined-cycle plant, whose PPA runs to 2036.

guidance_outlook: CGD margin guidance of about INR5-6 per SCM was given, with a target of about INR5.5-6.5 per SCM; management said trading margins will be maintained.
Morbi price is about INR75 per SCM (non-Morbi about INR68) per management; June was raised by about INR1.5. Management said Morbi demand can reach 8.8-8.9 mmscmd, about 10% above the current level.
FY27 capex guidance: about INR1,000 crore for CGD and about INR100 crore for E&P; no capex for trading.
Gas trading volume is expected to grow 25-30% by FY30-31 from the current 10-12 mmscmd, with prices seen as reasonable from FY28-29.
Tax: about INR1,900 crore of tax losses remain to be used, so no tax is expected on profits up to that amount; the balance is to be used within about 8 years.
GTL demerger share listing is expected to complete by end-July 2026; the listing approval for new Gujarat Energy shares (about 93 crore shares total) is expected within 7-10 days.
capex_capacity: CGD capex guidance is about INR1,000 crore; E&P capex about INR100 crore for drilling a few wells.
Gujarat Energy holds about 36.8-38% of GSPC LNG (investment about INR1,700 crore), following conversion of outstanding amounts into equity; it became a subsidiary.
GSPC Mundra LNG regasification terminal utilisation was about 17% in FY26; it is now at about 35-38% from May 2026.
Management is exploring a dedicated propane import jetty, JT and storage tanks near Morbi, with port authorities in Gujarat under discussion.
Long-term regasification capacity at Dahej is 2.25 MMTPA; long-term LNG totals about 2.96 MTPA (about 10.66 mmscmd).
demand_pricing: Morbi ceramic units on gas rose from 83 (1.66 mmscmd) in March 2026 to 710 units (about 8 mmscmd) by late May 2026; contracts are signed monthly.

Non-Morbi industrial pricing is about INR68 per SCM and Morbi about INR75 per SCM; an analyst's spot-LNG math suggested Morbi margins may be negative at current spot LNG prices, which management did not accept.
Sourcing mix (per management): APM about 2 mmscmd, New Well Gas 0.4-0.5 mmscmd, long-term LNG about 3.5 mmscmd (majority Brent-linked), short-term about 3.5 mmscmd.
FY26 gas trading sales by user: CGD companies about 52-53%, fertilisers about 27%, others (refinery, power, industry) the rest.
Two new long-term LNG SPAs signed in FY26 (Qatar Energy and Uniper, up to 1.36 MTPA combined); Qatar 1 MTPA ramps up to 2030; 2 cargoes already lost in May-June 2026 due to the West Asia conflict.

qa_highlights.question: Is Morbi volume at a peak, and what is the pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Current sales are about 8 mmscmd, with customers indicating up to 8.8-8.9 mmscmd. Pricing is about INR75 per SCM in Morbi and about INR68 elsewhere, indexed to exchange rate and calorific value.

qa_highlights.question: What are the one-off items in gas trading and the segment profit baseline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the recurring trading run rate is about INR1,000-1,100 crore a year. FY26 included about INR200 crore of one-off liability linked to a Petronet LNG back-to-back arrangement, plus a customs duty refund of about INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the power business and its outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PLF was about 1% at GPPC and about 6.5% at GSEG. Management is evaluating reviving the plants through alignment with other businesses. GUVNL pays fixed costs of about INR2.5-3 per unit. Management said the plants are not a drag at present, and a steady-state profit cannot be given until a new arrangement is identified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage LNG price risk as Morbi volumes grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Brent-linked long-term volumes from Qatar and Uniper are priced competitively against propane. It is also seeking Henry Hub-linked long-term volumes to give stable pricing for Morbi customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the deployment plan for surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has appointed McKinsey to develop a growth and deployment strategy. It expects to share the way forward in the next quarter or a subsequent one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company transfer trading profits to CGD on a cost basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intersegment pricing will be optimised over time as the two segments are evaluated separately. The company now has flexibility to make intersegment sales without the arm's-length constraint.

risks_watch: Propane supply tightness supports Morbi demand, but a normalisation could cut spot prices and volumes; management said it would still compete.
Spot LNG price and INR/USD moves could compress Morbi and CGD margins; an analyst's calculation showed a possible negative spread at spot LNG of about $17-18/MMBtu.

The INR1,334.61 crore trading EBIT includes one-offs, so the recurring run rate may be lower (about INR1,000-1,100 crore per management); also watch intersegment transfer pricing, which shifts profit between trading and CGD.
The power segment (about 1,000 MW) is loss-making with very low PLF; its revival plan and the 700 MW PPA economics are unresolved.

Cash and other financial assets are unclear: management cited about INR5,000 crore cash, while the balance sheet shows about INR1,300 crore cash plus about INR5,500 crore other financial assets, including GSFS-placed funds. The company will provide a breakup.
Watch Q1 FY27 results (early August 2026) for the first post-merger quarter and EBITDA by segment.

539336|2026-06.headline: Gujarat Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% to INR9,670 crores and PAT 78% to INR998 crores, led by gas trading EBT of INR726 crores.
539336|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR9,670 crores (up 63% YoY), EBITDA INR1,482 crores (up 65%) and PAT INR998 crores (up 78%), with total sales volume of 15.66 mmscmd. Gas trading EBT rose 206% to INR726 crores, helped by Brent-linked long-term contracts and a Morbi industrial volume surge during the Middle East-driven propane shortage. Management kept FY27 gas trading profit guidance at about INR1,100 crores (reiterated as INR1,100-1,200 crores in one answer) and CGD EBITDA guidance at INR5.5-6.5/scm, while saying Morbi volumes will likely settle near 3 mmscmd as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources.

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Sales volume 12.22 mmscmd, of which 8.9 mmscmd was transferred to CGD and about 3.3 mmscmd was external; EBT INR726 crores. Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd earlier, due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and lower power volumes; long-term third-party volume expected at 4.5-5 mmscmd in FY28-29.

segments.name: CGD - CNG
segments.commentary: Volume 3.76 mmscmd, up 13% from 3.33 mmscmd (Gujarat +12%, outside Gujarat +19%). Network at 844 stations after adding 6 and upgrading 9 in the quarter; plans for more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades in FY27.

segments.name: CGD - PNG domestic
segments.commentary: Added about 59,000 domestic PNG customers in the quarter, taking the base above 2.477 million households. Commercial PNG volume was 0.17 mmscmd with more than 16,600 commercial customers.

segments.name: PNG industrial
segments.commentary: Volume 7.17 mmscmd vs 4.71 mmscmd, up 64%. Morbi averaged 5.67 mmscmd and non-Morbi 2.04 mmscmd; non-Morbi realisation about INR70/scm and Morbi about INR78/scm, against propane at about INR65/scm.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Gas-based plants run at very low utilisation: about 6% PLF at the 51 MW GSEG plant and about 1% at Pipavav in Q1, with peak summer demand the only driver.

segments.name: E&P and renewables
segments.commentary: Q1 FY26 EBITDA was INR7 crores (E&P) and INR14 crores (renewables); Q4 FY26 was INR14 crores and INR5 crores. No Q1 FY27 figures were given on the call.

guidance_outlook: Gas trading profit guidance kept at about INR1,100 crores for FY27 on total trading volume, with a 4-5% margin target; one answer cited INR1,100-1,200 crores.
CGD EBITDA guidance kept at INR5.5-6.5/scm; Q2 FY27 is the earliest point for firmer FY27 numbers given Middle East volatility.
CGD capex guided at about INR1,000 crores; no capex planned for gas trading; propane import terminal capex excluded and at early study stage, with capex over the next two years.
Morbi gas volume expected at about 3 mmscmd near term; 1.8-2 mmscmd assumed as a floor on one-month contracts.
Non-Morbi industrial volume targeted at 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise.
Long-term sourcing about 28% (about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent) today, targeted at least 4 million tonnes by 2030; new long-term supply from 2028.
Concrete plan for deploying about INR7,200 crores cash expected by Q3 FY27.
GSPL Transmission listing expected towards early September 2026; Q2 results around mid-November.
capex_capacity: CGD capex of about INR1,000 crores guided for FY27; INR127 crores invested in CGD infrastructure in Q1.
CNG network at 844 stations; more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades planned in FY27.
Pipeline network about 45,900 km across six states and one union territory.
Own propane import and storage terminal near Morbi: sites shortlisted in Gujarat, detailed project report pending, capex over about two years and not in the INR1,000 crore plan.
Gas sourcing for CGD: about 14% APM, 6% new well gas, 2% GAIL pool, 9% long-term, and about 69% short-term or inter-segment.
demand_pricing: Morbi current run-rate about 3 mmscmd of gas vs about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from the US and Venezuela after July.
Management said spot prices near $20/mmBtu make gas costlier than propane, so volume recovery is unlikely near term.
Gas trading sourcing: about 20% long-term (Brent-linked, of which about 20% Henry Hub), 12.5% domestic, about 67% spot.

Morbi volume rose from about 0.4 mmscmd in April 2026 to about 8 mmscmd in May-June, with the Morbi cluster up 181% vs Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How do 15.66 mmscmd total volume, 12.2 mmscmd gas trading and 12.34 mmscmd CGD reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15.66 is the company total and CGD is 12.34; after removing the 8.9 mmscmd intercompany sale to CGD, external sales are about 3.32 mmscmd.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current Morbi run-rate and how does pricing compare with propane?
qa_highlights.answer: Current Morbi run-rate is about 3 mmscmd of gas versus about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources. Gas is priced about INR78/scm against propane at about INR65/scm.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNG growth outlook for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects CNG growth of about 12-13% to be sustained for the next couple of years, supported by more than 75 new stations planned in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will third-party gas trading volumes recover, and what is the long-term range?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd to about 3.3 mmscmd due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and weak power volumes. Management expects long-term third-party volume of 4.5-5 mmscmd, mainly in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a sourcing breakup for CGD and gas trading, and what is the long-term share?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD sourcing: about 14% APM, 6% new well gas, 2% GAIL pool, 9% long-term and about 69% short-term or inter-segment. Gas trading: about 20% long-term (about 20% of which is Henry Hub), 12.5% domestic and about 67% spot. Long-term share is about 28%, or about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent, targeted at 4 million tonnes or more by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gas trading margin high in Q1, and can it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to timely sourcing and Brent-linked long-term contracts. It ruled out negative trading quarters and maintained FY27 gas trading profit guidance of about INR1,100 crores on total volume, with a 4-5% margin target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CGD EBITDA position against guidance, and why is it below range?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD EBITDA was about INR5.18/scm, below the INR5.5-6.5/scm guidance, which management attributed to a larger volume base. Management kept the guidance and said it looks at portfolio margins rather than segment-level Morbi margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-Morbi industrial volume plans and constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-Morbi volume is about 2-2.2 mmscmd; management targets at least 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise. It cited infrastructure build-out, with about 86 new industries added in April-June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Morbi volume floor and how is the propane terminal funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumed 1.8-2 mmscmd as a floor on one-month contracts. The propane import terminal is at the site-shortlisting stage, excluded from the INR1,000 crore CGD capex, and would take about two years to build after a detailed project report.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR7,200 crore cash and dividends?

Power segment utilisation very low (about 6% PLF at GSEG and 1% at Pipavav); revival strategy to be shared in a few months.

539359|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 36.2% YoY to INR138.46 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.02% on raw material and gas cost spikes.
539359|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue for FY26 reached INR482.95 crore, up 35.32% YoY, with EBITDA of INR71.03 crore (14.71% margin) and PAT of INR23.20 crore. Q4 EBITDA margin dropped to 12.02% from the 16-17% range management cited earlier, which management attributed to raw material, gas, freight and outsourced labour cost increases in March 2026. Management expects margins to recover toward 15-16% if the war-related cost disruption does not worsen, and guided Q1 FY27 revenue at a similar run rate to Q4. Capacity is about 72,000 MTPA with FY26 output of 52,620 MT, and the company plans about 7,800 MT of foundry addition in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Large castings (gearboxes, transmission cases, differential carriers)
segments.commentary: Management calls large castings the main driver of product mix improvement, citing fewer competitors (about 8-10 in India for tractor large castings) and higher value addition.

segments.name: LFC (lost foam casting) via Meeta Casting
segments.commentary: Contributes about 10-15% of revenue and about 20% of the order book; management targets 30% in three years. Margin is about 1-2% higher than conventional castings.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Not yet material; product development and qualification ongoing with three to four products developed. Initial contributions expected in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue target of INR600 crore; management says 15% growth for the next two years gets there. Also cited 15% growth for the company against 6-8% expected from customers in FY27.
Margins expected to recover toward 15-16% (EBITDA) if no further war-related disruption; Q1 FY27 revenue expected similar to Q4 FY26.

FY27 capex of about INR25-30 crore, of which about INR35 crore is for the 7,800 MT foundry addition (the figures on the 7,800 MT project were given inconsistently in the call). FY28 LFC project of 2,400 MT, with about INR60-70 crore capex.
Long-term target of crossing 1 lakh MT capacity by FY28.
Target minimum EBITDA of 18-20% for planned US finishing operations, versus 14-15% in India.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 72,000 MTPA across Dera Bassi, Hoshiarpur, Mohali and Tahliwal. Utilisation about 73-74% (around 52,000 MT); management says 80-85% is achievable in FY27 if market holds.

FY28: about 2,400 MT of LFC capacity; capacity to cross 1 lakh MT. Management said LFC capacity mix would be about 70/30 to 65/35 (conventional/LFC) after this addition.
Greenfield LFC economics: 3,000 MT capacity at about INR75 crore versus INR120-150 crore for conventional, roughly 50% lower capex.

demand_pricing: Customers expect 6-8% growth in FY27 with H2 facing a high base; company expects about 15% from new products and projects.
Company says it gained share with almost all customers: market grew 16-17% while the company grew 34%.
Top three customers (M&M, Swaraj, TAFE, Escorts named) contribute about 50-55% of revenue.
Order book described as overbooked; Vishal's estimate of INR500-600 crore was affirmed as easily achievable, but no official figure was stated.

Raw material cost up about 4-6% in March; management says raw material is passed through with about a one-quarter lag, while freight pass-through is being negotiated (monthly for some customers, quarterly for others).

Exports started to South Korea (one lot shipped, another going); Europe being explored. US subsidiary (Omnia Engineering Inc., Delaware) acquired for $50,000 with up to $100,000 planned; not yet operational.

qa_highlights.question: What is installed capacity and maximum utilisation, and why have EBITDA margins fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Installed capacity is 72,000 MT; utilisation about 73-74%, with 80-85% achievable this year. Margin fell to 12% because raw material prices rose sharply in March, aggravated by gas issues; recovery expected from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall in Q4, and will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material rose about 4-6%, and gas, outsourced labour, manpower and freight costs also rose in March. Management expects a reversion to 15-16% margins if war-related disruption does not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan and funding for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR25-30 crore, with about INR35 crore for the 7,800 MT project per management. FY28 LFC project of 2,400 MT needs about INR60-70 crore, funded by debt and equity; FY27 funded by debt only.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels and leverage comfort?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose to about INR180 crore this year, with interest cost about INR22 crore. Management said net debt-to-equity will stay below 1 at all times; comfortable at about 0.65.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US entity's margin profile and plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The US entity is aimed at direct US customers; initial work would be manufacturing in India, with later possible acquisition or a US plant. Finishing-only US operations are expected to give 18-20% EBITDA margins versus 14-15% in India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LFC share of revenue and order book, and what is the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: LFC is about 10-15% of revenue and about 20% of the order book. Margin is 1-2% higher than conventional castings. Customers added include KION India (domestic) and one in South Korea.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margin recovery depends on stabilisation of gas, crude-linked chemicals and diesel/freight costs; freight pass-through is still under negotiation.
Debt rose to about INR180 crore in FY26, with interest about INR22 crore; FY28 capex funding mix depends on equity raise plans that were not specified.
The 7,800 MT addition's capex figure was stated inconsistently (INR35 crore vs an earlier INR60-70 crore for the project); clarity needed.
Customer concentration: top three customers are about 50-55% of revenue.
Legacy components (about 60% of mix per management) carry lower margins; the new-component mix shift will determine margin trajectory.
US entity and export ramp-up are early-stage, with no revenue or timeline disclosed.

We do 100% machined castings. We don't give raw castings.

539400|2026-03.headline: Mallcom Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 7% YoY to INR147 crore, but EBITDA margin fell 185 bps to 9.34% on raw material costs.
539400|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue was INR147 crore (+7% YoY), with EBITDA down 11% YoY to INR14 crore and margin at 9.34%, and PAT of INR6 crore (4.29% margin). For FY26, revenue was INR540 crore (+11%), EBITDA INR61 crore (11.21% margin, down 130 bps), and PAT INR30 crore; FY25 PAT included a one-time INR25 crore land-sale gain, so the years are not directly comparable. Export OEM realisations fell on weak US and EU demand and tariff-driven concessions, while the domestic business grew about 20%. Both new units (Sanand, Gujarat and Chandipur, West Bengal) are now commissioned and ramping up.

segments.name: Domestic (branded)
segments.commentary: Management says the domestic business grew about 20% YoY in FY26 and is the growth engine; branded business has better pricing power. Last month of Q4 was softer on cautious sentiment and gas shortages for some industries.

segments.name: Exports (OEM / white label)
segments.commentary: Realisations fell on weak US and EU demand and concessions to hold share. South America, Australia, Russia and Africa were described as doing well; Europe and US weak; Middle East okay. LatAm sales are white label.

segments.name: New products (PU coated gloves, PVC gumboots, nitrile)
segments.commentary: In-house manufacturing started as import substitutes; management says pricing is competitive with imports and margins are similar to company level. India PU glove imports estimated at INR80-90 crore.

segments.name: Sanand, Gujarat (workwear/Protec unit)
segments.commentary: Commercial production started; running at about 50% utilisation, with INR40 crore minimum annual revenue targeted from existing capacity.

guidance_outlook: Management says 10-12% revenue growth is the bare minimum for FY27 and it is confident of achieving it, with upside if conditions improve.
Management wants to return to pre-investment EBITDA margins over time, but said there are many ifs and buts at this stage; an analyst's 14-15% normalised margin framing was not explicitly confirmed.
Expects FY27 revenue growth to come more from domestic than exports.
Capex: INR34 crore spent in FY26; budget INR10-15 crore for FY27 and similar annual levels thereafter, covering maintenance plus added machinery at Sanand and Chandipur.
Expects to apply for a capital subsidy for Sanand, estimated at about INR10 crore under the state policy.
Expects debt, mainly working capital, to decline further and most debt to be repaid over about 4 years; finance cost could approach near zero in 3 years (analyst framing, CFO said 'possible').
capex_capacity: Sanand, Gujarat (Protec unit) has commenced commercial production; utilisation about 50%, with INR40 crore minimum annual revenue targeted.
Chandipur, West Bengal industrial safety shoe unit is fully operational; capitalised in FY26 with INR7 crore of subsidy received against INR14 crore machinery cost.
In-house manufacturing of PU coated gloves and PVC gumboots started.
FY26 capex about INR34 crore; FY27 budget INR10-15 crore, with ongoing annual spend in a similar range.
demand_pricing: Export OEM realisations fell in FY26 due to near-full-year prohibitive US tariffs, weak EU demand and concessions to retain share; price pass-through lags, especially in long-lead OEM business.
Input costs rose across textiles, leather, PU/PC/NBR polymers, driven by petro-linked prices, FX depreciation, freight and energy costs.
Domestic: price list revised twice in the last quarter; competitors also raised prices, and some stopped taking orders or cancelled open orders.

US: volumes fell, but management says this reflects tariff conditions, not product, quality or price. India is outside the US TAA list, so an FTA is seen as key to regaining share; order cycles run 3 months to 2-2.5 years.
Competition: China seen as better placed on raw material sourcing and currency; unorganised players expected to be hurt by the cost environment, which management sees as favouring organised players.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall, and which export product prices decreased?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower realisations were mainly in export OEM markets, due to weak demand and concessions to keep customers. Domestic price increases lag input cost rises.

qa_highlights.question: How much could 10-12% growth and a 14-15% normalised margin be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-12% growth is the bare minimum and it is confident of it. It wants to return to pre-investment EBITDA margins, which it describes as the profile it would like to maintain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt outlook and finance cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: no term loan; working capital debt is about flat YoY at INR110-115 crore. Expects further reduction and most debt repaid over about 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key domestic demand drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour code formalisation, BIS standards tightening, rising worker awareness, wider distribution, more marketing and fleet, and import substitution. Management says domestic growth is sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan and subsidy?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was about INR34 crore; FY27 budget is INR10-15 crore, including maintenance plus added machinery at Sanand and Chandipur. Sanand subsidy of about INR10 crore is expected to be applied for this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the addressable market for PU gloves and PVC gumboots?
qa_highlights.answer: India imports an estimated INR80-90 crore of PU gloves; PVC gumboot market size was not quantified. Export revenue is also targeted for both products.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from petro-linked raw materials, FX and freight, with lagged pass-through to both domestic and export customers.
US market access: India is outside the TAA list, so recovery depends on a trade deal; EU demand and FTA timing also uncertain.
Sanand utilisation (about 50%) and ramp-up of new products against the INR40 crore revenue target.
Domestic demand softness in the last month of Q4 and possible cost-conservation by customers.
Subsidy receipt for Sanand (about INR10 crore) and debt reduction pace.
Q4 PAT margin of 4.29% and EBITDA margin of 9.34% as the base for FY27 margin recovery.

539400|2026-06.headline: Mallcom Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 25% QoQ to Rs 110 crore, while EBITDA margin rose 317 bps to 12.51% on pricing and raw material relief.

EBITDA held flat QoQ at Rs 14 crore, with margin up to 12.51%, and PAT rose 5% QoQ to Rs 7 crore (6.03% margin). Domestic revenue of Rs 64 crore grew 10% QoQ and was the highest-ever Q1 domestic number; international revenue was Rs 46 crore. Management said port congestion and weak Western demand cost the company a targeted double-digit export growth.

segments.name: International / Export
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 46 crore, down sharply QoQ on weak Western demand and port congestion; management says exports are about 55% of the mix. Europe is down about Rs 20 crore YoY in Q1 against about Rs 170 crore for last year.

segments.name: Sanand plant
segments.commentary: Three lines now operating (helmets, foam caps, nasal caps); FY26 revenue about Rs 5 crore (Q4 only); FY27 minimum target Rs 40 crore, described as on track.

guidance_outlook: Management will not revise the Rs 1,000 crore revenue ambition for FY28, calling it a stretch but still a goal.
Top-line guidance of about 10-12% growth maintained; management hopes to reach the Rs 600 crore level for the year.
Export and domestic mix expected to approach 50:50 by year end, which management called realistic.
Aim to return to the regular margin profile, helped by price pass-through and Sanand efficiency.
Europe expected to grow YoY this year, with a target to recover the lost sales over the next three quarters; the India-EU FTA effect is seen mainly from next year.
Working capital borrowings expected flat through the year; term loans taken for Sanand capex and incentives.

qa_highlights.question: Are raw material prices trending and how should margins move?

qa_highlights.question: How much export growth was lost and why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both weak Western demand and port congestion. The company had targeted at least double-digit export growth, which it missed this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a margin base now and what about under-recovery and FX?

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise its Rs 1,000 crore target for FY28?

qa_highlights.question: Sanand revenue target and new lines?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: minimum FY27 target of Rs 40 crore, on track after Q1. FY26 was about Rs 5 crore. Three lines are operating; more capacity is being considered.

qa_highlights.question: Have any large LATAM or US export contracts been won?

Port congestion and container availability disrupting shipments and Middle East supply.

539404|2026-06.headline: Satin Q1 FY27 standalone PAT up 182% YoY to INR120 crore after absorbing a INR36 crore management overlay; reported ROA 3.55%.

Guidance for FY27 was kept at 20-25% consolidated AUM growth, 3-3.5% credit cost and 3.5-4% reported ROA, with a review at the half year.

539872|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.3% YoY to INR165.6 crore with gross margin up 210 bps to 48.3%; management guides 10-15% revenue growth for FY27.
539872|2026-06.overview: Bajaj Healthcare reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR165.6 crore, up 11.3% YoY and 8.2% QoQ, with EBITDA of about INR29.6 crore (17.8% margin) and PAT from continuing operations of INR13.9 crore (8.4% margin). Domestic API was the main growth driver at INR92.3 crore (up 27% YoY), while exports (INR50.1 crore) and formulations (INR23.3 crore) contributed the rest. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% and EBITDA margins of 18-20% for FY27 and FY28, and reiterated pipeline timelines for peptide, oncology API, and CDMO/novel-drug launches. Receivable days fell to 131 from 145 at FY26 end, and the call was the company's first earnings call.

segments.name: Formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23.3 crore in Q1. Cenobamate CDMO launch expected to add INR10-12 crore in FY27; Oncocare brand business covers 15+ brands across 23 states and 3 UTs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% YoY; profit growth guided at a similar rate. FY28 top-line growth also guided at a similar rate.
EBITDA margin of 18-20% for FY27 and FY28.
Capex of INR40-50 crore every year over the next few years.

Receivable days expected to settle at 110-120 days going forward.

Gen Rx Pharmaceutical facility in Nashik (solid dosage forms): acquisition pending NCLT approval; commercial production expected in H2 2027.

demand_pricing: API prices stable QoQ in Q1; management said future pricing depends on geopolitical developments and oil prices.
Semaglutide (first peptide planned) market price cited at USD120-150 per gram. Plant is designed for global markets, with initial work for India.
CDMO: DMFs filed in UK and EU and six CEP approvals received in the last 6-8 months. Management said first customer revenue could come at end-FY28, with quantum not yet estimated.
Cenobamate: SEC recommendation received; DCGI NOC and state licence still pending; tie-ups with eight Indian marketing companies, with the company acting as CDMO partner.
Suvorexant: BE studies completed; commercialisation expected Q4 FY28 because the patent is still in force.

Vitamin C is about 8-9% of revenue; backward integration via ICT MoU expected to complete in 2029. Eight to ten API molecules being backward-integrated, expected to be 20-25% of revenue, with a 1-2% margin uplift.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivable days trend and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days fell to 131 from 145 at FY26 end; management expects 110-120 days going forward.

540005|2026-03.headline: LTM to acquire Randstad's Europe and Australia tech and consulting arm: €469M revenue, €160M EV, plus a five-year Randstad GCC deal worth ~$55–60M initial scope.
540005|2026-03.overview: LTM announced on May 22, 2026 a proposed acquisition of Randstad's Technology and Consulting Services business in Europe and Australia, with annualized revenue of €469M (about $500M+) and a proposed enterprise value of €160M on a cash-free, debt-free basis. Management said the asset is a white-space play in continental Europe, Australia, and the aerospace & defence, automotive, utilities and BFS verticals, and will be run as a separate subsidiary. The call was Q&A-heavy on revenue decline, margin dilution, and the durability of client relationships; the transcript contains no reported Q4 FY26 financials.

540699|2026-06.headline: Dixon Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR15,557 crore, but EBITDA of INR472 crore (ex fair value gain) and PAT of INR218 crore reflect margin compression as Mobile PLI 1 expired.

Management attributed the margin compression to the expiry of Mobile PLI 1 in March 2026 and to input cost pass-through, which lowers percentage margins optically, mainly in mobile and IT hardware. Working capital absorbed roughly INR800 crore in the quarter, which management called temporary, linked to strategic inventory build and payouts of end-March cash.

540701|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 19% to INR 851 crore, with EBITDA of INR 163 crore (19.1%) despite INR 30 crore extra onerous-contract provisions.
540701|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 851 crore, up about 19% YoY, with CDMO up 21% to INR 690.8 crore and marketable molecules up 9.3% to INR 160.5 crore. EBITDA was about INR 163 crore (19.1% margin), held back by roughly INR 50 crore higher other expenses from onerous-contract provisions and a one-off CHF 2.5 million Swiss pension provision. For FY26, revenue was INR 2,932 crore (up about 8%), EBITDA INR 565 crore (19.3%, up 200 bps) and PAT INR 97.4 crore versus INR 3.2 crore. Management announced a promoter-entity 10-year unsecured external commercial borrowing, subject to shareholder approval, to repay high-cost Indian debt.

up about 21% YoY from INR 569 crore
CDMO up about 6.5%, marketable molecules up about 17%
down about CHF 11 million from CHF 157.6 million

segments.name: CDMO

segments.name: Marketable molecules (Vitamin D analogs, cholesterol)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 21.1% in Q4 and 18.8% for FY26, up about 940 bps on the year, helped by higher Vitamin D analog share and supplier diversification (wool grease).

EBITDA margin target of 25% in FY28 for both segments.

Group effective tax rate about 40% in FY27, about 30% in FY28, and 15-20% in about three years.
Net debt reduction target of at least CHF 10-15 million (about INR 150 crore) every year.
French subsidiary FY27 revenue of EUR 11-12 million and EBITDA loss narrowing to about EUR 6 million; EBITDA breakeven aimed for FY28.

India: a large innovator's tech transfer from Switzerland (CHF 20-25 million annual revenue currently in Switzerland; India could see about CHF 15-20 million after a roughly 30% customer discount) and a second innovator opportunity (at least CHF 20-25 million) are in progress.

Target CDMO/marketable molecules mix of about 85:15 over the next 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: How should depreciation and tax rate be modelled for FY27-FY28?

qa_highlights.question: Will interest cost fall after refinancing, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly interest could be INR 30-35 crore, conservatively from Q2 or Q3 FY27, after replacing about INR 800 crore of Indian debt costing about 10.5-11% with cheaper promoter-entity borrowing at about 4%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there FX risk from the Swiss-franc borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Swiss-franc revenue from India and subsidiaries acts as a natural hedge, so no hedging is planned. It cited India revenue of about INR 5,000 crore in foreign currency over the 10-year tenor against about INR 800 crore of debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 India outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 India revenue and profit are expected to be above FY26, with FY28 target of about INR 500 crore; the FY27 figure may be below the INR 400 crore mentioned. Management said the target holds whether or not the Swiss tech transfer proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the goodwill increase from INR 4,054 crore to INR 4,798 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was purely FX restatement at closing rates, with no additions. About INR 550 crore is standalone India goodwill from the 2017 merger and the rest is consolidation goodwill.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings rise and cash build up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said syndicated facilities were drawn to avoid commitment fees and the USD proceeds are held as deposits earning interest, while Swiss-franc borrowing costs under 4%. Management said net debt is the right metric.

qa_highlights.question: What is the French subsidiary outlook?

India ramp-up depends on tech transfers and innovator orders; visibility on the INR 500 crore FY28 target depends on contracts that are still pending.
Management said molecules can drop out even in late Phase 3, a risk for ADC and CDMO revenue.
FY27 guidance deferred, and the CHF 20-25 million India tech transfer timing is uncertain.
Quarterly phasing of ADC supplies is hard to predict, and management said QoQ comparisons are difficult.
Swiss-franc movements affect INR reported numbers, and the analyst noted a roughly 6-7% CHF depreciation against INR over six months.

The CDMO segment revenue fell to INR 5,343 mn while Marketable Molecules rose to INR 1,432 mn. 540716|2026-06.headline: ICICI Lombard Q1 FY27 PAT fell 46.0% to ₹4.03 bn, driven by a ₹1.65 bn Motor TP judgement provision and two large Fire losses.
540716|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 GDPI grew 7.5% to ₹83.18 bn, below industry growth of 10.9%, with retail lines driving growth while commercial lines de-grew 13.8%. Combined ratio rose to 107.2% from 102.9%, including a 2.8 pp hit from the Supreme Court Motor TP judgement provision and a 1.0 pp hit from two Fire large losses. Excluding these items, the combined ratio was 102.3% versus 102.2% a year ago, and PAT would have been ₹5.75 bn (down 23.0%). Investment income fell to ₹11.74 bn from ₹12.88 bn as capital gains halved, partly offset by higher portfolio yield and duration.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: De-grew 13.8% in Q1 FY27 amid pricing pressure; SME share rose to 33.6% from 28.4%. Fire line declined 27.8% for the industry and the company de-grew about 32%; June Fire de-growth improved to about 18% for the company.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Grew 14.0% in line with industry (13.9%), market share 10.5%; new vehicle sales up 33.6% vs industry 14.9%. Mix: private car 49.8%, two-wheeler 28.7%, commercial vehicle 21.5%. Motor combined ratio 106.6% in FY26 vs industry 128.0%.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Grew 24.9% vs industry 20.1%. Retail Health grew 69.5% with share up to 4.5% from 3.5%; Group Health grew 16.3% with 10.3% share. Management attributed the higher health loss ratio to industry-wide claim incidence, not company-specific.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give a quantified forward impact of the Motor TP judgement; said it is too early and will update each quarter.
Expects an upward Motor TP premium rate revision; judgement-driven industry loss ratio impact estimated at 12-15%, which it sees as the minimum price change needed.
Expects Fire price aggression to moderate after Q1, though full recovery of de-growth in the rest of the year is uncertain.
Health claim incidence watch-point for Q2 (monsoon-linked); next detailed update to come with October results.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning plans were discussed on the call; the call covered underwriting, pricing, reserving and claims only.

Capacity was referenced only qualitatively: management said reinsurance renewals were relatively soft and capacity had been made available across the industry, which drove Fire price competition. No company-specific capacity figures were given.

Motor claims and servicing scale were cited as operating metrics, not capacity: Preferred Partner Network served 75.6% of non-OEM motor claims in Q1 FY27 vs 74.6% in Q1 FY26; 168,521 health and travel claims were serviced through the IL TakeCare app vs 141,116 a year earlier.
Digital servicing capacity: digital interactions rose to 624K in Q1 FY27 from 214K in Q1 FY26; digital share of servicing was 69.0% in Q1 FY27 and 71.0% in June 2026.

demand_pricing: Industry Fire rates were cut sharply in the April renewal cycle; the reinsurance renewal was relatively soft, enabling capacity and competition.
Motor TP has seen no third-party price change for several years; the judgement adds a Motor TP loss ratio impact of 12-15% for the industry.

Digital interactions rose to 624K from 214K; digital share of servicing 69% in Q1 FY27 and 71% in June 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the provision is a holistic assessment of exposures as at June 30, covering past book as well as Q1 business; it declined to say whether it will recur, citing variability in future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the judgement affect closed cases, and what is the Fire loss ratio excluding the two large losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Closed cases typically do not reopen after court finality, so impact is largely on open exposures. Excluding the two large losses, Fire loss ratios should be within the historical 65-70% average range; the company has never exceeded 100% in Fire.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Health loss ratio rise despite GST benefit, and will it rise further in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects industry-wide higher claim incidence, similar to last year's Q1; it is watching monsoon-linked claims into Q2 and will update in October.

qa_highlights.question: Arbitration award of about ₹78 crore: provision and impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The award relates to a policy about seven to eight years old and is on a gross basis; the company will pursue legal remedies and believes the net P&L impact is not material given reinsurance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the reserve prudence buffer still generate releases given the ₹165 crore charge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its reserving philosophy is unchanged, prudence will continue, and reserving triangles should continue to show favourable development over cycles.

H1 was weaker, with PAT down 5.8% to ₹14.54 bn and combined ratio at 105.2%, reflecting the Q1 Supreme Court (Shishupal) Motor TP reserving of ₹1.65 bn and Q1 commercial large losses. GDPI grew 5.4% in H1 versus industry 8.9%, though ex-Crop and Mass Health Q2 growth of 13.9% was ahead of industry 13.2%. Management said no further Motor TP reserve top-up is needed and that the judgment is now business as usual.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: H1 growth 26.8% vs industry 21.0%. Retail Health grew 66.4% (industry 32.0%), share 4.7% in H1 and 5.0% exiting September. Group Health grew 15.4%, share stable at 8.8%; Group Health loss ratio 97.9% in Q2 vs 93.7% a year ago.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Ex-Fire growth 20.0% in Q2 and 13.2% in H1. Fire de-growth moderated to 21.2% in Q2 from 32.1% in Q1, with September at -6.0%. Fire market share 11.9% in Q2 (11.4% prior year); Marine cargo 19.0%; Engineering 16.4%; Liability 16.6%.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Management said it was deliberately cautious in underwriting Crop this year, which muted headline top-line growth against NEP growth.

Digital sourcing to be scaled from 6.0% to 15% of business under a defined roadmap.

qa_highlights.question: Why did commission and other opex ratios rise in Q2?

540719|2026-06.headline: SBI Life Q1 FY27 VNB rose 29% to INR14.1bn, but VNB margin fell to 26.2% as GST and a one-off GTI group deal diluted mix.
540719|2026-06.overview: Individual rated premium grew 14% to INR39.7bn with private market share of 22.2%, and all product segments and channels grew. Profit after tax rose 22% to INR7.2bn, helped by supportive market conditions, while the GST impact was INR2.3bn for the quarter. VNB margin of 26.2% was down year on year, which management attributed mainly to a higher share of lumpy group business (GTI) in APE. Management said the margin was within its 26–28% guidance, at the lower end, and expects it to move to the upper end as individual mix normalises.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group NBP INR32.9bn (37% of NBP), +41% YoY; group APE INR53.8bn, +36%; group protection APE INR12.3bn, +313%, driven by a large one-off GTI contract.

segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR1.9bn, +18%; pure protection +41% on individual APE; ROP share of individual protection 68% vs 73% a year ago.

segments.commentary: 47% of total APE; individual APE INR24.5bn, +10%; SBI branch productivity INR4.1mn, +7%. Other banks grew 19% on individual NBP and 31% on APE; their mix is about 80% non-ULIP.

segments.commentary: Individual APE INR13.1bn, +20%; agent productivity INR2 lakh; non-ULIP share rose from 43% to 46%; 34,000+ agents added gross and 11 new branches opened.

GST drag expected for one more quarter (Q2 FY27), with the impact ending thereafter; GST was waived from 22 September, so about 2.5 months of impact remain in Q1.

Regular-pay deferred annuity plan expected to launch within the next quarter.

Misselling ratio 0.02%; death claim settlement ratio 98.8%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 60 bps product-mix drag on VNB margin is due to the GTI group deal, and what is the normalised margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60 bps mix drag relates only to GTI and that the company does not disclose product-wise margins. It said margin should return to normal as IRP share normalises. The 40 bps assumption-related item reflects the March 2026 annual review, and there was no assumption change in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GST drag going to persist, and how do expenses look?
qa_highlights.answer: GST drag of about 1.1 percentage points in Q1 is expected to continue into Q2 and then fade. Management said the rise in other expenses reflects one-off stamp duty tied to higher sum assured and labour code impacts, and it expects these to normalise over the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will agency growth be sustainable and will the channel mix shift affect costs or margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Agency APE grew 20% in Q1, with the current quarter at 19%-plus. Management expects a stronger contribution from agency in the remaining three quarters and a balanced mix of banca and agency going forward. It did not discuss cost impact in detail.

qa_highlights.question: What proportion of ULIPs carry rider attachment, and how is protection classified?
qa_highlights.answer: Rider attachment on ULIPs is about 45–50%, up from roughly 35% when riders were introduced 1–1.5 years earlier. Riders are counted within individual protection, and rider APE was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is individual protection growth lower than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift from ROP to pure protection lowers ticket size, which makes headline growth look subdued. Individual protection grew 22% by its own measure against pure protection growth of 41%, with ROP share at 68%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the regular-pay deferred annuity plan launch slip, and what are the non-par and regulatory views?
qa_highlights.answer: The deferred annuity plan is expected in the next quarter and is being developed for an opportune time. On non-par, management said pricing is reviewed against yield movements. On regulation, management said it sees the company as well placed and expects future rules to be positive for the industry.

540725|2026-03.headline: Share India standalone Q4 FY26 PAT rose 368% YoY to INR 75 crore on revenue of INR 383 crore (+103%).
540725|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue nearly doubled to INR 383 crore and PAT rose to INR 75 crore from INR 16 crore, with EPS of INR 17.6 versus INR 11.7. For FY26, standalone PAT rose 20% to INR 298 crore on revenue of INR 395 crore. Consolidated FY26 PAT was flat-to-down at INR 324 crore versus INR 328 crore, held back by fair value adjustments on investments held by group companies. Management pushed diversification into MTF, PMS, wealth distribution, debt (Share India Cred), AIF and commodities, while flagging RBI curbs on intraday bank limits for prop trading.

qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said full-year borrowing costs will flow into FY27 and new NCD and third-party borrowing lines could cut costs by a few hundred basis points. Tier-3 direct branches are meant to remove mediators and lift NIM.
