segments.name: RegTech - IRIS CARBON (SaaS, enterprise)
segments.commentary: ARR grew 33% on disclosure-management wins; ESG reporting module launched as an add-on. Management targets about 35% ARR growth and says it is breaking into large enterprise accounts. Sales and marketing spend is planned to be stepped up in a measured way, at about 1.1-1.2x net ARR, and kept EBITDA positive.

segments.name: RegTech - IRIS iDEAL (BFSI automated regulatory reporting)
segments.commentary: ARR grew 17% despite slower Indian purchase decisions in H1 FY26. Company is exploring Africa and Middle East, with some Europe interest; revenue mix is subscription, implementation and licence.

segments.name: SupTech - iFile
segments.commentary: Added 3 new logos in FY26, including Government of Qatar for tax reporting, plus a deposit insurance management segment. Product suite is being extended to licensing, risk-based supervision, case management and decision management. Revenue is lumpier and expected to grow slower than SaaS; management expects 3-4 SupTech wins in a typical year.

segments.name: DataTech / IRIS Peridot (MSME)
segments.commentary: Spun off into a subsidiary for sharper focus. Loan facilitation piloted from February 2026 with 3 lenders onboarded so far; monetisation is at an early stage and management's internal target is earlier than the 2-year horizon an analyst suggested.

guidance_outlook: Revenue aspiration of INR500 crore, which management says needs growth slightly over 30% over the next 4-5 years.
SaaS ARR growth target of about 35% (stated externally), with management saying internally it could be higher.
SupTech expected to grow at a lower rate than SaaS, with possible lumpy upside.
Sales and marketing to rise in a measured way, with IRIS CARBON the main beneficiary; company intends to stay EBITDA positive.
Receivable days (DSO) comfortable at 75-80 days; further improvement expected to be progressively difficult unless enterprise SaaS accelerates.
Some cash to be retained for possible inorganic opportunities in RegTech adjacencies; no acquisition announced.
capex_capacity: No specific capex or capacity figures were discussed.
Cash of ~INR155 crore is being deployed into CARBON sales and marketing, with the balance held back for potential inorganic deals.
Planned on-ground sales and marketing hires in developed markets (US and Europe), started recently.
Moved to a new corporate office in Turbhe, Navi Mumbai.
demand_pricing: Disclosure-management category in US and Europe described as young, with many structured-data reporting prospects; US and Europe are the priority geographies for CARBON.
Customers are excited about AI and inquiries are rising; management says it has not yet seen enterprises building in-house software or AI-native entrants in its markets.
SupTech demand linked to regulator digitisation push; some Middle East pipeline is in discussion and could slip if the crisis extends beyond about June 2026.
Regulators show reluctance on cloud-based and generic AI for confidential data; company is exploring private or sovereign small language models. PFRDA is on a private cloud.
SaaS business is mainly Europe and US, so limited direct Middle East exposure per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the roadmap to the INR500 crore revenue target and by when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the INR500 crore aspiration, which needs growth slightly above 30% over 4-5 years. SaaS ARR targeted at about 35% growth; SupTech to grow slower, with possible surprises.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI helping, and does it raise competitive intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees AI as both opportunity and threat; it is building AI offerings and embedding AI in the development process. No competitive intensity increase seen so far from enterprises building in-house or AI-native entrants.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Middle East crisis on the year?
qa_highlights.answer: SaaS impact seen as minimal given Europe and US focus. SupTech pipeline linked to Middle East regulators could see delays if the crisis persists beyond roughly June; 3-4 SupTech wins still expected.

qa_highlights.question: Use of the cash balance: M&A, product or marketing spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic growth first. Sales and marketing at about 1.1-1.2x net ARR, possibly a bit higher, with no EBITDA-negative mode. Inorganic options are open but disciplined; some capital to be retained.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~30% growth be achieved: markets, products, headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: CARBON is the flagship with ESG added; adjacencies in capital-markets and energy reporting are early. iDEAL to expand into Africa, Middle East and Europe. iFile adding licensing, risk-based analytics and case management. Developed-market sales hiring has started.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivable days falling and what is the comfort level?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by enterprise SaaS mix rising and regulators paying promptly. Management says 75-80 days is comfortable; further improvement is progressively harder.

risks_watch: Middle East crisis could delay SupTech wins if it extends beyond roughly June 2026; government budgets may be hit by high oil prices.
Enterprise SaaS and AI disruption: management acknowledges volatility in enterprise software valuations and AI impact is uncertain.
Sales and marketing step-up at CARBON could pressure EBITDA margin from the ~14% base.
Peridot/MSME loan facilitation is at pilot stage with only 3 lenders; monetisation is unproven.
Regulator reluctance to adopt cloud and generic AI for confidential data may slow SupTech and AI-led product uptake.
Deployment of the ~INR155 crore cash into inorganic deals is undefined.
540735|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on SaaS growth and balance sheet, but cautious on the Middle East and AI, with management saying it is watchful but not unduly worried. Answers on M&A and the INR500 crore timeline were measured and non-committal on dates.
key_quotes: And we're already seeing 33% ARR growth, and we want to up it as we go forward.
We don't want to do a deal just because we have the capital.
We don't want to be doing this in EBITDA negative mode.
So I would start getting worried post June, I would say.

540743|2026-06.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 10% to INR2,852 crore; Crop Care fell 16.2% on delayed monsoon, while management still targets double-digit FY27 PBT growth.
540743|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales grew 10% YoY to INR2,852 crore despite a delayed monsoon and geopolitical-driven inflation. Animal Nutrition (revenue +12.6%, reported segment result +29%) and Oil Palm (revenue +28.9%, segment result +14.4%) carried the quarter. Crop Care revenue fell 16.2% on a dry June and slower kharif sowing, and Dairy margins were squeezed by milk procurement costs and packaging inflation. Astec reached EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago. Management reiterated FY27 double-digit consolidated PBT growth (versus earlier mid-teens guidance) but deferred a firmer view on Crop Care until end-September.

financial_highlights.change: Cattle feed volume +15%; total segment volume +7%
Segment result +14.4%; EBIT margin ~17% vs 19% a year ago (per analyst)
vs EBITDA loss of INR11 crore in Q1 FY26
Value-added share of sales 49% vs 42% a year ago

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue +12.6% on robust demand and better realisations; cattle feed volume +15% and overall segment volume +7%. Poultry volumes deliberately reduced in unprofitable geographies. Cattle feed is about 55-56% of the segment; fish feed about 7%.

segments.name: Oil Palm
segments.commentary: Revenue +28.9% on higher CPO and PKO realisations and volume; FFB volumes broadly flat versus a strong early-monsoon base. Segment result +14.4%, with margin down on a pricing-formula effect that management calls one-off.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Revenue -16.2% as a dry June and slow kharif sowing hit cotton herbicide volumes, with margin contraction. Ashitaka and Takai together contribute about 18-20% of Q1 sales; Ghassnash soybean herbicide launched.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago; revenue moderately lower on product mix. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of more than 20%, with an 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO dissilience around 50-52%.

segments.name: Dairy (CDPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.4% and volume +8%, but profitability hit by elevated milk procurement prices and packaging inflation. Route-to-market reconstitution (about 18-20 months) under new CEO Gaurav is starting.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly stable as live bird trading is planned to fall 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years. Branded B2C (Yummiez, Real Good) volume +28% and about 32% of the Foods business; profitability hit by input costs.

segments.name: Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej Agrovet)
segments.commentary: Returned to growth, with double-digit growth in volume, revenue and PBT.

qa_highlights.question: What FFB volume growth and EBITDA trajectory can Oil Palm deliver over 3-5 years, and what capex and returns are involved in value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kataria guided FFB volume growth of high single digit to early double digit over 4-5 years, targeting double digit; specialty fats refinery to start in September, with a 16-18% IRR hurdle and about 200 bps EBITDA uplift at scale. He did not give an explicit EBITDA number.

qa_highlights.question: Can Crop Care recover in H2, and is the consolidated mid-teens PBT growth still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was hit by a 40% June deficit; July is better than last year's base, and it will decide on the recovery by end-September. Consolidated growth now targeted at double digit, with the exact level to be given by end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Astec: revenue outlook and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Arijit Mukherjee said FY27 revenue growth is now expected at more than 20%, with the 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO margins intact and enterprise margin normalising as prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Will the palm oil shift need extra capex, and what is the Foods/Dairy pricing picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex stays within the INR300-350 crore envelope already guided. Dairy volume grew 8% but packaging and milk costs hit margin; Foods B2C is in a 3-4 year investment phase, with live bird trading being wound down.

qa_highlights.question: How much maize inflation has Animal Nutrition passed through, and what is EBIT per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60-70% of commodity cost increases passed on; EBIT per tonne guidance held at roughly INR2,050-2,150, with Q1 EBITDA per tonne in that range or slightly higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Oil Palm segment margin fall from 19% to 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to a one-off pricing-formula change in the quarter and flat FFB, offset by better OER; expects margins to even out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Crop Care lagging peers, and what are margins on the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is segment-mix and macro driven (cotton herbicide concentration), not share loss; new products carry lower margin than Hitweed but healthy, with total Crop Care EBIT margin seen at about 26-27%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated PBT growth: management still targets double-digit growth, narrowed from the earlier mid-teens guidance; exact position in the range to be given by end-September (end Q2).

Astec LifeSciences: FY27 revenue growth guided at more than 20% (up from the ~20% earlier guidance); Q1 revenue dip of 8-9% to be recovered in later quarters; CDMO dissilience around 50-52% for the year, with some CDMO shift from H1 to H2.
Astec enterprise margin: Q1 benefited from low-priced raw material and war-driven finished goods price increases; prices now easing, margin normalising. CDMO margins intact.

Oil Palm: FFB volume growth of high single digit to early double digit over the next 4-5 years (LRP); management says it targets double digit; full-year FFB growth guided at high single digit to double digit; margin drop expected to even out over the year.
Animal Nutrition: EBIT per tonne guidance held at roughly INR2,050-2,150 per tonne.
Crop Care: no firm FY27 numbers; recovery quantum to be assessed by end-September after cotton herbicide season. Crop Care EBIT margin expected to hold around 26-27% despite tough year.

Dairy: milk procurement prices expected to stay at current elevated levels for 2-3 quarters; packaging inflation expected to ease by August; some impact may persist in Q2; cost initiatives to be doubled down on in H2.
Godrej Foods: live bird trading to decline 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years; branded B2C to be in investment phase for 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Overall business-level capex guidance of roughly INR300-350 crore, phased over 3-4 quarters; includes the integrated palm oil complex (phase 1 started, nursery and CPO mill; seed garden in 18-24 months; refinery later) and specialty fats refinery (rollout late August/early September 2026); management says no new investment beyond this envelope.

Oil Palm area expansion: added about 17,000 hectares last year and on track to repeat this year; LRP target to take area from about 80,000 ha to about 150,000 ha, with Telangana and Northeast expansion; about 50% of plantations are juvenile (0-4 years).
New capex hurdle: IRR of around 16-18% required for new assets; management says the specialty fats downstream business, when scaled, adds roughly 200 bps to overall EBITDA profile.

Godrej Foods: investments in automation of plants and advertising behind branded B2C; NPD pipeline including chicken momos (launched about 4 months ago) and wet momos (planned in 3-4 months), and frozen chicken category push.
demand_pricing: Animal Nutrition: revenue +12.6% on demand and realisations; cattle feed volume +15%, fish feed volume up ~20%+ (about 7% of segment), cattle feed about 55-56% of segment; total segment volume +7% as poultry was deliberately cut in unprofitable geographies. Management says it passed on about 60-70% of commodity (maize) inflation.

Oil Palm: revenue +28.9% on higher CPO and PKO realisations; oil extraction ratio 18.8% vs 18.4%; FFB volume broadly flat against a strong early-monsoon base last year. Segment margin dipped on a pricing-formula change that management calls one-off.

Crop Care: revenue -16.2% on a 40% June rainfall deficit delaying sowing; cotton herbicide volume hit. Ashitaka (maize) and Takai (paddy insecticide) together 18-20% of Q1 sales; July said to be better than last year's base. Management said no share loss to competitors; cited product-mix differences versus peers.

Dairy (CDPL): volume +8% and value +11.5%; value-added share 49% vs 42%. Packaging inflation (linked to crude/LPG after Middle East conflict) and milk procurement prices hurt margin; industry passed on about 70% of price increases.

Godrej Foods: B2C (Yummiez and Real Good) volumes +28% (Yummiez +22%), about 32% of Foods business; overall Foods revenue only about 1-2% growth due to planned live bird decline; B2C value growth about 20%.
Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej Agrovet): strong double-digit growth in volume, value and PBT under new leadership.
risks_watch: Crop Care recovery depends on the cotton herbicide season and erratic rainfall; management will give a firm view only by end-September.
Dairy margin pressure from elevated milk procurement prices (expected to persist 2-3 quarters) and packaging costs, with some impact likely in Q2.
Oil Palm Q1 margin decline (19% to 17% EBIT) attributed to a pricing formula; watch whether H2 margin recovers as management expects.
Astec: CDMO revenue shifting from H1 into H2, and the 8-9% Q1 dip must be recovered to hit the more-than-20% FY27 target.
Animal Nutrition: poultry volume cuts and maize cost volatility; the segment reported volume growth (+7%) lags cattle feed (+15%).
Godrej Foods reported top line stays near flat (1-2%) while B2C invests; profitability is pressured by input costs and the investment phase.
key_quotes: So I would say, yes, there has been a hit in the quarter 1, which has very clearly come because of this weather pattern.
Nothing crosses our bridge broadly beyond -- until we are doing an IRR of around 16% to 18%, and this meets that bridge for us.
But I think one thing we're still pretty confident of is that we'll be able to target a double -digit growth still.
We have a tight filter on this very clearly. This is a high ROCE business for us.
540743|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on Oil Palm, Animal Nutrition and Astec, but cautious on Crop Care and the consolidated guidance, which management says will be narrowed only at end-September. Several answers stressed one-off factors (packaging, pricing formula, weather) while deferring specifics on Crop Care and dairy margins.

540749|2026-06.headline: MAS Financial Q1 FY27: consolidated AUM up 21% to INR16,100 crores and PAT up 27% to INR110 crores; credit cost guided 1.25%-1.75%.
540749|2026-06.overview: Consolidated AUM grew about 21% YoY to INR16,100 crores and PAT rose about 27% to INR110 crores, with standalone PAT up 25% to INR105 crores. Asset quality was stable, with standalone GNPA at 2.58% and NNPA at 1.70%, flat QoQ, and a management overlay of INR17.60 crores held. Borrowing cost fell 55 bps YoY to 9.25%, while credit cost rose to about 1.6% of AUM, which management attributed to higher on-book mix, a 5 bps rise in Stage 1/2 provisioning and prudent write-offs. Management reiterated 20-25% AUM growth guidance, with the call leaning toward the upper end for FY27.

segments.name: MEL (Micro/MSME loans)
segments.commentary: Book grew 23% from INR5,009 crores to INR6,153 crores; MEL is about 77% of loan book combined with SME.

segments.name: SME loans
segments.commentary: Grew 21% from INR4,526 crores to INR5,485 crores.

segments.name: Two-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: Grew 19% from INR872 crores to INR1,039 crores; management said Q1 is seasonally muted, with festive Q3/Q4 stronger.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle (used CV)
segments.commentary: Grew 13% from INR967 crores to INR1,096 crores; eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening, with growth push deferred 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Salaried personal loans
segments.commentary: Grew 21% from INR1,131 crores to INR1,374 crores; about 9% of the loan book.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: AUM INR976 crores, GS3 0.98% and NS3 0.68%; PBT up 62% to INR5.70 crores; average yield about 14%, credit cost about 0.5%. Expansion into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka starts this quarter.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance maintained at 20-25%, with management saying the full year is very likely to be at the higher end of the range.
Credit cost to stay in a 1.25%-1.75% range, depending on product mix; management pointed to commercial vehicles as high-yield, high-loss.
ROA target of 2.75%-3.25%, with an aspiration of 3%+.
Net interest margin target of 8%-8.5% on a 7%-7.5% spread; incremental borrowing cost 9.2%-9.25%, expected to stay stable (9.2%-9.3% per Q&A).
Direct distribution share (currently 66%-67%) expected to reach 70%-72% in 1-1.5 years; off-book target kept at 20-25% of AUM.
Used CV growth expected to pick up only after 1-2 quarters; housing finance AUM expected to inch up in the next few quarters.
Credit rating upgrade being pursued, timing not given; sub-9% borrowing cost called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters.
capex_capacity: Distribution of 16,500 centres through 209 branches, with more than 200 NBFC partners providing about 33% of originations; direct share 67%.
Employee count reduced by 380 in Q1 due to technology adoption; no quantified headcount target given.
In-house tech team of close to 100 people; LOS live for all products, with BRE added and straight-through processing improving.
Branches opened after March 2024 expected to mature (sweat) by 2027-28 or earlier.
demand_pricing: Standalone MSME/SME demand stable across manufacturing and trading; eligible demand fell in Q1 due to tighter credit screens on energy-dependent sectors (restaurants, gas-dependent manufacturing, export businesses).
Used CV demand robust, but eligible demand lower because of fuel-cost tightening.
Two-wheeler Q1 degrowth QoQ attributed to seasonality; monsoon and Gujarat floods flagged as temporary and not expected to cause major stress.
Working capital demand rising for some businesses on higher input costs; underwriting parameters also tightened.
Write-offs were INR29 crores in March and INR19 crores in June, offset by higher ECL provisioning, keeping impairment cost flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise from about 1.2-1.3% to about 1.6% of AUM despite the microfinance impact and Q4 write-offs last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher on-book assets (on-book up 8.25% QoQ vs AUM up 5.5%), which added INR6-7 crores of Stage 1/2 provisioning from a 5 bps rise to 0.7%. Prudent write-offs and mix shift toward higher-yield commercial vehicles also contributed; ROA not affected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-25% growth guidance at risk given the West Asia conflict and energy-linked stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said energy-dependent segments were tightened early and stress was limited; eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 but normalised, and guidance is expected to hold with the upper end targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Will borrowing cost fall further from 9.25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to predict and depends on RBI and liquidity; the target is to stabilise at 9.2%-9.3%, with a credit rating upgrade being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the Stage 1/2 provisioning increase and whether there are macro-related buffers?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 1/2 provisioning rose to 0.7% from 0.65%, adding INR6-7 crores; management described it as a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR10 crore OCPS redemption in the subsidiary MRHMFL?
qa_highlights.answer: The OCPS was refunded to the parent because the housing subsidiary's CRAR exceeded 37% and it did not need the capital.

qa_highlights.question: Why did off-book share fall and what is the housing finance growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Off-book is dynamic and chosen by price; target stays at 20-25%. Housing finance plans to expand into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka from Q1, with results expected in Q3-Q4.

risks_watch: Used CV: eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening; management says growth push is 1-2 quarters away, and CV is high-yield, high-loss, so credit cost direction depends on mix.

Credit cost: rose to about 1.6% of AUM from about 1.2-1.3% a year earlier; management guides a 1.25%-1.75% range and Stage 1/2 provisioning went to 0.7% from 0.65% (INR6-7 crores), which management calls a buffer.
Energy-linked and West Asia stress: eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 and management says it has normalised; the next quarter will show whether this holds.
Borrowing cost: 9.25% average with incremental cost at 9.2%-9.3%; a sub-9% level is called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters, and the credit rating upgrade has no timing.

Off-book share fell below the 20%-25% target this quarter; management says it is opportunistic and the target is unchanged. Gujarat floods and monsoon effects on two-wheeler and collections are still unquantified.
key_quotes: So, very high possibility, yes. We are working on that quite optimistic. Can't predict, but you are thinking on the right lines.
So, that is the impact which translates to roughly around between INR5 crores to INR7 crores in provisioning.
Difficult to comment right now because the cost of borrowing is dependent on the macro situation.
So, currently, sub-9 immediately within next 1 or 2 quarters looks like a far -fetched assumption.
540749|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on headline growth, profitability and asset quality, with the 20%-25% AUM guidance reaffirmed and the upper end targeted. More cautious and non-committal on credit cost trajectory, borrowing cost, used CV recovery timing and the flood impact, where management repeatedly said it cannot yet predict or quantify.

540750|2026-06.headline: IEX Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose about 12% to Rs 134.8 crore on Rs 202.8 crore revenue, with electricity volume up 16% to 37.5 billion units.
540750|2026-06.overview: IEX reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 202.8 crore and PAT of Rs 134.8 crore, up about 12% YoY, on electricity volume of 37.5 billion units (+16%). Real-Time Market growth was the main driver, with RTM up about 25% in Q1 and its share of mix reaching about 34% last year. Management used the analyst meet to push a set of new products (Green RTM, peak contracts, 11-month TAM, carbon trading, coal exchange) while pushing back on CERC's proposed market coupling and the Day-Ahead Market pilot, which it has challenged at APTEL and the Supreme Court. The call was mostly a policy and product narrative; no formal FY27 guidance was given.

segments.name: Electricity (DAM / RTM / TAM)
segments.commentary: RTM is now roughly the size of DAM; DAM share of mix fell from 95% in FY16 to about 39%, RTM rose to about 34% in FY26, and RTM is up about 25% in Q1 FY27. Term-Ahead Market and Green Market are about 7-8% of the mix.

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange, associate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 42 crore; Q1 FY27 volume 27.5 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 16 crore. DRHP filed for IPO of a 22.3% stake to bring IEX's 47.3% holding down to 25% under PNGRB rules, after a one-year extension.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC / environmental)
segments.commentary: Sole I-REC issuer in India; management cited about 200% growth in I-REC volumes last year. Q1 REC volumes were down sharply YoY, which management attributed to the first quarter and possible RPO buy-out confusion.

segments.name: Indian Coal Exchange (new)
segments.commentary: Incorporated as a separate company in June 2026; coal rules notified 4 June 2026 require e-auction and marketplace trades to move to exchanges within six months of launch. Market size cited at about 120 million tonnes today, with a target of at least 100 million tonnes in year one.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 volume or revenue guidance given; management expects RTM volumes to grow about 25-30% a year.
Management expects carbon credit trading to begin in FY27, with BEE targeting 1 October 2026.

Management expects the Green RTM, peak-power contracts (DAM and RTM) and 11-month TAM products to be approved by CERC; timing was not committed, and the 11-month TAM application has been pending for over two years.
Management sees the exchange-routed share of electricity rising to about 25% over five to six years, against about 14-15% short-term market today.
Management said it would consider a buyback in future, citing SEBI's revised market-buyback rules.
Management said the coal exchange's fee should exceed those of MSTC and M-Junction, since exchanges perform price discovery, clearing and settlement.
capex_capacity: Management cited about 80 GW of thermal capacity in the pipeline, 41 GW under construction with PPAs signed, 20 GW awarded, and 16 GW in planning; most is expected in FY31-FY33.
Management said it has built a hot standby for RTM and a DC-to-DR switch; both were positioned as ready for the proposed 5-minute bidding window.

BESS merchant capacity cited: ACME about 3,200 MWh, Juniper about 500 MWh, Adani about 3,400 MWh, with more than Rs 9,000 crore of BESS VGF support. Management said the arbitrage window may last 3-5 years.
The SECI 500 MW CfD pilot for peak power was cited as launched; it is a peak-power product, not solar.
demand_pricing: Management expects demand growth of about 5-5.5% a year, versus 11% in Q1 FY27 on heat and delayed monsoon. Peak demand touched about 271 GW in May and July.
Management said exchanges as a group grew 18% in FY26 against 1% demand growth.

On market coupling, CERC proposed Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, with DAM first. Management said it has challenged the July 2025 order at APTEL (order dated 13 February 2026) and is now before the Supreme Court; a second hearing was held on 27 July 2026.
Management said that even after coupling, DAM share could fall 20-40%, but said business impact would not be significant. The market-share loss figure is management's own estimate.
Management said top-10 sellers account for about 40% of the sell side and the top-buyer concentration is 50-60%, with 800-900 participants daily.

Management cited an RTM realisation issue in a Q&A: an analyst's per-unit realisation calculation (about 0.4 paisa vs 3.7 paisa a year earlier) was not reconciled; management pointed to incentives in REC and TAM.

financial_highlights.change: about 11% QoQ per management; YoY not stated

qa_highlights.question: What RTM share of the mix to expect over the next 3-5 years, and what could be the next star product after RTM (peak contracts, Green RTM, BESS)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RTM has grown about 30-35% CAGR since 2020 and expects RTM volumes to keep growing 25-30% a year, possibly exceeding DAM volumes over time; it named BESS as a potential next growth product. No numeric RTM share target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will IEX pursue a buyback given low valuations, and can IEX shareholders get a reservation in the IGX IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an IGX IPO reservation for IEX shareholders is not really possible as it is an independent IPO. It said a buyback will be considered in future, since SEBI has revised the rules for market buybacks.

qa_highlights.question: Why has RTM grown to near DAM size in India, unlike in Europe where DAM dominates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to 25-year PPAs covering about 85% of DISCOM demand, with DAM used for seasonal and daily shortfalls and RTM used to handle renewable variability; it said PPAs will persist because banks lend only against them.

qa_highlights.question: How far can exchange share of electricity grow given long-term PPAs dominate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exchange-routed share could reach about 25% of generation in five to six years, versus about 14-15% in the short-term market today, as bilateral and trader transactions shrink.

qa_highlights.question: Who bears the cost of Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, and will MCO fees force IEX to cut fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all costs are ultimately passed to consumers, directly or indirectly, and that cost allocation and fee questions are among the open issues Grid India has raised with CERC; no timeline or answer was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the likely timeline for final market coupling regulations, and what is the expected DAM market-share loss?

540776|2026-06.headline: 5paisa Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to INR 88.4 crore, PAT INR 11.6 crore; management flagged a slower quarter and expects growth to accelerate.
540776|2026-06.overview: Total revenue grew 14% YoY to INR 88.4 crore and PAT was INR 11.6 crore, with customers at 52.6 lakh. The average client funding book (MTF plus T+5) was INR 422 crore, up 3% QoQ, and mutual fund AUM reached INR 2,073 crore, up 18% QoQ. Management said volatility in the prior quarter moderated activity in Q1, with F&O ADTO slightly down and cash ADTO up. The company deployed part of the INR 468 crore rights issue proceeds into exchange margin, loan repayment and general corporate purposes.

segments.name: Funding (MTF and T+5)
segments.commentary: T+5 extended to 2,500 eligible scrips at interest from 0.045% per day; MTF extended to 1,500 scrips with funding limits up to INR 25 crore. Management said MTF has roughly doubled over about 15 months, mainly from existing customers.

segments.name: F&O / derivatives
segments.commentary: F&O ADTO dipped slightly in Q1. New launches include OI profile on Charts, OneClick execution and AlgoSpace, an algo trading platform aimed at sachet- and packet-sized algos.

segments.name: Cash equities
segments.commentary: Cash ADTO grew in Q1 per management, with no quantified figure given.

segments.name: Wealth / mutual funds
segments.commentary: MF AUM reached INR 2,073 crore, up 18% QoQ; management cites portfolio building as the basis for sticky, high-LTV customers.

guidance_outlook: Management expects growth to accelerate from Q2 onwards, citing product revamp and growth marketing; no numeric guidance given.
Product platform upgrades and a complete revamp are expected to move to production in the next few months.
Over the next 12 months the focus is on engagement, adoption and monetisation of new app rollouts, plus unit-economics improvement to reach operating leverage.
Rights issue capital to fund product and tech talent, partnerships and growth marketing; inorganic opportunities being evaluated selectively.
Third-party distribution: no in the very near term; may be considered in the medium term, with product adjacencies (LAS) first.
capex_capacity: Rights issue proceeds of INR 468 crore: INR 227 crore to exchange margin (RBI ended broker intraday facility from 1 July), about INR 150 crore to repay bank loans and CPs, and INR 88 crore general corporate purposes.
Management says the company is positioned to deploy capital into product, tech, and growth marketing, with no capex figures disclosed.
Customer acquisition channel mix to shift toward quality organic and paid, adjusted quarterly on CAC and RPC by channel.
demand_pricing: Management said revenue per customer (RPC) rose in recent months and in the latest quarter, and LTV is improving.
F&O-heavy customer base was hit by market volatility; management cited moderation across industry since F&O changes in October 2024.
Market share: management said some players gained and some lost share; said it is hard to attribute customer moves between firms.
Management is prioritising quality over headline customer additions; no CAC figures were disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 slowdown a one-off, and will growth pick up from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 saw moderation with some spillover from recent volatility; it expects growth to accelerate from here, driven by product and growth marketing.

qa_highlights.question: Why has ADTO growth and customer acquisition tapered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is focusing on quality acquisition, with RPC and LTV improving over recent months; ADTO depends on average order value and long-term customers.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 468 crore rights issue be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 227 crore to exchange margin, about INR 150 crore to bank and CP loan repayment, and INR 88 crore general corporate purposes (product, tech, marketing).

qa_highlights.question: What needs to change for revenue to grow at a healthy clip after three flat years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the revamped product, increased growth marketing, and new revenue lines in the pipeline, alongside MTF traction.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company start third-party distribution like IIFL Securities?
qa_highlights.answer: Not in the near term; it may be considered in the medium to long term, with core-adjacent products such as MTF and LAS first.

risks_watch: Q1 slowdown in ADTO and customer acquisition; management has not quantified the recovery path.
Competition from large scaled-up players; market share shifts were acknowledged but not quantified.
Execution risk on the platform revamp and the AI and MCP initiatives, which were still in beta.
Exchange margin and funding requirements after RBI ended broker intraday facility from 1 July.
Reliance on F&O revenue, which dipped in Q1.
540776|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on product and long-term opportunity, but candid that Q1 was slower and that volatility spilled over. Answers on ADTO and customer metrics were qualitative and deflected to RPC and LTV, with no quantified guidance.
key_quotes: So, it is slightly one-off. I mean, overall revenue-wise, yes, we've grown.
So, our focus is that we are able to also bring in a higher number of customers with higher quality.
So, I do believe that from these quarters on, we can see an acceleration in growth.

540776|2026-09.headline: 5paisa Q2 FY27 revenue INR 86.5 crore (+13% H1 growth to INR 175 crore); net profit fell to INR 7.1 crore as tech spend continued amid weak markets.
540776|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a soft quarter for Indian equity markets, with derivatives volumes and average daily turnover (INR 2.59 trillion) down after the cash-segment rollout. Revenue was INR 865 million (INR 86.5 crore) and first-half revenue grew 13% to about INR 1,750 million. Net profit was INR 7.1 crore, lower than Q1, as the company chose to keep investing in technology, product and brand. The rights issue lifted net worth to INR 11,360 million from INR 650 crore at end-March 2026, and the company launched a rebuilt trading and investing app, AlgoSpace and AI assistant "Ask 5paisa".

segments.name: Broking (allied)
segments.commentary: Allied broking income grew 25% YoY in the period. Derivatives volumes fell after the cash-segment rollout, per management.

segments.name: Other operating income
segments.commentary: Other operating income grew 18% YoY. No further breakdown given.

segments.name: Client funding / lending
segments.commentary: Average funding book around INR 480 crore, spread across a large client base rather than a few clients; management said growth is being pursued carefully.

segments.name: Mutual funds (distribution)
segments.commentary: Mutual fund assets on platform at INR 2,095 crore; AI assistant now gives fund recommendations and comparisons (category, expense ratio, fund management).

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance given on revenue, margins or profit.
Management says it will keep investing in technology, products and brands through the year ahead, and sees the current market softness as a phase in the cycle.

Trendlyne acquisition: Board approved end-July 2026; formal closing still pending. Post-closing, management will decide whether to merge it fully or keep it as a wholly owned subsidiary, and plans to bring Trendlyne's baskets, screeners and AI stack to the 5paisa app regardless of structure.
Company plans to launch an IPO-related product in the near future (no details).
capex_capacity: New trading and investing app rebuilt with new back-end APIs, OMS and RMS; about INR 62 million of costs capitalised this quarter, to be amortised over several years.
Collateral from shares, mutual funds and ETFs now managed in one place; instant withdrawals up to INR 2 lakh per customer account.
Product stack includes AlgoSpace (readymade algo strategies across cash, futures and options), Xstreme APIs, co-location and F&O 360 platform for active traders.
demand_pricing: Customer base 53.4 lakh; about 81,600 new customers added in the quarter; more than 24 million app users; over 95% of new customers onboarded fully self-service (DIY).
Active NSE clients about 46 million; average daily turnover INR 2.59 trillion, reflecting slower trading across the board.
India added roughly 16 million demat accounts in H1 FY27, which management cites as a long-term positive.
Early AI tool traction: products live only weeks to a few months; no retention or conversion data disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Trendlyne acquisition be positioned, and will it be integrated into the 5paisa app or run separately?
qa_highlights.answer: Board approved the deal end-July, but formal closing is pending; structure (merge or subsidiary) to be decided after closing. Product plan is to bring Trendlyne's baskets, screeners and AI features into the 5paisa app either way.

qa_highlights.question: What engagement or trade conversion is being seen from AI tools, and are users showing higher retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to say; most products have been live only for weeks to a few months. Management expects engagement to rise for mature, useful products, citing Ask 5paisa mutual fund recommendations and comparisons as an example, but has no retention data yet.

risks_watch: Weak trading activity: derivatives volumes and daily turnover fell after the cash-segment rollout; profit fell versus Q1 FY27.
Profitability under continued heavy spend on technology, product and brand, with the new app's capitalised cost (INR 62 million this quarter) to be amortised over several years.
Client funding book expansion (about INR 480 crore average) now that net worth has risen to INR 11,360 million; management says growth will be careful.
Trendlyne acquisition not yet closed; post-closing legal structure and integration plan still open.
Early-stage AI product adoption; no engagement, conversion or retention metrics disclosed yet.
540776|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the long-term opportunity and product rebuild, but candid that the quarter was weak and profit fell. Management was vague on the Trendlyne structure and AI engagement, saying both were too early to call.
key_quotes: We see it as a phase in the cycle, and we're using this time to build a stronger business.
Net Profit was INR 7.1 crore, lower than Q1, because we choose to keep investing in technology, product, and brands even though trading activity was slower across the board.
The rights issue has significantly strengthened our Balance Sheet.

540777|2026-06.headline: HDFC Life Q1 FY27 VNB rose 9% to INR 879 crores at a 25% margin, with individual APE up 7% and HDFC Bank channel subdued.
540777|2026-06.overview: Individual APE grew 7% YoY and overall APE 9%, led by credit life and group, while channels excluding HDFC Bank grew about 17% with agency up 21%. VNB rose 9% to INR 879 crores and new business margin was 25%, up 100 bps QoQ, after absorbing about 60 bps residual GST impact. Profit after tax was INR 611 crores (up 12%, or 17% excluding GST), embedded value INR 65,860 crores and solvency 185%. 13-month persistency moderated about 200 bps to 84%, and HDFC Bank channel business stayed soft as the company ceded share during competitive pricing in FY26 and says it has now recovered.

financial_highlights.change: +100 bps QoQ; GST impact approx. 60 bps
Improved after INR 1,000 crore preferential allotment by HDFC Bank; additional sub-debt capacity INR 500 crores (about 4% upside)

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: Grew 21% YoY, ahead of company average, with healthy traction in protection and annuity. Branches opened in the past 24 months contribute about 16% of agency APE; term and annuity share of agency rose from 15% to 27%.

segments.name: Non-bank alliances
segments.commentary: Retail protection grew 60% YoY, driven mainly by aggregators; market share across partners broadly stable.

segments.name: HDFC Bank channel
segments.commentary: Subdued growth as the bank base is large and the company let share go in competitive segments in 4-6 months of FY26. Share has recovered toward year-ago levels on a run-rate basis; HDFC Bank contributed 47% of retail APE this quarter.

segments.name: Banca beyond HDFC Bank
segments.commentary: Grew about 15% in the quarter as competitive intensity moderated across other banks.

segments.name: Product mix (individual APE)
segments.commentary: Unit-linked 44%, non-par savings 22% (run-rate mid-20s by quarter-end), participating 15%, retail protection 8% (about 11% including riders), annuities 11% (nearly doubled from 5%). Protection grew over 40% YoY; credit protect grew 19%.

segments.name: HDFC Pension Fund Management (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Market share 43% with AUM of about INR 1.75 lakh crores, up 33% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 aspiration unchanged: grow in line with or faster than the industry, and deliver VNB growth broadly in line with APE growth.
Industry growth base case about 15-17%; company needs to grow a little over 16% over the remaining nine months to match industry-level growth.
New business margin expected to remain range-bound around current levels (about 25%); management says the company will prioritise growth over margin expansion.
Residual GST impact of about 60 bps expected to be neutralised over the coming quarters; it will be in the base from H2.
Protection growth rates may moderate in H2 as the recent tailwind normalises; non-par share expected to improve gradually; unit-linked mix not expected to rise meaningfully.
Solvency capacity: management is comfortable with a 15-18 month runway at the current run rate, including sub-debt capacity; looks forward to risk-based capital transition.

qa_highlights.question: Why has margin improved only modestly over the last 7-8 years versus peers, and what is the basis for confidence in FY27 growth and VNB?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins expanded 100-150 bps per two-year period to FY22, then fell about 90 bps (FY22-24) on regulatory changes, with 26.3% in FY24 and a 100 bps surrender-charge impact in FY25; the GST impact was 300 bps, of which about 110 bps remained at FY26 end, 50 bps was absorbed in Q1 and about 60 bps is still to go. Growth confidence rests on agency (up 21%) and proprietary channels (up over 20%).

qa_highlights.question: Will non-par and product mix sustain, and what happens to margins if ULIP picks up?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said ULIP mix will not rise meaningfully, non-par expected to hold mid-20s share, annuities to stay well above last year, and NBM to stay around 25%-odd. Protection's share may stay roughly where it is, and growth may be higher in the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Has the HDFC Bank counter share recovered, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bank share has returned to roughly the level of a year ago on a run-rate basis, with pricing more benign; the company declined to give channel-wise growth guidance and said it is tracking selectively by segment (non-par, protection, par over unit-linked).

qa_highlights.question: Is the non-par recovery demand-led or a result of company pricing and yield-curve effects?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is a combination: competitor intensity has eased, the company can compete on sensible terms, headline rates are higher than a year ago, and customer asset allocation toward guaranteed products is also a driver. He said the company will not compete on price alone.

qa_highlights.question: What is the banca growth outlook, and how does HDFC Bank compare on a 2-year CAGR basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Banca beyond HDFC Bank grew about 15% in Q1. HDFC Bank was described as marginally lower or flattish YoY; on a 2-year CAGR basis it is similar to other banks at about 10%, and management guided 10-12% growth for HDFC Bank.

qa_highlights.question: How much runway does capital have before a fundraise, and what is the variable annuity opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Solvency is 185% with INR 500 crore sub-debt capacity (about 4% upside); management is comfortable with 15-18 months runway at the current run rate. Variable annuity: two product structures launched, aimed at customers willing to commit for a longer period, slightly younger and with lower ticket sizes; margins said to be above company average.

qa_highlights.question: What is the persistency outlook, given traditional persistency fell from 88-89% to about 83%?
qa_highlights.answer: Appointed Actuary cited a shift to lower ticket sizes after the tax change, a product feature that drove lapses (now moderated, about 40-50 bps effect), and the Q1 March-pace effect. Expected traditional persistency range is 84-85%; 87-88% was not expected in the near term.

capex_capacity: Solvency ratio 185% after INR 1,000 crore preferential allotment by HDFC Bank; additional sub-debt capacity INR 500 crores, equal to about 4% solvency upside.

Management says the current run rate is comfortable with a 15-18 month runway on current capital plus sub-debt capacity; expects transition to risk-based capital (RBC) at some point, timing not specified.
AUM crossed INR 4 trillion this quarter.

Branch network: 700-plus branches across 600-plus cities; expansion slowed to selective cohorts this year. Branches opened in past 24 months contribute about 16% of agency APE. Branch breakeven about 18 months (12-18 months in larger markets, 18-30 months in smaller markets); maturity about 2.5 years.
Regulatory: IFRS implementation on track; timing of RBC framework still awaited. Draft rules reportedly allow life insurers to participate in repo market.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 individual APE grew 7% YoY and WRP 8%; overall APE 9%, led by credit life and group. 2-year individual APE CAGR 10%. Retail private market share 16.3%.

Channels excluding HDFC Bank grew about 17%; agency grew 21%; proprietary channels grew above 20%; banca beyond HDFC Bank about 15%; non-bank alliances retail protection up 60% YoY, mainly aggregators.

HDFC Bank channel subdued; company says it let share go in 4-6 months of FY26 in competitive segments. Share now back to roughly year-ago levels on run-rate basis (management said 'first quarter last year' level). HDFC Bank contributed 47% of retail APE this quarter. Management guides bank channel growth of about 10-12% for the year (per CFO-level answer), with flattish Q1 growth.

Product mix of individual APE: unit-linked 44%, non-par savings 22% (run rate mid-20s by quarter-end, from about 18% last year), participating 15%, retail protection 8% (about 11% incl. riders), annuities 11% (from 5%). Protection up over 40% YoY; credit protect up 19% on MFI recovery.
Persistency: 13-month down about 200 bps to 84%; 61st month up over 150 bps to 65%. Renewal collections up 19%. Mgmt expects traditional persistency in 84-85% range.

Pricing and margin: Q1 VNB INR 879 crores, up 9% YoY; NBM 25%, up 100 bps QoQ; residual GST impact about 60 bps. Management guides NBM range-bound near current levels, prioritising growth over margin expansion. Ex-GST margin cited as 25.6% vs 25.1% opening.
Industry growth base case 15-17%; company needs a little over 16% growth over the remaining nine months to match industry.
Non-par products: rate actioning on select cohorts, favourable yield environment and competitor repositioning cited as drivers; management says customers shifting toward guaranteed products.
risks_watch: HDFC Bank channel recovery: Q1 growth is flattish and management guides only 10-12% for the year; the company says share is back but gave no quantified target.
Margin: NBM guided range-bound around 25% with about 60 bps of GST residual still to be absorbed; management says growth takes priority, so VNB growth may lag APE if pricing gets more aggressive.
Persistency: 13-month persistency fell about 200 bps to 84%; management expects 84-85% for traditional business over the coming year.
Protection growth may moderate in H2 against a high base; ticket size is being diluted by lower-ticket protection and INR 50,000-1 lakh policies.
Industry growth assumption of 15-17%: company must grow a little over 16% over the remaining nine months to hit industry-level growth.
Regulatory: RBC transition timing still unspecified; RBI third-party distribution rules effective January 1; IRDAI distribution-remuneration paper awaited; geopolitical and oil-price risks flagged.
key_quotes: Channels other than HDFC Bank collectively grew at 17% in Q1 FY27, led by a strong performance by our agency channel and healthy momentum across non -bank alliances
Going forward, while margins should improve with scale and product mix, as stated at the beginning of this year, we will continue to prioritize growth over margin expansion.

We remain disciplined in our approach anchored in customer acquisition, product competitiveness and quality of business and confident that the machinery we have built is positioned to deliver on both.
540777|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the agency and proprietary channels and on the FY27 aspiration, but cautious and somewhat evasive on HDFC Bank channel numbers, declining to give channel-level growth or counter-share targets. Management was also guarded on the margin outlook, repeatedly saying it would trade margin for growth and that the outcome would be a 'range'.

540777|2026-09.headline: HDFC Life H1 FY27 VNB rose 12% to ₹2,037 crore at a 24.7% margin, while solvency fell to 180% on capital consumption.
540777|2026-09.overview: Q2 individual APE growth of 13% (overall) and 11% in H1 kept HDFC Life ahead of the private industry, with individual weighted received premium up 11% in Q2 and market share up 10bps to 16.2%. VNB reached ₹2,037 crore (up 12%, Q2 up 15%) and margin expanded to 24.7% from 24.5%. Persistency softened on unit-linked renewals and a non-par cohort, and the EV walk showed negative operating and investment variances from equity underperformance, yield rises and wider credit spreads. Solvency fell to 180%, prompting a ₹500 crore subordinated debt raise. Management spent much of the call on the IRDAI distribution-economics consultation paper, where it was non-committal on specifics.

financial_highlights.change: Regulatory requirement 150%; ₹500 crore sub-debt expected to add about 4 percentage points
Q2 individual weighted received premium +11% vs private industry +10%

segments.name: Bancassurance (HDFC Bank)
segments.commentary: HDFC Bank-sourced individual APE grew 12% in Q2, slightly ahead of company growth; the bank accounts for about 48% of APE in Q2 but less than 40% of NBP. Other bancassurance partners grew 13% in Q2, and a new J&K Bank partnership was announced.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Agency grew 13% in H1, faster than the company and the agency market. Branches opened in the last ~30 months contribute about 17% of agency business versus 12% a year ago; protection and annuity together are about 30% of channel mix versus 15% previously.

segments.name: Product mix (individual APE, H1)
segments.commentary: Unit-linked 45%, non-par savings 22% (from about 18%), participating 13%, annuity 12% (versus 4-5% previously), retail protection 8% (from about 7%). Retail protection grew 33% in H1; protection plus riders is 11% of APE; credit protect grew 19%.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Pension business AUM reached ₹1.8 lakh crore, up 28% YoY. MSCI ESG rating upgraded to AAA from AA.

guidance_outlook: Expects individual APE growth in FY27 to be in line with the industry, after 9% in H1.
VNB growth to be in line with APE or slightly ahead; management will prioritise VNB growth over margin, with margin an outcome of mix and competition.
GST cost benefit (about 15% cost reduction) gets fully baked into the business model from H2 FY27; scale recovery is expected to lift margins, but most will be reinvested.
Expects persistency to recover by year-end, particularly unit-linked renewals, with the non-par cohort run-off progressing.
Expects to remain comfortably above the 150% regulatory minimum through FY27 after the ₹500 crore sub-debt, which is expected to close in the current quarter.
Protection growth expected to normalise in H2 against a 57% base (H2 FY26 post-GST), while remaining strong on a two-year CAGR basis.
On the expense ratio (about 21%, over half commissions), management said reaching 15% under the discussion-paper commissions is mathematically achievable; glide path still to be determined.
Management views 1 January as an unlikely effective date for distribution reforms; the earliest plausible date is 1 April.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion: over 250 agency branches added in the last ~30 months; branches contribute about 17% of agency business.
Technology architecture rollout is expected to support customer- and partner-facing capabilities; investments to continue.
Capital: solvency at 180% after capital consumption from writing long-term profitable products; management expects RBC transition discussions and a timeline around next year.
demand_pricing: Unit-linked demand resilient despite equity volatility; renewal collections softer in unit-linked, while new business flows into unit-linked remained strong.
HDFC Bank IRRs made competitive via higher yields, enabling a share recovery in non-par; no change in commercial payouts, according to management.
Annuity mix rose on variable annuity launch (Q4 FY26); new business premium share of annuity is about 17% (from about 14%).
Average ticket size: savings about ₹1.1 lakh, protection about ₹40-45 thousand; protection at 8% of APE implies about 2.5x that share on policy count.

Sector competition: management says the market is intensely competitive; the proposed commission caps are expected to hit brokers and corporate agents most, then banks, with agency least affected (management's categorisation).

qa_highlights.question: What changed at HDFC Bank that drove growth recovery, and did IRRs or commissions change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited granular branch-level engagement, a withdrawal of extra contests about a year ago, and fixing credit and people issues over the last 3-4 months. Rates were kept competitive with higher yields; no change in commercial payouts.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EV walk operating variance is persistency, and what drove the investment variance?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating variance was primarily unit-linked persistency plus residual non-par run-off. Investment variance came from equity returns of about 3-3.5% versus 5% expected, a 25-30bps short-end yield rise, and wider credit spreads.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the capital consumption and how will solvency evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term profitable products lock capital under the current regime; the sub-debt adds about 4 percentage points, and management expects to remain comfortably above 150% through FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How do the proposed commission limits affect VNB margin and EoM?
qa_highlights.answer: Expense ratio about 21%, with commissions more than half; under the proposed levels, commissions fall to half or less, so a 15% EoM is mathematically achievable, subject to scale and glide-path considerations.

qa_highlights.question: Is persistency pressure concentrated in TULIPs or the wider unit-linked book?
qa_highlights.answer: Not limited to any product: pressure is uniform across unit-linked. Recent unit-linked persistency variance is captured in the EV; management expects most to be recovered by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit life share, and what is the HDFC Bank share of it?
qa_highlights.answer: HDFC Bank contributes less than one-third of credit life business, which is diversified across MFIs, NBFCs, banks and the HDFC Group. Management would not disclose the bundled-versus-separate premium collection mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Palghar GST demand, and does the appeal change the provisioning stance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the balance-sheet figure is correct and it is treated as a contingent liability (₹942 crore base, with the accrued total in the books). Interest is excluded and management is confident on the merits, so no provision was taken; contingent liabilities rose to ₹2,207 crore from ₹1,870 crore.

risks_watch: Distribution-reform consultation: commission caps, closed-architecture tilt and possible credit-life restrictions could affect bancassurance and group business; draft regulation timing is uncertain.
Unit-linked renewal persistency and the non-par cohort run-off: recovery is expected by year-end and needs monitoring.
Solvency at 180% with capital consumption ongoing; RBC transition timing (possibly next year) is open.
Palghar GST demand (₹942 crore base, contingent liability) and the reported ₹2,423 crore figure in the appeal: the exact amount and solvency impact remained unclear.
Protection growth normalisation in H2 as the GST-exemption base effect kicks in (base growth of 57% in H2 FY26).
Equity and yield volatility driving investment variance and the EV walk.
540777|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and VNB momentum, and on the bank channel recovery, but evasive on distribution reforms, the VNB margin path, variable annuity economics and the Palghar figure, which management deferred until drafts are issued.
key_quotes: We remain confident in the long-term opportunity for the industry and in our ability to further strengthen our position within it.
Our approach is fairly clear and we'll stay with that, that we'll want to maximize VNB growth, and margins will be an outcome of everything that we see around us.
No, the regulator and government have been very reasonable in their expectation when the GST change happened because it was very, very clear and visible to the customer.

540795|2026-06.headline: Dynamic Cables Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to a record Q1 level, with EBITDA up 41% to INR38 crore and order book at INR811 crore.
540795|2026-06.overview: Management reported record first-quarter revenue, up 33% YoY, with EBITDA up 41% to INR38 crore (margin 10.9%) and PAT up 37% to INR25 crore. Growth was largely price-driven: volume grew only 5-6% against a high base of roughly 25-26% last year, as aluminium price spikes led to order postponements in April-May. The company entered the US market in the quarter with first supplies, and the new capacity expansion is on track for commissioning from September 2026, with meaningful revenue expected from Q4. Order book stood at INR811 crore as of 30 June 2026, with customers booking shorter cycles at elevated prices.

segments.name: HV cables
segments.commentary: 68% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Core growth driver alongside T&D demand.

segments.name: LV cables
segments.commentary: 30% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Company has been moving mix away from LV toward HV and MV.

segments.name: Conductor
segments.commentary: 2% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Conductor volume growth was lower than cable volume growth in the quarter.

segments.name: Solar / renewable cables
segments.commentary: About 20% of revenue in Q1; expected to remain in a similar range for FY27 H1, rising in H2 as new plant comes on. Management sees 25-30% growth for the next 3-4 years.

segments.name: Railway signalling
segments.commentary: Temporarily held back due to weak margins and competition; not a shutdown. Zero contribution in last Q1, so no base effect this quarter.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 13% of revenue. US contributed about 15% of exports in its first quarter; Asia, Southeast Asia and Africa remain the core; Middle East negligible.

guidance_outlook: No formal annual guidance; management reiterated 18-20% growth record over the last 10-15 years and aims to sustain a similar long-term rate, with some quarters of higher, others of moderate growth.
New plant (about INR45 crore capex) to commission from September 2026; meaningful revenue expected only from Q4 FY27.
Target optimum utilisation of 80-85% of the new plant by end FY28, roughly 18 months from commencement.

capex_capacity: Ascent-K Circuit HDI PCB plant in Noida: construction to start around June 2026, 15-16 months to build, then 3-4 months of trial production; mass production from Q3-Q4 FY28. Backed by over INR4,500 crore of ECMS investment approvals across Ascent-K, Ascent and Shogini.
Ascent Circuits Hosur: construction delayed about one quarter by a pollution consent issue; trial production by Q3 FY27 and commercial production by mid-February 2027.

FY26 total capex about INR1,070 crore, of which INR550 crore capitalised and the balance in CWIP for operations in FY27. FY27 capex of about INR1,200 crore for Ascent plus INR700-800 crore for other entities.

Subsidies: about 48% of plant and machinery via ECMS and 42% from the UP government on building and plant and machinery, received with a 5-6 year lag. Land received at about a 25% discount; the subsidy flow is expected from FY28.

Sri City RAC capacity augmented. Railway Faridabad greenfield plant in trial production. Yujin factory in Korea completed, awaiting RDSO approval (12-15 months), with INR178 crore couplers order book.
demand_pricing: Industry view: RAC volumes were down about 30% in Q1 and Q2 FY26 and recovered in Q3-Q4, leaving FY26 roughly flat. Industry expected to grow about 20% in Q1 FY27 and 12-13% for FY27.

Price increases of about 14% YoY on finished goods: one in January 2026 from the star-rating change and one in April 2026 for commodity costs. Copper clad laminate prices are up more than 60% in one year and still rising; gold is up about 60%.
PCB pricing: Tier 1 EMS pass-through works on a quarterly lag, but PCB (Tier 2) has about a two-quarter lag. Two price increases of about 15% and 18% have been received, with more under negotiation.
Compressor import relief: government allowed imports of about 30% of last year's volumes for compressors below 2 tonne, extended for a year. Management says there is no compressor shortage.
Electronics margin pressure: PCBA about 5% and PCB about 12-13% versus a normal 16-17%. Management expects the price increases to flow through over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RAC industry growth expectations for Q1 and FY27, and which segments face margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry expected to grow about 20% in Q1 FY27 and 12-13% for the full year. Margin pressure comes from minimum wage hikes (35% in Haryana, about 22% in UP), CCL and gold costs, and currency depreciation. Indian Railway fixed-price contracts cannot pass costs through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10-12% price increase reasonable?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases are about 14% YoY, from a January star-rating change and an April commodity-driven hike.

qa_highlights.question: Will compressor shortages hurt FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says there is no shortage. Five new domestic manufacturers have come up, and imports of 30% of last year's volumes are allowed. Commercial AC compressors are still largely imported.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Consumer Durables finished-goods share rise, and is it realisation-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished goods rose because gas-charging customers moved to ODM solutions, not because of realisation. Finished goods fell from about 80% at listing in FY18 to about 40% now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PCB versus PCBA mix and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 Electronics: PCBA about INR2,281 crore at about 5% margin; PCB about INR600 crore at 12-13%; Power-One about 15% margin; Unitronics not disclosed as it is listed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and net cash outflow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 gross capex INR1,800-2,000 crore with cash outflow of about INR1,100-1,200 crore. FY28 cash outflow of about INR1,400-1,500 crore.

risks_watch: FY27 margin squeeze of 50-100 bps from commodity inflation, currency depreciation and minimum wage revisions in UP, Haryana and other states.
PCB price pass-through lag of about two quarters and the Tier 2 position, which limit near-term recovery.
Net debt rising to INR700-800 crore by March 2027 while capex is heavy; working capital days up to 29 from 9 due to inventory build.
Ascent Hosur construction delay (about one quarter) and Ascent-K HDI timelines; subsidies arrive with a 5-6 year lag.
Non-controlling interest from CCPS: auditors assumed about 30% dilution as a maximum, with actual dilution expected to be lower; NCI remains a balance-sheet item.
Electronics customer shifts from purchase to job-work could cause organic top-line volatility; organic growth was subdued in Q4.
540902|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity, with an explicit caution on near-term margins. Management was candid about the 50-100 bps FY27 squeeze and the PCB lag, and gave specific numbers for capex and cash flow. Management declined to give Unitronics-level detail because it is listed.
key_quotes: So our endeavor on going towards the value side of the businesses is because in B2B business, what we are trying to attempt is we are trying to balance the left and right.
To sum up, we expect a margin pressure of 50 to 100 bps at consolidated level, which is of temporary in nature and expected to normalize as macro environment improves.

540902|2026-06.headline: Amber Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA 28% to INR337 crore, with Electronics EBITDA more than doubling.
540902|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA grew 28% to INR337 crore, with adjusted PAT of INR126 crore (up 19%) before a INR123 crore exceptional loss. Electronics was the standout, with revenue up 29% and EBITDA more than doubling to a 10.8% margin. Railway & Defense EBITDA fell 26% on mix, copper, currency and Haryana minimum wage hikes. Management flagged that PCB margins were compressed by a roughly two-quarter pass-through lag and that cost pressure persists through H1, while Q1 benefited from pre-stocking of compressors and copper. The IL JIN facility incident was a new overhang, with insurance cover and the impact still being assessed.

segments.name: Consumer Durable
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,758 crore (+8%) and EBITDA INR214 crore (+12%) despite commodity and minimum wage headwinds; management attributed the modest growth to a high base. RAC is roughly 55-60% of the division, with the remainder non-RAC.

segments.name: Electronics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR985 crore (+29%) and EBITDA INR107 crore (10.8% margin, up from about 6.4%). Bare PCB margin compressed on copper clad laminate (CCL) costs, and the EMS segment grew more slowly as customers destocked and shifted to job work. Management reiterated FY27 growth of about 40%.

segments.name: Railway Sub-systems & Defense
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore (+18%) but EBITDA fell 26% to INR16 crore on product mix, including first trains supplied through a principal, plus copper, currency and a 35% Haryana minimum wage hike. FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-35% and EBITDA margin at 15-16%.

guidance_outlook: Electronics: FY27 growth of about 40% reiterated; EMS full-year guidance intact per Sanjay Arora.
Railway Sub-systems & Defense: FY27 revenue growth 30-35% and EBITDA margin 15-16%.
Consumer Durable: growth in line with RAC industry, cited as 13-15%; no percentage margin guidance given.
Group margin: earlier 50-100 bps decline guidance for FY27 now moderated, with margins seen normalising if no further currency or commodity disruption.
PCB margin: currently about 12% versus about 16% normal; expected to recover from Q3 FY27 to a 15-16% normalised range, subject to no further CCL price rises.

Oppo mobile: trial production in Q4 FY27, commercial production from Q1 FY28, about 8 million units in year one, rising to 15-16 million in year two; revenue-recognition model to be clarified in 15-20 days.
IL JIN: fundraise enabling resolution up to INR5,000 crore; quantum and form not yet decided. IL JIN production impact being assessed, with guidance expected to be met.
capex_capacity: PCB capex: about INR3,200 crore at Jewar (UP), where construction has started and trial production is about 18 months away; Hosur (Tamil Nadu) about INR1,000 crore, with the plant to be running this financial year; Shogini (Pune) INR500 crore. All three were approved under the ECMS scheme.
Jewar HDI PCB groundbreaking held with Ascent-K / Korea Circuit; air conditioner plant construction planned to start in 2028, with trial production in 2029.
Sidwal greenfield facility in Faridabad (HVAC, pantry, doors, gangways) is now operational.
Asset turn in PCB business about 0.8:1 depending on complexity.
CCL backward integration: Amber in discussion with JV partners; target own CCL plants by 2029-30.
demand_pricing: Consumer Durable: BEE tonnage labelling mandatory from 1 July 2026 has created mixed inventory in the trade; management expects inventory to clear by Diwali, a strong summer from November, and not very high festive demand.
Q1 Consumer Durable margins were helped by pre-buying of compressors and copper ahead of QCO enforcement, and by a premium mix (5-star and 2-tonne). Management said this would not be annualised.
PCB: pass-through to customers is progressing, with some customers raising prices in July. Copper clad laminate prices keep rising, driven by AI and data-centre demand and a shortage.
Electronics TAM: management cited $185 billion of electronics consumption, a $16-17 billion addressable market for PCB, PCBA and power electronics today, and an estimated $35-40 billion by FY30.
Power electronics (PLC, HMI, solar inverters, UPS, BESS) expected to grow 35-40%.
