qa_highlights.question: Santhosh Seshadri (Avendus) asked about Oppo mobile export discussions, PLI eligibility, and PCB fixed-price contract exposure.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export talks with Oppo are early and export would be considered after one year of domestic production; three ECMS approvals (INR3,200 crore Jewar, about INR1,000 crore Hosur, INR500 crore Shogini) are in place; PCB pass-through runs on a two-quarter lag as tier-2 supplier, with some customers already raising prices in July. Draft PLI guidelines are awaited.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Bhartia (Investec) asked whether Q1 consumer durable margins reflected raw material inflation and inventory benefit, and about H1 margin outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said Q1 benefited from pre-stocking of compressors and copper ahead of QCO enforcement and a premium mix (5-star and 2-tonne), which will not be annualised. He said margins are not expected to compress and the full-year outlook remains in line with projections.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Bhartia asked about the operational impact of the IL JIN incident.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said reconstruction permission was received the previous day and assessment is under way. Guided numbers for the quarter are still expected to be met, and exchanges will be informed.

qa_highlights.question: Dhruv Jain (Ambit) asked why Electronics growth looks lower excluding acquisitions, and about FY27 guidance and railway margin outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Arora said EMS growth slowed because customers destocked and some shifted to job work, and smart meter and smart watch segments declined; full-year EMS guidance is intact. For Railways, Jasbir Singh guided FY27 revenue growth of 30-35% and margin of 15-16%, citing fixed-price railway contracts and first trains supplied through a principal.

qa_highlights.question: Keshav Lahoti (HDFC Securities) asked why minority interest swung from INR28 crore positive to INR19 crore negative, and about the IL JIN incident impact.
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhir Goyal said the swing was checked later: the INR123 crore exceptional loss sits in Electronics entities with minority holders, pushing the minority share negative. Jasbir Singh said assets are insured, production has shifted to other IL JIN locations, and the impact will be quantified within a week.

qa_highlights.question: Sameet Sinha (Macquarie) asked about input cost pass-through timing and local CCL manufacturing.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said consumer durable is tier 1 with a one-quarter lag, while PCB is tier 2 with a two-quarter lag, so pass-through starts from Q4. A first Wipro CCL plant is nearly operational, two more are planned, and Amber is in JV talks targeting own CCL plants by FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Achal Lohade (Nuvama) asked about PCB margin quantum, next-two-quarter margin path, and drivers of the 40% Electronics growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said normalised PCB margin is about 16% versus about 12% now, with Q2 still impacted and recovery from Q3 to a 15-16% range, subject to no further CCL price rises. All three Electronics divisions (PCBA, PCB, industrial power electronics) are expected to drive the 40% growth. Sudhir Goyal said a group-level minority percentage cannot be given.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavik Mehta (JP Morgan) asked whether the consumer durable industry growth and the 50-100 bps FY27 margin decline guidance still hold, and the timing of Oppo revenue recognition clarity.
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said consumer durable growth is in line with industry, cited at 13-15%. Jasbir Singh said the 50-100 bps decline is moderated, with margins normalising absent further currency or commodity disruption. Oppo revenue-recognition clarity is expected in 15-20 days.

qa_highlights.question: Indrajit Agarwal (CLSA) asked about Oppo revenue booking entity, minority stake in IL JIN, and consolidated net debt.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh said the booking entity (IL JIN or Amber) depends on ERP integration and will be formalised before mid-September. Sudhir Goyal said minority is computed on a diluted basis of about 60% with about 39-40% treated as minority interest, and net debt was about INR1,225 crore at 30 June 2026 versus about INR510 crore at March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Rahul Agarwal (IKIGAI) asked for an entity-wise Electronics revenue build-up over three years.
qa_highlights.answer: Jasbir Singh declined a three-year number, citing asset turn of 0.8:1 and the capex plan (Jewar INR3,200 crore, Hosur INR1,000 crore). Power electronics is guided to grow 35-40%, and the Electronics TAM is $16-17 billion today, estimated at $35-40 billion by FY30. He did not accept the INR5,000 crore consolidated electronics sales framing.

risks_watch: IL JIN facility incident: final loss quantification and insurance recovery still pending; management promised an update within a week and a reassessment of the guided numbers.
PCB margin recovery depends on customer price pass-through and no further CCL price increases; Q2 FY27 is expected to remain impacted at about 12% margin versus about 16% normal.
Q1 consumer durable margin benefited from pre-stocking and a premium mix that management said will not be annualised; watch for normalisation as the BEE tonnage labelling mix clears by Diwali.

Net debt rose to about INR1,225 crore at 30 June 2026 from about INR510 crore at March 2026, alongside a fundraise enabling resolution of up to INR5,000 crore at IL JIN with quantum and form undecided.
Oppo mobile: revenue-recognition model (IL JIN vs Amber level) to be decided by mid-September; PLI eligibility depends on draft guidelines not yet issued; trial production targeted for Q4 FY27.
Minority interest swung to negative INR19 crore from positive INR28 crore; the adjusted minority figure was not provided on the call and was to be calculated later.
key_quotes: But what we have seen in July is that there are some customers who have increased the cost. So our margins are coming back to where it was.
But let me tell everybody on the call that the guided number of what we did last quarter, we are hopeful that we should be in line to deliver despite of this disruption.
So we are not looking at any margin compression.
But only subject to no further CCL price increases are happening.
540902|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth, the Oppo project, and the 40% Electronics and 30-35% Railways guidance, but cautious and evasive on near-term margins, the IL JIN impact, and any quantified multi-year targets. Management repeatedly declined to give numbers on consumer durable margins, three-year revenue build-up, and group minority allocation, citing volatility.

540935|2026-03.headline: Galaxy Surfactants Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell to INR122 crore (from INR135 crore) and EBITDA/MT to INR20,114; Q1 FY27 guided to high end of 6-8% volume growth.
540935|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was hit by West Asia war disruptions to logistics, feedstock availability and customer ordering, with Egypt operations stalled through March. EBITDA declined year-on-year to INR122 crore and EBITDA per metric ton to INR20,114 from INR21,715. India volumes grew 8% YoY in Q4 while AMET volumes fell 15% and RoW fell 7%, with the Americas a relative bright spot after US tariff reversals. Management guided only for Q1 FY27 (high end of 6-8% volume growth and high end of INR19,000-21,000/MT EBITDA), declining to give full-year guidance given the uncertainty.

Q1 FY27: EBITDA per MT at the higher end of the INR19,000-21,000 range.

Maintenance capex about INR20-30 crore per year.
Product launches include Galsoft Lumithic (amino acid-based self-thickening mild surfactant) shown at in-cosmetics Paris.

EPC/project income recognised on a percentage-of-completion basis; not material in FY26, with bulk expected in FY27.

Competitive pressure in AMET from local players that are backward integrated, who have taken share from global customers.
Mix benefits expected from Americas specialty and Europe project pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why was specialty revenue flat QoQ (INR493 crore to INR498 crore) despite US tariff reversal, and how big is India's specialty mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the flat QoQ figure to product mix in US Q4 as products were shifted after tariff reversal. India specialty base is small, but D2C brands are growing their presence and use specialty ingredients.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term specialty mix outlook and the outlook for FY27-28 volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to grow both segments, expects a 60:40 to 70:30 range depending on performance, and still sees 60:40 to 65:35 by 2031. No FY27-28 volume guidance beyond Q1 given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for fatty alcohol prices and pass-through, and the risk of down-trading?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through is possible with a lag of about 1 month. Petrochemical feedstocks have risen more than oleochemicals, and the current challenge is supply availability rather than demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Egypt facility's status on raw materials, logistics and demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand not a challenge; March was disrupted by stuck inbound materials. Operations restored from mid-April, and management expects May and June to run uninterrupted.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Q1 volume guidance rely mainly on supply constraints at competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; the guidance is driven by India recovery to 8-10% growth, US business revival and AMET supply recovery, with a caveat that the outlook holds only if current conditions do not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Why has AMET fallen from ~90,000 MT to ~60,000 MT and what is the market outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Local backward-integrated players gained share; Egypt plant idle in March. Management said AMET has likely bottomed, with market growth of about 3-4%.

AMET: continued share loss to local players, currency and inflation issues in Egypt and Turkey, and credit risk in certain markets.

Wellness segment progress, described by management as behind plan.

540935|2026-06.headline: Galaxy Surfactants Q1 FY27 EBITDA hit a record INR 252.5 crore (INR 35,458/MT), nearly double YoY; FY27 EBITDA/MT guidance raised to INR 24,000–25,000.
540935|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR 252.5 crore from INR 135.1 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA per metric ton at INR 35,458 versus about INR 20,009 a year earlier. Consolidated volumes grew 5% YoY, with India up 11% and Rest of World up 6%, while AMET volumes fell 4% YoY but rose 19% QoQ after West Asia logistics disruptions cut April–May supply. Management attributed the margin jump to reformulation-led volume recovery, a richer specialty mix, commercial execution and feedstock volatility, and said some of these gains may not persist. FY27 volume guidance of 6–8% was maintained, while EBITDA/MT guidance was raised to INR 24,000–25,000 from INR 19,000–21,000; management implied roughly INR 21,000–22,000 per MT for the remaining three quarters.

segments.commentary: Volumes up 11% YoY, led by double-digit growth in performance surfactants and high single-digit growth in specialty products; non-Tier 1 and direct-to-consumer volumes grew near double digit.

segments.name: Rest of World (Americas, APAC, Europe)
segments.commentary: Volumes up 6% YoY; Americas led on tariff clarity and TRI-K premium specialties; APAC grew double-digit. Specialty mix improved, lifting EBITDA/MT.

segments.name: AMET (incl. Egypt)
segments.commentary: Volumes down 4% YoY but up 19% QoQ; about seven weeks of Q1 at the Egypt site were effectively lost because raw materials were stuck at Jebel Ali, Jeddah and Port Said/Suez ports; management called this supply-led, not demand-led.

segments.name: EPC service income (Mexico project)
segments.commentary: Separate business model, not part of performance segment; income recognised in Q1 with amount not disclosed (management said not significant to overall numbers); recognition to complete by end of FY27.

Fatty alcohol expected to trade sideways at INR 2,600–2,800/MT (ex-Indonesia-type range), with no major expected jumps or corrections.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA/kg at INR 35,000 in Q1, and how much came from inventory gains or mix?

qa_highlights.question: Is the specialty share decline from about 40% to 34% a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said specialty absolute revenue grew strongly; the share fell because performance products grew faster, enlarging the denominator.

qa_highlights.question: Will AMET return to positive volume growth in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was supply-led, not demand-led, with Egypt effectively washed out for about seven weeks; sequential growth of 18–19% and June momentum support a recovery, and it sees AMET returning to growth this year absent a new shock.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of reformulation reversing in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reformulation remains favourable while petrochemical and oleochemical balance holds; it does not see a big risk currently but will monitor coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 22–23/kg gross margin or INR 25/kg EBITDA a steady-state base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the structure has improved but said it wants at least one more quarter before changing long-term guidance, to avoid overpromising.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pricing gain is from finished-goods inventory spikes or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said freight costs, mix shift toward dry (100%/95% active) products, and the reformulation mix all lifted realisations; it declined to quantify the ASP increase excluding these.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for fatty alcohol prices and Indonesia's biodiesel mandate?
qa_highlights.answer: Palm oil is around USD 1,100–1,200/MT and the mandate is largely priced in; fatty alcohol expected to hold at INR 2,600–2,800 on a sideways basis, with El Nino a possible supply-side risk for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fleur's Rs 2,500-3,000 crore deployment and Warburg's Rs 960 crore be done at peak-cycle prices, and what are the IRR expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no hurry to deploy and that it is not in an up cycle, since India occupancy is in the mid-60s versus a 70-72% up-cycle threshold. It will focus on demand-dense top 6-7 cities, nearby 3-5 hour international markets and leisure locations, using brownfield, operating assets at 6-8x, greenfield and long leases, with returns targeted at about 60% post-fees ROCE and a conservative downturn assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 and FY28 net EBITDA margins recover, given the 47% analyst estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 will be well above 47%. It targets at least 50% in FY28 as renovation spend drops to about 1% of revenue and GST drag falls from about 2% of net revenue, with ARR rising 5-6% in Q2 and further in winter.

qa_highlights.question: Is Mumbai guidance being cut, and will Aurika Mumbai reach double-digit RevPAR growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was an aberration and that Q2 will be better, citing about 2,000 new rooms near the Mumbai airport. It said RevPAR is stabilised and the focus is now on repricing Aurika ARR, and declined to give a numerical RevPAR target before Q2 results.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 2,000-room opening target for FY27 slip, given 334 rooms opened in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said slippage is normal in the business but it is broadly confident of about 2,000 rooms, based on the current pipeline and owner relationships.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net room additions lag the 334 rooms opened in Q1, and what was the management fee compounding outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tarudhan Valley (70 rooms) was terminated and Nestor (130 rooms, no fees) was removed, so fee-earning additions were lower. It said about 1,300 rooms were added year-on-year and that about 5,000 managed rooms signed in FY26 are due to open by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the renovation timeline, and how much margin was lost to renovation versus GST and SAR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 renovation spend was Rs 9.8 crore (about 2.25-2.3% of revenue) versus a normal Rs 3 crore, and that about 300 rooms were done in Q1 with a similar number in Q2. It said refurbishments of about 800 rooms are planned in H2 and that the renovation drag disappears in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fleur's acquisition push raise debt above 2x EBITDA, and how will the debt be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt may briefly exceed 2x EBITDA during construction, with a long-term target near 2x. Fleur debt is about Rs 1,100-1,200 crore; group debt is about Rs 1,275 crore after excluding about Rs 200 crore of cash. Warburg's Rs 960 crore will be deployed before listing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demerger timeline and status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapil Sharma said CCI approval is done and SEBI and exchange scrutiny is in progress, followed by NCLT filing and hearings. Completion is targeted in H1 CY2027, with Fleur listing in the late second half of calendar 2027 as the conservative assumption.

risks_watch: Q2 delivery versus management's claim that July was strong and August solid; the Q2 ARR recovery of 5-6% and the balance of negotiated versus non-negotiated business are unverified until the next print.
GST input-credit loss persists at about 2% of net revenue; the pace of pricing above Rs 7,500 (52% of room sales currently below) determines whether the drag falls as guided.
Mumbai and Gurgaon corporate demand softness and the roughly 2,000-room Mumbai airport supply overhang; Aurika Mumbai repricing may not translate into RevPAR growth.
Execution risk on the ~2,000-room FY27 opening target (334 opened in Q1) and on managed-hotel friction, including terminations that reduce net room additions.
Fleur capital deployment of Rs 2,500-3,000 crore and the debt-to-EBITDA path, plus demerger approvals (SEBI, shareholders, creditors, GST, NCLT) that could delay the H1 CY2027 completion.
Renovation spend and margin recovery depend on the H2 refurb schedule (about 800 rooms) and on FY28 margin of at least 50%, which management itself called a stretch if not achieved.
key_quotes: But I would say this is temporarily; this was undertaken largely to react to the swing to the situation that we had in Q1.
And there is no reason why our EBITDA margins net should be less than 50%.
We are not in an up cycle. We are not in an up cycle.

541301|2026-06.headline: Orient Electric Q1 FY27 revenue grew 23.5% YoY with PAT up 79.7% to INR31.5 crores, though gross margin fell to 29.8% on commodity inflation.
541301|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 saw a strong summer-led demand recovery from mid-April, with revenue up 23.5% YoY and ECD revenue up 22.7% to INR669 crores. Gross margin moderated to 29.8% under commodity and labour cost pressure, but EBITDA margin rose 102 bps YoY to 7% as fixed-cost discipline and Project Sanchay savings (INR10 crores) offset the pressure. Management took multiple calibrated price increases across categories, with fans cited at around 15-16% cumulative since December. Management declined to give margin guidance, reiterating only an aspiration of 32-34% gross margin and continued path to double-digit EBITDA margin.

segments.name: ECD (Fans, Appliances)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR669 crores, up 22.7% YoY, with high double-digit fan growth and double-digit appliance growth. BLDC grew 36% YoY and new products were 30% of fan revenue; premium mix reached 36% of domestic fan revenue.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Consumer (B2C) lighting grew high double digits; B2B/C-Loom grew high single digits, with tender business deliberately reduced. Lighting margin declined 40 bps YoY due to a 2-3 week lag in passing on commodity costs. High-value looms share rose to 60%, up 500 bps.

segments.name: Switchgear and Switches
segments.commentary: Both grew at double-digit rates. Management is launching a higher-value MCB subcategory in Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Wires
segments.commentary: Grew more than 200% YoY from a small base. Currently house wires only, sold mainly in North and East markets, with cross-sell through the fan dealer network (about 45% of large fan dealers also sell wires).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Grew double digits, led by Africa and SAARC; Middle East was impacted. Hyderabad plant certifications completed over the last 2-3 quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to a 32-34% gross margin, but declined to guide given volatile inflation.
Management is committed to a path to double-digit EBITDA margin; timing depends on inflation. EBITDA margin trend: 5.3% (3 years ago), 6.6%, 6.9%, 8.2% in Q4, 7% in Q1 FY27.
Further Sanchay accruals expected in Q2 FY27 after INR10 crores in Q1.
Long-term aim of a healthy double-digit revenue CAGR; first milestone of INR5,000 crores revenue, with a prior 14-15% CAGR framework.
Marketing spend held at 4.4-4.5% of revenue (5.5% last year on the old basis, per management's comparison).
Management expects employee cost to stay range-bound as a percentage of sales, with automation helping over the long term but not in Q2.
capex_capacity: Ongoing automation of plants and processes to reduce labour cost dependence; benefits expected over the long term rather than in Q2.
Hyderabad plant is a core export base; international certifications completed.
Continued capex on new products, maintenance and capacity enhancement, described as spent as required rather than cut.
New product launches: Aero O2 (oxygen-enriching ceiling fan), Aerosilent (under 50 dB), Ecotech Volt; 3 Red Dot Design awards won.
demand_pricing: Demand: cooling net demand revived from mid-April and stayed robust through May, moderating toward quarter end. Management said Q1 was a balanced sell-in and sell-out quarter with no inventory build-up.

Pricing: fans had 6 price increases from December to June, cumulatively about 15-16%, with about 10% sequential QoQ in fans. Appliances had about 4 increases (high single to double digit). Lighting rose about 10% over 5-6 months. Switchgear rose high double digit. Wires are priced with a 15-day lag to LME.
Competition: management said most leading brands did not take a June price increase, while start-up brands took about half of Orient's increase. Orient says it has priced slightly ahead of peers.
DTM network added about 3,600 retailers in the quarter. E-commerce grew double digits.
Management said Chinese TPW fans are more price-competitive than Indian products; Europe entry is targeted before the next season.

qa_highlights.question: How much of ECD growth came from price increases, and how much more pricing is needed to offset raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was volume plus value across categories, with fans taking about 6 increases from December to June (about 10% sequential in Q1). It said further price action will be calibrated to commodity moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is there trade inventory build-up in Q1, and how do DTM and non-DTM markets compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no inventory build-up and the quarter was secondary-led. Both DTM and MD markets grew healthy double digits with volume growth, and no split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross margin recover in Q2 and what margin range is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 32-34% gross margin aspiration but gave no guidance. It said some commodity prices reversed in recent days, Sanchay accruals will continue, and it will act calibrated to inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall YoY, and was ad spend cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said marketing spend was flat in value YoY, with a shift from IPL to digital and premium media. Marketing was 4.5% of sales versus 5.5% last year and is planned at 4.4-4.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs keep rising, and is operating leverage exhausted?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost rose 10.7% YoY because of minimum wage increases, but fell to 8.9% of sales from 9.9% a year ago. Management expects it to stay range-bound as a share of sales, with automation as the lever.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lighting margin decline and B2B performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the 40 bps lighting margin decline to a 2-3 week lag in passing on commodity increases. B2C grew high double digits, B2B C-Loom grew high single digits, and tender business was cut deliberately.

risks_watch: Commodity volatility (copper, aluminium, LME-linked wires) and pass-through lag, which compressed gross margin to 29.8%.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage increases, with employee cost up 10.7% YoY.
Price-led growth may be tested if the industry does not follow Orient's price increases; start-up brands priced below it.
Quarter-end demand moderation and festive-season sentiment; channel inventory normalisation.
Wires scale-up and the switchgear/switch product pipeline, including the higher-value MCB launch in Q2.

Management was defensive when asked about the margin outlook and the post-war commodity cycle, which it said is still ongoing.

541301|2026-09.headline: Orient Electric Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25.2% YoY to INR879 crores and PAT more than doubled to INR27 crores, but gross margin fell to 29% on inflation.
541301|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 25.2% YoY to INR879 crores in Q2 FY27, with H1 revenue at INR1,829 crores (+24.3%). EBITDA rose 49.7% YoY to INR57 crores, with margin up 106 bps to 6.5%, helped by Project Sanchay savings of about INR13 crores in the quarter. Gross margin was 29% in Q2 (29.4% in H1) as copper, aluminium, steel, plastics and crude-linked inputs kept rising faster than price increases. Management said gross margin should recover only as inflation slows, and it held a long-run gross margin guidance of about 32% and a double-digit EBITDA margin aspiration.

segments.name: Electrical Consumer Durables (ECD)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR550 crores, +24.9% YoY. Fans grew high double digits and gained share; BLDC grew about 26% YoY and is about 30% of ceiling fan mix; premium fans about 40% of fan mix. Appliances grew double digits led by water heaters and garment care.

Revenue CAGR guidance raised to more than 15% (previously 15%-plus), with H1 growth at 24.3%.
Working capital expected to fall back to about 20 days over the next four to six quarters via channel financing programs.
Project Sanchay expected to exceed last year's full-year savings of about INR70 crores in H2 FY27 as accruals rise.
Hyderabad plant utilisation expected to rise in Q3-Q4 for next-season production; steady-state margin benefit of about 20-30 bps.

Hyderabad to start producing models that sell well in South to cut logistics and warehousing costs.

Working capital at 34 days, with cash discipline prioritised alongside portfolio investment and distribution expansion.
demand_pricing: Price increases: fans about 9% in Q1, about 3% in Q2 and about 3% in October; appliances about 6% in Q1 and about 3% in Q2; lighting 6-7% in Q1, about 6% in Q2 and about 2% in October; switchgear 7-8% in Q1 and 6% in Q2; wires raised every 2-3 weeks as a fast follower.
Price increases recovered about 80% of inflation in fans, about 90% in appliances, nearly 100% in wires and 80-100% in other categories, per management.

Quick commerce about 15% of digital revenue, growing about 100% YoY; e-commerce grew high double digits.

BLDC ASP index about 1.11 vs industry average of 1, up from 1.04 over six quarters.
B2B is double digit overall; about 25% of lighting business is B2B; B2B growth has been slower than B2C.
Gross margin decline of about 250 bps over two quarters attributed by management to input inflation rather than under-pricing; mix changes in house wires and switchgear also cited.

qa_highlights.question: Did price hikes cause inventory up-stocking in September, and is there any one-off in growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price hikes since April have not led to abnormal primary up-stocking; Q2 season buying was split between September and October, with no one-off effect.

qa_highlights.question: How big is BLDC as a share of sales and what are the plans to grow it?
qa_highlights.answer: BLDC grew about 26% YoY, consistently for 8 quarters, and is about 30% of ceiling fan mix versus about 17-18% for the industry excluding large BLDC players.

qa_highlights.question: What is R&D spend and how is new product success measured?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is about 0.8-0.9% of turnover; NPDs are about 30% of fan revenue with a 90%-plus commercialisation success rate, tracked by reach, repeats and third-party market share.

qa_highlights.question: When can operating margin reach double digits, and why is working capital at 34 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to get much closer to double digits in H2 onwards, within four to six quarters, if inflation eases. Receivable days rose due to DTM and new segments; channel financing should bring working capital back to about 20 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the growth and pricing trajectory move FY27 growth towards a 15%-plus CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 growth was 24.3%; management guided to more than 15% CAGR, which is slightly more aggressive than the earlier guidance, with volume growth expected to rise as a share of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall about 250 bps over two quarters despite price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflation has outpaced price increases, pricing has been passed on ahead of peers, and BLDC ASP indexing improved to 1.11; mix changes in house wires and switchgear also contributed.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery to about 32% depends on inflation easing; copper touches new highs about every two weeks and steel moved from about 65 to above 80.

Working capital at 34 days versus target of about 20 days; receivables rising with DTM expansion.
Wires expansion is limited to North, East and parts of South; pan-India launch not yet done.
Project Sanchay savings need to step up in H2 to beat FY26 full-year level of about INR70 crores.
Hyderabad plant utilisation at about 40% on single shift.

qa_highlights.question: Relevance of conventional platforms versus autonomous vessels, and GRSE's strategy in autonomy.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the revenue in the 31 March provisional figure materially different from the final reported number?

qa_highlights.question: Why is NGC delayed, and when will it be signed? Will there be one or two winners on smaller projects?

qa_highlights.question: When will NGC revenue start and how will revenue and EBITDA margins look for FY27-FY29?

qa_highlights.question: What is the NGC vendor ecosystem and electronics content?

qa_highlights.question: Can the company take large European commercial orders and target higher margins?

qa_highlights.question: How are commodity cost increases handled?

542011|2026-06.headline: GRSE Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 39% YoY to ₹1,815 crore and PAT 44% to ₹173 crore; order book ₹13,596 crore.
542011|2026-06.overview: Management reported total income of ₹1,914 crore (+38% YoY), revenue from operations of ₹1,815 crore (+39%), and PAT of ₹173 crore (+44%) with EPS of ₹15.09 versus ₹10.49. The company said this was its 17th consecutive quarter of upward trend in financials. Order book stands at ₹13,596 crore across 11 projects and 44 marine platforms, and the Next Generation Corvette (NGC) contract is still awaited with management guiding signing within the quarter. Capacity expansion (brownfield and greenfield, roughly ₹4,200 crore combined capex) was the main strategic update, alongside Navratna status granted on 19 June 2026.

financial_highlights.change: First time below ₹15,000 crore in 10 years, per management

Management called it sinusoidal, tied to delivery phase

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Next Generation Corvette contract been delayed, and when would revenue recognition start if signed today?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the contract slipped from FY26-end/Q1 and is now expected to be signed this quarter, with no red flags seen. Revenue recognition would begin in FY28 after a pre-production design and equipment-ordering phase; the eight-ship project completes around 2034-35.

qa_highlights.question: Does GRSE have capability for unmanned and autonomous naval vessels, and does the expansion plan address it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has capability, citing an unmanned surface vessel prototype, a project for NSTL (DRDO) and an autonomous underwater platform prototype tested about a year ago. It is taking part in Navy-steered autonomy projects and was shortlisted for another underwater unmanned platform.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex quantum for greenfield and brownfield expansion, and what capability will it add?

Raichak greenfield yard in West Bengal is about ₹2,200 crore with 3-5 years to operationalise; the Gujarat-side total ship solution facility is about ₹2,000 crore with about 3 years to operationalise. qa_highlights.question: How will GRSE participate in large commercial tenders (MR tankers, VLGC, Aframax, container ships) given capacity limits?

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 execution momentum be sustained, or will growth slow from the ~35-40% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current quarter's performance can be replicated, pointing to about ₹4,500 crore left on P-17 Alpha and about ₹1,816 crore on anti-submarine craft. It noted FY26 delivered eight ships and that the next quarter should see deliveries and higher contract workforce costs.

Bailey Bridge is 100%, deck machinery about 90%, and the diesel engine co-production targets 55-60%.

qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses fell because Q4 FY26 included commissioning costs for three ships that did not recur. Management expects the next pay commission to add 15-20% to employee costs, in line with past commissions.

542066|2026-06.headline: ATGL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR1,908 crore and EBITDA was INR281 crore, while gas volumes grew 13% to 303 MMSCM amid margin pressure from spot gas.
542066|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 gas sales of 303 MMSCM (up 13% YoY), with CNG up 18% and PNG up 4%, and revenue of INR1,908 crore (up 27% YoY) with EBITDA of INR281 crore. West Asia tensions pushed Brent-linked RLNG and NWG prices higher, and the government withdrew the pooled gas mechanism after a peace deal, forcing ATGL to buy spot gas (around 15% of consumption after curtailment). Management acknowledged that operating margins have compressed over six to eight quarters, which it attributed mainly to market-driven gas prices and declining APM allocation. Management expects margins to recover once Middle East supply normalises, but gave no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why have operating margins compressed from about 25% to 15% over six to eight quarters, and when will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited market-driven gas prices and the declining APM allocation as the main causes. Management expects margins to recover once Middle East supply returns, with US and Qatar supply expected to lower rates, but gave no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gas sourcing mix and why did gas cost rise by about INR5/SCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic volumes are about 62% and imported RLNG about 38%. Higher Brent prices lifted NWG and RLNG costs. Management said NWG is 12% of the Indian crude basket and was above $5/MMBTU in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How much gas is bought on the spot market and when will it reduce?
qa_highlights.answer: Spot volumes are around 15% of total consumption after curtailment. Management said curtailed volumes should return over time, but it could not predict the timing given the Middle East situation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the government likely to restart the pooled gas mechanism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry representations are ongoing and it expects some positive news if Middle East tensions persist. The mechanism is expected to return in a similar form as fertiliser demand falls after sowing.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any difficulties in adding customers, and is manpower a constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no major issues, though permissions in some areas and monsoon rains slow work. Manpower is being addressed through training, ITI and diploma tie-ups; deemed approvals are helping, with 90-99% of authorities cooperating.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue guidance is available for coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no revenue guidance. It said volume growth will continue at a similar pace, with the main challenge being to fill the gap created by spot volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Net fibre price risk and why EPC revenue fell?

542867|2026-09.overview: CSB Bank reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs.183 Cr, up 22% QoQ and 14% YoY, with net interest income of Rs.510 Cr (up 7% QoQ, 20% YoY). NIM widened to 3.81% from 3.66% in Q1, driven by a higher yield on advances (10.92%) and stable cost of funds. Fee income rebounded 20% QoQ, though overall fee income was down about 22% YoY due to market-linked non-core lines. Asset quality improved on GNPA (1.58%) and NNPA (0.33%), with credit cost at 24 bps, though elevated write-offs of fully provided card and unsecured book were flagged. Management said it is entering a "scale phase" with retail liability build-out, SME growth restarting, and guidance of ROA 1.5% to 1.8% next year.

543259|2026-06.headline: Home First Q1 FY27: AUM up 25.7% YoY to INR16,938 crore and PAT up 34.5% YoY to INR160 crore, with stable asset quality.

Profit after tax rose 34.5% YoY to INR160 crore, driven by 38.2% growth in net interest income and NIM expanding to 6.0% from 5.9%. Asset quality was flat across 1+ DPD (4.7%), 30+ DPD (3.2%) and GS3 (1.8%), and management said Q1 collections were better than usual. CFO Nutan Patwari will step down from executive responsibilities effective August 31, 2026, and the Board is evaluating candidates for the role.

543260|2026-03.headline: Stove Kraft Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 32.4% YoY to INR414.5 crore, with PAT of INR6.1 crore and EBITDA margin of 9.5%.
543260|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 32.4% YoY to INR414.5 crore, driven by induction cooktops (15.5% of revenue, value up 89.4% YoY) and small appliances. Gross margin held at 38.6%, flat YoY, while EBITDA rose 33.9% to INR39.5 crore at a 9.5% margin. FY26 revenue grew 10.9% to INR1,607.4 crore and EBITDA margin was 10.3%, below the roughly 11% management says it aims to protect. Management guided to upwards of 15% revenue growth in FY27, citing small appliances, export recovery and IKEA billing from Q1 FY27.

demand_pricing: Management cited surging induction cooktop demand after the Iran war and geopolitical supply disruptions, and said demand is shifting from an emergency option to a daily-use appliance.

Interest rose on supplier credit and sale-and-leaseback, while borrowing costs fell. Management said freight, warranty, business promotion and sales commission grew in line with revenue; sales commission rose about INR10 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA margin expected to rise above 11%?

qa_highlights.question: How much capacity and capex is needed to double induction production?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is about 2 million units now and run-rate is 4-5 million. Added capex is small (assembly and testing lines). FY27 capex is about INR40 crore including retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivables are largely channel-financed (most collected within 15 days), payables are on an invoice platform (paid in 90 days versus 45-day MSME terms), and it is confident of staying in the 24-30 day range. Aluminium and steel stock was built ahead of price rises.

qa_highlights.question: Are new stores accretive, and what is the same-store growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Average sales per store rose to INR4.7 lakh from INR3.8 lakh. Management said Q4 same-store growth was 25-30% for mature stores. Franchisee economics: INR2 lakh fixed fee plus 15-30% store margin; inventory stays on company books, funded by franchisee deposits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IKEA revenue ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Three product lines are awarded. Revenue begins Q1 FY27, with about INR40-50 crore before FY27 year-end and INR200-250 crore at full utilisation of all three lines.

Q4 other expenses at about INR62 crore, up sharply with sales commission and freight; the call gave no quantification of the margin impact of retail mix.
Sustainability of the induction demand surge; the pipeline refill by peers could affect growth.
Import dependence on glass (33-40% of import content), PCBs and magnets for induction cooktops, with no domestic glass capacity.
Export recovery is gradual, and price increases were only agreed from 1 June.
Capex and cash flow disclosure: management said figures would be shared offline, and the net-of-supplier-credit figures were not fully reconciled on the call.
CFO transition: Subhadeep Pal takes over as CFO from 16 May 2026.

543260|2026-06.headline: Stove Kraft Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 41.3% YoY to INR480.6 crore, with EBITDA up 50.9% to INR53.8 crore and margin at 11.2%.

Working capital rose to 45 days on festive inventory build-up, and management guided to Q2 growth despite a high base.

segments.name: Non-stick cookware

segments.name: Small appliances and gas cooktops

Non-induction categories targeted to grow about 15%+ consistently, with a stated aim near 20%; overall growth targeted at 15-20%.

demand_pricing: Induction cooktop demand remains above pre-war levels; management expects traction to continue but not at the initial spike levels.

Q1 exchange-offer programme (mainly in EBOs and general trade) cited as a regular seasonal driver; GPOs up about 80% and general trade up about 50%.
Festive calendar spread across Q2 and Q3 (Onam in August, Dussehra in early October, Diwali in November).
South region about 50% of general trade contribution; North and West growing faster from a smaller base.

qa_highlights.question: How should growth look for Q2 and Q3 FY27, given festive timing and LPG-related demand anxiety?

qa_highlights.question: Will margin improvement be sustainable, and are further price hikes still needed?

qa_highlights.question: How is the export business trending, and what is the outlook for exports plus IKEA?

qa_highlights.question: What is the induction cooktop run rate versus pre-war levels, and how much of FY27 revenue can it be?

543332|2026-06.headline: Epigral Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR709 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 25% from 27% amid West Asia cost pressures.
543332|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 15% YoY to INR709 crore on higher volumes and realisations, while EBITDA rose 10% to INR179 crore and margin eased to 25% from 27%. Adjusted PAT grew 25% to INR99 crore against INR79 crore a year earlier, though the prior-year reported PAT of INR160 crore included an INR81 crore deferred tax credit. ROCE fell to 16% (18% excluding capital work in progress) and net debt/EBITDA rose to 0.8x. Management announced a Board-approved INR600 crore plan for an epoxy resin and formulations plant (125,000 tpa) and a multipurpose plant (MPP).

financial_highlights.change: +15% YoY vs INR615 crore in Q1 FY26
+25% vs adjusted PAT of INR79 crore in Q1 FY26; Q1 FY26 reported PAT INR160 crore incl. INR81 crore deferred tax
vs 24% as on 30 June 2025; 18% excluding capital work in progress
vs INR439 crore as on 30 June 2025

financial_highlights.value: INR35,000-36,000/t in Q1 FY27 (about INR31,000-32,000 currently)

segments.name: Chlor-alkali (caustic soda/ECU)
segments.commentary: Caustic soda capacity utilisation about 75% in Q1 FY27. ECU realisation about INR35,000-36,000 in Q1, easing to about INR31,000-32,000 currently; chlorine realisation about negative INR4,000.

segments.name: Epichlorohydrin (ECH)
segments.commentary: ECH utilisation about 70-75% in Q1. Current ECH realisation about INR180-185/t, down from INR200-210 during the war-time peak. Capacity expansion from 50,000 to 100,000 tpa is progressing on time and within budget, with commissioning expected in a couple of months.

segments.name: CPVC
segments.commentary: CPVC utilisation about 50-55% in Q1 as pipe customers managed PVC inventory amid volatility. Realisation about INR110-115/kg currently. Management expects demand to pick up from Q3 with monsoon seasonality; a 75,000 tpa expansion is underway.

segments.name: Chlorotoluenes / chloromethanes / peroxide
segments.commentary: Chloromethanes running about 100%; hydrogen peroxide about 85-90%. Chlorotoluenes capex of about INR250 crore done; expected revenue INR300-350 crore at optimum level, with the combined chlorotoluene and MPP top line targeted at INR700-800 crore.

guidance_outlook: Long-term growth target of 15-20% CAGR over 3-5 years in top line and bottom line, with an internal aspiration of about 20%.
Epoxy and MPP projects together: peak revenue of INR1,300-1,500 crore once plants reach optimum levels; ROCE target about 20%, with margins lower than the existing 22-24% range.
Capex of about INR400 crore each in FY27 and FY28; the INR600 crore epoxy and MPP project funded about 40% internally and 60% debt.
Pilot facility for epoxy and MPP expected to be operational by September 2026 (Q2 FY27); MPP completion targeted in FY28.
Chlorotoluene and MPP derivatives target of INR500 crore revenue within about three years, with ramp-up likely in FY29-FY30.
Tax rate expected at about 25%.
capex_capacity: Epoxy resin and formulations: 125,000 tpa, with more than 50% of raw material value sourced internally (ECH and caustic soda). Management said LER will be a smaller share of the mix.

Multipurpose plant (MPP) for chlorotoluene and ECH downstream derivatives (pharma/agrochemical intermediates, water treatment chemicals); the combined epoxy and MPP project is INR600 crore, with no split given.
ECH capacity doubling from 50,000 to 100,000 tpa; post-expansion, about 50% of ECH is to be consumed in-house and 50% sold.
CPVC expansion of 75,000 tpa underway, progressing on schedule and within budget.
Power: no further captive power plant; energy to come from long-term solar and wind hybrid contracts (two 20 MW contracts).
demand_pricing: Epoxy demand estimated at 2.5-3 lakh tonnes, expected to grow at double-digit rates; management expects export opportunities to Europe after an India-EU FTA.
Caustic: management expects India to remain a net importer given alumina capacity growth; short-term oversupply risk for a couple of years.

CPVC: management said near-term overcapacity is likely as Grasim and others add capacity; pricing of CPVC is about INR110-115/kg and ethylene-based PVC pricing is not expected to be materially affected by the recent MIP.
Glycerin/ECH: management said glycerin prices are driven by palm oil and biodiesel policy as well as crude and propylene, and that ECH prices are volatile.
Management said the 2.5-3 lakh tonne epoxy demand is growing at double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Is the epoxy capacity announcement mainly LER or does it include value-added products, and what is the market size split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 125,000 tpa capacity includes LER plus value-added and formulations, with LER a smaller share of the mix. Epoxy demand is estimated at 2.5-3 lakh tonnes, growing at double-digit rates, with Europe seen as an export opportunity after an India-EU FTA.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q1 FY27 and Q4 FY26 ECU realisations and utilisation levels?
qa_highlights.answer: ECU was about INR35,000-36,000/t in Q1 FY27 and about INR30,000 in Q4 FY26, easing to about INR31,000-32,000 currently. Utilisation was about 75% for caustic soda, 70-75% for ECH, 50-55% for CPVC, about 100% for chloromethanes and 85-90% for peroxide.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of the INR600 crore capex between epoxy and MPP, and peak revenue from both projects?
qa_highlights.answer: No split was given; the INR600 crore is a combined figure. Peak revenue from both projects together is expected at INR1,300-1,500 crore once plants reach optimum levels, with ROCE targeted around 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the epoxy margin dilution change the 22-24% combined margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said epoxy margins will be lower in percentage terms because turnover per unit of investment is about 3-4x that of the existing portfolio. Project evaluation focuses on ROCE, which epoxy still meets.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR600 crore project mean peak total revenue of INR4,000-4,500 crore, given current revenue of about INR2,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rejected that reading. It said existing capacity can still ramp up and the ECH and CPVC expansions are due in a couple of months, and that epoxy and MPP together add INR1,300-1,500 crore at peak.

qa_highlights.question: What growth rate should be expected and is the target on top line or bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15-20% CAGR over 3-5 years, with an internal aspiration of about 20%, for both top line and bottom line.

qa_highlights.question: How do the CPVC and PVC pricing respond to the recent MIP, and what is the outlook for CPVC demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MIP mainly hit carbide-based PVC, not the ethylene-based PVC Epigral uses, so no major impact is expected. CPVC realisation is about INR110-115/kg. Demand is expected to pick up from Q3 with monsoon seasonality, though near-term overcapacity is likely as new capacity comes on.

qa_highlights.question: What are the chlorotoluenes and MPP capex, revenue and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Chlorotoluenes capex of about INR250 crore is done, with expected revenue of INR300-350 crore at optimum. Including MPP, the combined top line is targeted at INR700-800 crore, at an estimated margin of about 22-23%, with 1.5-2 years to optimum utilisation.

risks_watch: Epoxy and MPP margins will be lower than the 22-24% range, with ROCE of about 20% the stated offset; the margin trajectory of the combined business is not guided numerically.
CPVC overcapacity as Grasim and others add capacity, with utilisation at 50-55% in Q1 FY27 and a demand recovery expected only from Q3.
Caustic oversupply risk for a couple of years from domestic capacity additions, with utilisation at about 75% and ECU easing from INR35,000-36,000 to INR31,000-32,000/t.
ECH realisation fell from INR200-210/kg at the war-time peak to about INR180-185/t currently; ECH and glycerin prices are volatile, linked to crude, propylene and biodiesel policy.
Execution: the pilot facility is due by September 2026, ECH capacity doubling to 100,000 tpa and the 75,000 tpa CPVC expansion are due in a couple of months, and the MPP is targeted for FY28.
Leverage and returns: net debt/EBITDA rose to 0.8x from 0.6x, ROCE fell to 16% from 24%, and the INR600 crore project is 60% debt-funded.
Capex of about INR400 crore each in FY27 and FY28 keeps balance-sheet strain and the ROCE trajectory in focus.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 FY27 presented a highly challenging operating environment across all the segments, including chemicals.
Even against this volatile backdrop Epigral demonstrated a resilience, delivering a revenue growth of 15% and EBITDA margin of 25%.
So definitely, EBITDA margin in terms of percentage, definitely, it is coming lower.
Rather than giving guidance on margin, I can tell you that ROCE, we are targeting in the range of 20%.
543332|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term growth, expansion execution and the epoxy and MPP projects, but cautious and at times evasive on near-term pricing and margins. It declined to give a breakup of the INR600 crore capex or a numeric margin guide for the new projects, and said near-term PVC, ECH and caustic prices are too volatile to forecast.

543334|2026-06.headline: Nuvoco Q1 FY27: volume up 5% YoY to 5.3 mt and EBITDA up 7% to INR572 crore, highest-ever Q1 for both.
543334|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 volume rose 5% YoY to 5.3 million tons and EBITDA rose 7% YoY to INR572 crore, the company's highest-ever first-quarter volume and EBITDA. Realisation rose about INR320 per ton QoQ, largely offset by about INR230 per ton of cost inflation (power and fuel, raw material, packing bags, freight, fixed-cost deleverage), leaving a net EBITDA gain of about INR90 per ton. Management said the Surat grinding unit (2 mtpa) was inaugurated on 11 July 2026, ahead of schedule, and Kutch clinker and grinding remain on track for phased start from Q3 FY27. Management guided Q2 cost increase of about INR100 per ton, with power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton and packing and freight easing.

financial_highlights.change: Cost inflation about INR230 per ton; net EBITDA impact about INR90 per ton

Fuel cost expected to stay broadly flat in Q2 (1.52 could move to 1.55); petcoke inventory adequate for the quarter at similar cost; Q3 may carry higher-cost inventory.
FY27 volume growth target of about 7-8%, in line with market demand expectations of 7-8% over the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of East debottlenecking (CTOs for Jojobera, Panagarh, Jajpur, Arasmeta)?
qa_highlights.answer: Jojobera and Panagarh CTOs almost done; Jajpur awaits NIPL certificate; Arasmeta technical design done and ball mill procurement underway. All four to be ready by end FY27 and needed for FY28; no delay per management.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 realisation gain was price versus trade mix and geo-mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Three drivers: price increases (biggest), premium mix with Concreto, Duraguard Microfiber and Uno (about 5 mt premium and super-premium), and geo-mix shift toward high-realisation states (Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Western MP). Trade mix unchanged at 75%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost outlook for Q2 and fuel and packing trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Total cost up about INR100 per ton QoQ (plus or minus INR20-30). Petcoke inventory covers Q2 at similar cost; packing bags to ease INR20-25 per ton; rake availability improving to about 4 per day; power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton from shutdowns.

qa_highlights.question: Will Gujarat (Surat and Kutch) EBITDA per ton converge with the company average, and how fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Year 1 EBITDA per ton will be lower due to high costs and aggressive volume push, with no dilution of price intended; modelling shows Gujarat EBITDA per ton equal to rest-of-North in years 2-3. Kutch, Sachana and Surat form a hub-and-spoke network.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any change to FY27 capex and what is the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex unchanged at INR900 crore with about INR370 crore spent in Q1; FY28 capex INR950-1,000 crore including Vadraj, Sachana terminal and routine spend.

Gujarat ramp: Year-1 EBITDA per ton below company average; pricing discipline under aggressive volume push.
Kutch and Surat timelines: Kutch clinker start earliest around January 2027; Kutch grinding civil works to finish Q2 FY27; Sachana terminal Q2 FY28.

Premium share fell from 44% to 42% QoQ; watch whether it recovers.
543334|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on execution and cost control, with Surat inaugurated early and Q2 cost outlook given specific numbers; cautious on geopolitics and fuel. 543334|2026-09.headline: Nuvoco Q2 FY27: volume up 9% YoY and revenue up ~14%, but energy cost rose ~INR90/ton QoQ; Q3 fuel guided to INR1.8/mn kcal from INR1.59.
543334|2026-09.overview: Management described a challenging quarter driven by a renewed Middle East escalation, petcoke and domestic coal price spikes, and monsoon disruption in the East. Volume grew 9% YoY, revenue about 14% and EBITDA about 11%, supported by premiumization at a record 45% and trade mix of 75%. Fuel cost rose from INR1.52 to INR1.59 per million kcal in Q2, and management guided Q3 to INR1.8 with about INR100-120/ton net cost inflation QoQ, offset by an October price hike of about INR20/ton. Vadraj's Surat grinding unit (2 MTPA) was commissioned in late September, and net debt rose above INR5,000 crore on working capital and capex, with a guided return to 2-2.5x net debt/EBITDA in the next 4-6 quarters.

segments.name: Gujarat (Vadraj / Surat & Kutch)
segments.commentary: Surat 2 MTPA grinding unit commissioned in late September; running at ~1.5 MTPA annualised, targeting 2 MTPA in Q4 FY27 with 50-60% utilisation in Q4 and 70-75% in FY28. Kutch clinker line expected in Q4 FY27, with jetty operational by first week of December.

segments.commentary: Strong volume growth in Q2 per management. Around 1 million tons of cement capacity to be released from Rajasthan from Q4 for North sales, as Surat supplies Gujarat.

segments.name: East
segments.commentary: Erratic monsoon weighed on demand in Q2; East expansion deferred from Q3-Q4 FY27 to Q1-Q2 FY28. Price hike of about INR20/ton in trade and non-trade taken in October.

Q3 FY27 net cost inflation guided at INR100-120/ton QoQ (energy ~INR70-80, packing bags ~INR20, busy-season surcharge waiver ~INR10), offset by ~INR20/ton price increase taken in October.
Industry demand expected at ~8% growth in H2 FY27; company guides 8-9% blended volume growth across North, West and East.
FY27 capex ~INR1,200 crore (INR780 crore spent in H1, ~INR420 crore in H2); FY28 capex INR800-900 crore.
Net debt expected to return to around March 2026 levels by end FY27; 2-2.5x net debt/EBITDA in the next 4-6 quarters, and below 2x once Vadraj volumes scale.
Surat incremental costs of ~INR30-40 crore expected in Q3 (interest and depreciation), partly above and below EBITDA.
Vadraj/Gujarat EBITDA per ton expected to match Nuvoco's all-India EBITDA per ton around FY29 (possibly FY28 Q4 to Q1 FY29).
Company targets 35 MTPA cement capacity by FY28.
capex_capacity: Surat (Vadraj) 2 MTPA grinding unit at Limla, Surat commissioned late September 2026; ~3,500-3,600 tons/day peak output against ~5,500 tons/day capacity.

Viramgam (Sachana) bulk cement terminal with railway siding under construction; INR50 crore spend planned in H2 FY27.
East debottlenecking delayed from Q3-Q4 FY27 to Q1-Q2 FY28 to prioritise Vadraj cash flow and management bandwidth.
CleanMax agreement for 46.4 MW wind-solar hybrid project in Rajasthan, expected ~100 million units/year.
demand_pricing: Industry demand grew in Q2 but varied regionally; monsoon disrupted the East while low-rainfall regions performed better. Prices did not improve as expected in Q2.

Price action: non-trade up ~INR20-25/ton in North after 15 September, trade cut INR5-7/ton in North in late September, then ~INR20/ton increases in non-trade (North and East) and trade (East) in October.
Premium product mix at 45%; Duraguard Microfiber and Concreto Uno each crossed 1 million ton volumes, with Concreto Uno reaching it in under 18 months.
Management expects post-Diwali demand pickup and believes price increases will hold through the balance of the year.
Management sees 5% demand impact only if back-to-back adverse monsoon or drought years occur; assumes this does not happen in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What was average fuel cost in Q2 and what is the spot impact at petcoke near $187?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel cost rose from INR1.52 to INR1.59 per million kcal (energy ~INR1,080/ton vs INR1,005 in Q1). Q3 is guided at INR1.8, adding ~INR70-80/ton, with petcoke covered for Q3 and Q4 through mid-February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the overall Q3 vs Q2 cost outlook and how will it be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Net cost inflation of INR100-120/ton: energy +INR70-80, packing +INR20, raw materials ~+INR10, offset by ~INR20/ton price increase plus fixed-cost leverage from higher volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What is Surat's utilisation and run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Running at ~1.5 MTPA annualised; target 2 MTPA in Q4 FY27 with 50-60% utilisation in Q4 and 70-75% in FY28, as Kutch grinding is not available in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex ~INR1,200 crore (INR780 crore in H1, ~INR420 crore in H2, of which INR1,000 crore for Vadraj); FY28 INR800-900 crore. East expansion delayed 6-8 months to FY28 H1.

qa_highlights.question: How will net debt evolve and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt crossed INR5,000 crore (INR200 crore working capital build plus capex). Expected to return to March 2026 levels by end FY27, and to hover at 2-2.5x EBITDA over 4-6 quarters, with the long-term target below 2x.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest expense fall and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing costs for Surat were capitalised until commercial operations started in late September; interest and depreciation will rise QoQ from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 reported tax rate 41.6% because MAT credit is unavailable under the old regime; the company will decide on regime transition within 3-4 months and share the implications.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Vadraj EBITDA per ton outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Gujarat and Western Maharashtra EBITDA per ton expected to match Nuvoco's all-India level in year 3 (FY29, possibly FY28 Q4 to Q1 FY29), subject to cost inflation being offset by prices.

risks_watch: Petcoke prices near $190 with potential to exceed $200/ton; full impact of high-cost petcoke expected from March 2027 onwards.
Domestic coal auction premiums and rake shortages; linkage coal supply expected to ease from early November.
Price hikes must hold post-Diwali; any reversal would erode the expected Q3 benefit.
Surat clinker is currently sourced from Chhattisgarh and Chittor at high cost until Kutch clinker starts; the Q3 to Q4 margin dent was not quantified on the call.
Net debt at above INR5,000 crore vs the INR3,500-4,000 crore comfort range; deleveraging depends on H2 working capital release.
Tax regime transition decision pending; affects tax rate from FY28.
Geopolitical developments (Middle East) remain a watch item.

But since we could not convert it to revenue by whatever reasons or restrictions imposed by the government or by reasons beyond our control.
