543984|2026-03.headline: FY26 total income rose to INR 1,279 crore with 12.3% revenue growth; net debt/EBITDA ~3x (3.07x) and FY27 revenue guided at 10-11%.
543984|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue growth was 12.3% against a 9-11% guidance band, with same-store RevPAR up 9.5%, despite several one-off disruptions that cut revenue by an estimated INR 45-52 crore. Consolidated EBITDA rose 8.8% to INR 463 crore at a 36.2% margin, and the GST slab change weighed on H2 margins. Q4 EBITDA fell 6% YoY to about INR 120 crore, which management attributes to GST, FF&E charges, pre-opening costs and the Middle East conflict hitting March revenue. Net debt fell to INR 1,450 crore after the GIC infusion, and a deferred tax credit of about INR 330 crore lifted reported PAT to about INR 567 crore. Management guided FY27 same-store revenue growth of 9-10% and total revenue growth of 10-11%, and a 38%-plus group margin.

financial_highlights.change: -6% YoY; ~INR 149 crore adjusted for one-offs (+16.8% YoY)
Includes ~INR 330 crore deferred tax income in Q4 and ~INR 83 crore impairment reversal; includes gain on Caspia Delhi sale

financial_highlights.metric: Free cash flow FY26 (after interest and lease MG)

segments.name: Core markets (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune, Delhi NCR)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 76% of asset income in FY26. Delhi NCR same-store RevPAR declined about 9%; management expects mid-teens growth there in FY27 as Hyatt Place Gurgaon renovation completed by end-Q3 FY26.

segments.name: Upscale and upper-upscale portfolio
segments.commentary: Upscale hotels run at upwards of 42-43% margins; Holiday Inn Express margins at 41-42%. Incremental pipeline is weighted to upscale, limiting exposure to sub-INR 7,500 room rates.

segments.name: Asset recycling and non-core hotels
segments.commentary: Monetised 4 non-core hotels for INR 210 crore at about 20x EV/EBITDA over three years. Target now INR 200-250 crore over the next two years; Caspia Delhi was sold for INR 63 crore with EBITDA of about INR 1.5-2 crore.

segments.name: RARE India (experiential leisure)
segments.commentary: Acquired 70% stake in a curated platform of 73 hotels and about 1,000 rooms; under discussion for affiliation with Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 same-store revenue growth expected at 9-10%; total revenue growth underwritten at 10-11% with caution given the Middle East crisis, versus about 14% if no crisis.
Group EBITDA margin guided at about 38%, with 38%-plus maintained through the year; management says margins should reach 40%-plus on a normalised basis over time.
GST impact is permanent in absolute terms and has been about INR 7.5 crore YoY in Q3 and about INR 10 crore in Q4; normalises from Q3 FY27 on a YoY basis.
FY27 interest expense about INR 127 crore on existing debt; guided at INR 135-140 crore including a 15-20 bps rate-hardening assumption.
Net debt/EBITDA to stabilise at about 2.5x in 12-18 months; currently 3.07x.
FY27 capex INR 250-270 crore (about INR 150 crore for W Hyderabad, opening at end-FY27); FY28 similar run-rate, mainly Westin Bangalore. Total pipeline capex about INR 2,200 crore over five years.
capex_capacity: W Hyderabad (HITEC City) to open at end-FY27; expected to add about 6-7% revenue growth on a run-rate basis from FY28.
Pipeline openings: Tribute Bangalore Whitefield at end-FY28; Westin Bangalore Whitefield, Ingka Noida (162 rooms, variable lease) and Marriott Stiperumbudur (135 rooms, Chennai) in FY29-FY30.
Navi Mumbai 700-room Westin and Fairfield project announced; One Financial District Hyderabad (260 rooms) under development. Management excluded both from revenue and EBITDA forecasts.
GIC platform: INR 750 crore for a 35% stake in a 1,000-room upscale platform; INR 600 crore received, INR 150 crore balance over about two years linked to Westin Tribute Bangalore capex.
Over five years FY27-FY31, free cash of about INR 1,550 crore (flat base) plus about INR 1,000 crore from same-store growth; more than INR 3,000 crore cumulative after new openings, per management.
demand_pricing: QTD revenue growth (April-May 2026) is double-digit; April was flattish and May strong, against a weak May 2025 base affected by Operation Sindoor.

Q4 revenue growth ran about 12% through February before the Middle East conflict pulled March to below -1%; interrupted by the India-Pakistan conflict (May), August floods, December airline disruption and March Middle East conflict.
One-off disruptions cut FY26 revenue by INR 45-52 crore; management says underlying growth would have been 16-17%.
Management says inbound and long-haul travel is recovering (including US); repricing expected to restart as business rebalances. Occupancy described as strong.
Bangalore: about 17,000-18,000 rooms; supply growth about 5-5.5% CAGR, with more than half of future supply concentrated on the airport-Hebbal corridor where SAMHI has no presence.

Median flow-through about 55%, with 55%-plus expected; a Q4 margin drag came from a low-margin outdoor and corporate catering contract at Hyatt Regency Pune (about INR 13-14 crore), which management says ends from May 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How are April and May trending, and what is FY27 like-for-like growth after a favourable FY26 base?
qa_highlights.answer: QTD growth is double-digit: April flattish, May strong against a weak May 2025 base. Management expects YoY growth to stay in double digits through Q1 FY27 despite the Gulf crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Will GST be a permanent margin reduction, and what margins are expected in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: GST impact is permanent in absolute terms, but management expects about 38% group margin, 38%-plus through the year, as pipeline is upscale with few rooms below INR 7,500.

qa_highlights.question: Is there construction delay risk, and will the focus shift to acquisitions or asset recycling?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating and growth teams are separate. Acquisitions stay opportunistic, guided by discount-to-replacement-cost, mid-teens ROCE and no long-lead greenfield. Asset recycling will continue with a few more candidates identified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue growth outlook including new openings, and the interest cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Same-store growth of 9-10% plus about 3-4% incremental from renovated assets; total about 14% if no crisis. Guided at 10-11% for caution. Interest guided at INR 135-140 crore including rate hardening.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins not improve in Q4 and what is the GST drag and lease accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a low-margin catering contract (INR 13-14 crore revenue) that ends from May. GST drag is about INR 3 crore on a YoY basis per management's arithmetic. Variable lease payments (1.5-2% of revenue) go through P&L; lease-treatment impact on EBITDA margins is about 150-170 bps higher.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROCE target, net debt/EBITDA path and capex funding for FY31?
qa_highlights.answer: Current asset pool can deliver 14-15% ROCE. Net debt/EBITDA to stabilise around 2.5x in 12-18 months. Free cash base of about INR 310 crore assumed flat; management assumes no operating leverage and no EBITDA from Navi Mumbai or One Financial District; W Hyderabad and Ingka expected to add INR 400-500 crore EBITDA by FY31.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: March revenue fell below -1% YoY and the effect is still continuing into April; management says it may keep affecting Q1 FY27 absolute numbers.
GST slab change (12% with input credit to 5% without) is permanent; margin dilution persists and sub-INR 7,500 room sales could rise in crisis periods.
Interest-rate hardening: management has assumed 15-20 bps rise; currency weakness is cited as a risk.
Bangalore supply: heavy Outer Ring Road and airport-Hebbal supply could pressure occupancy, which management says has already taken a hit over recent quarters.
Execution risk on pipeline (W Hyderabad end-FY27, Tribute and Westin Bangalore, Navi Mumbai greenfield) and capex of about INR 2,200 crore over five years.
Capital allocation: a Board-level discussion on buybacks or shareholder returns is ongoing with no commitment; asset recycling could extend to minority dilution at asset level (not committed).
Deferred tax income of about INR 330 crore is non-cash; reported PAT is inflated by one-offs and is not a run-rate measure.
key_quotes: So we do expect a 55%-plus flow-through. 50% is underwhelming, 60% is where we arc happy.
We're running really strong capacity utilization across the group.
Notwithstanding the share price or the discount Viraj, we are under a fiduciary obligation to create sharcholder value and allocate capital
But I think the discipline will decide what we do in future.
So I think structurally, the company will secure its place at 40%-plus reported margins.
543984|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the long-term plan: management repeatedly underwrites 9-11% same-store revenue growth, 2.5x leverage and the INR 2,200 crore capex, and says upside exists. Cautious on the near term, citing the Middle East conflict, GST permanence and rate hardening, and it deflects on acquisitions, buybacks and asset-level minority dilution, which it treats as uncommitted.

543984|2026-06.headline: SAMHI Q1 FY27: same-store RevPAR up 9.6% to Rs 5,220 at 79.3% occupancy, while reported EBITDA fell 4% YoY on a one-time base and GST impact.
543984|2026-06.overview: Total income rose 7.3% YoY to Rs 308.3 crore reported, or 10.8% on a comparable basis after excluding Rs 9.3 crore one-time other income in the prior-year base. Same-store revenue grew about 9.1% and same-store RevPAR grew 9.6%, with occupancy up to 79.3% from 74.2%. Reported EBITDA fell about 4% YoY, which management attributes to a one-time Rs 9.2 crore GST impact and a prior-year one-time item; comparable EBITDA margin was about 12.1%. Management also sought a board enabling resolution for a Rs 750 crore capital raise, which drew heavy analyst questioning.

financial_highlights.change: +7.3% YoY reported; +10.8% comparable (ex Rs 9.3 crore one-time income in base)

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 100 crore (per analyst's math, not stated as a figure by management)
financial_highlights.change: down about 4% YoY reported; comparable margin about 12.1%

financial_highlights.value: about 3.2x TTM; about 2.4x for operating assets excluding growth capital

financial_highlights.change: about 300 bps lower than at IPO
unchanged since last upgrade in FY26

segments.name: Upper upscale portfolio
segments.commentary: Occupancy 78.4% in Q1 with RevPAR growth below mid-scale; management says the raw ARR growth was about 3.5%-4% across all segments.

segments.name: Mid-scale portfolio
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 13.7% with occupancy at 81.3%, outperforming the broader upscale portfolio in the quarter.

segments.name: RARE India (asset-light leisure)
segments.commentary: 75 hotels, 1,046 rooms across 15 states; management guides Rs 100-120 crore top line and Rs 35-40 crore EBITDA once stabilised in about 1.5-2 years, against about Rs 47 crore invested to date.

segments.name: F&B
segments.commentary: F&B revenue grew about 3.7-4% YoY against room revenue growth of about 14%, attributed to a shift to domestic guests, a Bangalore restaurant renovation and event cancellations moved into July-August.

guidance_outlook: Long-term same-store revenue growth expectation of 9%-11% reiterated; management says the same-store total revenue growth of about 9%-9.5% sits within this range.

Business plan targets revenue from about Rs 1,200 crore to about Rs 3,000 crore and cumulative free cash flow of over Rs 3,000 crore over FY27-FY31 (the call says Rs 2,000 crore once in error, corrected to Rs 3,000 crore).
Upscale share of revenue expected to rise from about 40%-41% today to about 60% by FY30.
Net debt/EBITDA of about 2.4x expected by FY28, not by end FY27 as an analyst assumed.
GST margin drag to be lower in H2 than H1; YoY GST impact of about Rs 9 crore to be removed from Q3 onward.
Early July trends described as ahead of Q1 exit, with growth split about evenly between rate and occupancy; management cautioned that one month is not representative.
capex_capacity: Seven new hotels in the committed pipeline total 1,660 rooms, mostly upper upscale and upscale; about 450 rooms are being rebranded from upper midscale to upscale.
W Hyderabad targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 (or calendar 2027); management flagged possible regulatory delays.
Courtyard Pune: back-office and MEP renovation under way; public area and guest room renovation deferred to about April 2027, taking 5-6 months.
Navi Mumbai (100% SAMHI-owned, outside the GIC JV): on-site start targeted for 1 April 2027, with a 3-4 year build; capex to stay small through FY28 and ramp in FY29-FY30.

Uttarakhand (Binsar, Almora) 8-acre estate Itmenaan acquisition for about Rs 12 crore; total leisure capital including RARE around Rs 60 crore, with management expecting leisure to stay near 10% of capital allocation.
demand_pricing: Office absorption in core markets about 11 million sq ft in Q1, against about 58 million sq ft for FY26; Bangalore, Hyderabad and Pune were over 65% of GCC leasing.
Passenger traffic was roughly flat YoY in Q1 after an early-quarter dip tied to geopolitics and Gulf carrier limits; the latter half recovered.
Domestic guests rose to 82% of room nights sold from 78% a year ago; 36% of days had occupancy above 90%.
Rate growth was soft because international guests, who pay a 10-20% premium, declined; management expects rate to recover in H2 as the mix rebalances.
Upscale and upper upscale hotels earn about 4x the revenue per key of midscale hotels on a same-store basis in FY26.
GST change from 12% with input tax credit to 5% without it cost about Rs 9.2 crore in Q1 and hits midscale rooms priced below Rs 7,500 more than upscale.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna (Ambit): Why acquire the Itmenaan estate given weak revenue history, how is Leisure capital allocation growing, and what RARE opportunities are being evaluated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hotel was idle for about a year and a half after owners moved to Canada and was delisted from RARE; it expects relisting and repricing toward Rs 20,000-40,000 rates in Kumaon. Total RARE capital is about Rs 47 crore, about Rs 60 crore with Itmenaan, and leisure should stay near 10% of capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna: How much of FY27 growth is rate versus occupancy, and has July shown a sharp recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy drives growth in the first six months, with rate recovering in H2 as domestic mix rebalances from 82% toward a higher-premium international mix. July is 'trending far ahead' of Q1 exit, with rate growth now visible, but management declined to give numbers and cautioned one month is not representative.

qa_highlights.question: Jinesh Joshi (PL Capital): Are RARE sign-ups to the Marriott Outdoor Collection program on track, and why must the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution be taken now?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40 of 75 RARE hotels have agreed to join; management said sign-ups are ahead of its expectations and the pace is the issue, with 10-12 hotels on rival platforms. On the resolution, management said it will be taken every year so the Board can act in time; no specific deal is identified.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja (Antique): Is the ADR slowdown (about 2.6-2.7% growth) due to West Asia disruption and Marriott-led inventory, and is occupancy at about 79% a tactical rate trade-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate is soft because inbound international travel fell, and it focuses on same-store total revenue growth of about 9%-9.5%, within the 9%-11% long-term range. In July, total revenue growth split about half rate and half occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja: Why an equity-linked enabling resolution rather than debt, given the investment surplus discussed at the Analyst Day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resolution is a general enabling step to respond to unknown problems or opportunities and keep the balance sheet strong. It added that the Rs 1,200 crore to Rs 3,000 crore revenue path has no assumed acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Shrinjana Mittal (MS Capital): Is upper upscale underperforming midscale because of downtrading, and why is GST drag above 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw ARR growth was about 3.5%-4% across segments, and midscale RevPAR grew 13.7% at 81.3% occupancy versus 78.4% for upper upscale. GST drag is larger in Q1 and Q2 from volume sales below Rs 7,500, is lower in H2, and is about 2% per management.

qa_highlights.question: Vaibhav Muley (Haitong): Why did F&B growth slow to about 4%, and what is the GIC partnership scope?
qa_highlights.answer: F&B grew about 3.5%-4% against room revenue growth of 14%, due to a shift to domestic guests (80%-83%), a Bangalore restaurant renovation, and West Asia-related event cancellations moved to July-August. GIC has a right to 35% of new upscale deals post-JV, with no talks on existing assets; Navi Mumbai and W Hyderabad are 100% SAMHI-owned.

qa_highlights.question: Prashant Biyani (Elara): Timing for Grand Hyatt pre-positioning at Hyatt Regency Pune, W Hyderabad and Courtyard Pune openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Grand Hyatt repositioning is not being pursued. W Hyderabad is targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 or calendar 2027, with regulatory delays possible. Courtyard Pune public areas and guest room renovation is deferred to about April 2027 for 5-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Gupta (Asit C Mehta): How does RARE revenue recognition work, and what are RARE's revenue, margin and EBITDA targets?
qa_highlights.answer: RARE earns booking commission and, in some hotels, higher revenue share akin to franchise fees; hotel room revenue stays with owners. Management guides Rs 100-120 crore top line at about 35% margin and Rs 35-40 crore EBITDA once stabilised in about 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mahadevia (Moneygrow): Can RARE ROCE double the group's roughly 10%, and why is EBITDA flat while PBT is up 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RARE could reach 5x group ROCE and target 50%-55% ROCE, with about 95% EBITDA-to-PBT flow-through and no finance cost. On EBITDA, it cited the Rs 9 crore one-time other income in the prior-year base and about Rs 9 crore GST drag, with YoY relief from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Gianani (MC Research): Does the annual enabling resolution overhang equity, and how is ROCE on acquisitions in a costlier market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said such provisions are common among capital-intensive peers and no debt-equity mix has been decided. It said acquisitions still target operationally distressed assets, even at market peaks, with renovation, rebranding and asset management as the value levers.

qa_highlights.question: Ashish (Leo Capital): What is the Navi Mumbai status, timeline and capex phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy issues are resolved, with statutory approvals expected in the next few months and design work to be presented next quarter. On-site start is targeted for 1 April 2027, with a 3-4 year build, capex small through FY28, and main spend in FY29-FY30.

risks_watch: Rate softness from lower international inbound mix: rate growth is expected to recover only in H2 FY27, and July's split is one month of data.

EBITDA trajectory: Q1 reported EBITDA was down about 4% YoY; the one-time Rs 9 crore base item and about Rs 9.2 crore GST drag should fall out from Q2 and Q3, but management has not guided EBITDA figures.
Leverage path: management says about 2.4x net debt/EBITDA is reached by FY28, not end-FY27, and disputes an analyst's assumption of 2.5x by year-end.
Equity dilution overhang from the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution, which management says will be taken annually; no use or debt-equity mix defined.
Project execution: W Hyderabad could slip past 2H FY28 due to regulatory approvals; Courtyard Pune renovation timeline depends on April 2027 start; Navi Mumbai on-site start in April 2027.
RARE execution: Marriott Outdoor Collection sign-ups (about 40 of 75 hotels) and RARE's shift to fee income with limited disclosure of RARE RevPAR.
key_quotes: Same-store RevPAR grew 9.6% year-on-year to approximately Rs. 5,220, with portfolio occupancy at 79.3%, which was up from 74.2% in the year-ago quarter.
Put simply, every new upscale key we now add brings in more revenue per key and a better margin than the midscale it often replaces or sits alongside.
We didn't say 2.5x by end of FY 2027. We think we will get there by FY 2028, both because of EBITDA.
Navi Mumbai, we were originally planning to be on-site, hit the ground by end of this fiscal year.
543984|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics, occupancy and the 9%-11% long-term revenue growth band, but defensive and repetitive on the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution, which it frames as routine governance. It was cautious on rate recovery and on July trends, declining to give numbers and warning that one month is not representative.

543985|2026-03.headline: Zaggle FY26 standalone revenue rose about 42% to INR1,853 crores, but FY27 standalone growth guidance slows to 25-30% as DICE moves to an asset purchase.
543985|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 results, with standalone revenue of about INR1,853 crores (up 42%) and PAT of about INR133 crores (up 52%). Q4 standalone revenue was about INR593 crores (up 44%) with reported EBITDA of about INR55 crores. The DICE acquisition was restructured from a 100% share purchase (originally INR123 crores) to an asset purchase for about INR68 crores excluding GST, which moves its costs onto the standalone P&L. Management withheld EBITDA guidance until integration completes, and cash flow is now the top priority, with operating cash flow about minus INR6 crores in the quarter.

segments.name: Zaggle core (Save, Propel, Zoyer)
segments.commentary: Program fees were about 41% of revenue and SaaS about 2% in FY26. Zoyer and BROME drove a significant rise in interchange fees. Management is deliberately reducing redemption-led Propel models that absorb cash, and expects Propel margin to recover toward about 5.5% from about 4% in Q4.

segments.name: 86400 (formerly Mobileware)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from about INR34 crores in FY25 to about INR74 crores in FY26 (up 118%). EBITDA rose from about INR5.4 crores to about INR18 crores and PAT from about INR1.6 crores to INR11 crores, driven by UPI volumes and new bank partners.

segments.name: GreenEdge
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from about INR36.5 crores in FY25 to about INR103.7 crores in FY26 (up about 184%). EBITDA rose from about INR3.4 crores to about INR11 crores and PAT from INR2.1 crores to about INR8.1 crores. Standalone revenue growth of 40-50% is projected for FY27.

segments.name: Zagg.money (formerly Rio.Money)
segments.commentary: New acquisition for retail credit cards on UPI and TPAP. Management reports an annualised run rate of about 36,000-40,000 new cards, with a base of about 25,000 cardholders. Revenue is referral fees and interchange share with no balance-sheet risk.

segments.name: TaxSpanner (to be rebranded Z.tax)
segments.commentary: Management said performance was unsatisfactory last year. Rebranding and a Tax AI copilot launch are planned for Q2 FY27, and Quesscorp partnership covers a base of 5 lakh-plus users.

segments.name: DICE (asset purchase)
segments.commentary: Acquired as a spend management suite, IP and enterprise contracts for about INR68 crores excluding GST, against an original INR123 crores share-purchase valuation. DICE was loss-making in FY25 and likely in FY26; FY25 revenue was about INR10 crores, with FY26 described as significantly higher. Around 100-plus team members join.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at about 25-30%; consolidated growth at about 40%.
EBITDA guidance deferred to 'the next few months' until DICE integration completes, since DICE costs now sit on the standalone P&L.
Medium-term guidance of 14-15% over five years is maintained, with margin ramp of roughly 1 percentage point a year expected to be temporarily disrupted.
Five-year goal of INR500 crores revenue and INR65 crores EBITDA reiterated.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in coming quarters; cash flow named the top priority, followed by revenue growth and margin expansion.
US operations now targeted by fiscal year-end (FY27), pushed back from June 2026; UAE expansion on hold pending regional peace.
Propel margin expected to return to about 5.5% in coming years.
Employee and other costs likely to rise in the next quarter as DICE staff are onboarded.
capex_capacity: Capitalised development costs rose to about INR56 crores in H2 FY26 from about INR30 crores in H1 FY26; about INR107 crores capitalised in total, mostly manpower, for new product development only.
Management declined to give a FY27 capitalisation estimate, citing AI-driven investment needs for global products.
Short-term borrowing of about INR40-50 crores taken to deploy capital quickly; a INR10 crores loan to DICE was fully adjusted against the INR68 crores payout.
Management intends to deploy QIP proceeds over coming quarters for M&A and growth.
EffiaSoft acquisition dropped after reassessment of strategic need.
demand_pricing: Around 3.9 million active users on Zaggle cards and software; more than 3,900 corporate customers.
Marquee wins in Q4 include Rebel Foods, Saurashtra Cement, Blue Star, Fanuc, Generali Central Insurance, Federal Bank and others; cross-sell to Hexalog, GMR and CNH International.
Cashback and incentives are about 68% of revenue per an analyst cited metric; management said it will dial these down over time as spend management matures, and does not give GTV splits.
Fleet management and forex products are early-stage; Adani, Think Gas and AGP Pratham cited as customers, with OMC contracts still being pursued.
Management says the 2026 credit card business is growing faster than initial expectations, with card acquisition the lead indicator before spend-led revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why are capitalised development costs nearly doubled, and does free cash flow better reflect earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only new product development is capitalised, not maintenance, and it will track operating and free cash flow more closely.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Propel margins fall from about 10% to 4% YoY in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the full-year margin of about 6% and said it is exiting redemption-heavy Propel models that absorb cash, sacrificing some margin; it expects about 5.5% in coming years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 standalone growth guided at 25-30% after 42% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the much larger base (about 5-6x since IPO) and a deliberate cash-flow focus that may slow Propel Points growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise from about INR40 crores to INR129 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split receivables by business, said the net receivable position was negative about INR33-34 crores at end-September and is now close to breakeven, and cited trade receivables as one cash lever.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated operating cash flow about minus INR52 crores versus about minus INR6 crores standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the subsidiaries are nascent businesses recently acquired, with investments made and efficiency gains to come.

qa_highlights.question: Does DICE dilute the EBITDA run rate and the 11-12% margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DICE's impact is no worse than originally envisaged, with costs now on standalone P&L; it was loss-making and EBITDA guidance will follow integration.

qa_highlights.question: Is Propel worth keeping given its low net revenue and working-capital use?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Propel is a feeder for cross-sell and stickiness, about 90% of spend sits in program fees, and cash and ROCE optimisation is under way.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow remains negative (about minus INR6 crores standalone; about minus INR52 crores consolidated) and receivables have risen sharply.
DICE integration may lift employee and other costs in the next quarter, with EBITDA guidance still pending.
Propel margin compression and cutbacks in cashback and redemption models could slow growth and affect customer retention.
Overseas expansion (UAE and US) is delayed by regional conflict; the US launch slipped to FY27 year-end, and the company has no on-ground presence in the Middle East.
CFO role is interim after Aditya Kumar Grandhi's departure; a permanent CFO is expected soon.
Discrepancies in call figures (for example standalone FY26 EBITDA of INR181 vs INR183 crores and a GreenEdge growth percentage correction) should be checked against the filed results.

up about 51-61% YoY; figures differ between speakers
improved from Q2 FY26 when trade receivables net position was about minus INR33-34 crores

financial_highlights.value: Program fees about INR222 crores; Propel Points about INR358 crores; SaaS platform fees about INR13.1 crores (about 2.2%)

financial_highlights.change: up from about INR40 crores YoY

key_quotes: We are minutely focused on improving the cash flow and bringing it to a high positive level.

544009|2026-06.headline: Blue Jet Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% QoQ to INR293 crore and EBITDA hit INR98 crore, with PI/API restart offset by INR30 crore contrast media goods in transit.
544009|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR293 crore, up 25% QoQ, with operating EBITDA margin of 33.5% versus 30.4% in Q4 FY26. Growth came mainly from PI and API, where supply of an intermediate restarted after customer destocking. Contrast media revenue fell sharply (about 40% QoQ per analyst) because roughly INR30 crore of goods were in transit at quarter end, which management says will be recognised next quarter. Raw material inflation from March 2026 weighed on gross margin, which fell about 3 points to 53%. Mahad (Unit 3) is now expected to commission later this calendar year, slightly ahead of the earlier H2 guidance.

qa_highlights.answer: Closing goods in transit were about INR30 crore higher than opening, which will be recognised next quarter. Plant utilisation is ~70% steady; production unchanged and production-to-dispatch at 100%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating income jump to INR16.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the bulk to forex gain and higher interest income, and later clarified the line item is driven mainly by export incentives tied to export levels and byproduct sales; the ratio to exports should remain in a similar range.

qa_highlights.question: Is PI/API growth lumpy or secular, and what visibility exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: secular growth in end-market demand plus a strong order book and consistent production give good visibility for at least 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Vizag and cardiovascular-related opportunity translate into sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to speculate, saying it will go by orders on hand; order book described as good and an update to come when more information is available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the peptides strategy and differentiation from other Indian CDMOs?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on peptide fragments first (liquid phase), with selective forward integration into final peptides for large CDMOs or innovators; no participation in generic front-end peptides. Management intends to quantify the peptide-related RFPs in coming quarters.

544012|2026-03.headline: Cello World Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR654 crore (record quarter), but EBITDA margin fell to 20.9%; FY27 revenue guided at 10-12% growth.
544012|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was a record INR653.6 crore, up 11% YoY, with EBITDA of INR136.6 crore (20.9% margin) and PAT of INR90.1 crore (13.8% margin). FY26 revenue grew 8.8% to INR2,323.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR526.4 crore (22.7%) and PAT margin of 14.3%, weighed down by glassware losses and steel bottle ramp-up costs. Management described FY26 as a year of corrective initiatives and said Q1 FY27 looks challenging due to the Middle East-linked cost and demand headwinds. Steel bottle capacity is ramping in phases toward full scale by July 2026, and the Wimplast merger and a restructuring scheme took effect from 27 May 2026.

segments.name: Writing instruments
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR128 crore (19.6% of total), up 64% YoY including Cello brand from Q4; excluding Cello, grew at a healthy double-digit rate. FY26 segment revenue about INR368 crore; FY27 target INR500 crore plus.

segments.name: Moulded furniture and allied
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about 14% of total; moulded furniture fell 13.5% YoY in line with industry demand. Wimplast merged into the company; gross margin 39.5%.

segments.commentary: Sales fell 25% in FY26 due to capacity constraints, with stock-outs in insulated steel. Two lines running in Q4, four more in Q1 FY27 and two further lines expected soon; peak revenue of current capacity about INR300 crore.

segments.name: Glassware (within consumerware)
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 60% due to Chinese dumping; segment at breakeven. Management targets peak revenue of about INR300 crore at 28-30% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Opalware (within consumerware)
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 85%, leaving about 15% headroom; management plans to exhaust capacity before any expansion, which would need a greenfield site in Rajasthan.

qa_highlights.question: Why was steel bottle capacity delayed from Q4 FY26 to Q2 FY27, and what is the revenue impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no delay: lines started in phases, with 2 in Q4, 4 in Q1 FY27 and 2 more after. Steel ware sales fell about 25% in FY26 due to capacity constraints.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 guidance for revenue growth and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of 10-12% and EBITDA margin up about 2-2.5 percentage points, with a possible change depending on the crisis.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin compression in consumerware and writing instruments in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Glassware revenue grew without profit, steel ware margin fell 5-6% from costlier OEM sourcing, and appliances carried lower margins. Cello pens were loss-making before the acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Is the top-line guidance conservative given 12-20% MRP hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said value growth will come, but volumes could be subdued this year. The price increases may not hold for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash is there and how will it be used? Any buyback plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is being held for adjacent inorganic opportunities with distribution or manufacturing synergies, which may depress return ratios. No buyback is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan to reduce receivable days?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is to cut 15-odd days to under 100 days, through better channel inventory checks, distributor stock liquidation support and SKU rationalisation. Government tenders stretched receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q4 core stationery growth (about 19%) driven by channel stocking ahead of price rises?

qa_highlights.question: Could EBITDA margins fall below the 16.5-17.5% band if the crude-driven inflation persists?

qa_highlights.question: What was the total price increase in the FY23 Ukraine-war cycle?

qa_highlights.question: What share of raw materials is crude-linked, and how much inventory is raw material?

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin compress while gross margin held steady in Q4?

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue guidance and does it include the new plant?

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex guidance rise, and how is it funded?

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR850-1,000 crore total for the 45-acre project separate from Phase 1?

544045|2026-06.headline: DOMS Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 19.2% to INR670 crore, but EBITDA fell 16.4% to INR82.6 crore as margin dropped to 12.3% on raw material inflation.
544045|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue grew 19.2% YoY to INR670 crore on volume growth, with only a calibrated price increase of about 4-5%. EBITDA margin compressed to 12.3% from 17.6%, mainly from roughly 400 bps gross margin decline due to West Asia-linked raw material inflation (about 20% average RM price rise in Q1), plus ESOP, new-facility and channel partner event costs. PAT fell to INR45.3 crore from INR59.1 crore, with PAT margin at 6.8% versus 10.5%. Management chose volume and market share over near-term margin, calls the margin dip temporary, and gave limited visibility on margins given fluctuating raw material costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why not take larger price hikes, and will margins stay weak in FY27 and normalise only in FY28? Also, how much can H2 revenue grow beyond 20%, and what is Reynolds' FY28 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritised volume-led growth and market share; price increases were calibrated and raw material prices eased toward end-June before rising again in recent weeks. Margins are structurally intact with a return to the 16-17% guided range once prices stabilise. 18-20% FY27 revenue guidance reaffirmed; Reynolds adds little incremental volume as it uses diverted existing capacity, and it is expected to contribute about 10% of revenue by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material price has been passed on, how much is left, and what are the one-off costs in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Average price increase taken is about 4-5% against about 20% average RM price rise in Q1, which translates to 10-11% consumption cost increase, leaving about 500 bps to pass on. ESOP added about 0.2% to cost; the channel partner event cost about 0.4% of margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Reynolds nib (OEM) business not acquired, and what is the backward integration plan for tips?

qa_highlights.question: Why is Uniclan's EBITDA margin intact while stationery margins fell about 600 bps, and will Q2 see further gross margin pressure from higher-cost inventory?

Management said DOMS carries low inventory of locally bought polymers, so no major inventory-cost effect, and Q2 seasonal fixed-cost absorption in diapers should offset part of the impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why were exports flattish and why did West India revenue fall from about INR186 crore to about INR140 crore?

West India fell due to lower merchant export sales via western India customers. Full-year export share guided at 13-15% (about 12% currently), helped by new pencil capacity.

544046|2026-03.headline: INOX India Q4 FY26 total income rose 24.2% YoY to INR475 crores; FY26 revenue INR1,632 crores (+21.2%) with 23.8% adjusted EBITDA margin and INR1,514 crore order book.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Agartala occupancy fall, and is the year-end target intact?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Raipur loss and ARPOB trajectory on track?

qa_highlights.question: Is the ARPOB rise sustainable, and is it price-led?

qa_highlights.question: Will the company guide medium-term on occupancy and revenue?

qa_highlights.question: Expected FY27 EBITDA run-rate?

Cautious and deflecting on Agartala occupancy (ALOS cut, election curbs), Raipur ramp timing and Jamshedpur approvals, and declined medium-term occupancy or revenue guidance, deferring it to MUFG.

544133|2026-03.headline: Exicom Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 46% YoY to INR 388 crores and consolidated EBITDA turned positive at INR 0.3 crore for the first time since Tritium acquisition.
544133|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 revenue grew 33% YoY to INR 282 crores with EBITDA of INR 29.9 crores (10.6% margin), driven by Critical Power (+23% YoY) and EVSE (+60% YoY). Consolidated revenue of INR 388 crores (+46% YoY) included Tritium, and consolidated EBITDA turned marginally positive. For full FY26, consolidated EBITDA was still negative at INR 103 crores and adjusted PAT was negative at INR 258 crores, with higher finance cost and one-time exceptional costs (VRS, Tritium retention, labour code). Management flagged a temporary inventory and receivables build as Hyderabad ramped up alongside Gurgaon.

financial_highlights.change: hit by finance cost, exceptional items, labour code

segments.name: Critical Power (standalone)

segments.name: EVSE / EV charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Grew 60% YoY in Q4 and 40% for FY26; record quarterly EV charging revenue of INR 88 crores (management figure, basis not specified). Full-year EVSE consolidated growth 72%; Q4 consolidated EVSE +83% YoY.

segments.name: Tritium (US/Australia, EV charging)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about $10 million (sales $9.7 million), record order intake $10 million; EBITDA losses down about 30% QoQ. Management targets ~3x revenue and 25% lower EBITDA losses, with EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Tritium: revenue to scale about 3x and EBITDA losses to fall about 25%; EBITDA breakeven targeted in Q4 FY27. Management said losses fall less sharply than revenue because low-cost acquired inventory is being used up, with margins normalising after about one quarter.
Exports: target to lift Critical Power export share to 20% in FY27 from ~10-15%.
Non-telecom BESS: internal target of over INR 50 crores business in FY26 from pilot-stage orders; management sees BESS possibly reaching ~30% of Critical Power over 2-3 years if successful.

Three Tritium products (TRI-FLEX inverter and two others) launching May-July 2026; management cites about INR 850 crores of combined FY28 revenue potential, subject to pilots. TRI-FLEX hyperscaler factory acceptance test ongoing, potentially $30-35 million FY28 revenue.
Gurgaon production to shift majority to Hyderabad over the next 2-3 months; inventory build expected to normalise over coming quarters.

Additional open opportunities of about INR 400 crores beyond the INR 1,000 crore Critical Power order book, including about INR 100 crores of new BharatNet tenders and about INR 150 crores of uncovered-village Phase-2.

Tritium manufacturing in Tennessee, US; R&D in Brisbane, Australia; Exicom R&D in Gurgaon (hardware) and Bangalore (software), with 130+ engineers.
Ring-topology PC charger: first pilot in Q4 FY26, mass production planned in FY27.
Exicom One: 80 sites executed in Q4 under this integrated products-and-services program.

Standalone gross margin expanded to 27% on richer EVSE mix and fewer low-margin lithium battery sales.

qa_highlights.question: What charging infrastructure is needed for commercial EV adoption and where is it happening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adoption is in fixed-route captive use such as ports, cement distribution and mining with 200-300 trucks; intercity commercial electrification is still about two years away.

qa_highlights.question: What is the product and revenue potential of the TRI-FLEX inverter and its applications?
qa_highlights.answer: TRI-FLEX converts grid power to high-voltage DC for DC microgrids, BESS integration and 800V data centres. A hyperscaler pilot is in testing and, if successful, could unlock significant FY28 revenue ($30-35 million cited).

qa_highlights.question: How will the company win customers for the two other new Tritium products in the US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said development was done with existing strategic customers, and it has line of sight to long-term contracts once pilots succeed.

qa_highlights.question: Does Exicom have OEM tie-ups for supplying chargers with vehicles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Exicom is the largest home charger maker, with about a 50% chance a new EV in India comes with an Exicom charger, and it has OEM partnerships for home and fast chargers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS offering and its scaling path over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets commercial and industrial modular BESS, not utility, transmission, distribution or home. About 10-20 small projects were deployed in Q4, with an FY26 target above INR 50 crores, and BESS could reach about 30% of Critical Power over 2-3 years.

BESS cell supply dependent on imports until local cell manufacturing arrives.

544133|2026-06.headline: Exicom Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 57% YoY to INR237 crore with EBITDA margin at 8.8%; consolidated EBITDA loss narrowed to INR22 crore.
544133|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 57% YoY to INR236.8 crore, with Critical Power up 80% to INR176 crore and EV up 15% to INR61 crore. Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to INR20.9 crore (8.8% margin), helped by operating leverage and richer mix. Consolidated revenue rose 61% to INR331.1 crore, but consolidated EBITDA was a loss of INR21.9 crore (down from INR38.6 crore loss), as Tritium margins normalised after drawing down low-cost acquired inventory. Management guided to consolidated EBITDA breakeven within two quarters and Tritium breakeven by Q4 FY27, while working capital rose on parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad plant operations and higher receivables.

segments.name: Critical Power (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR176-177 crore, up 73-80% YoY and down ~11% QoQ; BharatNet is among the largest contributors, with a 60% share in that project per management. Export sales about INR15 crore (~8% of Critical Power).

segments.name: EV Charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR61 crore, up 15% YoY but down QoQ from Q4 DC-charger pull-forward; consolidated EV grew 50%. FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of total.

segments.name: Tritium (consolidated, US DC fast charging)
segments.commentary: Revenue about USD10-10.5 million in Q1, second consecutive quarter above USD10 million; bookings about USD20.8-21 million, roughly double the usual ~USD10 million per quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA breakeven expected within the next two quarters (management could not specify Q2 or Q3).
Tritium EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27, with 3x revenue growth versus last year targeted.
Standalone Critical Power exports targeted to rise from ~8% to ~15% of Critical Power sales within FY27.
AC charger monthly run rate expected to rise ~50% over the next three months.

Tritium large strategic contracts (USD20-30 million for CY27 from Fortune 100 trials, USD20 million GRID-FLEX from hyperscaler) contingent on trial success.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant commissioned in Q4 FY26 and fully in production in Q1 FY27; management says it gives 3x production capability versus Gurgaon.

Management said DC charger utilisation is ~65% (90-100% for DC power system lines), AC charger ~100%, and PCBA and battery lines ~100%.
Ordered an additional AC charger line; management said the Hyderabad plant was built for ~2x AC capacity.
Tritium US factory capacity is about USD100 million a year versus ~USD10 million current quarterly revenue run rate (about one-quarter utilised).
demand_pricing: Critical Power order book ~INR1,000 crore; consolidated order book INR1,400 crore-plus as of 30 June 2026.
Large DC power system order of INR85 crore from a leading Indian telco; supply agreement with a large tower company for power systems and batteries.
BharatNet: INR700 crore open orders plus ~INR800 crore of service orders over 10 years; BSNL Phase 2 expected ~2,000 sites at INR90-100 crore.

EV charger order book about INR200 crore for AC/DC chargers in India plus ~USD2 million export orders; 10 new export countries won; 15 new network operators added in Q1.
Margins on some large orders were hit by forex and commodity price increases, partly offset by volumes.
Supply disruptions in semiconductors, plastics and copper were cited as the main constraint, not capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated EBITDA swung from breakeven in Q4 FY26 to a INR22 crore loss in Q1; what drove the sequential drop and when does breakeven return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q4 seasonality in Indian business and Tritium's low-cost acquired inventory eroding, lowering Tritium margins. It still expects Tritium EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27 and consolidated breakeven within the next two quarters, without specifying Q2 or Q3.

qa_highlights.question: When will Tritium's doubled order intake convert to revenue, and is the 3x growth and Q4 FY27 breakeven target still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the USD20 million backlog as of 1 July plus new bookings and large strategic wins (double-digit million dollars, executing from calendar 2027 Q1) give confidence in 3x revenue growth and Q4 FY27 EBITDA breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: What is Hyderabad plant utilisation and where will it reach in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyderabad was built for about 2x AC charger capacity and roughly 4,000 DC chargers. Utilisation is about 65% on DC chargers, close to 100% on AC chargers, 90-100% on DC power system lines, and close to 100% on PCBA and battery lines. AC charger monthly run rate is expected to rise about 50% over the next three months, and another AC line has been ordered.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EV revenue mix and growth outlook, and why is the AC capacity figure inconsistent with the annual report (42,000 to 222,000 units)?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of revenue, with mix expected to stay similar or rise slightly. Management said the 222,000 figure is right and that 48,000 was single-shift, with the doubling based on double-shift operation; it will revert with an exact answer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone depreciation rise, and what is the Tritium capitalisation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone depreciation rose about 67% YoY to INR10.3 crore, with management attributing an increase of INR10-12 crore to the new plant. Tritium's higher depreciation reflects capitalised R&D and acquisition-related servicing costs, which management expects to be amortised over 5-7 years.

qa_highlights.question: Can EV charger market share and unit volumes be estimated from EV registrations, and why was standalone EV growth only 15% when AC demand is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a very high share of wallbox chargers but not portable chargers, and volume depends on whether OEMs bundle wallboxes. Its DRHP cited 60% wallbox share, and it estimates current wallbox share at north of 50%. The 15% standalone EV growth reflects Q4 DC charger pull-forward; AC may have grown about 30% and DC about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US Tritium factory capacity and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the US factory can service about USD100 million a year, about 2.5x the current ~USD10 million quarterly revenue, and it is running at about one-quarter of that today due to the ongoing turnaround.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA breakeven timing is not pinned down (Q2 or Q3 FY27), and Tritium breakeven is targeted only for Q4 FY27; the Tritium margin cushion from acquired low-cost inventory has already eroded.
Tritium strategic contracts (USD20-30 million for CY27 from Fortune 100 trials, USD20 million GRID-FLEX) are contingent on trial success and calendar 2026 conversion.

Working capital pressure from parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad operations: elevated inventory and receivables, plus ~INR8.7 crore of Q1 parallel-run fixed costs expected to phase out over coming quarters.
Margin pressure from forex, commodity and US-led input cost increases on large orders, and supply disruption in semiconductors, plastics and copper.
Depreciation step-up (standalone +67% YoY, consolidated +57%) will weigh on PAT until plant utilisation and Tritium revenue scale.

Shift in EV growth from DC to AC chargers and reliance on Q4 pull-forward; watch whether standalone EV growth accelerates beyond 15% YoY.
key_quotes: So the overall performance on a stand-alone revenue rose by 57% year-on-year to INR237 crores and our EBITDA more than doubled to INR21 crores lifting the EBITDA margins to 8.8%.
But on a consolidated basis, the breakeven may be over the next 2 quarters itself. I can't specify whether quarter 2 or 3.
Some of the challenges today is not capacity, it's supply chain disruption.

544133|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on order book, Tritium turnaround and the Hyderabad capacity build-out, but cautious on timing, as management repeatedly declined to specify exact quarters for breakeven. Some answers were loose or deflected (for example the capacity-figure reconciliation and blended EV market share), with the management promising to revert.

544134|2026-06.headline: Platinum Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR 108.9 crore (from INR 115.4 crore) and PAT to INR 11.13 crore as Palghar ramp-up weighed.
544134|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue declined about 5.6% YoY to INR 108.9 crore while EBITDA fell to INR 13.44 crore at a 12.34% margin, versus INR 15.16 crore at 13.14% a year earlier. Standalone revenue grew about 7.3% YoY to INR 110.4 crore, but standalone EBITDA margin was 11.64%. The expanded Palghar facility only became fully operational on 21 May 2026, so the quarter carried ramp-up costs and lower lead-free PVC offtake. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 30-40% and kept Egypt commercial production targeted before 31 December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How did pipe demand look in July and August, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pipe demand degrew in Q1 across pipe companies, picked up from August, and is expected to stay good through December as PVC prices stabilised and turned upward.

qa_highlights.question: What were Oleo sales in Q1 FY27 and can the segment reach INR 55-60 crore by year-end?

qa_highlights.question: When will CPVC margins recover toward 20-22%?
qa_highlights.answer: CPVC margin is about 18% now and management targets 20-21% by Q4 FY27. Recovery depends on demand, since supply currently exceeds demand, and on local raw material sourcing, which is adding cost.

qa_highlights.question: Volume, price and mix split, new customers, and stabilizer versus specialty volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share product volume data and suggested the analyst connect offline.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA margin is structural versus temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower sales-related expenses, since the company skipped exhibitions in Q1, and lower ECL provisions offset the drop in contribution margin, leaving EBITDA margin impact negligible. Lead-free PVC offtake was lower, which hurt mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the utilisation of the existing stabilizer capacity and the threshold to sustain margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The expanded plant was fully operational only from 21 May 2026, so utilisation is expected to be around 30-35% in Q2 and Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-off items in other income or forex in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: A forex gain of about INR 1 crore was reflected in other income.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30-40% still maintained, and how much Egypt revenue is included?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 30-40% growth for FY27 and said the company is already on track, though demand was weak due to the war. Egypt is only partly included: FY27 Egypt estimate is cut to INR 30-35 crore from INR 50-60 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Oleo revenue potential over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 Oleo target is INR 65-70 crore and the three-year target is INR 150-200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Lubrizol and Aditya Birla CPVC resin capacity on Platinum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resin capacity is complementary, since additives are about 25% of a CPVC compound and resin about 75%. The company has supplied Supreme and Prince Pipes for 1-2 years, and the transition will take time.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and pricing pressure in lead-free and CPVC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no direct CPVC additive competition in India apart from one other Indian company. In lead-free, Baerlocher and Reagens are the main competitors, Goldstab is mainly lead-based, and pricing levels are understood by all players.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook versus the roughly 23% margins of FY23-FY24?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the change to a mix shift from high-margin lead-free to lower-margin CPVC, which started at a 3-7% contribution margin. Guidance is PAT margin of 11-12% and EBITDA margin of 13-15%, reiterated from the previous call.

qa_highlights.question: Project-wise capex, timelines and revenue potential for Egypt and Palghar?
qa_highlights.answer: Egypt is expected by December 2026, with INR 250-300 crore top line over three years. Palghar peak potential is INR 700-800 crore over three years, and top-line CAGR is about 35% over three years.

qa_highlights.question: What bottlenecks could delay commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not expect much delay.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the stearates plant and its effect on revenue?

qa_highlights.question: Status of Rivadu Lifesciences pharma and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Business model is still being defined. Some revenue started this quarter, with collaborations with overseas companies under negotiation. No figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material inflation pass-through and contractual mechanisms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can pass on raw material price rises in normal conditions, but in the current war and shipping environment it cannot pass on sudden freight, CFS and transport costs. Lower lead-free PVC offtake was cited as the main Q1 margin driver.

qa_highlights.question: Egypt versus Palghar capex and why revenue potential differs?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR 67 crore for Egypt and INR 71 crore for Palghar. Both have about 60,000 tpa capacity, but Egypt is mainly lead stabilisers, priced at INR 110-150 per kg versus INR 250-300 for CPVC and INR 170-220 for calcium zinc in India.

qa_highlights.question: Incremental working capital needed for Egypt?

Management declined to guide on Q2 FY27 flight growth or on margin trajectory, saying growth depends on ATV and supply.

Budget-hotel Peace of Mind products and a PMS to be tested on select properties, with rollout over the subsequent quarters of FY27.
Capitalisation of AI/platform costs stated to be in the same range as the prior quarter, per the CFO; no absolute number given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise while technology costs were flat QoQ, and what is the AI capitalisation figure?

qa_highlights.question: Are train contribution margin gains from the Spanish or consolidated business, or organic?

qa_highlights.question: Will the easier base support flight growth acceleration?

qa_highlights.question: Bus net take rate fell QoQ to 10.8%: is discounting rising and will it recover to 11-11.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Aloke said 11-11.5% is the gross take rate and that discounting has been range-bound over the last 6-8 quarters, with no intention to get aggressive. The Q1 dip reflected the seasonal AMJ peak with more marketing and discounts, and the company was more disciplined than peers.

544192|2026-09.headline: ixigo Q2 FY27 GTV rose 22% to INR 5,304 crore and PAT hit a record, but adjusted EBITDA fell 17% to INR 23.6 crore on a stepped-up hotel investment.
544192|2026-09.overview: Consolidated GTV grew 22% YoY to INR 5,304.47 crore and revenue from operations rose 13% to INR 320.96 crore, with contribution margin up 14% to INR 124.86 crore. Adjusted EBITDA fell 17% to INR 23.58 crore from INR 28.48 crore as management deliberately funded hotel people and technology spend. Reported PAT was an all-time high of INR 63.42 crore, aided by a INR 40.66 crore exceptional gain on the partial sale of Freshbus. Flights were weak: GTV grew 37% on higher fares, but revenue fell 8% as take rate compressed from 9.4% to 7%. Hotels were disclosed as a separate segment for the first time.

Hotel take rate expected to edge up over the next 3-4 quarters; no guidance given on the level for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did flight revenue per ticket fall 13-14% against the recent average; is this a permanent share-gain strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher discounts were needed to keep NBU flight users affordable given the 30% fare rise, and international mix and convenience fees also compressed take rate. It said it would not step up discounts further at current fares.

qa_highlights.question: Is there early visibility on Q3 flight trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Festive demand is a shade lower than expected; management is cautious on flights and not guiding to aggressive growth, but says it will keep growing.

qa_highlights.question: When will hotel take rate reach 16-17% and when will the segment be profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Take rate will edge up over the next 3-4 quarters as direct supply grows, with no next-year guidance. Profitability is not targeted near term; investment is expected for 2-3 years, with spending tied to observed returns and payback periods.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors frame hotel investment within guardrails?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment was INR 1 crore-plus above CM and about INR 10 crore below CM this quarter. Guardrails are customer payback periods and keeping company-level EBITDA in the mid-single-digit range, with a near-term range of INR 10-12 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What GTV mix can be expected over 3-4 years, and will rail share gains continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Hotels could be the second-largest GTV contributor in 4-5 years. Management expects rail GTV share to decline from the early 40s given 4-5% annual capacity growth; buses to be the second-fastest growing line after hotels.

qa_highlights.question: How much of a threat do consumer AI agents pose, and which segments are most exposed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI-platform traffic is still a low single-digit share and sees specialist vertical agents, and ixigo's proprietary data and peace-of-mind products as differentiators. Building products is easy; trust and distribution are the hard parts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus growth of about 28% too slow given supply and rail constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is comfortable with the current pace, trading growth for margin and a sustainable business, and noted bus CM is about 53% of revenue.

Rail: management says recovery is not yet proven beyond the festive season; rail GTV share may decline.
AI agents: consumer AI platforms could disintermediate bookings; the agentic booking flow awaits regulatory clarity before launch.
Inorganic: Brevistay consolidation adds to hotel growth; future acquisitions are unspecified.

544198|2026-03.headline: DEE Development FY26 revenue rose 38% to Rs 1,142 Cr and PAT 76.9% to Rs 77.2 Cr; order book Rs 2,040 Cr with FY27 inflow guided above Rs 2,000 Cr.
544198|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first year after most of the growth capex cycle, with Anjar fabrication and the seamless pipe plant commissioned. Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 361.6 Cr (+26.3% YoY) and PAT Rs 27.7 Cr, against a high Q4 FY25 base that included Q3 spillover. Management split the business into core (piping, heavy fabrication) and non-core (power, biomass pallets), with core EBITDA of Rs 210.5 Cr (+64.2%) excluding non-core losses. The company guided to a Rs 1,500 Cr revenue commitment for FY27, a Rs 2,500 Cr revenue target by FY30, and a consolidated EBITDA margin above 19%, while the Malwa Power tariff revision and the Thailand HRSG job-work order were the main new items.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said most orders are linked to the overseas HRSG market. Thailand works on job-work basis, so the Rs 150 Cr figure is mostly value-add rather than full revenue, with EBITDA margin above 20% and only minor capex.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the gross margin decline is commodity inflation versus mix, and what are the alloy and job-work splits?

qa_highlights.question: Are order flows and margins sustainable with the new Anjar and seamless plants?

qa_highlights.question: Why is order book up about 50% while guidance is 20-25% growth, and why did inventory stay flat?

544202|2026-03.headline: Stanley Lifestyles FY26 gross margin rose 151 bps to 57.5%, but Q4 revenue fell on B2B export pull-down and management guides only conservative FY27 growth.
544202|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a transition year spent acquiring franchise markets (Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune) into company-owned stores and consolidating subsidiaries into one listed entity.
