Margins recovered to about INR 7-8 a kg from around May 15, and management says operations are back to normal levels. Sales volume was 112,000 tonnes versus 104,000 tonnes a year earlier, and operating cash flow was about INR 121 crore. Management reiterated 20% volume and EBITDA growth for the rest of FY27 and kept capex at INR 200-250 crore a year.

financial_highlights.value: about INR 4-4.5 a kg for the quarter
financial_highlights.change: first 45 days about INR 2 a kg; later period INR 7-8 a kg

segments.name: Core B2B wire business
segments.commentary: Absorbed a cost shock on about 30-40 days of firm-price orders; new orders were priced at INR 8 a kg blended. Management says volume growth lagged its 20% target because of a demand dip and customer destocking.

segments.name: B2C (farming, fencing, poultry steel wire)
segments.commentary: Launched in the quarter and contributed about 10% of sales. Management targets B2C at 25% of total sales, which is 50% of the low-carbon business, and says B2C EBITDA per tonne is 20-30% above B2B low-carbon.

segments.name: Speciality wires (IHT, OHT, Steel Cord)
segments.commentary: IHT capacity is 9,000 tonnes, rising to 15,000 tonnes with OHT by year-end. IHT utilisation is at 35-40% and targeted at about 50% next month. Steel Cord has a 20,000-tonne pilot and received its first trial order from a leading Indian tire maker; four trials are expected, each taking about two to three months.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth of 20% for the rest of FY27, with EBITDA growth guided at a similar 20% or more.
EBITDA per kg is expected to stay around INR 7-8 a kg after the Q1 disruption.
Capex capped at INR 200-250 crore a year, including FY27; IHT and OHT utilisation targeted at 60-80% by year-end.
Speciality target of about INR 2 lakh tonnes of capacity, with EBITDA of INR 600-800 crore on INR 2,000-2,500 crore of investment (per management's math).
Target of 25% ROCE in the current business over a short period.
Operating cash flow target of INR 350 crore for FY27, per management.
capex_capacity: Total installed capacity is about 680,000 tonnes; FY27 started with 680,000 tonnes plus 60,000 tonnes that can be commissioned as needed.
Management aims to start each year with 20-25% spare capacity and historically runs at 85-90% utilisation.
Sanand facility wire expansion of about 90,000 tonnes is under way; some surplus land there may be sold in part.
Dadri greenfield facility had early hiccups that management says are resolved, and ramp-up is now under way.
OHT wire is expected to commission shortly and be fully operational by year-end.
demand_pricing: Demand is recovering across most sectors, including exports and automotive; management says 2Q and 3Q are seasonally weaker in infra.
Management says the industry grows 7-8% while Bansal has grown about 20% a year over the last two decades.
Speciality: India is 60-65% imported and Bansal targets 45-50% share of that market at full capacity; export is not seen as viable because of raw material cost gaps of INR 10-15 a kg.
IHT EBITDA is about INR 10-20 a kg at optimum utilisation, with 80% of customers already approving the product.
Gas costs rose about 1.5x on a blended basis and had not come down as of the call.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and growth hold if the geopolitical and oil-price issue persists for several quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management absorbed about INR 5,000 a tonne of consumable cost on firm-price orders for the first 45 days, which took EBITDA down to about INR 2 a kg. Margins have been back at INR 7-8 a kg since about May 15.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company run a cost-plus model, and why did the quarter's margin fall so sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: The model is cost-plus, but about 30-40 days of inventory was tied to fixed-rate orders, so the cost rise hit immediately. New orders were booked at escalated prices from April.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book from the first Steel Cord trial customer and when will a firm order come?
qa_highlights.answer: It is only a trial order with no firm order book yet. Four trials are expected, each taking about two to three months, so a firm order could take six to eight months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CFO guidance rise to about INR 800 crore across FY27 and FY28 from about INR 600 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 600 crore figure was a combined two-year target. FY26 delivered about INR 330 crore against a INR 250 crore target, and FY27's target is INR 350 crore, with INR 115 crore already generated in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What are the IHT and OHT margins and utilisation path?
qa_highlights.answer: IHT is at 35-40% utilisation, targeting about 50% next month. Break-even is at about 60% utilisation, with decent margins at 70-80%. Combined IHT and OHT EBITDA is expected at INR 10-20 a kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is capped at INR 200-250 crore a year to support 20-25% volume growth. Management said there will be no unusually high capex year apart from Speciality.

risks_watch: Gas and consumable costs had not eased by the call, and a reversal could create inventory losses on the 30-40 days of stock held at cost.
Volume growth must reach about 145,000 tonnes a quarter over the next three quarters, which implies roughly 85% utilisation.
Receivable and payable days: the company used payables financing and vendor advances, and management plans to cut receivable days.
Speciality ROCE depends on the Steel Cord ramp, which is still in trial stages with no firm order book.
Sanand land: management clarified that the land is not being sold outright, which resolves the earlier confusion over asset-held-for-sale presentation.
544209|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on recovery and growth, with management saying the fundamental challenges are almost over. Management was cautious on Speciality timelines and on pricing, noting "a lot of uncertainty is still remaining" and that Steel Cord is still a long process.
key_quotes: Now as of today, even with all of this crisis today, we see that the demand is there.
We are operating at regular EBITDA with an escalated cost.
Once we reach an optimum capacity utilization, I would say that we can expect similar EBITDA, like we are thinking of Steel Cord or something like that in percentage.
We will cap our CAPEX at about INR 200 crore-INR 250 crore every year to give us runway for each year.

544209|2026-09.headline: Bansal Wire posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 1,308 crore (+24% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 105 crore, with EBITDA/ton near Rs 8,000 aided partly by inventory gain.
544209|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a record quarter for revenue, EBITDA, PAT and EBITDA per ton, recovering from a Q1 hit from industrial gas disruption and higher input costs. Sales volume was about 1,29,000 tons versus 1,14,609 tons in Q2 FY26, and operating cash flow was Rs 218 crore in the quarter and Rs 339 crore in H1. Management said about Rs 200/ton of EBITDA was a one-time inventory gain and guided to Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2. Raw material (wire rod) shortages hit October output, which management said is a short-term issue.

segments.name: IHT / OHT specialty wire
segments.commentary: IHT wire reached positive EBITDA last quarter; management cites Rs 15,000-20,000/ton EBITDA for the specialty wire group. IHT capacity is 9,000 tons, with 6,000 tons OHT being installed to reach 15,000 tons in one to two quarters.

segments.name: Steel tyre cord
segments.commentary: Current capacity about 20,000 tons, with a goal of 2 lakh tons. Pricing is about Rs 130-140/kg. First trial order received in Q2, with a second trial order expected in 10-15 days; commercialisation possible within this year.

segments.name: Bead wire
segments.commentary: Nameplate capacity about 30,000 tons, with 10,000-15,000 tons currently run annually. Management cites Rs 12,000-15,000/ton EBITDA. Approvals not yet started; focus to resume in one to two quarters.

segments.name: LRPC
segments.commentary: Less than 1% of sales. Management said it earns modest margins (about Rs 5,000-8,000/ton typical) due to industry overcapacity.

segments.name: B2C (farming, fencing, poultry)
segments.commentary: About 10-12% of Q2 volumes; management says B2C EBITDA is at least 50% higher than B2B.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth of 20% YoY for H2 FY27 (Q3 and Q4 vs prior-year H2); management said Q1 losses cannot be recovered.
EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2 FY27; management said Rs 7,000-8,000/ton is achievable for FY27 barring major geopolitical change.
Operating cash flow target of about Rs 800 crore across FY27 and FY28 combined; about Rs 350 crore already generated in H1 FY27.
Capacity to rise from 6.8 lakh tons to about 8.3 lakh tons by end of next year (60,000 tons Dadri brownfield plus about 90,000 tons Sanand greenfield).
Indicative annual capex of Rs 200-225 crore (also cited as Rs 200-250 crore per year), funded from internal accruals.
Long-term EBITDA/ton target of Rs 8,000-10,000, and above Rs 10,000 as specialty wire scales.
capex_capacity: Dadri: 60,000 tons additional low and high carbon wire capacity, mostly built; capitalisation expected by end of Q3 or Q4 FY27. Also 6,000 tons OHT wire, expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

Sanand (southern Gujarat) greenfield: about 90,000 tons of stainless steel and low carbon wire, with about Rs 150 crore capex excluding land (land acquired about a year ago). Some capitalisation expected from next quarter or the quarter after.
CWIP closing balance Rs 177 crore.
Steel tyre cord: 20,000 tons current capacity, with a 2 lakh ton goal; a bigger capex will follow customer approvals.
Management expects 4-5x asset turnover on new capacity.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as healthy across automotive, infra, agriculture, power and transmission, and general engineering. Constraint is raw material supply rather than demand.
Wire rod shortage over the last 1.5-2 months as suppliers shifted output to TMT. Company holds about 1.5 months of inventory; October output was hit at some plants, which management says is now back.
Low carbon was about 55% of volume in Q2 (lower end of 55-60% target), supporting blended margin.
Gas prices are about 2.5x the regular level, passed through to customers. Availability has been stable for about one quarter.

Steel tyre cord India demand is 2.5-3 lakh tons, mostly imported. Management expects radialisation (about 60% in India truck/bus) to drive growth. Management says there is no Indian domestic competitor; Bekaert is the main competitor.
Management says it will cap any single customer at 20-25% of total sales for steel cord.

qa_highlights.question: When will steel tyre cord and IHT/OHT translate into revenue and EBITDA, and what is the EBITDA per ton for specialty wire?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel tyre cord is in trials, with a second trial order expected in 10-15 days and commercialisation possible within the year. Specialty wire EBITDA is about Rs 15,000-20,000/ton, and IHT has turned EBITDA positive.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 EBITDA/ton came from inventory gains, and is Rs 7,000-7,500 conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gain was about Rs 200/ton, so underlying EBITDA was about Rs 7,800-7,900/ton. Management said its own strategy is Rs 7,000-7,500 and it is not guiding above that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% volume growth guidance for H2 only, and is it at risk from raw material shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: It applies to H2 FY27, meaning Q3 and Q4 volumes up 20% YoY. Management said raw material shortages are temporary and that lost days can be made up the following month.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of Sanand and Dadri CWIP and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: CWIP is Rs 177 crore, mostly Dadri 60,000 tons. Sanand needs about Rs 150 crore capex excluding land.

qa_highlights.question: Steel cord capacity plan and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is 20,000 tons, the target is 2 lakh tons, and realisation is about Rs 130-140/kg. Management said a major capex will follow customer approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Is Rs 7-7.5/kg the right base for H2 earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 7,000-7,500/ton is the H2 EBITDA commitment, and a better outcome is possible but not guided.

risks_watch: Raw material (wire rod) availability: shortages in October and supplier breakdowns could cut Q3 and Q4 volumes below the 20% growth guidance.
Gas prices at about 2.5x normal; management says pass-through to customers is in place, but this is a margin risk.
Q2 EBITDA/ton includes about Rs 200/ton inventory gain, so sustainability of the Rs 7,800-8,000 level is uncertain.
Steel cord commercialisation depends on customer approvals; management expects the first two quarters of ramp-up to be slow.
Sanand greenfield and Dadri ramp-up execution; capex may move beyond the stated timelines.
LRPC is loss-making at the margin due to industry overcapacity; management says it is less than 1% of sales.
544209|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on results and guidance, with management saying it prefers to guide conservatively. It was candid about near-term raw material disruption and the Q1 gas hit. Answers on steel cord timelines were more hedged, using phrases such as "hopefully" and "if everything goes well".
key_quotes: We have achieved our highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, and profit after tax.
So, we will rather be a little conservative than not delivering on our guidance.
Sir, our thought process is that we should maintain our margins at about Rs. 7,000 to Rs. 7,500.
In the long run, yes, we would definitely look at Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 10,000.

544210|2026-06.headline: Emcure Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, with EBITDA of INR 508 crore (19.7% margin) and PAT up 35-36%.
544210|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, led by international markets (up 34.2% to INR 1,485 crore) while India grew 10.2% to INR 1,095 crore. EBITDA rose 25.8% to INR 508 crore with margin up 50 bps to 19.7%, and PAT grew about 36% to INR 292 crore. Gross margin fell to 58.4% on geographic and product mix, and net debt rose to INR 1,103 crore. Management reiterated low-to-mid teens FY27 revenue growth (now toward the higher end) and 70-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion. Board changes were announced: Chairman Berjis Desai retires at AGM and CEO Satish Mehta becomes Chairman; Samit Mehta becomes COO and CEO of Gennova, which is now 100% owned.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,095 crore, +10.2% YoY. Ex-Sanofi OAD and Roche in-licensed brands, growth was about 6-7%. Price contributed about 4-5%, new launches 1-2%. Management says no channel filling in the quarter.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 537 crore, +32.8% YoY, driven by base business and liposomal amphotericin B (Ampho). Ampho is introduced in pretty much all countries, but tender-based procurement means lumpy orders.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 427 crore, +24.6% YoY, on new launches and share gains. Semaglutide filing expected in the next few months; Quebec launch via Dr. Reddy's is uncertain.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 522 crore, +44.8% YoY, led by ARV. About two-thirds of ROW was ARV this quarter; management expects ARV at about 50-55% of ROW for the full year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at low-to-mid teens, with management now more comfortable at the higher end of that range, driven by ARV order book visibility.
EBITDA margin expansion of 70-100 bps for FY27 reiterated.
FY27 gross margin guided at about 59% (earlier 60-61% framing), as higher international and ARV mix dilutes gross margin while EBITDA is accretive.
R&D for FY27 guided at 4-5% of revenue; spend expected to pick up in the rest of the year.
India growth expected in line with industry in Q2 FY27 and faster than industry in H2 FY27 as the Zuventus base effect eases.
Net debt expected to rise to about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 FY27 after the Mantra and Gennova payouts (INR 450-500 crore), then turn net cash by end-FY28.
Management expects sequential improvement each quarter.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were given on the call.
Gennova consolidated to 100% after acquiring a 12.05% minority stake; Mantra acquisition payout completed in July 2026.
demand_pricing: International constant-currency growth about 12% (about 12-13% per later answer), against about 6-7% FX tailwind at company level.
India price growth about 4-5% YoY; new launches 1-2%; the remainder is volume.

Poviztra (semaglutide biosimilar with Novo Nordisk) is growing month on month, but management says 40-50 brands have launched in the market and it is hard to separate channel stocking from consumption. Pricing was set very competitively.
Gross margin pressure reflects B2B-type international businesses (lower gross margin, higher EBITDA contribution), with Europe and ARV growing faster.
Management says Zuventus is stabilised and consolidated, now moving to acceleration.

qa_highlights.question: Is India's double-digit growth clean, or is there channel filling after Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no channel filling this quarter; growth is normalised and expected to improve further in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What share of ROW is ARV, and does FY27 base make FY28 harder?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds of ROW is ARV this quarter; full-year ARV share is expected at about 50-55% of ROW, with growth in both ARV and non-ARV.

qa_highlights.question: When will domestic growth be back in line with the market, and what is organic growth ex-in-licensed brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 FY27 is expected to be in line with industry and H2 faster. Ex-Sanofi OAD and Roche, growth was about 6-7%. Poviztra is a new launch; OAD moves into the base next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is constant-currency international growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-level FX impact was about 6-7%; international growth would have been about 12% in constant currency (12-13% in later answer).

qa_highlights.question: Why is Canada semaglutide a second-wave filing, and what is the Quebec launch timing with Dr. Reddy's?
qa_highlights.answer: Filing expected in the next few months, delayed because semaglutide was pursued as a global development. Quebec timing depends on Dr. Reddy's supply; management will defer to them.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline and where does it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix from Europe and ARV growth; FY27 gross margin guided at about 59%. Management says B2B international businesses are EBITDA-accretive despite lower gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: When will net debt turn to net cash and how does it trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt expected at about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 after acquisition payouts; net cash by about end-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 R&D spend?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is guided at 4-5% of revenue for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 99 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,103 crore (CFO also cited INR 1,560 crore in Q&A)

risks_watch: India growth: management guides Q2 FY27 in line with industry and H2 faster as the Zuventus base eases; Q1 organic ex-in-licensed growth was about 6-7%, so watch whether the Q2 and H2 acceleration materialises.

Poviztra (semaglutide biosimilar) competition: 40-50 brands launched, management cannot separate channel stocking from consumption and says the market needs 3-6 months to play out; pricing set very competitively.
Gross margin dilution from Europe, ARV and B2B international mix; FY27 guided at about 59% versus earlier 60-61% framing.

Net debt: reported INR 1,103 crore in the presentation, but the CFO cited INR 1,560 crore in Q&A; guidance of about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 FY27 and net cash by end-FY28 depends on working capital normalising.
Canada semaglutide: filing expected in the next few months (second wave); Quebec launch timing depends on Dr. Reddy's supply and management is deferring to them.
Lumpy European Ampho orders due to tender-based procurement, and ARV dependence in ROW (about 50-55% of ROW for FY27).
key_quotes: There is no channel filling in this quarter, Kunal. This is a normalized growth that we have.
I don't have a crystal ball here . As far as we are concerned, we are marketing innovation.
So, by the end of next quarter, we should have a net debt of close to around INR 1,450 crore.

544210|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the quarter, the 5-year plan and the Zuventus turnaround, with repeated bullish language on domestic acceleration. Management was more cautious and evasive on Poviztra market share and channel stocking, on Quebec semaglutide timing (deferred to Dr. Reddy's), and on the net debt figure, which differed between the CFO's remarks.

544213|2026-03.headline: Aelea Commodities H2 FY26 standalone revenue Rs 189.50 cr with 13.10% EBITDA margin and Rs 12.35 cr PAT; FY26 revenue up 112% to Rs 363.12 cr.
544213|2026-03.overview: Management reported H2 FY26 standalone revenue of Rs 189.50 cr, EBITDA of Rs 24.82 cr (13.10% margin) and PAT of Rs 12.35 cr (6.52% margin), versus losses a year earlier. For FY26, standalone revenue rose 112.07% to Rs 363.12 cr, EBITDA was Rs 40.20 cr (11.07% margin) and PAT Rs 21.19 cr, with EPS of Rs 10.40 versus Rs 0.65. Consolidated FY26 revenue was Rs 381.50 cr (up 109.46%) and PAT Rs 21.32 cr. The call was dominated by a 10-year (FY37) strategy presentation, with the Q&A focused on higher finance costs, working capital and inventory build, CNSL plant timing, and FY27 guidance, which was not quantified.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone revenue from operations, H2 FY26

financial_highlights.change: Compared with losses in the corresponding period last year

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated revenue from operations, H2 FY26

segments.name: Cashew kernel processing (core)
segments.commentary: Processes raw cashew nuts (RCN) into wholes and pieces; average mix 63% wholes and 37% pieces, with average kernel realisation of about Rs 590-595/kg. Around 16,000 tonnes of RCN processed in H2 and a similar volume in H1. About 95% of raw material is African-origin, sourced via merchant traders.

segments.name: CNSL / by-products (oil extraction, solar)
segments.commentary: CNSL extraction facility of above 50 MT is under construction, with management guiding to benefits from around H2 FY27 and a product-level EBITDA margin of about 10%. Rooftop solar is installed; ground-mounted solar awaits government approval. B2C consumer pouches are about 1% of sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27: management expects top-line and bottom-line growth at rates similar to FY26, but declined to give a revenue number; an analyst's Rs 500 cr FY27 revenue figure was not confirmed.
FY28: too early to comment; management said it will revisit after about six more months of work.
EBITDA margin: management says the company normally operates at around 10-11% EBITDA margin, which it says it has broadly met.
Finance cost: management expects it to stay at similar or higher levels as the company deepens its value chain, and said absolute figures will grow with scale.
CNSL plant: construction nearly complete with about 30 days of works remaining; commissioning depends on government approvals. Phase 3 capex is expected later in the year.
B2C: targeted at roughly 13-15% EBITDA margin in the long run, pursued through a product basket rather than e-commerce.
capex_capacity: Capacity scaling from 40 MT/day to 140 MT/day, which management says is backed by IPO proceeds; current utilisation about 94-95%.
Phase 2 (CNSL) capex is already committed and underway, with only a small amount pending; Phase 3 capex is expected in the later part of the year.
Ground-mounted solar is pending government approval because of changes to norms for consuming solar power; rooftop solar is complete.
Long-term 2037 strategy targets 1,000 MT/day cashew capacity, plus almond, walnut, pistachio and makhana processing (makhana with a 50-tonne capacity plan).
A Maharashtra cultivation project and capex was flagged by an analyst as not updated; management said it is still being worked on and not crystallised.
demand_pricing: Management said processing is constrained by raw-material quality rather than machine capacity; the company says it fully used its enhanced capacity during H2.
Raw-material sourcing has moved deeper into the value chain (direct sourcing at about 60-65%), which lifted margins but raised working capital and finance costs.
Geopolitical disruption: longer sea transit from Africa, currency swings of around 50 paise a day, and higher RCN price volatility, with no material price impact yet.
Institutional clients are a stated priority for longer-term visibility, but institutions are about one-fifth the size of general trade in the market.
Inventory rose to about Rs 100 cr and management expects it to increase further with growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise from about Rs 2 cr to Rs 8 cr?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company moved deeper into the value chain, where suppliers do not give credit, but margins are better. Finance cost is expected to stay at similar or higher levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 and FY28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth is expected to be similar to FY26 in rate, with no numbers given. FY28 comment deferred about six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNSL plant timeline and contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction nearly complete with approvals pending; benefits expected around H2. Management said CNSL adds EBITDA rather than top line, at about 10% product-level EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and RCN volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 94-95%. About 16,000 tonnes of RCN were processed in H2, roughly the same as H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix between Africa and India?
qa_highlights.answer: About 95% of processing is African-origin, sourced through merchant traders based in Singapore or Dubai, and 5% is local.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2C strategy and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C is about 1% of sales. Management said it will grow organically rather than through heavy marketing, targeting roughly 13-15% EBITDA margin on a product basket.

risks_watch: Working capital and finance cost: rising short-term borrowing and inventory (about Rs 100 cr) as sourcing deepens; management gave no debt-to-equity red line.
CNSL and ground-mounted solar commissioning depends on government approvals, which have no fixed timeline.
Geopolitical and shipping disruption from Africa, with longer transit and higher currency and RCN price volatility.
Management declined to quantify FY27 or FY28 numbers; watch whether growth matches the stated similar rate.
Related-party or structural details on the Maharashtra project remain unclear and not yet crystallised.
544213|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the 10-year strategy and FY26 results, but evasive on forward numbers: it repeatedly declined to give FY27 or FY28 figures, the Maharashtra project and timelines, and it deflected on B2C sales and the cause of higher finance cost.
key_quotes: So, for FY27, we are likely to continue our growth rate.

At the end of the day, it's cashew and you, me, or whoever goes at buying it would like to see what is the per gram, per 100 gram price and compare it with wherever you are, other source of buying is.
So we have roughly 95% of the entire processing depending on the African origins only.

544222|2026-03.headline: Akums Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA rose 61.6% YoY to INR152 crore (13.1% margin), with FY26 revenue up 5.8% to INR4,359 crore.
544222|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,158 crore, up 9.7% YoY and flat QoQ, while adjusted EBITDA reached INR152 crore, driven by CDMO profitability and trade generics turning EBITDA positive. Reported Q4 PAT of INR81 crore was held down versus the prior year by a large deferred tax asset benefit in the base; PBT rose to INR121 crore from INR75 crore. FY26 PAT fell to INR256 crore from INR344 crore, which included a INR106 crore DTA benefit in FY25. Management guided to double-digit CDMO volume growth in H1 FY27, a sharp narrowing of API losses, and a Zambia supply contract of about $25 million per year from Q2 FY27.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR3,485 crore (+8.6%) and EBITDA INR467 crore (+2.9%). Q4 revenue INR952 crore (+13.4% YoY, +4% QoQ) and EBITDA INR137 crore (+54.9% YoY, +9.1% QoQ); management cited operating leverage from better utilisation and newer facilities.

segments.name: Domestic branded formulations (Akumentis)

544225|2026-03.overview: Management framed Q4 FY26 as a reset quarter: gross margin reached 38.5% (33.5% excluding PLI) versus 13.7% a year earlier, and consolidated OpEx including leases fell to Rs 428 crore from Rs 844 crore. Revenue was weak because deliveries were depressed by internal service and operations fixes, with FY26 consolidated revenue at Rs 2,253 crore on 173,794 deliveries. Management says registrations have recovered for three months, orders are running ahead of registrations, and Q1 FY27 guidance is 40,000-45,000 orders and Rs 500-550 crore revenue. The Gigafactory's first 3 GWh is in ramp-up with the remaining 3.5 GWh slated for June, and the company is pushing Shakti and Roadster bike growth.

financial_highlights.change: vs 34.3% in Q3 FY26 and 13.7% in Q4 FY25
first operating cash flow positive quarter

financial_highlights.metric: Auto segment CFO / FCF Q4 FY26
financial_highlights.value: Rs 213 crore CFO, Rs 173 crore FCF

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated OpEx incl. leases Q4 FY26
financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 844 crore in Q4 FY25
vs over Rs 500 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,550-1,600 crore gross cash; about Rs 2,500 crore debt; net debt about Rs 950 crore

segments.name: Auto (electric two-wheelers)
segments.commentary: Generates 100% of revenue today; Auto CFO Rs 213 crore and FCF Rs 173 crore in Q4 FY26. Roadster bikes are about 15% of April gross orders, with Ola holding about 50% share of electric motorcycles.

segments.name: Cell (Gigafactory)
segments.commentary: 2.5 GWh operational, with 6 GWh installation largely complete; commercialisation of the full 6 GWh expected by end of Q1 FY27. Still in investment phase, with cell CapEx for 6 GWh essentially done apart from payouts in Q1-Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Shakti / Mahashakti (ESS)
segments.commentary: Shakti launched last quarter and supply-constrained because cells are prioritised for Auto; Mahashakti grid storage on a prismatic LFP platform is in product development with details due over the next couple of quarters.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27: 40,000-45,000 orders and consolidated revenue of Rs 500-550 crore, nearly double Q4 level.
Adjusted operating EBITDA breakeven at about 20,000-25,000 units per month on consolidated basis, subject to pricing mix and commodity conditions.
Consolidated OpEx to move toward about Rs 350 crore, with management also citing Rs 300-350 crore next quarter and Rs 100-120 crore per month in coming quarters.
Auto expected to reach adjusted operating EBITDA and cash flow positivity through FY27.
Operating cash burn of Rs 300-500 crore over FY27 as volumes rise; positive after 20,000-25,000 orders per month. Debt repayments of Rs 400+ crore in FY27.

Gigafactory: about 2+ GWh output by September 2026; FY27 allocation about 2 GWh captive, 1+ GWh external auto sales, remainder for Shakti/Mahashakti. Full vehicle portfolio to move to own cells by September 2026.
Maintenance CapEx for Auto about Rs 50 crore per year; R&D to be mid-single-digit % of revenue as revenue ramps.
Expansion from 6 GWh to 20 GWh and prismatic capacity contingent on raising capital at cell subsidiary level, planned this financial year.
capex_capacity: Auto capacity of up to 1 million units per year already built; no meaningful incremental CapEx needed to scale.
Gigafactory: 2.5 GWh operational; 3 GWh commissioned and ramping; remaining 3.5 GWh to be completed in June 2026 after container delays linked to the Iran war.
Combined asset base can support about Rs 15,000-20,000 crore annual revenue across Auto and Cell without meaningful incremental CapEx.
Expansion beyond 6 GWh to 20 GWh, and prismatic cell capacity, to be funded by separate capital raise at cell subsidiary.
demand_pricing: Registrations: about 10,000 in March, 12,000 in April (up 20% MoM while the broader e-2W industry fell over 22%), and May trending to 14,000-15,000; management expects 17,000-18,000 units per month from rebound, then 20,000-22,000 over the next quarter.
Average ASP about Rs 1.4 lakh; gross profit about Rs 50,000 per vehicle. Q4 ASP was lowered by a revenue-recognition change for extended warranty packages, a one-time hit of about Rs 20-30 crore.
Company runs very low free inventory of 3-4 days and has an auto backlog; no dealer model, so orders, registrations and deliveries are reported separately.
Own 4680 cells cheaper than imported cells on BOM even at low volume; expected 10-15% advantage at 6 GWh including overheads.
Brand recall and NPS are cited as above industry averages; no TV or print advertising at present, though some advertising may come in coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 revenue not reflect strong March sales and the orders data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March registrations were about 10,000 and April about 12,000, with May trending 14,000-15,000; Q4 revenue was low because operations were being fixed and volumes restarted only mid-March, with production backlog spilling into Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bridge from current volumes to the 20,000 units/month breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebound should reach about 17,000-18,000 units per month including about 15% bikes; better service stability and inventory availability could take volumes to 20,000-22,000 over the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Advantage of own cells versus imported cells?
qa_highlights.answer: Own cells are already cheaper on pure BOM even at low volumes; at 6 GWh with overheads the advantage is expected to be 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why not advertise in print media, and is the Rs 2,000 crore cell monetisation progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Company prefers word-of-mouth and does not do TV or IPL sponsorship; may advertise in coming months. Cell monetisation requires a subsidiary-level capital raise; management has inbound PE interest but gave no timing beyond 'in due course'.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the one-time ASP change and will prior quarters be restated?
qa_highlights.answer: Extended warranty packages moved from upfront to deferred revenue recognition after discussion with auditors, a Rs 20-30 crore impact already baked into published numbers; no restatement of prior quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 CapEx, R&D and cash burn outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Auto maintenance CapEx about Rs 50 crore per year, PPE CapEx below Rs 50 crore; cell CapEx for 6 GWh essentially complete; R&D mid-single-digit % of revenue; operating cash burn Rs 300-500 crore in FY27, turning positive after 20,000-25,000 orders per month.

qa_highlights.question: Status of solid-state and sodium-ion cell technologies?
qa_highlights.answer: Both are at lab scale; focus is on ramping 46-series NMC, with an LFP cell to start ramping in the factory next quarter; solid-state and sodium to be commercialised as the industry matures.

qa_highlights.question: Why are service issues linked to parts unavailability, and why NMC for Shakti?
qa_highlights.answer: Parts were not stocked at service centres and procurement was reactive (20-30 day fulfilment); now stocked locally and procured on forecasts. Shakti uses NMC today and will move to LFP next quarter; Shakti ramp is slower because NMC 46-series goes to Auto.

risks_watch: Volume recovery must reach 20,000-25,000 units per month for adjusted EBITDA breakeven; Q1 FY27 guidance is 40,000-45,000 orders versus registrations trending at 14,000-15,000 in May.
Gigafactory ramp: 3 GWh still ramping, 3.5 GWh due in June, and 2+ GWh output targeted by September; supply-chain localisation and commodity (lithium upcycle) pressures.
Funding dependence: 20 GWh expansion and prismatic capacity require a subsidiary capital raise with no firm timeline; net debt about Rs 950 crore and Rs 400+ crore repayments in FY27.
Service and parts supply chain still incomplete; store experience described as improved but not yet at earlier levels.
Bike EV and Roadster ramp and new product launches (Mahashakti, LFP Shakti) depend on supply and timing; an Analyst Day is planned in one to two months.
Margin sustainability: management flagged short-term commodity pressure and aggressive growth investment in the last month or two.
544225|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins, cash flow and demand recovery, with numbers given for most claims. Cautious and less specific on the cell monetisation, timelines for the 20 GWh expansion, and service execution, where answers were often deferred to later quarters.
key_quotes: Q4 was the first operating cash flow positive quarter.
And for our Auto business, there is no more CapEx needed as we scale up.
So, by end of next quarter, which is September, we expect our Gigafactory to be producing about 2+ GWh already.
We don't plan to have any dealerships in our auto business, we believe our strategy is correct.

544225|2026-06.headline: Ola Electric Q1 FY27 deliveries nearly doubled QoQ to ~39,200 units, Auto revenue ₹455 crore (+72% QoQ), Auto gross margin 30.5%.
544225|2026-06.overview: Ola returned to volume growth in Q1 FY27, with deliveries of ~39,200 units (nearly 2x QoQ) and orders of ~44,000, while electric two-wheeler registrations grew 97% against a market up ~17% QoQ, lifting share from 5.1% to 8.4%. Auto revenue rose 72% QoQ to ₹455 crore with gross profit of ₹139 crore and Auto gross margin held at 30.5%. Consolidated opex fell 22% QoQ to ₹333 crore (including a ~₹55 crore one-time reversal of a Cell ACC PLI penalty provision), and adjusted operating EBITDA improved to –₹195 crore from –₹326 crore in Q4 FY26. Management pivoted Auto distribution from company-owned to a multi-channel model with dealers, with the first batch slated to go live on Janmashtami (4 September), and reiterated a Cell gigafactory ramp to 6 GWh.

financial_highlights.change: -22% QoQ from ₹428 crore in Q4; ~₹380 crore excluding ~₹55 crore one-time PLI provision reversal
from 5.1%; Ola registrations +97% QoQ vs market ~+17%

segments.name: Auto (scooters, motorcycles)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹455 crore (+72% QoQ), gross profit ₹139 crore, gross margin 30.5%. Premium business recovering; motorcycles starting to grow in northern plains. Roadster a small minority of sales; 9.1 kWh variant supply constrained by 4680 cell shortage.

segments.name: Cell business
segments.commentary: 4680 NMC cells commercially deployed; a few hundred thousand cells produced and in customer vehicles. Production paused in Q1 to take capacity from 2.5 GWh to 6 GWh; restart expected later in August. 46100 LFP cell BIS-certified. Yields high-70s to ~80% at pause, target >90% within a quarter of restart.

segments.name: Ola Shakti / Mahashakti (energy storage)
segments.commentary: Only a few hundred NMC-based Shakti units delivered in Q1, no meaningful revenue; NMC version pared back on sub-target margins. Shakti Gen 2 (LFP) to be announced 15 August. First Mahashakti MoU with Axis Energy for 20 GWh over 5-6 years; early Mahashakti revenue hoped for Q3 or Q4.

guidance_outlook: Auto ASP to stay broadly around ₹1.25 lakh, plus or minus 5%.
Auto gross margin target ~30-32%; expected to hold above 30% over next one to two quarters and improve as commodity prices ease.
Opex to fall to ₹300-325 crore range over the next couple of quarters.
Gross margin steady to slightly growing and volumes steady to slightly growing while cutting opex; no formal FY volume guidance.

Gigafactory at 6 GWh to be fully commissioned in Q1 FY27 quarter (also stated as operational by September); expansion from 6 GWh to 20 GWh (prismatic) targeted in FY27, funded by Cell-company equity rather than parent equity.
Service revenue target ~₹400-500 crore by FY2027-28 from installed base of over one million customers.
Capex beyond Cell project about ₹30-50 crore; ₹50 crore used as target number.
Pending 4680-cell Roadster deliveries to be completed over Q2 and Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Cell capacity: 2.5 GWh installed, production paused for ~2-3 months to take capacity to 6 GWh; installation expected to finish within a week to ten days, with restart later in August.
Auto factory scaled to ~1 million units per year; no material Auto capex foreseen.
Remaining Cell capex funded through debt; equity contribution largely complete.
Ongoing capex beyond Cell project ~₹30-50 crore; ₹50 crore used as target.
Prismatic cell R&D expected complete by end of CY2026; 6 to 20 GWh expansion intended to be equity-funded at the Cell company.
Depreciation policy aligned to industry norms, causing ~₹10-20 crore delta.
demand_pricing: Ola registrations +97% QoQ vs electric 2W market +17%; share 5.1% to 8.4%; growth across all regions.
Electric 2W penetration in India crossed 10% for the first time in June 2026.
ASP fell sharply QoQ, ~90% due to product mix; premium scooter sales recovering.

Dealer model: ~500 current touchpoints (analyst figure); company stores to become fewer, larger experience centres; ~1,000 expressions of interest from prospective dealers; 20-30 dealers engaged for about a month before announcement.
Service challenges attributed to parts availability (vendor issues, geopolitical factors); dealers to stock parts on cash-and-carry basis.
Shakti to be sold through company stores, automotive dealers and industry-specific inverter/battery channels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ASP decline sharply sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 90% to product mix; ASP guided at ~₹1.25 lakh ±5%.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year volume guidance and Q4 exit rate?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance; management expects steady growth but declined quarter-on-quarter numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Own-cell penetration and Shakti revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: A few thousand own-cell vehicles on road; about 3 of ~9-10 SKUs use 4680 cells. Shakti Gen 1 (NMC) had no meaningful revenue; Gen 2 (LFP) on 15 August.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Beyond the Cell project, capex ~₹30-50 crore, with ₹50 crore as target; Auto needs hardly any capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Policy aligned to industry norms after aggressive depreciation; delta ~₹10-20 crore, no write-off mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: LFP vs NMC mix and 20 GWh expansion timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all Auto to move to LFP over time, ~20% of Auto stays NMC; Shakti/Mahashakti all LFP. 20 GWh expansion (prismatic) in FY27 with separate Cell-company equity; yields high-70s to ~80% at pause.

qa_highlights.question: Scale of energy storage opportunity and Axis Energy MoU?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites CEA estimate of ~400 GWh needed over 5-6 years, which it views as an underestimate; Mahashakti expected to have round-trip efficiency a few points above peers and safety above standard 5 MWh containers.

qa_highlights.question: Roadster contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Small minority of sales; deliveries slightly below orders in Q1 due to 4680 cell shortage.

risks_watch: Cell production paused to take capacity from 2.5 GWh to 6 GWh; restart guided for later in August, with yields at high-70s to ~80% at pause and a target above 90% within a quarter of restart.
Roadster deliveries constrained by 4680-cell shortage; pending vehicles to be delivered over Q2 and Q3 FY27.

Dealer model rollout: first batch slated for Janmashtami (4 September); management declined to share a dealership count target, and service/parts availability depends on dealers' cash-and-carry parts stocking.
No formal FY27 volume guidance; management declined to give quarter-on-quarter or Q4 exit rate, so volume trajectory after Q1 remains unquantified.
Product announcements on 15 August (Shakti Gen 2 LFP, Mahashakti details); early Mahashakti revenue hoped for Q3 or Q4, with the Axis Energy customer identity not disclosed.
20 GWh prismatic expansion targeted in FY27, funded by separate Cell-company equity that is yet to be raised; prismatic R&D expected complete by end of CY2026.
Auto gross margin target of ~30-32% depends on commodity prices easing; management expects margins above 30% for the next one to two quarters.
key_quotes: Deliveries increased to approximately 39,200 units, nearly doubling quarter-on-quarter, while orders increased to approximately 44,000.
Over the next couple of quarters, we expect opex to come down into the ₹300-325 crore range, which is where our target is.
We will not give formal guidance or a forecast, but I can explain our approach.
Please wait until later this month, when we will have some announcements on that.
544225|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's volume recovery, market share gain and opex reduction, and on margin stability above 30%. Noticeably cautious on forward volumes, declining to give formal guidance, a dealer count target, Mahashakti revenue specifics or the Axis Energy customer identity.

544226|2026-03.headline: FirstCry Q4 FY26: consol revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr for FY26; Q4 adjusted EBITDA up 18% to ₹118.7 Cr amid India gross margin pressure.
544226|2026-03.overview: Brainbees (FirstCry) reported Q4 and FY26 with consolidated FY26 revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr, adjusted EBITDA up 24% to about ₹486 Cr, and free cash flow positive for the full year. India multi-channel grew 11.4% in Q4 but gross margin fell on diaper price competition from quick-commerce and horizontal players, plus a transitory manufacturing hit from rupee depreciation and crude-linked inputs. Management says the offline channel grew about 15% in Q4 after a product-mix shift, and that RocketBees and Qwik delivery initiatives are lifting service levels, with the benefit expected to show in FY27. International losses fell 35% in FY26 and GlobalBees core categories grew 28%.

segments.name: India multi-channel
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +11.4% and FY26 revenue +9%; GMV +11% in FY26, crossing $1 billion for the first time. Management says the segment stayed PAT and cash flow positive in FY26. Non-diapering is over 85% of GMV; diapering (about 15% of business) faces heavy price competition.

segments.name: International (UAE and KSA)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue above $100 million, growing about 10% in FY26; Q4 revenue +9%. Gross margin rose 240 bps for FY26 (470 bps in Q4). Management did not give a timeline for reaching break-even.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: FY26 consolidated revenue +20% (organic, after brand rationalisation) and core categories +28%. Adjusted EBITDA post-corporate expenses was 5.8% of revenue in Q4 (₹26.5 Cr) and about 3% for FY26 after ESOP cost. Brand rationalisation is expected to finish by end Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Others (preschool)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue +11% with EBITDA margin about 27% (vs 24% in FY25). Preschools more than doubled from 208 at end FY24, and enrolled students are almost 3x in two years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India multi-channel GMV and revenue growth guided to be much superior to FY26; management expects sequential quarterly improvement to continue.
India multi-channel FY27 EBITDA (rupee terms) guided to grow double digits, per management's 'should' answer; margin expansion expected outside diapering.
Gross margin loss from the Q3 diaper competition (about 140 bps) expected to take 4-6 quarters to reverse; manufacturing-related loss expected to be recovered from Q2 FY27 via pass-through.
Company-owned and FOFO stores: about 100 openings planned in FY27 after pausing COCO openings in FY26 (10 COCO stores added in FY26).
Qwik expected to reach roughly 10% of total B2C online shipments over FY27; RocketBees already at 40%+ of online delivery volume, with a target of 45-50% by mid-2026.
Continued international loss reduction in FY27; management aims to take losses to zero as early as possible.
capex_capacity: RocketBees own-network coverage grew from 13 cities (Q2) to 22 (Q3) to 62 cities (Q4); management aims to cross 50 cities by next quarter-end.
Qwik quick-delivery pilot began 1 Dec 2025 and now runs in 5 cities; it delivers in under 3 hours and is already over 20% of online orders in the covered catchments.
Logistics cost front-loading of about 40-60 bps for a few quarters until RocketBees and Qwik networks mature.
Asset-light delivery model: dedicated regional first-mile and mid-mile partners and dedicated last-mile partners on in-house technology.
Offline initiative (width-to-depth product assortment change) went live in Q4 FY26 and drove about 15% offline GMV growth.
Management says on-time delivery exceeds 92%.
demand_pricing: Diapering faces irrational price competition from quick-commerce and horizontal platforms (listed and unlisted); management expects this to last 4-6 quarters.
Q4 online GMV grew about 10.5%, and online growth held at about 11-12% across all four quarters of FY26. Offline GMV grew about 15% in Q4.
Annual unique transacting customers in India multi-channel: 11 million.
India multi-channel Q4 orders +10% and GMV +12%; AOV in International is about 4x India's.
Management says the Middle East has seen some moderation in consumer sentiment and import complexities, but it is 'beyond anyone's control'.
Ages 6-12 is the fastest-growing age cohort in India multi-channel.

qa_highlights.question: What share of orders now goes through FirstCry's own delivery network, and what is the logistics cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Share rose from about 28% at end Q3 to over 40% at end March 2026, with a target of 45-50% by mid-year. Logistics cost is front-loaded by about 40-60 bps for a few quarters until networks mature.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company pause COCO store openings in FY26, and what is the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Openings were paused for capital efficiency given macro conditions. Management plans about 100 stores in FY27 across COCO and FOFO formats, citing the best offline growth in seven quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is the gross margin pressure in diapering split between competition and input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: The 140 bps Q3 competitive hit has continued into Q4. The remaining manufacturing-related hit from rupee depreciation and crude-linked inputs is transitory and expected to be recovered from Q2 FY27 as prices are passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the online growth slowdown structural, given offline grew faster than the 11% overall?
qa_highlights.answer: Online GMV grew about 10.5% in Q4 and 11-12% through FY26. Management expects RocketBees and Qwik to lift online growth in FY27, with results lagging. Product mix between online and offline has not changed.

qa_highlights.question: Can India multi-channel EBITDA grow double digits in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing recovery of the manufacturing hit by Q2 (three quarters of benefit), continued margin expansion in the non-diaper categories, and operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Middle East situation affecting international revenue and break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer sentiment has moderated and import complexities have emerged. Management sees this as an opportunity to optimise discounting and marketing and to improve home-brand mix, and says the focus remains sustainable growth over top-line chasing.

risks_watch: Diaper price war from quick-commerce and horizontal platforms could keep gross margins under pressure beyond the 4-6 quarter window management has given.
Management has tied the FY27 recovery to a Q2 pass-through of manufacturing costs, with rupee depreciation and crude prices as the swing factors.
Middle East consumer sentiment and import complexities could slow International, where revenue growth was about 9-10%.
Online growth has run at about 10-12% and needs to accelerate in FY27 for the stated guidance to hold.
GlobalBees brand rationalisation is due to finish by end Q1 FY27; the consolidated growth figure will lag until then.
Management declined to quantify AI-driven savings, saying the number will come in later quarterly updates. It also said there have been no buyback or acquisition discussions.
544226|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the India multi-channel recovery and the FY27 growth outlook, backed by the offline and delivery-network metrics. Cautious and somewhat deflecting on diaper margins, the Middle East, and quantifying AI benefits, which management said would come in later updates.
key_quotes: We are happy to state that we continue to remain PAT and cash flow positive for an India multi-channel business for the entire FY26.
So, from Q2 onwards, the gross margin loss because of crude-linked raw metal prices and rupee depreciation should be covered.
We are already crossing 20% of our overall online orders under our Qwik initiative and where we are able to deliver the customer in less than 3 hours.
It's not small. It's going to be meaningful.

544226|2026-06.headline: Brainbees Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to ₹2,106 crore, but India multi-channel gross margin fell ~260 bps YoY, holding adjusted EBITDA margin at 4.24%.
544226|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to ₹2,106 crore, with GMV up 12% to ₹2,807 crore and AUTC up 10% to 11.8 million. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 4.24% from 4.98%, and gross margin dropped to 36.5% from 38.5%, mainly from India multi-channel diapering competition and manufacturing cost pass-through lag. Management said diapering competition is easing and that the crude/rupee cost pass-through completes by end-Q2, but gave no firm timeline for margin recovery. Growth drivers cited were RocketBees (over 50% of online shipments), FC Qwik (125,000 shipments in June across 12 cities) and offline GMV growth of 15%.

segments.name: India multi-channel
segments.commentary: Revenue +18% YoY, best in seven quarters; GMV +12%, orders +12%, AUTC +10%. Non-diapering is ~85% of GMV; gross margin down ~260 bps YoY and EBITDA margin down ~290 bps YoY on diapering competition and manufacturing input costs. Remains PAT positive.

segments.name: International (Middle East)
segments.commentary: Revenue +12% YoY, AUTC +7%, GMV +9%. Adjusted EBITDA loss reduced 22% YoY; loss-to-revenue improved from 10% to 7%. Management targets EBITDA neutrality but gave no timeline.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat due to a planned warehouse and inventory transition for one core brand, expected to complete in Q2 with growth recovering from Q3. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 3.9% from 1%.

segments.name: Preschool (FirstCry Intellitots)
segments.commentary: Revenue +47% to ₹19 crore and adjusted EBITDA +65% to ₹5 crore. Over 500 preschools; management targets at least 1,000 over the next couple of years, organically, with no M&A being evaluated.

guidance_outlook: Management expects India multi-channel growth to stay elevated for subsequent FY27 quarters, citing RocketBees, FC Qwik and offline store expansion.
Crude/rupee-linked price increases in manufacturing expected to be fully passed on by end-Q2 FY27, with full margin normalisation for that component from Q3.
Diapering margin recovery expected over four to six quarters, with competitive intensity easing in July and August per management.
Adding around 100 net offline stores in FY27 (management said 90-100); FY28 expansion expected to be larger.
Management declined to give a timeline for International EBITDA breakeven, pointing to input metrics instead.
Management said the 280 bps gross margin gap should 'dramatically' reduce, but gave no quantified target for the full year.
capex_capacity: Offline store expansion was paused for two quarters to realign the product portfolio; now resuming with ~100 net new stores targeted in FY27.
RocketBees expanded from 62 to 72 cities and now handles over 50% of online shipments, a target set two quarters ago and met by June 2026. Delivery turnaround time improved ~20%.
FC Qwik (2-hour quick delivery) grew from ~60,000 shipments in five cities in March to 125,000 in 12 cities in June. Management targets 10% of total shipments on FC Qwik and 20% in specific pincodes.
Manufacturing business is passing crude-linked raw material and rupee-depreciation cost increases to customers.
demand_pricing: Diapering faces heightened competition from quick commerce discounting and new entrants. Management says branded diapering has started improving in Q1 and competitive intensity is softer in July and August.
Non-diapering categories (~85% of GMV, fashion >50% of GMV, home brands >50% of business) are performing well; management said gross margin is expected to improve through home brand and fashion mix.
GMV growth (12%) trails India revenue growth (18%) because the revenue line includes manufacturing and the GMV is at MRP, with GST 2.0 reducing MRP from Q2.
Management said non-diapering consumables are about 15% of India GMV, with healthy margins and no challenge from quick commerce.
Offline GMV grew 15% in Q1 after the width-to-depth assortment change, which added lower price points without a material gross margin impact.

financial_highlights.value: Down ~260 bps YoY (~20 bps recovered vs Q4's 280 bps drop)

financial_highlights.metric: International adjusted EBITDA loss as % of revenue
GlobalBees adjusted EBITDA margin (post corporate expenses)

qa_highlights.question: Jay Laddha asked how much of the manufacturing-related gross margin loss was recovered in Q1 and whether International breakeven timing or FY27 guidance had any update.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India multi-channel gross margin recovered about 20 bps of the 280 bps Q4 drop, with full pass-through of crude and rupee costs by end-Q2. On International, Abhinav Sharma declined to give a breakeven quarter, pointing to inputs (home brand mix, high-margin brand curation, quality customer acquisition); the loss-to-revenue ratio moved from -16% in March 2025 to -7% in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Kumar asked whether India multi-channel growth can be sustained next quarter and when margin will recover.
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to remain elevated for the next few quarters on RocketBees, FC Qwik and offline stores. Margin recovery is expected faster than the 4-6 quarter diapering normalisation, with diapering competition easing in July and August and crude/rupee pass-through complete by end-Q2, full recovery likely from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Ranodeep Sen asked about the company's right to win in diapering against pharmacy and private-label entrants, and whether M&A is being considered in preschool.
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goel said diapering retention is hard for private labels and that quick commerce discounting is temporary; branded diapering showed some improvement in Q1. Supam Maheshwari said FC Qwik and the full-destination model support retention. qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki asked whether the sequential India multi-channel EBITDA margin decline is due to crude-linked inflation and whether H2 EBITDA margin will at least match last year.

For FY26, revenue rose 23.58% to INR8,081.58 million and EBITDA was INR939.29 million, with margins hit by higher manpower cost, tech spend, ETS price competition and a one-time doubtful-debt provision of about INR80 million. Analysts pressed on margin compression, falling revenue per trip and competitive pricing in ETS; management attributed the trend partly to shorter trips and airport transfers.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 20-25 bps FY27 NIM compression, and is there any pricing relief or PLR hike possibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the compression mainly to yield decline: high-yield book is running off while new business comes in at lower yields in a stable rate regime. Acquisition pricing has been stable, and no large-scale upward pricing move is assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 credit cost drop to 5 bps? Are there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, two one-offs: a Q4 FY26 Stage 2 provision build that was not repeated, and a roughly INR2,300 crore assignment that released Stage 1 provisions. Management said to treat it as about 5 bps; the FY27 guide stays at 10-15 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM fall 13-14 bps when spreads were flat and cost of funds fell 7 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: The spread is computed on period-end portfolio yield versus average cost of funds, so it moved only 3-4 bps. The margin decline is from portfolio yield compression, which will continue through FY27 and offset the cost-of-funds benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of funds outlook for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds is expected to be sideways in Q2 FY27 with a downward bias, helped by hedging, repayment of older high-cost borrowings and resets of some older borrowings to lower rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the LAP and DF Stage 2 to Stage 3 movement not raising provisions, and is there stress in LAP?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP provisions are formula-based on DPD, so roll-backs and roll-ins net off; the LAP movement was INR18 crore in total, not one account. DF provisioning was already held at 48-49% on the account. Management cited LAP GNPA in a 46-76 bps range over seven quarters and said there is no segment or geography concern.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 1 provisions stay flat despite a INR7,500 crore rise in Stage 1 assets?
qa_highlights.answer: The annual January ECL recalibration lowered Stage 1 rates on most portfolios because credit performance was stronger, and the mix of new and attrited customers also shifted. Management said there is no simple pool-to-pool calculation.

risks_watch: NIM compression of 20-25 bps for FY27 with Q2-Q3 further declines of 6-10 bps; watch yield on new disbursements vs run-off.

Sambhav ticket size and Tier 2/3 expansion may dilute average ticket size and yield; the affordable segment is ramping.

Cost of funds fell 17 bps QoQ to about 7.0% from fixed-to-floating NCD conversion, offsetting a 10 bps portfolio yield decline, so NIM dipped 2 bps to 3.7%. Management said the repo hike will pass through roughly 80% to both liabilities and assets, but acquisition pricing from banks is still unclear and is the main margin and attrition risk. Guidance on AUM growth (21-23%) and NIM compression (~25 bps for the year) was not revised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did developer finance decline QoQ, and what is the strategy for the DF book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher repayments from project cash flows plus slower disbursements drove the decline, not a conscious strategy. DF sanctions rose sharply in H1, and the target is 15-17% of the portfolio, with recovery expected in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the repo hikes compress margins and how much pass-through is possible on the prime side?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80-82% of repo hikes flow through to cost of funds and to portfolio pricing, so the main margin risk is on acquisition pricing. If prime acquisition pricing lags, attrition and BT-out rise and the company shifts toward non-prime.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the fall in fee income?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income rose on higher insurance income (attachment rates higher with Sambhav growth) and higher foreclosure income in the quarter, not a decline. Fee-related expenses are marginal and range-bound.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20 bps cost of funds decline a one-off, and what is the exit COF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a starting point, not a one-off, though part came from one-time maturity of high-priced borrowings. Three 25 bps hikes would take COF up about 61 bps, from roughly 7% in September to about 7.6% by March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did home loan originations decline QoQ, and what is the YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly movements are seasonal and the company tracks AUM rather than disbursals. Home loan disbursal growth was 24% YoY, close to the company's 25% disbursement growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will guidance be revised given NIM expansion this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no revision for now. NIM compression of about 25 bps is still expected, and AUM growth could slow to 22-23% if acquisition pricing lags, given the rise in BT-out rates.

Management attributed growth to volumes across M&HCV, trailers and tractors, and said the extrusion axle beam line is now in production. Steel and conversion-cost pass-throughs are being settled, with the tractor industry already settled from April 1 and CV settlement pending. Management said Q1 is in line with its FY27 targets, though June-July demand is seasonally subdued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export target and the size of the European tier 1 order?

qa_highlights.question: Is the trailer-axle growth of about 34% share gain, given single-digit industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was largely Q4 FY26 order spillover. Management declined to comment on market share; capacity expansion should allow further growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst margin quarter behind us, with QoQ expansion ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects QoQ margin expansion. Steel pass-through is retrospective but will come in gradually. Conversion cost increase is the larger factor.

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-five customer revenue fall between DRHP and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the top-five share fell from about 60-63% to 58-59% through diversification, and it would check the INR figures.

qa_highlights.question: What are utilisation and debt plans, and does capex need to increase?
qa_highlights.answer: No further forging or casting capex is needed; utilisation is about 70%. No new debt for the existing business. Seamless term loan of about INR100 crore is only partly drawn.
