544254|2026-03.headline: Tolins Tyres FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 12% to INR327.12 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR47.8 crore and PAT to INR35.69 crore.
544254|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew about 12% YoY to INR327.12 crore, while EBITDA (excluding other income) declined to INR47.8 crore from INR57.91 crore, with margin at 14.6%. PAT fell to INR35.69 crore from INR38.67 crore, and basic EPS was INR9.03. Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 12% to INR77.99 crore, but Q4 EBITDA fell to INR11.22 crore (14.4% margin) from INR13.57 crore, with PAT of INR8.94 crore. Management attributed the pressure to a GST rate mismatch on retreading materials, higher inventory, longer receivable cycles and West Asia disruption, and gave only a soft FY27 outlook of maintaining FY26 performance.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR292.45 crore in FY25, about +12% YoY
vs INR57.91 crore in FY25, decline
vs INR38.67 crore in FY25, decline
vs INR69.53 crore in Q4 FY25, about +12% YoY
vs INR13.57 crore in Q4 FY25, decline

segments.name: Retreading materials (tread rubber, PCTR)
segments.commentary: Management said about 60% of sales come from tread rubber; retread margins were hit by the GST mismatch (18% on retread materials vs 5% on new agricultural tyres), and dealer off-take fell. Industry association has sought a 5% GST rate on retreads, which the government is reportedly considering.

segments.name: Tyres (incl. agricultural, two-wheeler, tractor rear)
segments.commentary: Tyre production rose to 5,35,870 units in FY26 from 3,93,253 in FY25, about 36% growth, while top-line growth lagged. Utilisation in the Indian tyre segment was about 45%. A new heavy-duty tractor rear tyre has received an encouraging dealer response.

segments.name: UAE operations (Ras Al Khaimah)
segments.commentary: Plant capacity is 1,200 metric tons, with utilisation below 50%; management said margins are better than India, but GCC demand fell from the last quarter of FY26. Utilisation is expected to drop to 30-40% in the near term before recovering to 40-50%. Receivables are rising in the UAE.

segments.name: Exports, precured tyres and US business
segments.commentary: Management said US business started last year and repeat orders are slowly coming in, with a Europe push under way. Logistics are impacted by the Middle East war. No quantified export revenue was given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: management expects to at least maintain FY26 levels of performance, and will review this after Q2 FY27 depending on how the situation evolves.
Management expects West Asia and India-related disruptions to normalise by end of Q2 FY27 (pricing, raw material and shipping), which would support better Q3 and Q4.
EBITDA margin: management said 10% to 13% is an acceptable range, with a further 2-3% from waste and scrap reduction and operational efficiency.
Management expects a Terra Rubber recycling-linked margin benefit in FY26/FY27 through in-house offtake; no quantified synergy was given.
Management expects capex to be limited this year because existing capacity is sufficient to meet demand, and says the government is likely to correct the GST imbalance.
capex_capacity: Ras Al Khaimah (UAE) plant capacity is 1,200 metric tons, with utilisation below 50%; the plant has been operating for about 10 years.
Indian utilisation is about 45-55%: retread segment about 55% and tyre segment about 45%.
Gujarat depot commenced operations on December 1, 2025, serving tyre and retread products in Western India.
No significant capex is planned for FY27, as existing capacity is sufficient; cost reduction is focused on automation and AI-based planning tools.
Terra Rubber has started manufacturing and processing scrap into products trialled on road; management is scouting acquisitions but nothing is finalised and no numbers were shared.
demand_pricing: Tyre production volume grew 36% YoY in FY26 (5,35,870 vs 3,93,253 units) and PCTR grew about 10%; bonding gum and flaps grew 56%.
The GST cut on new commercial and agricultural tyres (from 28% to 18% and 5%, respectively) left retread materials at 18%, which narrowed retreading's 30-40% price advantage to about 20%.
Q4 tyre volumes fell QoQ due to dealer off-take hesitancy amid war-related uncertainty in March 2026.
Dealer credit was extended by about one month to 4-5 months, with a stated plan to revert to 3-4 months; China dumping in GCC is extending credit terms up to a year.
Management said competition is intense with tyre majors in retreading materials, but it believes its 40-year expertise gives it an edge.

qa_highlights.question: Why was top-line growth only about 12% against the 20% growth previously guided, and how do gross current assets of INR309 crore compare with revenue of INR327 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20% was an optimistic projection and that actual growth was about 12%. It pointed to 36% growth in tyre volumes, with the gap explained by selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive, and what is the sales and marketing strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said credit periods were extended by about one month due to GST and geopolitical uncertainty, with the aim of reducing them over a few quarters. Management said branding spend is small and that it relies on a strong marketing manager team.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and margin of the Ras Al Khaimah UAE plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 1,200 MT with utilisation below 50%. The CFO said UAE margins are better than India's, and utilisation could fall to 30-40% in the next three months before recovering to 40-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline in Q4 and FY26, and when will GST be corrected?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the decline to margin pressure in retreads from the GST imbalance and weaker dealer off-take. The industry body has asked for a 5% retread GST rate, and the government is considering it.

qa_highlights.question: What are the three biggest growth drivers beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher tyre production volumes, precured tyres (Europe and the US, where repeat orders are starting), and Terra Rubber integration for in-house raw material offtake.

qa_highlights.question: Why did tyre volumes decline QoQ, and why did working capital rise from about INR230 crore to near INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volumes fell because of March uncertainty. Working capital is driven by 3-4 months of dealer credit, about 4-5 months of inventory across more than 1,200 SKUs and seasonal rubber prices, and government retentions. IPO proceeds were partly used to fund inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 top-line guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects at least to maintain FY26 performance and will review after Q2 FY27, preferring to commit less and perform better.

risks_watch: Gross current assets of about INR309 crore versus revenue of INR327 crore indicate high working capital intensity; dealer credit rising to 4-5 months.
The GST mismatch on retread materials (18% vs 5% on new agricultural tyres) is still unresolved; watch the GST Council decision.
UAE utilisation below 50% with receivable risk and China dumping in GCC; management is cautious on aggressive expansion.
Q4 volumes fell QoQ and EBITDA margin declined, so watch whether Q1 FY27 volumes and margins recover.
The Terra Rubber integration and acquisition plans remain unquantified, and no synergy numbers were given.
544254|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and tyre volumes but cautious on near-term outlook: management repeatedly tied recovery to the West Asia situation and GST policy resolving by Q2 FY27. Evasive on specific numbers, for example declining to commit to FY27 growth and declining to give clear margin guidance.
key_quotes: But due to a lot of other factors, we could do at least 12%. That is the growth what we could attain.
So we expect similar performance of FY25-'26. So, we believe that it is better to commit less and perform better.
We always try to keep minimum 10% margin, that is a fact, but then due to our efficiency, otherwise our pricing will not be feasible in the market.
We are not taking, not considering any of these options as a priority or low priority, because we are moving in both the verticals.

544256|2026-03.headline: P N Gadgil FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR10,000 crore to INR10,739 crore (+40% YoY); Q4 gross margin fell to 9.7% on a 40% bullion mix.
544256|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR10,739 crore, with full-year gross margin up 280 bps to 12% and EBITDA margin up 180 bps to 6.6%. Q4 revenue grew 123% YoY to INR3,544 crore, but gross margin fell to 9.7% (about 230 bps down YoY) as gold bars and coins rose to 40% of sales, plus one-time discounts and franchise mix. Management attributes the Q4 margin dip to mix and one-offs, and it guided FY27 revenue of INR13,500 crore, EBITDA margin 7-7.5% and PAT margin 4%, with a review next quarter given the import duty hike.

financial_highlights.change: about -230 bps YoY; gross profit +80% YoY

segments.name: Retail (COCO)
segments.commentary: FY26 retail revenue INR8,131 crore (+51% YoY), SSSG 43%; Q4 retail INR2,600 crore (+102% YoY). Stud ratio for FY26 at 9.9%.

segments.name: Franchise (FOCO)
segments.commentary: FY26 franchise revenue INR1,292 crore (+83% YoY); Q4 INR430 crore (+132% YoY). Franchise gross margin cited at 2.5-3%.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR529 crore (+105% YoY); Q4 INR152 crore (+67% YoY).

segments.name: Other segments
segments.commentary: Q4 contribution INR357 crore; includes gold bars and coins, which carry roughly 0.5-1% gross margin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance INR13,500 crore, versus the earlier INR12,000-12,500 crore reference; retail AOP about INR9,800 crore (+23% on about INR8,000 crore).
FY27 EBITDA margin 7-7.5% and PAT margin about 4%; gross margin guidance 12-13%, which management says is unchanged.
Guidance to be updated next quarter depending on how market conditions evolve.
Bars and coins expected at about 25% of sales in FY27 (FY26: about 32%); the import duty hike is expected to cut that segment by 20-22% of total sales.
FY27 store plan of 25 new stores: 5-7 COCO and the balance FOCO (about 20 franchise), mostly outside Maharashtra (Gurgaon, Lucknow/UP, Gujarat).
Hedging target raised to 75-80% in FY27 (67% at end-Q4 FY26, about 60% average for FY26).
capex_capacity: 78 stores across 36 cities at 31 March 2026; 25 stores added in FY26, including 12 in Q4 (8 COCO, 4 FOCO).
Non-Maharashtra stores contribute about 10% of business; UP, Bihar and MP stores reached about 1x annualised stock turn in year one, against a 0.8x guidance.
Average revenue per store INR137.7 crore; revenue per sq ft INR4,51,000; net profit per store INR5.25 crore; inventory turnover 3.8x.
Management says it does not plan many COCO stores in FY27, favouring the asset-light franchise model.
QIP enabling board resolution valid until end of August 2026; management says the QIP is not needed for growth. Promoter shareholding must reach 75% by September 2027.
demand_pricing: Q4 event sales: Foundation Day INR365 crore, Gudi Padwa INR171 crore (+38% YoY), Gratitude Day INR225 crore.
Q4 volumes: gold +27% YoY, silver +37%, diamond +125%, despite a sharp gold price run.
Old gold exchange about 40% of business, targeted at 50%+; make-to-order about 30-35% (22% outside Maharashtra vs 30-32% in Maharashtra).
Average transaction value above INR1 lakh in FY26.

Q4 gross margin hit by about 150 bps from bars and coins (INR450 crore to INR1,400 crore; Q3 INR1,100 crore), about 100 bps from lower stud mix, and INR40-45 crore of making-charge discounts (INR399/gram), plus INR50 crore+ of promotional and trade discounts. Franchise sales rose about INR200 crore QoQ.
Gains from the unhedged portion: INR7.4 crore in Q4 FY25, INR45 crore in Q3 FY26, INR20 crore in Q4 FY26.
Management says the import duty and the advance authorisation scheme do not apply to its domestic business; the duty is passed to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the customs duty hike and advance authorisation on sales and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the advance authorisation targets exporters, so it does not apply. The duty is passed to consumers, with no margin impact; it may shift demand from bars and coins toward exchanging old gold for jewellery.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging levels for FY26 and the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging was 57% in Q4 FY25, 63% in Q3 FY26 and 67% in Q4 FY26, averaging about 60% for FY26. The target is 75-80% in FY27, held back by MCX margin and premium costs of 15-20% that tied up cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance raised from INR12,000 crore to INR13,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 beat the INR9,500 crore guidance by about INR1,000 crore. Management cites non-Maharashtra demand (about 10% of business) and strong same-store growth, which pushed the range up to INR13,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the margin drivers one-off rather than structural, given likely repeat discounts and franchise growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the discounts were one-time events worth about 0.5% of Q4 sales. Bars and coins (40% of Q4 sales) drove most of the dip, and it expects that mix to normalise to about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin split between bars and coins and jewellery?
qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins earn 0.5-1% gross margin; plain gold jewellery earns 12.5-13%. Franchise gross margin is about 2-3%, nearly net margin since the franchisee bears all costs.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory turnover decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the 3.8x FY26 turnover to about 8 COCO stores opened in Q4 that have not matured. It says turnover has been broadly flat, declining slightly over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 store additions and non-Maharashtra plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan of 25 stores: 5-7 COCO and the balance FOCO, mostly outside Maharashtra (UP, Bihar, MP, Gujarat, Gurgaon). Demand for franchises is strong and under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year bars and coins share and promoter shareholding timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins were about 32% of FY26 sales. The promoter must reach 75% by September 2027, three years after the September 2024 listing.

risks_watch: Q4 gross margin at 9.7% versus 12-13% guidance; management says the mix shift will normalise, but its explanation of one-offs has been challenged.
Import duty hike may reduce bars and coins demand (20-22% of sales); whether jewellery exchange offsets it is unproven, and management said it is too early to quantify FY27 volume.
Hedging at 67% is short of the 75-80% target; MCX margin costs and unhedged gains affect margin volatility.
Franchise mix rising (FOCO margins about 2-3%) could weigh on gross margin as the network expands.
Inventory turnover fell to 3.8x as new stores ramp; the new-market ramp needs watching.
Promoter shareholding must reach 75% by September 2027; the QIP enabling resolution lapses end-August 2026.
544256|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the full-year result and the FY27 guidance, but defensive on Q4 margins: management repeatedly ties the drop to bars and coins and one-off promotions and says it is not structural. It was less specific on FY27 volume, the QIP and hedging costs, and said it would update guidance next quarter.
key_quotes: So, the three factors primarily which can identify to this are higher share of gold bars and coins in the overall sales mix.
We therefore view the gross margin impact as largely one-time and mix-driven, not structural, and remain focused on improving product mix and margins as our stores mature.
So, we feel looking at these positives, you know, we feel that INR12,500 can be stretched to INR13,500, and that's where the guidance is coming from.
The business is self-sufficient.

544256|2026-06.headline: PNG Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, with EBITDA up 57% to INR192.4 crore and PAT up 52% to INR105.3 crore.
544256|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, driven by retail (up 56%, with 46% SSSG), franchise (up 8%) and e-commerce (up 20%). EBITDA margin expanded 80 bps to 8.0% and PAT margin rose 40 bps to 4.4%, with gross margin flat at 13.2% reported. Management kept FY27 guidance (around 25 store additions to 103 stores, about 7% EBITDA margin, about INR400 crore other expenses) and flagged that Q1 other expenses were low due to cuts in marketing and no store launches. Hedging gains and lower other income were discussed in detail, and the promoter stake and franchise economics drew scrutiny.

Network targets: about 140 stores by March 2028 and about 177 by March 2029 (about 113 legacy and 64 litestyle; about 75 COCO and 40 FOCO by March 2029).

UP stores running 18%+ studded versus 15% projection; 8-10 UP franchise openings planned in FY27; Ayodhya store opening soon.
Capital allocation focused on store expansion, franchise network, digital and operational excellence, funded from internal accruals.
Management plans a QIP at a suitable time to reduce promoter holding (above 75%); board enabling resolution already in place.
demand_pricing: Management said demand held up through April-June despite record gold prices, supported by weddings and Akshaya Tritiya; Adhik Maas was muted due to high silver prices.
Weddings postponed by Adhik Maas expected to benefit Q2 and a large part of Q3.
Customers shifting towards lightweight jewellery, studded products and old gold exchange, favouring organised players.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin flat YoY despite mix shift toward retail, and what is the ideal retail margin at a 10-11% studded ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported gross margin is flat because hedging gains are shown separately; ex-hedging adjusted gross margin is up about 40-50 bps YoY. Management targets 12.5-13.5% retail margin at a 10-11% studded ratio, and 13-14% overall retail gross margin including hedging gains.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses grow only about 5% despite store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited conservative spending amid demand uncertainty, lower scheme-redemption discounts, marketing kept within 1.5% of sales with 250-300 hoardings cut, and no store launches in Q1. Spending will rise in Q3-Q4 with expansion, but EBITDA guidance is still expected to be met.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 other expense guidance and why was other income so different between Q4 and Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses are guided at about 3% of sales, roughly INR400 crore for FY27. Other income was about INR10 crore in Q1 versus about INR12 crore in Q4 per the CFO, who said lower fixed deposits placed on mortgage drove the decline; cash and hedging margin money also hold some balances.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store expansion and COCO/FOCO mix plan through FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan adds 25 stores in FY27 to reach 103 (63 COCO, balance FOCO), then 37 each in FY28 and FY29 to reach 140 and 177. By March 2029, about 75 COCO and 40 FOCO, with 113 legacy and 64 litestyle stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory and hedging plan?
qa_highlights.answer: PAT margin underlying ex-hedging is targeted at 4.1-4.25% in FY27 per the CFO, versus about 4.2% per the CEO; 4.5-4.7% by FY29. Hedging is about 70%+ now, targeted at about 80% around Q3 FY27 and fully hedged in FY28. Hedging gains were about INR45 crore in Q3 FY26, INR20 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR5.5-6 crore in Q2 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How is Litestyle progressing on studded mix, gross margin and store count?
qa_highlights.answer: Studded ratio is about 32.9-34% now, targeted at about 50% in a couple of years. Current litestyle gross margin is about 18-20%, versus 30-35% for the format once studded mix rises. Litestyle store target is 65-70 by March 2029 and about 100 over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: Why are franchise revenue growth (8%) and e-commerce growth lower than company-operated stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Franchise sales are booked as B2B, so initial stocking and replenishment timing affect quarterly numbers; management expects franchise openings to pick up in Q2-Q3 (about 10 legacy and 5 litestyle). E-commerce is deliberately shifting mix away from bars and coins toward jewellery, so margins should improve but total sales growth may slow.

risks_watch: Reported gross margin flat YoY; expansion of hedging gains is shrinking as hedging coverage rises toward 80% by Q3 FY27 and full coverage in FY28, so reported margin depends on underlying retail mix.
Other expenses are guided to rise in Q3-Q4 with store openings; Q1 spend (about 5% growth) was unusually low, so H2 cost run-rate against about INR400 crore guidance needs monitoring.
Franchise revenue growth of 8% versus company-operated retail growth of 56%; visibility into franchise B2C sell-through is still being built and management has only recently gained system access.
Promoter holding above 75% with a QIP planned at a suitable time; timing and size are not specified and the stock overhang remains.
Gold metal loan of INR1,500-1,550 crore to fall by INR500-600 crore by FY29; execution of the debt-reduction path and the litestyle studded-mix shift (from about 34% toward 50%) are key checkpoints.

Other income fell to about INR10 crore from about INR12 crore in Q4 per the CFO, after the analyst cited INR31 crore; the figure was disputed on the call and should be reconciled against the filed numbers.

Despite elevated gold prices, our performa nce remains in line with our previously communicated guidance.

544256|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, store expansion and the long-term plan, with precise targets given across FY27-FY29. Cautious and somewhat evasive on the reasons for flat gross margin and the other income gap, leaning on adjusted (ex-hedging) figures and deferring some answers to later quarters.

544258|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 5.0% as Middle East crisis cut EXIM volumes 11% QoQ.
544258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew about 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, the fourth straight quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA fell from INR27 crore to INR25 crore, with margin down from 5.6% to 5.0%, and PAT dropped from INR10.8 crore to INR8.3 crore. Total containers handled were 57,754, up 4.3% YoY but down 7% QoQ, with EXIM down 10.96% QoQ and domestic almost flat. For FY26, containers rose 6.14% to 2,26,578, and management attributed the shortfall from double-digit growth to the March disruption from the Strait of Hormuz closure.

financial_highlights.change: +4% QoQ from INR478 crore in Q3
down from INR27 crore in Q3
down from INR10.8 crore in Q3; margin 1.7% vs 2.3%

financial_highlights.value: over INR70 crore (management cited INR74 crore in Q&A)

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 23,350 containers, up 17.79% YoY and down less than 1% QoQ, helped by pivots to chemicals, FMCG, aggregates and salt. FY26 volume 86,353, up 8.16% YoY.

segments.name: Devaliya MMCT (Morbi)

Management expects sequential improvement in both top line and bottom line from Q1 FY27, and says it is comfortable with the trend in May.
Management targets debtor days below 120 in FY27.

Management expects operating cash flow to improve as realisations and EXIM volumes recover.

Own specialised container fleet is over 1,000 units.
Devaliya MMCT (32 acres, Morbi) is fully operational; fixed rail services run from Devaliya to CMLK, Bangalore, Chennai, Calcutta and Guwahati at lower frequency.
FY27 capex of INR100 crore covers specialised containers, commercial vehicles, reach stackers, forklifts and large cranes.
demand_pricing: Management says the order book is strong, with pedigreed customers for the rest of the year, and that the East Coast EXIM pipeline is robust.
Domestic demand for specialised containers is strong, with similar orders in the pipeline for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise from INR172 crore to INR217 crore despite IPO net proceeds of about INR363 crore, of which about INR163 crore went to debt repayment?

544277|2026-06.headline: Waaree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79.2% YoY to INR7,932 crore and order book hit a record INR61,500 crore, though operating EBITDA margin was 18.2%.

544285|2026-06.headline: Swiggy guides Quick Commerce contribution margin to 0 to -100 bps for growth, with 4-week cumulative NOV growth at 10% vs 1% prior.
544285|2026-06.overview: Swiggy's Q1 FY27 call (held July 30, 2026) centred on a deliberate pivot from contribution-margin protection to growth in Quick Commerce (Instamart). Management said it reached contribution margin breakeven, closing the last quarter at -0.2%, and now guides to a 0 to -100 bps range to fund store expansion, speed, serviceability and assortment. Take-rate gains were attributed to brand monetisation, advertising and user-fee changes, with management calling them sustainable. Food delivery growth was about 18% adjusted for cancellations, with 18-20% YoY guidance maintained, and management dismissed zero-commission competition from Toing's rivals as unsustainable. Toing, the new value-led food platform, is loss-making and was a major focus, with a Capital Markets Day planned for the following week.

segments.commentary: Adjusted growth about 18% YoY; YoY guidance 18-20% maintained. Take rate about 3%, with a target of 5%; management expects steady margin accretion.

Monetisation (brand take rate, advertising, user fees) drove a large part of the 4-5 quarter improvement to CM breakeven; management says these revenues are sustainable.

qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritises growth within a 0 to -100 bps CM band. Take-rate gains come from brand negotiations, advertising and user-fee monetisation, which management says will not reverse.

qa_highlights.question: Is the food delivery zero-commission model a threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Kapoor argued zero commission is not sustainable; costs must be recovered from restaurants, consumers or delivery partners. Competition is expected in affordability, not premium.

qa_highlights.question: Wage hike and last-mile cost escalation?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual salary revision sits below CM. Minimum wage hikes in some states affect picking and packing; impact described as not material. Last-mile cost rose on seasonal factors including elections and harvest migration; efficiency offset kept the YoY dip to 20 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Are competitors capitalising costs or securitising payables?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Bothra said Swiggy does not capitalise employee, tech token or store costs, and is not aware of payables securitisation practices by peers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Instamart growth plan and store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth from transacting users and frequency; more stores in existing cities as hyper-local stores hit 2,500-3,000 orders/day. Spend priorities are store expansion, speed and serviceability, and selection availability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did platform frequency decline and is private-label conflict with ads a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it culled low-value MTUs over recent quarters, and QC's lower frequency dilutes the blended metric. Private brands carry higher margins and are experience-driven, so conflict with ads was not seen as material.

Food delivery guidance of 18-20% YoY growth on the standalone business was reiterated, with Adjusted EBITDA up about INR 50 crore for the quarter and take rate above 26%. Toing, the affordability platform, is being run as a range-bound investment; management asked for another quarter or two before judging whether it is a scalable model. Quick commerce contribution margin guidance is 0 to -100 bps, with 100 bps Adjusted EBITDA improvement guided for Q3, and a move to an inventory model starting mid-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How should losses in quick commerce evolve and will Swiggy refocus on Tier-2 markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quick commerce returned to growth with 13.4% QoQ NOV growth and 1.3 million MTUs added, and that it is not looking to expand geographically beyond its current footprint of around 130 cities.

qa_highlights.question: Is Toing an experiment or ready to scale, and what metrics decide this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management asked for another one to two quarters before deciding. Metrics are repeat-user unit economics in early cities, customer acquisition cost as the base expands, and delivery cost reduction; investment is discretionary and range-bound.

qa_highlights.question: Is the contribution margin trajectory in quick commerce improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 0 to -100 bps contribution margin with sequential improvement and 100 bps Adjusted EBITDA improvement in Q3, with the inventory model contributing no benefit in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store capacity threshold for adding new dark stores?

qa_highlights.question: Will food margins be sacrificed for growth as competition rises?

qa_highlights.question: Why has the NOV per store gap with Blinkit persisted, and has competition eased?

Growth was strong in retail health (reported 47.1%, like-to-like 35.5%) while group business was flat amid a challenging B2B pricing environment. The company moved fully to Ind AS in Q1, with parallel IFRS 17-style disclosures continuing for public reporting. Management said July loss ratio trends were in line with plan and reiterated the FY29 mid-to-high-teens ROE target.

qa_highlights.question: Gaurav Malhotra: What is the effective tax rate this year and next?

544305|2026-06.headline: MobiKwik posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR76 million, its third straight profitable quarter, with payments GMV up 50% YoY to INR587 billion.
544305|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as its most profitable quarter yet, with PAT of INR76 million and EBITDA of INR158 million, up INR470 million YoY. Payments gross profit rose 31% YoY to INR777 million and financial services gross profit grew 5.6x to INR433 million. Lending disbursements dipped in Q1, while payments revenue fell as card-linked categories were paused under regulatory pressure and UPI (near-zero take rate) grew. Management targets full-year PAT of about INR400 million and EBITDA of about INR750 million including other income, and is scaling a merchant acquiring business that is still loss-making.

financial_highlights.change: Swing of INR495 million vs Q1 FY26; up from INR45 million in Q4 per management

544309|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY (12% constant currency) to INR893 crores, with reported EBITDA of INR294 crores at 33% margin.
544309|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached about INR893 crores, up 21% YoY and 12% in constant currency, with forex gains neutral versus Q4. Reported EBITDA was INR294 crores (33%); management says it was about 35% after adding back roughly INR20 crores of one-time TruBridge acquisition costs. PAT was INR193-194 crores, up about 28% YoY. TruBridge closed on July 10, 2026, so Q1 figures are legacy IKS only; management reset TruBridge's steady-state revenue to about $300 million a year (from $340 million pre-close) while keeping its roughly $68 million EBITDA, and reaffirmed a FY30 EBITDA True North of at least INR3,000 crores without further dilution beyond ESOPs.

~+28% YoY; higher if adjusted for acquisition costs

Two non-profitable IT and early-out service lines (~$8 million a quarter revenue) to be exited; ~$2-3 million a quarter of customer discounts expected during transformation. Revenue growth outlook not yet given.

guidance_outlook: FY30 True North: at least INR3,000 crores EBITDA, targeted with marginal ESOP dilution only and no return to net debt above pre-TruBridge levels.
Blended EBITDA margin expected to return to early-to-mid 30s from a pro forma 26-27% drop over the next couple of years, via technology, offshore human-in-the-loop, and SG&A synergies.

FY27 expected to remain EPS accretive despite the TruBridge revenue reset, per management.

capex_capacity: Headcount inflated above need ahead of TruBridge integration, including investment in TruBridge RCM customers; combined base just over 16,000 employees.
TruBridge acquisition priced at about $550 million for ~$68 million EBITDA, described as accretive.
Five-year lock-in deal signed recently at healthy pricing; no explicit capex figures disclosed.
Patent approved for AAW model (propensity to show/no-show and propensity to pay), deployed in MyCareHub.
demand_pricing: Legacy IKS cross-sell into large health systems showing early land-and-expand wins: Advocate Health Care (top-five US health system, >$35 billion revenue) expanded in RCM and coding; a large California system is moving regions to Epic; a national musculoskeletal aggregator signed a significant RCM deal; StrideCare (vascular) partnership.

Competitive intensity rising; management cites ~30 vendors moving from point solutions to platforms, including Abridge's clinician intelligence launch. Pricing pressure expected but pricing 'not the biggest issue' outside non-deterministic tasks.
Market: total TAM above $260 billion (overall growing ~8%); outsourced TAM ~$35 billion growing ~12%.
Axia Women's Health case study: $12 million cash impact, 96% coding accuracy, reduced denials.
Epic relationship described as strengthening; TruBridge also collaborating with Epic in rural market.

qa_highlights.question: What organic constant-currency growth is healthy over the medium term, and is margin expansion coming from currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin growth is not from currency: revenue grew 12% CC on 4.2% headcount growth; adjusted EBITDA is 35% with neutral forex. Aspiration is 12%+ CC on legacy IKS, not guidance; TruBridge growth to be set in two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How does SLM fit with LLMs, and where does glass-box/explainable AI sit?
qa_highlights.answer: Three SLM approaches: standalone SLMs, LLM-distilled SLMs, and hierarchical SLM-plus-LLM. Explainability comes from knowledge graphs acquired via ARAI. Management would not commit to a 60% token-usage reduction, saying it will emerge over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire TruBridge and what criteria govern acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Chosen because the rural market is large, TruBridge holds 30%+ share as one of two dominant rural EHRs, and its service mix resembles ambulatory. Criteria: strategic thesis first, leverage tolerable relative to EBITDA, and accretive price; $68 million EBITDA bought for ~$550 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge's margin of 22-23% fixable, and does the INR3,000 crore target rule out M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers include existing and in-build technology plus offshore human-in-the-loop to restore early-to-mid 30s margins. INR3,000 crores is achievable without another acquisition, but M&A is not ruled out; white space seen as large.

qa_highlights.question: Does Abridge's platform move threaten IKS, and is pricing under pressure in renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management respects Abridge but sees ~30 vendors aspiring to platforms and rising competition. Recent five-year deal signed at healthy price; pricing pressure expected but margin leverage maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge still EPS accretive for FY27 after revenue reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; EBITDA is unchanged, so management says EPS accretion is absolute and possibly a bit higher than previously expected.

risks_watch: TruBridge revenue reset: steady-state revenue cut to about $300 million from $340 million, with ~$8 million a quarter of non-profitable service lines to be exited and ~$2-3 million a quarter of customer discounts during transformation; track whether the $68 million EBITDA holds through the reset.

TruBridge margin recovery: TruBridge runs at a 22-23% margin versus the early-to-mid 30s blended target; progress depends on technology deployment and offshore human-in-the-loop, with management saying it needs two to three quarters to size TruBridge growth.
Integration costs: about INR20 crores of one-time acquisition costs in Q1 and integration expenses expected in Q2 at a similar range; watch reported versus adjusted EBITDA gap.

Competitive intensity: management cites around 30 vendors moving from point solutions to platforms, including Abridge; management expects pricing pressure to rise, though it says pricing is not the biggest issue outside non-deterministic tasks.

Legacy IKS growth versus the 12%+ constant-currency aspiration (Q1 at 12%), with headcount inflated ahead of TruBridge integration; also the INR3,000 crore FY30 True North, which management says is achievable without further acquisitions but does not rule them out.
key_quotes: And so, our commitment to building a single institutionalized culture that is really driven around outcomes, I think one of the things that's coming out as this whole AI hype cycle flushes itself out is that the AI is great as a technology, but if it can't improve outcomes from a cost and quality perspective, then that's not going to be worth it, right?

I wish I could tell you that based on the combination of these approaches, my token utilization will drop by 60% versus a traditional LLM approach. I'm not smart enough to tell you that today, but over a period of time that metric will emerge for us.

544309|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the legacy IKS franchise, the Q1 margin and the FY30 True North, which management repeated with a 'good line of sight' framing. Cautious and explicitly non-committal on TruBridge revenue growth, the 60% token-reduction claim, and the 12%+ growth figure, which it calls an aspiration rather than guidance.

544310|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 57% to INR235.1 crore with EBITDA margin of 25.7%; order book above INR400 crore and FY27 order-booking target of INR500+ crore.
544310|2026-03.overview: Yash Highvoltage reported record FY26 revenue of INR235.1 crore (up 57%), EBITDA of INR60.4 crore (up 75%, 25.7% margin, about 260 bps higher) and PAT of INR37.4 crore (15.9% margin). H2 FY26 revenue was INR135.5 crore (up 46% YoY), with H2 EBITDA of INR37.2 crore and PAT of INR23.7 crore. Order book stood at over INR400 crore on 31 March 2026. Management said the Greenfield RIP facility is in final commissioning, with trial production by end Q2 FY27 and commercial production targeted around October 2026.

segments.name: OIP bushings
segments.commentary: Roughly half of FY26 volumes (about 3,500-3,600 units out of about 7,200); management says OIP is in shortage and deliveries are constrained by capacity, with a brownfield expansion planned.

segments.name: RIP bushings
segments.commentary: Roughly half of FY26 volumes (about 3,500-3,600 units); core is still imported (about 95% per the presentation), and localisation via the Greenfield facility at Jarod is targeted in H2 FY27.

segments.name: HCP / high current
segments.commentary: Balance of volumes in FY26 (combined with OIP, about 15-18% of order book per management).

segments.name: Retrofit
segments.commentary: About 6-7% of overall revenue per management; described as high-margin, with no segment EBITDA disclosed.

segments.name: Sukrut Electric (acquired)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR25-26 crore; management targets INR150-160 crore in 4-5 years (5-6x growth). No Sukrut EBITDA guidance given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 invoicing target of INR360-400 crore (management: 40-45% growth).
Order inflow target of at least INR500 crore in FY27.
EBITDA margin to be maintained around 24-25% in FY27; margin expansion expected from FY28 as import dependence falls.
Long-term growth aspiration of around 40-42% for the next four to five years.
Exports to reach at least 20% of revenue in the next two to three years.
Greenfield RIP facility: trial production by end Q2 FY27, commercial RIP core production about 3-4 months after internal trials and type tests; management targets October 2026.
Total capacity to rise to about 15,000 bushings (about INR700 crore revenue potential), with about INR100 crore for OIP and the balance for RIP.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 9,000-10,000 bushings; about 7,000+ produced in FY26 (75-80% utilisation); FY27 utilisation target 65-70%.
Greenfield facility at Jarod (about 20 km from Baroda airport): design expanded from 220 kV to 550 kV; adds about 5,000-7,000 units a year, focused on RIP/RIS.
Greenfield capex of about INR153 crore, of which about INR80 crore spent; balance expected within two to three months.
Equity raise approval up to INR150 crore; management is eyeing INR100-110 crore for capex (550 kV production, testing, brownfield) and working capital of INR28-30 crore.
Constraints in autoclave capacity; new autoclaves being invested in. Brownfield OIP expansion planned to address OIP shortage.
demand_pricing: Management says demand exceeds global bushing supply; transformer OEMs are giving blanket orders for 24-36 months.
Prices are secured with suppliers and customers via pass-through arrangements for commodity and currency moves; management says indirect cost escalation from oil/gas is being passed on.
Management sees no direct impact from the Middle East war; no exports to or imports from affected countries.
Management says Chinese bushings have never been restricted in India, yet Indian buyers have not bought them, citing pricing, availability and service.
Competitive RIP entrants in India named as CG Power, Hitachi India and MIM (Massa Izolyator Mehru).

qa_highlights.question: Top-line growth expected over the next 2-3 years and impact of the Middle East war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 40-42% growth for the next four to five years (38-40% CAGR over the past five to six years); no direct war impact, only indirect cost escalation passed on to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new RIP plant contribute revenue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production by end Q2 FY27; job-work assembly and testing revenue starts earlier, with indigenous RIP commercial revenue expected towards year-end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross and EBITDA margins improve in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonally higher H2 volumes, scale-driven negotiation, customer price recovery, supplier price negotiation and currency hedging; no single specific reason.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of margin compression if lower-kV capacity comes online across the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to hold given rising global demand, localisation of RIP cores and export pricing for RIP, and sees input-stage margin expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sukrut revenue potential and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Sukrut revenue about INR25-26 crore in FY26, targeted at INR150-160 crore in 4-5 years; management declined to give Sukrut EBITDA guidance until later in the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total capacity after expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15,000 bushings with a revenue potential of close to INR700 crore; about INR100 crore OIP and the balance RIP.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity rather than debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is mathematically cheaper but it wants good investors on the cap table and prefers to remain debt-free.

qa_highlights.question: Cyber incident impact?
qa_highlights.answer: No recovery to date; a police complaint has been filed and the expense has already been charged to the P&L.

risks_watch: Commissioning and type-test success for the Greenfield RIP core line; management says a 2-3 month delay would not affect FY27 guidance.
Input-cost and currency volatility from oil, gas, insulators and rupee depreciation; Middle East war effects over the next two to three months.
Supply-chain bottlenecks: vendor development takes about 6 months and suppliers may deprioritise the company; people attrition in a niche skill set.
Pricing and capacity risk if sub-400 kV capacity expands industry-wide, or if restrictions on Chinese bushings are eased.
Sukrut integration and profitability not yet disclosed; equity raise size (INR100-110 crore vs INR150 crore approval) still to be finalised.
Swiss technology contract for core knowledge runs to mid-2027 for supplies; the agreement itself has ended.
544310|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, growth and order visibility, but measured and somewhat hedged on timelines and specifics. Management declined to give several numbers (RIP/OIP realisations, retrofit EBITDA, Sukrut EBITDA) and kept some answers general.
key_quotes: Financial year '26 has been a landmark year in the journey of Yash Highvoltage.
So, we, we have a target to book at least INR500 plus crores order this year also.
Sukrut, we assume that in next four to five years, we should be able to cross at least INR150 to INR160 crores of revenue.

544310|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 95% YoY to INR194.5 crores, with EBITDA margin up to 28.1% and PAT of INR36 crores (18.6% margin).
544310|2026-09.overview: Yash Highvoltage reported H1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR194.5 crores, up 95% YoY, with volume up about 40% to roughly 4,000 bushings. Gross margin expanded to 48.3% from 42.4%, and EBITDA rose 139% to INR55 crores, lifting margin to 28.1% from 23.3%. Order book stood at INR760 crores as of 30 September 2026, against INR400 crores at the start of FY27, with execution over 15 to 18 months. Greenfield capex of INR220 crores is INR106 crores spent so far, with the balance over the next 12 months, and management reiterated the Brownfield expansion completing by Q3.

US: representation agreements cover close to 27 states; agents in close to 30 countries; OIP export orders carry 6-15 month lead times.

qa_highlights.question: What drove EBITDA margin to 28% and is it sustainable into H2 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited product mix, sales and procurement improvements, factory efficiency and overhead absorption from higher volume; said the aim is to maintain or improve margins without giving a specific number.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins rise to 32-35% after core localization?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah declined to give a specific target, saying the company will see the impact of localized production before committing; earlier guidance was about 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Order book from exports and share of export orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Export order book is about INR40-50 crores, roughly 5-7% of the INR700-odd crore book at the time of the call.

qa_highlights.question: H1 production split between RIP and OIP?
qa_highlights.answer: Close to 1,500 OIP and close to 2,200 RIP bushings were produced in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential from expanded capacity and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined Unit 1 and Unit 2 invoicing potential of INR900-1,000 crores, with full utilisation by 2030-31.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth in H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 4,000 bushings in H1 FY27 versus 2,950 in H1 FY26, around 40% growth; no product-wise split given.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and non-current assets rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days were 47 in H1 FY27 versus 45 for full FY26; the rise in other non-current assets to INR40 crores from INR11 crores reflects advances to international core vendors to secure slots.

H2 revenue linearity: management aims for balanced H1 and H2, but past years saw H2 outperform.

544311|2026-03.headline: IGI Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue and EBITDA each grew 21% YoY to INR 3,686 mn and INR 2,360 mn, with volumes up 16% to 3.64 mn reports.
544311|2026-03.overview: Q4 (Jan–Mar 2026) was the first quarter reported after the switch from calendar to financial year, so the 15-month period (Jan 2025–Mar 2026) is the main comparison basis. Growth was led by lab-grown diamonds (LGD +35%) and LGD jewelry (+29%), while natural diamond jewelry fell 19% on gold and silver price volatility. The AGL acquisition (closed 30 Jan 2026) contributed about 2 pts to revenue and 3 pts to EBITDA growth in the quarter. Management guided to 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA growth for FY27 and said margins would be held at last year's levels.

financial_highlights.value: INR 2,963 mn from operations; total revenue INR 3,124 mn

EBITDA margin to be maintained at last year's levels; management said it will not allow margin erosion but is investing in AI/ML, brand building and US sales leadership.
Growth expected mainly from LGD capacity build-up and deeper penetration in natural diamonds, with AGL gemstone certification as a fifth segment.
Management said FY26 was ahead of the original guidance and that FY25 was over-delivered; the FY27 numbers are broad guidelines rather than firm targets.
Q4 is seasonally strong for LGD mix; management expects the LGD mix to taper through the year after Christmas and Diwali quarters.
capex_capacity: Lab-grown manufacturing capacity additions are happening mainly in Surat, India; management said the full impact of capacity additions has not yet shown in results and will ramp through FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA growth achievable, and will INR depreciation help margins?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company has aimed for these growth rates for two years and expects them to continue. Margins are to be held at last year's levels despite investment in AI/ML, brand and the US sales organisation.

qa_highlights.question: Has LGD and ND pricing remained stable, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: No structural pricing changes in Q4. Mix is an outcome rather than a driver, and the company focuses on the growth of each segment.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the decline in natural diamond jewelry, and what is the US leadership progress?
qa_highlights.answer: The decline is attributed to gold and silver price increases and volatility in India. A new US leader has been in place for 3–4 months and the sales team is being strengthened.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs not rise after the gemologist hiring plan, and how do exports square with the growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost rose 16% QoQ as costs built up. Management said export values in rupees or dollars understate volume, since LGD carats have roughly doubled while value per carat has fallen.

qa_highlights.question: What is IGI's market share in natural diamonds, and why are 30–35% of stones uncertified?
qa_highlights.answer: IGI is second globally, with roughly 20–25% global share and over 50% in India (estimates). Uncertified stones are mostly small sizes with low commercial value.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers behind FY27 EBITDA growth exceeding revenue growth, and where is LGD capacity being added?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage, since incremental revenue flows largely to the bottom line. All LGD capacity additions are in Surat, India, while the US and Europe act as retail and marketing offices.

544311|2026-06.headline: IGI Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23% YoY to INR 3,708 million and EBITDA 29% to INR 2,238 million, with 60.4% margin.
544311|2026-06.overview: Consolidated certification revenue grew 23% YoY to INR 3,598 million on 17% volume growth, with LGD, LGD Jewellery and the newly consolidated AGL gemstones segment all contributing. Group EBITDA rose 29% to INR 2,238 million and margin expanded 270 bps to 60.4%, while PAT grew 31% to INR 1,657 million. India standalone growth was slower on EBITDA (15%) because of commission payouts to overseas subsidiaries, front-loaded IPL sponsorship and headcount additions. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA growth, with AGL adding a couple of percentage points on top.

demand_pricing: Wholesale LGD pricing has been stable at roughly INR 80-120 per carat over the last two years; the last price correction was in April-May 2024, when LGD realisation fell about 25%.

Management reported a turnaround-time target of two to three days and said AI/ML is being used to cut processing time.

qa_highlights.question: How will LGD pricing per report evolve as grower capacity expands, and will volume growth force price concessions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rising consumer demand for affordable LGD keeps growers expanding, and that certification by IGI is what makes an LGD stone a diamond; no pricing pressure was specifically quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15% revenue guidance inclusive of AGL?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the 15% applies to the base business, with AGL adding a couple of percentage points on top.

qa_highlights.question: How much was the IPL marketing spend in the quarter and what was the employee addition?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR 5 crore was spent on sponsorship and marketing in the quarter, with additional leadership investments; management said headcount was added for technical and process staff, but the number was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the realisation improvement and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed about 2-3 points of the 5% ASP growth to AGL and about 2% to base-business mix; underlying pricing is described as stable, and higher carat per report was cited.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the international EBITDA margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to leads from overseas retailers, with commission payouts from India to these geographies recorded in other expenses; operating leverage was said to flow through similarly to India.

qa_highlights.question: Is the commission payout to subsidiaries material, and what is the standalone EBITDA ex-commission?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to isolate it, saying the India and overseas businesses are interdependent and the consolidated margin should be the focus; it confirmed incremental consolidated EBITDA is the relevant measure.

qa_highlights.question: How many LGD growers exist and what is the capacity growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give capacity figures; growers are reported to be talking about doubling their business over three years, with US-led demand and increasing India demand.

segments.commentary: Grew 47% in Q2 and 46% in H1. Management cited growth in Europe, Latin America and Australia alongside the US.

Management said no LGD slowdown is expected in coming quarters, citing grower capacity additions. Natural diamond business is expected to keep momentum for the next two quarters.
October trends were described as rock solid, with Diwali on 8 November 2026 versus 20 October 2025, which shifts some festive stocking into October.
Capital allocation order: growth investment first, then M&A, then dividends. Dividend decisions are made by the Board with each results set.
Management expects EBITDA growth to keep outpacing revenue growth through operating leverage, but did not give a steady-state margin figure.
capex_capacity: Large Indian growers are adding reactors and doubling capacity within 3 years, per management; supply is described as at its base rather than its peak.
Operations started in Italy this year, Saudi Arabia is being prepared, and a company was set up in Botswana in September.
AI-based work allocation and scheduling is now in use in labs, letting the same team grade more stones faster without changing grading standards.
AGL colour-stone methods are being rolled out in IGI's other labs, with dedicated setups planned for large customers. Global expansion of AGL services is planned but locations were not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Lab-grown wholesale prices have stabilised in the INR 118-120 range per management's Investor Day deck. Certification costs 2-3% of retail price.

Q2 ARP rose 4% YoY to INR 891: AGL added 2%, and the base business added 2% from a higher LGD mix (54% vs 52%). Sequentially, ARP fell about 12% on a lower LGD loose mix (down 4%) and a higher jewellery mix.
Natural diamond buyers are delaying purchases due to high and volatile gold prices.
Management said 4Cs grading remains the reporting standard and that it sees no demand shift to simplified classification. It said there are no printing rights for certificates granted to anyone.

qa_highlights.question: Is the LGD revenue surge a pre-festive stocking effect, and will Q3 taper?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LGD revenue has been steady at about INR 2,100 million in Q1 and Q2 and expects no slowdown, citing grower capacity additions. Natural growth is expected to pick up, with traction starting and momentum expected to continue for two more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Should guidance be raised given H1 overshoot?

qa_highlights.question: How will the surplus cash be used: M&A or higher dividends?

qa_highlights.question: Is there grading inconsistency at IGI, and are the top Surat manufacturers printing certificates?

qa_highlights.question: Does the AI push allow smaller labs to compete cheaply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IGI's image dataset from c.4.5 million certificates a quarter is hard to replicate and is used to build its AI and ML capability, improving turnaround times.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin in India fall and when will the investments pay off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the India margin drop of about 340 bps to leadership hiring, marketing and commission spend. It gave no timeline for payback, but said the group margin was 60.1% for FY26, 60.4% in Q1 and 61.4% in Q2.

Diwali timing shift means some Q2 festive demand was pulled from Q3 by September stocking. Watch Q3 for payback.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to the INR 7,000 crore-plus revenue target?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Punjab Phase 1 utilisation outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to currency, raw materials and PTA supply?

Phase 2 Punjab and cotton yarn timelines (end FY27 and 10-12 months after ground-breaking) and the still-unannounced equipment orders.
PTA supply delays from GAIL and Indian Oil and the duty waiver status.
