So, whatever I am saying here, I am being very conservative.

544402|2026-03.headline: Jash Engineering FY26 consolidated revenue rose only 1% to INR757 crore; FY27 guidance is INR875 crore at 12-13% PAT margin.
544402|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated income was INR757 crore versus INR746 crore, with management calling the growth disappointing. US tariff volatility (25% in January, 50% in June) led to slower US production, and the Middle East war disrupted Middle East deliveries and shipping to Far East and Southeast Asia. Domestic business grew 18% and held margins, so standalone PAT margin fell only from 14.38% to 13.38%. Management guides FY27 revenue of INR875 crore against an order book of INR899 crore (as on 1 May) and about INR45 crore already billed.

financial_highlights.change: vs 14.39% in FY25 and 14.21% in FY24 (management quoted 14.38% for prior year in opening remarks)
INR827 crore at end-March per BSE monthly data cited by analyst; INR627 crore export, INR272 crore India

financial_highlights.value: INR67 crore total (INR37 crore plant and machinery, INR30 crore acquisitions)
Includes about INR10 crore one-off US bank charge
INR9 crore vs about INR3 crore normal

segments.name: Waterfront Fluid Controls (UK)
segments.commentary: Revenue guided to about INR60 crore, 75-85% of last year; UK AMP cycle slowdown delayed growth, with GBP5.5-6 million (about INR65-70 crore) projected and strong growth expected from H2. Penstocks UK acquisition completed early April, to merge with Waterfront.

segments.name: Rodney Hunt (US)
segments.commentary: Order book about USD38-39 million; FY26 revenue around USD30 million, FY27 target USD38 million, more than 25% growth on last year. New Houston plant and Saudi plant targeted for commissioning by December 2027.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Water control gates are the largest product line, followed by screens and valves (valves rose to 13% of mix from 11%); hydro power, pumping and other about 8%. Mix shift away from Far East (16% to 10%) noted by analyst.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Management cites about 44.5% of business in India and about 55% outside India. US was about 45% of revenue per analyst.

segments.name: WestTech / Jash Process Equipment
segments.commentary: Acquired mid-January 2026; contributes a small share of FY26 revenue. Guided to about INR40 crore in FY27 (analyst reading); outsourced manufacturing to be moved into Jash plants to cut costs.

segments.name: Shivpad (India)
segments.commentary: Merged into Jash Engineering; Q4 quality and labour issues described as largely resolved after retraining team at Indore; no incremental capacity added.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue target INR875 crore, backed by INR899 crore order book and about INR45 crore billed as of early May; INR28 crore negotiated and INR80 crore under negotiation.
FY27 PAT margin guided at 12-13%; gross margin guided at 50-55%.

Five-year target to double revenue from INR757 crore to above INR1,500 crore; capacity of about INR1,200 crore on 2-3 shifts with current Indian plants, rising above INR1,500 crore once Houston and Saudi plants are online.
Rodney Hunt USD target: USD75 million in five years, from about USD30 million today.
Q4 gross margin gain attributed to forex (billing at about INR92/USD against INR82 estimate); management says it lasts while the dollar stays high.
FY27 capex planned at about INR15-16 crore for the five Indian plants; US and Saudi capex not yet quantified.
Singapore sea-level projects: offers of about USD800-900 million submitted; first orders possibly from 2029, awards from 2028.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR67 crore: INR37 crore plant and machinery and INR30 crore acquisitions.
FY27 Indian plant capex about INR15-16 crore across five plants.

Rodney Hunt Houston plant: land and drawings approved, but cost quotes have risen to USD7-8.5 million versus USD4.2 million placed earlier; prior contractor closed down. Commissioning target December 2027.
Saudi Arabia plant: company set up, land not yet acquired; site visit planned end-June/July 2026; commissioning target December 2027 (earlier December 2026).
Rodney Hunt Orange (Massachusetts) constrained by production staff shortage; new capacity chosen in Houston.
demand_pricing: US tariff: management says stability matters more than level; 25% to 50% increase mid-year led to under-estimated costs on January-June orders. Section 232 shift cited as continuing uncertainty.
Export order book about INR627 crore; over 75% of export order in hand expected to benefit from forex gains.
Hong Kong Yuen Long Barrage project about INR40 crore (including small gates and valves); Chennai desalination project (VA Tech) over INR35 crore; Saudi Al Haer sewage treatment project in progress.
Middle East deliveries still blocked; order intake continues in Southeast Asia, Middle East, Far East and Europe.
Raw material prices rising: about 20% rise in India raw material cost per CFO; US steel also more expensive.

qa_highlights.question: Is domestic revenue flat in FY27 given INR327 crore FY26 base versus INR320 crore projected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the mix is balanced by choice; domestic margins are higher because low-margin domestic jobs are not taken. Domestic may rise if exports fall short.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 gross margin improvement only forex or pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex-driven: orders quoted at INR82/USD and billed at about INR92 gain INR10 per dollar. Gross margin guided at 50-55% for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance conservative given WestTech and carry-over?
qa_highlights.answer: Management calls it conservative given WestTech integration and the US tariff history; it expects growth of 13-17% and margin of at least 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Rodney Hunt capacity and growth after Houston and Saudi plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Target USD75 million in five years; USD100 million not planned. Plant costs rose sharply, and US hiring constraints shaped the Houston decision.

qa_highlights.question: Are there more acquisitions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is open to opportunities that are small and scalable; it is merging subsidiaries of similar businesses to reduce their number.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Singapore sea-level opportunity size INR5,000-6,000 crore and when does it start?
qa_highlights.answer: Clarified as offers of USD800-900 million, not an order; awards start 2028, first orders 2029, spread over 20-25 years; market share targeted 20-40%.

risks_watch: US tariff regime changes (Section 232 shift) and steel input cost inflation affecting project margins.
Middle East war delaying dispatches; Saudi plant land acquisition and commissioning timeline (December 2027) at risk.
Rodney Hunt Houston plant cost overrun (USD4.2 million to USD7-8.5 million) and hiring constraints in Orange, Massachusetts.
Other expenses inflated by one-off bank charge; overheads growing 7-10% against low revenue growth.
Forex-driven margin gain may reverse if the dollar falls; order book conversion and Q1 billing (INR36 crore overflow from March).
WestTech and Penstocks integration; margin outlook at WestTech not yet guided.
544402|2026-03.management_tone: Candid and conservative on guidance, while confident on the order book and domestic business. Management is cautious on US expansion and attributes the weak year mainly to tariff and war disruption.
key_quotes: If it is 50%, we are happy with that 50% . However, it should continue at that , variation results into our estimating at lower tariff, and then when the higher tariff comes into play, it results into losses for us
So, I would rather remain conservative and try to achieve whatever I say rather than being too optimistic and then failing again and again.
Order flow will not get impacted, if you need water, you need water.

544402|2026-06.headline: Jash Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 17% YoY to Rs156 crore and PAT turned positive at about Rs5 crore; FY27 target Rs875 crore reiterated.
544402|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs156 crore, up about 17% YoY, with PAT moving from about minus Rs5 crore to plus Rs5 crore and gross and EBITDA margins both higher YoY. Management said shipments to Qatar, Singapore and other Middle East customers were held back (about Rs15 crore in total), so the quarter was below what management expected. Consolidated order book stands at Rs932 crore (India Rs293 crore, outside India Rs639 crore). Management reiterated FY27 revenue of Rs875 crore and PAT of about Rs100-105 crore, and said Rs1,500 crore revenue is targeted by 2031.

financial_highlights.change: from about minus Rs5 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: India Rs70 crore; outside India Rs80 crore

financial_highlights.change: PAT up significantly; standalone PAT margin about 13% in Q1

financial_highlights.value: Rs932 crore (India Rs293 crore; outside India Rs639 crore)
Jash Engineering Rs559 crore; Rodney Hunt Rs369 crore; Jash Process Equipment Rs29 crore; Waterfront Rs34 crore

segments.name: Jash Engineering (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 21% YoY with significantly higher PAT; order book Rs559 crore. Management says standalone PAT margin is about 13% in Q1.

segments.name: Rodney Hunt (US)
segments.commentary: Order book Rs369 crore; management targets over $35-36 million revenue in FY27 with profitability, and expects an 8-9% PAT margin. Management called Q1 a 'first quarter blues' quarter. Management also said the order book is close to $40 million.

segments.name: Jash Process Equipment (ex-WesTech)
segments.commentary: Order book only Rs29 crore; management said Rs150-200 crore of orders were lost in the last three to four months and a full review is under way. Management called this entity a concern.

segments.name: Waterfront
segments.commentary: Revenue up marginally YoY but profit up on high-margin executed orders; management reiterated Rs5 million-plus revenue target with significant profit. Order book Rs34 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of Rs875 crore (India Rs320 crore; outside India Rs555 crore), reiterated; management said there is potential to go beyond this but size is premature until Q2 or Q3 results.
FY27 PAT of about Rs100-105 crore stated in closing remarks; separately, PAT margin of 13-14% described as achievable for the year, depending on geopolitics.
Rs1,500 crore revenue targeted by 2031; FY28 revenue guidance of about Rs1,025 crore mentioned.
Further tariff refund of about Rs7.5 crore pending, expected to be filed and resolved in FY27 after legal vetting.
Saudi Arabia plant: land expected by end of CY2026, plant ready by December 2027, operations by March 2028. US (Houston/Orange) plant: land already acquired, contractor being finalised.
capex_capacity: Foundry expansion and gate and valve manufacturing expansion commissioned in Q1 FY27; management says capacity is up about 30%.

Capex estimates of about $12 million for the US plant and $4 million for Saudi Arabia; about $3 million already held as deposits in the US; the rest from internal accruals and debt (management expects debt of about $3-4 million); US banks reportedly willing to fund.
Data-centre pressure vessels: capacity of about 75-80 vessels a year in the existing Indore setup; management says a new plant may be needed if order flow is sustained.
Chennai plant ramp-up is still in progress; new production head moved there two weeks before the call.
demand_pricing: Pipeline: orders worth Rs72 crore already negotiated; a further Rs60 crore under negotiation; management expects about Rs72 crore more to be added in the current month.

Data-centre vessels: first order for 4 units; a 32-unit order under negotiation; more than 600 vessels quoted. Management says per-vessel value is Rs30-60 lakh and margins will be similar to other business.
US tariff: 15.6% currently (10% special tariff plus 5.6%); management is budgeting for 25% and says it will not price for 100%.
About 70% of US orders are to be made in America and 30% in India; management is cautious on new US order booking. A few large orders above $7 million each are under negotiation but not being pushed.
Mahr Maschinenbau (Austria): taking orders now, with manufacturing in UK and India; first jobs are 16 screens (2 for UK, 14 for Iraq); expected revenue about Rs15 crore per the presentation.
Competition in domestic water control gates and industrial process equipment: Tega, Delkor, Metso Minerals named as main competitors.

Singapore: a Rs6,000 crore figure discussed earlier was for project reports, not a bid; management says the overall Singapore investment is around Rs50,000-60,000 crore, spread over 15-20 years, and Jash's equipment is about 10% of project cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was product-wise and region-wise breakup dropped from the presentation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IR team concluded order mix changes too much quarter to quarter, so data will be shown year-on-year going forward; a Q1 split of Rs70 crore India and Rs80 crore outside India was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 margin gain is from tariff refund versus manufacturing benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a combination; the Rs5.6 crore tariff refund was booked in consumption. Dharmendra Jain also said the revenue reversal for deferred March recognition (Rs27-28 crore) was offset in June, leaving about Rs10 crore positive.

qa_highlights.question: Rodney Hunt margin profile and path to 10% PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 40% of revenue is from old orders and 60% from new orders; expected PAT margin is 8-9%; 10% may be reached by FY28 if things go well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Russia-sanctions/tariff risk and bidding in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bidding continues but aggressive order-chasing has slowed; it will review after the next US visit, and a US Senate bill was cited as a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Saudi and US plant timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi: approvals received, land application submitted, plant ready by December 2027 and operational by March 2028. US: land acquired, contractor to be finalised; both targeted in operation by March 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs875 crore FY27 target expected to be exceeded and what is executable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said order book of Rs932 crore is not all executable this year because some orders are deferred to FY28; there is scope to exceed Rs875 crore but it is too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Jash Process Equipment (WesTech) underperform?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costing systems differed from what was expected at acquisition and marketing was not aggressive; a two-to-three-quarter transition is needed to set a clear direction.

risks_watch: US tariff and Russia-sanctions bill: management is budgeting 25% against the current 15.6%, has slowed aggressive order-chasing, and is not pricing for 100%; a US Senate bill was cited as a live risk.

Middle East shipments: Rs15 crore of Qatar, Singapore and Middle East material held back (Qatar stuck for over three months; Red Sea route closed after Houthi attacks); Singapore payment dispute on a particular client.
Jash Process Equipment (ex-WesTech): order book only Rs29 crore after Rs150-200 crore of orders lost in three to four months; full review under way, with a two-to-three-quarter transition.
Order book conversion: Rs932 crore order book is not fully executable in FY27 as some orders are deferred to FY28; Rs875 crore target depends on Rs72 crore pipeline additions this month.
Rodney Hunt: Q1 described as a weak quarter ('first quarter blues'); 8-9% PAT margin path to 10% depends on geopolitics; monitor Q2 and Q3 execution.

Tariff refund pipeline: further Rs7.5 crore refund pending legal vetting, expected in FY27; US and Saudi plant timelines (Saudi land by end CY2026, US contractor not yet finalised) and funding mix (about $3-4 million debt).
key_quotes: So, I would say overall the quarter has been satisfactory, not as much as I would have desired, but it is still much better than what we were last year.
Bidding has not been slowed down, but aggressively trying to get orders has been slowed down because the situation is so alarming that if something goes wrong, we spoil the margin.
Whenever you acquire a new company, we always think everything is very rosy at the time of acquisition.
And so, with that on positive note, I will say that we would meet our projections given earlier, which is Rs.875 crore with around Rs.100-105 crore profit after tax for the year.
544402|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the full year: management reiterated Rs875 crore revenue and Rs100-105 crore PAT and called the year 'quite bullish'. It was cautious and defensive on the US market, Russia-sanctions and tariff risk, Rodney Hunt margins, and the Jash Process Equipment underperformance, and it avoided giving firm numbers on FY27 upside or the 10% Rodney Hunt PAT timing.

544403|2026-06.headline: ABLBL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 2,046 crore and EBITDA 14% to Rs 327 crore, with margin up 50 bps to 16%.
544403|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 2,046 crore, the third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with EBITDA up 14% to Rs 327 crore and PAT up 21% to Rs 29 crore. Lifestyle Brands grew 10% to Rs 1,725 crore at an 18.5% EBITDA margin, while Emerging Brands grew 19% to Rs 332 crore at a 4.3% margin. Management attributed a modest demand moderation to adhik maas during the peak wedding period and a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2 that depressed wholesale growth to 5%. Gross margin contracted about 150 bps, which management attributed to channel mix and provisioning rather than raw material costs.

financial_highlights.change: Down ~150 bps YoY per analyst question; management called it marginally lower

segments.name: Lifestyle Brands
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,725 crore (+10% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 319 crore at 18.5% margin. Retail grew 10% with 7% LFL across almost 3,000 stores; e-commerce grew 23% group-wide and over 50% on the company's own platform.

segments.name: Emerging Brands (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 332 crore (+19% YoY), with retail LFL of 11% and e-commerce growth above 30%. Retail network crossed 400 stores; EBITDA margin 4.3%, up 240 bps.

segments.name: Channels (group)
segments.commentary: Retail grew 10% with 8% LFL, the seventh straight quarter of LFL growth. Wholesale grew 5% on primary billing, though underlying secondary growth was early double-digit.

guidance_outlook: Gross store additions of more than 300 in FY27, with net additions of 150-200 after closures of about 120-140 stores.
Cost inflation of 3-4% expected for Q2-Q3 FY27 from raw materials, logistics and minimum wages; mostly to be offset by productivity and cost rationalisation, plus small price hikes.
Management expects Q1+Q2 wholesale primary billing to even out, with the Q1 shortfall moving into Q2.
Small-town retail (about 500 stores) is about 15-16% of retail revenue and is expected to exceed 20% of portfolio over the next three to four years.
Management aims for sustained double-digit growth and margin expansion; it expects retail to grow in early double digits.
Reebok revenue is about Rs 500 crore (from about Rs 250 crore at acquisition); management sees close to 20% long-term growth possible.
capex_capacity: Retail footprint of 3,362 stores (about 5 million sq ft) across more than 800 cities and towns at quarter end; more than 65 gross openings in Q1 (Aditya Bansal's question: 68 gross).
Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha; Karnataka concentration is limited.
Reebok has about 200 stores versus 500-700 for other premium brands, indicating a long retail runway.
Van Heusen Innerwear distribution is about 38,000-40,000 outlets; management expects roughly 20% network addition over the next couple of years.
Two Reebok factories still operate outside India pending BIS annual renewal; domestic sourcing is being built up.
demand_pricing: Q1 demand was broadly consistent with the prior-year trend; adhik maas caused modest moderation in the peak wedding period.
Wholesale grew 5%, with a 10-15 day festive primary-billing shift into Q2; management says secondary was early double-digit.
Small-town stores grew over 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros; small-town growth has been double-digit for five consecutive quarters.
Price hikes were small and varied by brand and category, taken to offset input-cost increases; management says no meaningful apparel inflation is visible.
Marketing spend was about 3.5% of sales in Q1, down from last year because of IPL spend in the base quarter.
E-commerce profitability is said to be close to retail profitability, with growth now coming without deep discounting.
Quick commerce is small for the company; innerwear is the largest category there.
Casual wear share is rising by 2-3 percentage points a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why the divergence between primary and secondary sales in Lifestyle wholesale, and how will it evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: A 10-15 day festive timing shift moved primary billing into Q2; management expects Q1 and Q2 combined to be as strong as other channels.

qa_highlights.question: What cost inflation is expected and will prices rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 saw marginal to no cost pressure. Management expects 3-4% cost increase in Q2-Q3 from raw materials, logistics and minimum wages, offset mainly by productivity and some price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 150 bps gross margin contraction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited channel mix and slightly higher inventory-age provisioning, not raw material costs, and said the effect is not material and will even out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to Karnataka minimum wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Garmenting was never part of the notified hike, which is under High Court challenge. Manufacturing is about 40% of production, diversified across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

qa_highlights.question: How are the net store adds and LFL growth reconciled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to more than 300 gross and 150-200 net additions in FY27 after 120-140 closures; network growth of 5-6% plus 7-8% LFL supports early double-digit retail growth.

qa_highlights.question: How do small-town and Tier 1 growth compare, and how is Gen-Z targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Tier 3-4 is growing above 15% versus about 10% in Tier 1 metros. Gen-Z is served through sub-brands and collections (for example Peter England's Vybe), with no share figures disclosed.

risks_watch: Wholesale growth of 5% and gross margin contraction of about 150 bps in Q1; watch whether the festive shift reverses in Q2.
3-4% cost inflation in Q2-Q3 and the wage-regulation outcome in Karnataka at the High Court.
Consumer wallet pressure from inflation; management says it has seen no meaningful demand shift so far but is cautious about H2.
Reebok BIS certification risk on imports from factories outside India, renewed annually.
Net store additions of 150-200 against a gross plan above 300; watch LFL sustainability through closures.
key_quotes: So, when you look at Quarter 2, you will find the Quarter 1 plus Quarter 2 in as strong a place as rest of the channels.
We expect a major part of it comes through productivity and the rest through cost rationalization.
But we are cautious that this may play out in the second half of the year.
Over the years, we have managed to bring this channel profitability very close to our retail profitability.
544403|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on headline growth, margin expansion and store roll-out, and openly described Q1 wholesale as a timing shift. It was cautious on H2 demand from consumer wallet inflation and on 3-4% cost inflation in Q2-Q3, and it deflected on brand-wise revenue splits and gross margin drivers.

544405|2026-03.headline: Belrise Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR25,528 mn with EBITDA margin at 11.4%; FY26 adjusted PAT up 41% to INR5,020 mn.
544405|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total revenue grew 12% YoY to INR25,528 mn and manufacturing revenue grew 21% to INR21,763 mn, while EBITDA rose only 5% to INR2,901 mn, with margin at 11.4%. Adjusted PAT rose 17% to INR1,290 mn, with a one-time INR94.7 mn operational loss at the aerospace and defence subsidiary absorbed in the quarter. For FY26, total revenue grew 15% to INR95,091 mn and adjusted PAT grew 41% to INR5,020 mn. Management reported new two-wheeler and exhaust/fuel-tank orders, the Chester Hall acquisition in the UK, and guidance of mid-teens growth with broadly stable margins for FY27.

segments.name: Two-wheeler and three-wheeler
segments.commentary: Contributed 83.2% of Q4 manufacturing revenue and 82.0% in FY26. Content per vehicle rose 65-70% during FY26 (management also cited 60-65% on another basis), with two-wheeler content per vehicle moving from about INR12,000 to INR20,000 including the Badve Auto Comps and Eximius merger.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.2% of Q4 and 5.2% of FY26 manufacturing revenue. Suspension business currently serves two- and three-wheeler OEMs only, not PV OEMs.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.4% of Q4 and 8.3% of FY26 manufacturing revenue. CV segment grew 32% in Q4 and 35% in FY26.

segments.name: Four-wheeler
segments.commentary: Four-wheeler business grew 71% in Q4 and 37% in FY26 (transcript initially said 31%, corrected to 37% in footnote). Content per vehicle rose from about INR25,000 to INR40,000-45,000 with the H-One acquisition.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence (Belrise Aerospace and Defense)
segments.commentary: Acquired SDM (France) in Q3 FY26 and Chester Hall (UK) in Q4 FY26. Q4 carried a one-time operational loss of INR94.7 mn from startup costs, legal and professional fees and personnel costs; management expects SDM to be EBITDA positive in 2027.

guidance_outlook: Mid-teens revenue growth expected to continue, supported by the order book.
EBITDA margins expected to remain broadly stable versus FY26 levels (FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 12.1%); cost pressures seen as short-term and not expected to affect medium-to-long-term margins.
Capex expected at 6% to 6.5% of manufacturing revenue, with R&D included within this range.
Doubling four-wheeler and CV revenue versus FY25 within the current fiscal year requires about 40% to 45% growth, per management endeavour.
Final dividend of INR0.55 per share declared.
SDM expected to turn EBITDA positive in 2027 after the one-time Q4 loss.
capex_capacity: Bangalore brownfield expansion to supply exhaust systems and fuel tanks to a fast-growing two- and three-wheeler OEM; production slated to begin Q2 FY27 with peak annual revenue of INR90 crore.
Large order from a Japanese two-wheeler OEM for exhaust systems and metal components; peak annual revenue about INR220 crore, production starting Q4 FY26-27 (transcript says 'this fiscal year').
Haridwar plant ramp-up: trial parts dispatched to a large two-wheeler OEM; peak production targeted within FY27, sourcing from Greater Noida and Pantnagar.
Chassis, battery trays and metal components for an emerging EV player; supplies expected to start Q3 of the fiscal year.
Management declined to give plant-level utilisation or break-even timelines for new plants (Chennai, Pune, Bhiwandi).
Over 850 robots deployed across the company; medium-term vision is a large integrated aerospace and defence facility in India.
demand_pricing: Sector saw strong Q4 growth, helped by the GST rate cut late last year; management hopes for structural rather than pull-forward demand.
Back-to-back raw material pricing model passes steel and plastic cost changes to customers with a lag, limiting margin impact.

Q4 headwinds: oil-crisis-related supply chain disruption, higher raw material, energy and logistics costs, and Haryana minimum wage increase. Fuel and labour costs expected to be passed on over time; transport cost recovery still under discussion with key OEMs.
Two-wheeler segment only recently returned to pre-COVID peak; management sees long-term headroom.
Aerospace demand described as very strong, with OEM order backlogs of 8-10+ years; qualification cycles of 12-24 months cited as the main barrier.
Chester Hall: rejection rate 0.5%-1%; advanced discussions to transfer part of its subcontracted work to India.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend through the quarters, and how will the company absorb commodity, fuel and labour cost pressures to hold full-year margins stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 was hit by the INR94.7 mn one-time aerospace loss and acquisition fees, both called one-time. Fuel and labour costs to be passed on over time; transport costs still under discussion. Full-year guidance maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How large can the two new two-wheeler OEM customers become over two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects both to become very large over 2-3 years, with content per vehicle rising sharply and cross-model penetration. The Japanese OEM order is about INR200 crore annually, and the Bangalore program is one of the sharpest ramp-ups in three years.

qa_highlights.question: How much can aerospace contribute in four to five years, and can manufacturing move to India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets aerospace above 10% of revenue and sees India as a best-cost base. It is in talks with OEMs to shift Chester Hall subcontracted work and new orders from Europe to India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the QIP of INR2,000 crore for?
qa_highlights.answer: Only an enabling resolution has been approved; no specific use was given, and management will update when there is progress.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive edge in exhaust systems, and what margin is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Edge comes from automation (850+ robots), high verticalisation, NVH engineering and stainless-steel plating capability. Management corrected the INR400 crore figure: the orders are INR220 crore and INR90 crore, about INR310 crore peak combined. No margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will R&D spend scale with aerospace and steering/high-tensile products?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is included within the 6%-6.5% capex range. The R&D team has more than 163 people. Management directionally agreed on hiring and partnerships but gave no specific target.

qa_highlights.question: Will the trading business be localised, spun off or hived off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not commented on hiving off the trading business and will update later.

qa_highlights.question: Does suspension have passenger vehicle customers, and what are suspension and H-One revenue and PAT figures?
qa_highlights.answer: No PV customers yet; the suspension business serves only two- and three-wheeler OEMs, with four marquee customers, three onboarded in the last 18 months. Management did not have suspension, polymer or H-One revenue and PAT figures and will follow up offline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inorganic strategy for FY27, and what are the content per vehicle and plant utilisation trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are chosen on customers, capabilities and verticalisation at mild valuations (book value to mid-single-digit EV/EBITDA); all four acquisitions are EPS and ROCE accretive. Content per vehicle has risen 60-65% in two-wheelers and is 40-45% in four-wheelers and CVs. Plant utilisation and break-even were not disclosed.

risks_watch: Margin trajectory: management guides FY26-level EBITDA margins (12.1%) but Q4 EBITDA margin was 11.4%; watch whether the one-time INR94.7 mn aerospace loss and acquisition fees recur or fade in Q1 FY27.
Oil-crisis cost pass-through: fuel and labour costs to be passed on over time, transport cost recovery still under discussion with key OEMs; a lag in recovery could compress margins.

Execution of new programmes: Bangalore brownfield (production from Q2 FY27), Japanese OEM exhaust/metal order (production from Q4 FY26-27), Haridwar ramp to peak within FY27, and EV-player chassis supplies from Q3; monitor ramp timing.
Aerospace: SDM expected EBITDA positive in 2027; Chester Hall transfer of subcontracted work to India is in advanced talks but not yet signed; qualification cycles of 12-24 months.

Capital and disclosure gaps: QIP of INR2,000 mn-equivalent (INR2,000 crore) approved only as an enabling resolution with no use specified; plant-level utilisation and break-even not disclosed; suspension, polymer and H-One standalone revenue and PAT to follow offline; trading business hive-off undecided.
key_quotes: Our first commitment was to deliver mid -teens revenue growth while keeping our EBITDA margins stable. And I am glad to share that we achieved this.
We expect this loss to be one -time and expect SDM to be EBITDA positive in the year 2027.
At this point of time, it's only an enabling resolution.
We are unable to comment on plant-specific questions on utilization and break-even.

544405|2026-06.headline: Belrise Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR25,465 million, EBITDA margin 11.5%, PAT up 9% to INR1,217 million.

544407|2026-03.headline: Aegis Vopak FY26 revenue rose 17% to INR923.1 crores and net profit 52.1% to INR341.9 crores; Q4 revenue up 22.2% to INR243.5 crores.
544407|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the company's first full year as a listed entity, with revenue from operations up 17% YoY to INR923.1 crores and operating EBITDA up 19.4% to INR686.5 crores. Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22.2% YoY to INR243.5 crores, with Q4 operating EBITDA up 24.2% to INR179.2 crores and net profit up 15.3% to INR73.9 crores. Management said FY25 and FY26 figures were restated to consolidate Hindustan Aegis LPG Limited, which was acquired as a 75% stake in Haldia. JNPT liquid expansion (318,100 CBM) mostly operational in H1 FY27, with full completion targeted by around October; contributes from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What supports a USD5 billion capex plan when only USD1.2 billion has been spent so far?

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue mix by customer and contract term?

qa_highlights.question: Lease expiries and business mix over the next three years?

qa_highlights.question: FY27 guidance and FY27/FY28 capex?

qa_highlights.question: JNPT expansion timing and realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning starts around next month, with most capacity running by H1 and completion around October; realisations are expected to be strong from the start.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kandla-Gorakhpur, Mangalore-Hassan and Uran-Chakan pipeline timing?

544407|2026-06.headline: Aegis Vopak Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, with liquid terminaling up 31% and operating EBITDA up 15.6% to INR179.4 crore.
544407|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 12.4% YoY to INR233.8 crore, led by liquid terminaling (INR126.5 crore, +31% YoY) while gas terminaling fell 3.5% YoY to INR107.2 crore. Operating EBITDA rose 15.6% YoY to INR179.4 crore (about 76.7% margin) and cash PAT was INR124.9 crore. Management said the board approved a 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA and 49,577 cbm of liquid capacity at Kochi, and that the Pipavav ammonia terminal (36,000 MT static) was commissioned. Management framed a $5 billion capex plan through FY2030-31, of which about INR10,000 crore is to be commissioned by March/June 2027.

segments.name: Liquid terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR126.5 crore, up 31% YoY, driven by higher volumes, new capacity and product mix; management cited JNPA plot 1 maturing (about INR6,000 realization per unit vs blended INR3,000) and better-located capacity commissioned last year.

segments.name: Gas terminaling
segments.commentary: Revenue INR107.2 crore, down 3.5% YoY on LPG import disruption from the Middle East; management said volumes held up via diversified sourcing and multi-location distribution. Standard throughput rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow volumes at least 25% YoY every year; management said AVTL delivered 3.9 million MT in the last year and expects more than 25% growth.
Liquid capacity to rise from about 1.7 million cbm to about 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end.
About INR10,000 crore of expansion (JNPA, ammonia, liquid) expected to be commissioned by March 2027 or June 2027 at the latest.
Kochi 49,577 cbm expected by early next financial year; CRL4 at Kandla (about 94,148 cbm) targeted for later next year.

capex_capacity: JNPA expansion: 318,100 cbm liquid storage, 77,236 MT LPG capacity and a 35,000 MT LPG bottling plant, total outlay INR1,675 crore; first phase of about 100,000 cbm expected in Q3 FY27.
JNPA: board approved a 52,000 MT refrigerated LPG tank; existing liquid capacity about 101,900 cbm.
Kochi: board sanctioned 49,577 cbm; total liquid capacity to reach 132,122 cbm from 82,545 cbm.

Pipavav: 36,000 MT ammonia storage commissioned; 0.5 million MT/yr 15-year take-or-pay petroleum product agreement to start by year-end via additional liquid rail gantry; VLGC-compliant jetty by APM Terminals expected this year; Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline connection expected in the first half of FY27 (per Q&A, 2-3 months).

Mangalore: 75,000 cbm added last year, total 193,000 cbm; evaluating 60,000 cbm more; LPG rail gantry and bottling investment INR52.5 crore. Haldia: 226,890 cbm liquid storage plus 3 acres of land acquired; Haldia-Panagarh pipeline (HPCL, 60 km) expected October-November 2026.
demand_pricing: LPG throughput is priced per metric ton, not per storage day, and management said there is no escalation; the focus is on volume growth.

Management attributed gas volume resilience to diversified sourcing (ITOCHU partnership, non-Middle East cargoes) and ullage availability; it said domestic LPG shortfall had recovered to about 80-85% of normal by July.
Ammonia realizations described as 2.5-3x LPG realizations; first-year utilization projected at 20-25% of the 36,000 MT static capacity (prorated for an August start).
Pipavav: 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc for part of ammonia capacity for its DAP plant.

qa_highlights.question: Are LPG throughput charges fixed by counterparty and term, and why haven't terminal charges risen while distribution margins did?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard rate about INR1,175/MT, INR1,200/MT for some principals; charges are per MT with no escalation. Management said terminaling is infrastructure usage, while distribution margins reflect sourcing and inventory risk during the geopolitical disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AVTL gain share versus national LPG imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited non-Middle East sourcing (none of its ships were stuck), a partner in ITOCHU, and wider distribution using freed-up ullage across more locations than Mumbai and Kandla.

qa_highlights.question: Is 25% volume growth sustainable, and what is the Haldia pipeline impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for at least 25% YoY growth; four pipelines are due this year (Jamnagar-Loni done; Kandla-Gorakhpur at Kandla and Pipavav in 2-3 months; Haldia-Panagarh in 2-3 months). Haldia-Panagarh is HPCL's 60 km line; the Panagarh bottling plant is 0.5 million MT/yr and currently about 0.25 million MT is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and liquid capacity path to FY28, and what is the Pipavav take-or-pay economics?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10,000 crore to be commissioned by March/June 2027; liquid capacity 1.7 to 2.2 million cbm in FY27 and close to 3 million cbm by FY28 end. The Pipavav 0.5 million MT is higher utilization of existing capacity via rail gantry, not new tankage.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth plans beyond the INR10,000 crore phase and the $5 billion program?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing organic and inorganic options, inland depots, strategic storage and industrial terminals, and said binding agreements will be announced as signed. The $5 billion plan through FY2030-31 is reaffirmed, with timing expected to be lumpy.

qa_highlights.question: Why did liquid revenue jump when capacity did not change?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity added last year was only partly in the base year and has now matured, JNPA plot 1 is fully running, and product mix has changed, which takes time.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?

544408|2026-06.headline: Leela Palaces Q1 FY27: operating revenue up 28% to INR3,520 mn and operating EBITDA up 41% to INR1,434 mn, margin 41%.

In the new SPV, our shareholding with GMR is 30% and therefore it doesn't get consolidated going forward.

So, the investment is already made, the capacity is in place, and we are ready. When traffic returns, and history tells us it will, TFS is well -positioned to benefit from the network and groundwork we have put in place over the past 12 months.

544444|2026-03.headline: Glen Industries H2 FY26 PAT of INR8.20 crore on INR108.60 crore income; management targets INR500 crore turnover and INR90 crore EBITDA in FY28.
544444|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income was INR205.16 crore, EBITDA INR38.50 crore and PAT INR16.50 crore, with H2 FY26 income of INR108.60 crore, EBITDA INR18.69 crore and PAT INR8.20 crore. Management attributed margin compression from about 23-24% in FY25 to about 18-19% in FY26 to passing on PLA price benefits to customers. A capacity expansion (plastic food containers roughly 3x, plus about 750 MT paper-based food packaging including paper cups) has a revised project cost of INR130-135 crore, now expected to start commercial production from September 2026. Raw material prices rose sharply after the West Asia conflict, with polypropylene peaking near INR150/kg and now about INR135/kg.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin FY26 (as cited on call)
financial_highlights.change: down from about 23-24% in FY25 per management and analyst

financial_highlights.value: Thin-wall food containers 82.72%; PLA and paper straws 17.16%; mould designing 0.12%

segments.name: Thin-wall food containers
segments.commentary: About 82.72% of FY26 revenue with capacity utilisation of about 77.74%. Raw-material price pass-through is monthly, impacting turnover by about INR2.5 crore per month during the recent price rise.

segments.name: PLA and paper straws
segments.commentary: About 17.16% of FY26 revenue; utilisation about 28.33% (PLA) and 34.13% (paper). Management says these are seasonal, peak-season-only (4-4.5 months), and sees utilisation capped near 35%; no further straw capex planned.

segments.name: Mould designing services
segments.commentary: About 0.12% of FY26 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY28 target: turnover above INR500 crore with EBITDA of about INR90 crore (about 18-19% margin), based on pre-war raw material prices.
Expansion revenue: existing capacity about INR200-215 crore; new project adds about INR300 crore; combined about INR500 crore per annum.
FY27 incremental revenue from new capacity estimated at INR100-125 crore, depending on stabilisation speed; some revenue expected in FY27.
Commercial production targeted from September 2026, with full project operational by October-December 2026.
Management says EBITDA margin sustainable at 18-19% over the long run; paper cup margin around 18%.
Eight additional injection moulding machines (20 to 29) expected to add about INR15 crore annual revenue.
capex_capacity: Expansion project cost revised to INR130-135 crore from about INR100 crore, citing rupee depreciation (85-86 to about 96 per USD-equivalent as stated), wider scope in building and machinery, and printing machines.
Funding: INR50 crore term loan and INR50 crore IPO proceeds for original INR100 crore; incremental INR30-32 crore from internal accruals; no additional debt or equity planned.
Commissioning delayed about three months due to SIR and West Bengal elections holding up building plan approvals; commercial production now expected from September 2026.
Injection moulding machines raised from 20 to 29.
Existing land parcel remains mortgaged to bank; to be released after new facility is capitalised.
Management says no further straw capex; straw capacity sufficient for demand.
demand_pricing: PLA price about INR205/kg now vs INR195-197/kg pre-war; polypropylene about INR135/kg now vs INR90-92/kg pre-war, peaking near INR150/kg; paper stable (locally sourced).
Pass-through: PLA price changes passed on to customers from March; food container prices adjusted monthly; management says absolute margin preserved though percentage margin falls.

Raw material sourcing: about 85% imported (mainly Middle East earlier), 15% from Indian Oil; imported material from China at 5-6% price advantage; Middle East supply expected to normalise in 1-2 months.
Raw material inventory above 3 months currently; finished goods 2-2.5 months.

Customer concentration: no customer above 5-6% of total sales; top 4-5 export customers (US, UK, Greece) account for about 50-60% of export sales; over 300 domestic distributors; Parle about 25% of corporate sales as stated.
Exports: about 40 recurring international clients across Europe, US, Australia, South Korea; export revenue declined in FY26 due to lower polymer prices vs FY25, not volume or war.
Geography: eastern India about 35% of revenue; north and west next.
Competition: few national/export players in India with HACCP and FSSC certifications; management cites brand and standards as barriers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline and what is the sustainable range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PLA price benefits were passed to customers in FY26, lowering margin from about 23% (FY25) to about 18-19%; sustainable range stated as 18-19%.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion capex, timeline and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Project cost revised to INR130-135 crore; commercial production from September 2026, full operations by December 2026; combined revenue potential about INR500 crore per annum.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation of straws and paper products given seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said straw utilisation can not exceed about 35% due to 4-4.5 month peak season; paper cups are not currently manufactured, and the expansion includes paper cups with about 18% margin.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of raw material price rise on FY27 turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated about INR2-2.5 crore per month turnover uplift from price pass-through, with no change to absolute margin; guidance remains based on pre-war prices.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any production disruption from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no disruption; about two months of inventory was held and two months' requirement was imported from China.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: PP and PLA prices remain elevated; management says guidance excludes current prices and could reverse within about two months of conflict ending.
Margin percentage compression in price-rising periods; EBITDA margin moved from about 17-18% to higher levels in prior halves.
Execution risk on the new project: approvals delayed about three months, commissioning expected September 2026, with capacity ramp-up pace determining FY27 revenue.
Seasonal demand in straws (beverage sector) keeping utilisation low around 28-34%.
Working capital build: raw material inventory above 3 months and inventory cycle of 5-5.5 months against about 4 months normal, affecting ROCE.
Customer and export concentration: top export accounts about 50-60% of export sales.
Undisclosed land parcel and future diversification plans; management declined to specify new products.
544444|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing pass-through and FY28 targets, but defensive when questioned on margin decline and straw utilisation. Several answers were repetitive or unclear, and management declined to disclose future product plans.
key_quotes: So, if we add both of them, existing capacity and the additional capacity, we will be able to achieve a turnover of INR500 crores per annum going forward.
We always have been maintaining that our EBITDA margin will be within 18% to 19%.
We are not projecting on the basis of increased promising prices. We are projecting on the stable prices before the war.
No customer is more than, you can say, 5% to 6% of our total sales.

544447|2026-06.headline: Smartworks Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR 546 crores, with normalized EBITDA margin at 19.6% and guidance of 28-30% revenue growth reaffirmed.
544447|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR 546 crores, up 44% YoY and 5% QoQ, while normalized EBITDA grew 74% YoY to INR 107 crores at a 19.6% margin. Normalized PAT nearly tripled YoY to INR 39 crores. Growth was supported by mature-centre occupancy (committed 92%) and a higher share of 1,000+ seat clients, GCCs and multi-city clients, though overall occupancy dipped to 81% from 82% QoQ as new centres filled up. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance (28-30% revenue growth, 19-20% normalized EBITDA margin, 13 million sq ft by March 2027) and started a heavy capex cycle of INR 550-600 crores for the year.

financial_highlights.change: vs 16.2% in Q1 FY26 and 19% in Q4 FY26
vs negative INR 4.9 crores a year ago
vs INR 22 crores in same quarter last year

segments.name: Core rental (enterprise annuity)
segments.commentary: Enterprise annuity demand is 92% of rental revenue; 1,000+ seat cohort is 41% of revenue (37% in FY26). Committed contracted revenue is about INR 5,400 crores, covering 87% of FY27 revenue.

segments.name: GCC clients
segments.commentary: GCCs contribute 21% of revenue, up from 15% in FY26. Recent wins include a Swiss bank and a manufacturing GCC; a Japanese NBFC subsidiary took space in Mumbai.

segments.name: Singapore
segments.commentary: Work Studio acquired, taking the portfolio to over 1,500 seats (about 2% of revenue); 400-450 seats now available to sell, funded from Singapore cash flows. Management says no further meaningful expansion planned.

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: Non-lease rental revenue rose to over INR 68 crores from INR 22 crores YoY, and is take-rate based with no direct cost. VAS guidance is not built into the FY27 projections.

guidance_outlook: Reaffirmed FY27 revenue growth of 28-30%, normalized EBITDA margin of 19-20%, and operational footprint above 13 million sq ft by March 2027.
Plans to add 2.5-3 million sq ft of operational space in FY27; more than 3.5 million sq ft signed, giving a buffer of about 0.7-0.8 million sq ft.
Capex guided at INR 550-600 crores for FY27, with heavy spend in the next two quarters.
Management expects ROCE to expand meaningfully through FY28 as capex cohorts mature.
Revenue jump expected mainly in Q3 or Q4 as new centres ramp up (about 12 months to ramp).
capex_capacity: Operational footprint 10.4 million sq ft as of June 2026; 1.9 million sq ft under fit-out; 0.3 million sq ft added in Q1 and 2.1 million sq ft over the last 12 months.

About 3 million sq ft to come online over the next 9 months, including Eastbridge (Mumbai) and Eastside (Pune), both landing in H2 FY27. Vikhroli asset is 8.15 lakh sq ft, described as the world's largest standalone managed campus.
New fit-out capex is INR 1,350 per sq ft, rising about 5% a year; refurbishment is about 15% of initial capex every three years (around INR 5 per sq ft per year, by management's estimate).
Every building needed for the next two years is secured; FY29 work has begun. Long-term rights give 10-15 years of access.
Security deposits of INR 33 crores paid to landlords to lock buildings for FY28 and part of FY29.
demand_pricing: Occupancy 81% (vs 82% in Q4 FY26), reflecting new centres still filling. Mature centres at 89% on 9.1 million sq ft; committed occupancy 92%. Management guides 80-85% occupancy over the next three quarters.

Seat retention 74% in Q1, with client count down while occupied seats and revenue rose. Management says the churn is deliberate repricing of older, lower-rate clients; the annual retention range it cited was 80-88%.
Realization on incremental mature-footprint seats leased in Q1 FY27 was about INR 181 per sq ft per month, up from about INR 170 a year earlier. Management cited a rental INR 185 per seat figure.
Mix: IT/ITES down to 35% of clients (from over 40%); target 25-30/35%. Multi-city clients 35% of revenue (31% in FY26).
Pre-commitment: about 30-35% of new buildings is pre-committed by existing or incoming clients. Landlord mix is about 65% non-institutional and 35% institutional.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the Singapore Work Studio acquisition, expected revenue and occupancy, and whether fit-out costs of INR 1,350 face inflation.
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired from internal cash flows at roughly construction cost; the target was about 60% occupied. Singapore is about 80,000 sq ft in total and 2% of revenue, with 400-450 seats now available to sell. Expansion will not be meaningful, and capex is set at INR 550-600 crores for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the expansion is speculative, and how much is pre-leased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 30-35% of any new building is pre-committed by existing clients, and occupancy ramps to 80-85% within 13-14 months, as seen on prior centres.

qa_highlights.question: Is the drop in retention a sign of demand weakness, and will similar churn continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 74% was Q2-seasonal churn; mature committed occupancy is 92%, and most churned space is already re-let. Churn is expected to fall in Q3 and Q4, as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there supply risk from developer delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply is covered by a buffer of 0.7-0.8 million sq ft over the 2.5-3 million sq ft target, and management is working with institutional developers such as DLF, Hiranandani, Tata, Panchshil and Salarpuria.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 28-30% guidance built, given the existing base is at 92% committed occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the base is almost fully sold, so growth depends on new centres that take about 12 months to ramp. Growth is expected to show mainly in Q3 or Q4, and the range is one management is confident about.

qa_highlights.question: Why did OCF/EBITDA dip, and what about VAS margins and pricing power?
qa_highlights.answer: The dip reflects INR 33 crores of security deposits paid to landlords. VAS is take-rate based with no direct cost, so it is margin accretive, but it is only in pilot stages and not in FY27 projections. Management said the nearest competitor prices 10-15% higher than Smartworks.

risks_watch: Occupancy may stay at 80-85% in the next three quarters as large new centres ramp, and it could drop further.
Revenue guidance depends on new-centre ramp-up and handover timing, with most of the uplift in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Capex of INR 550-600 crores is front-loaded; FCF is negative (INR -56 crores in Q1) and depends on OCF recovering after deposit payments.
IT/ITES share is falling, and management could not give a call-centre (AI-exposed) breakdown.
Retention of 74% in Q1 needs to recover in the seasonally stronger H2 to validate the 80-88% annual range management cited.
Revenue and EBITDA margin depend on keeping the 19-20% range while absorbing new cohorts.
Management corrected several numbers during the call (Singapore occupancy, seat count, IT/ITES share, retention), so the transcript figures should be checked against the presentation.
544447|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional. Management was emphatic about visibility, compounding margins and supply security. It was more defensive on retention (74%), the OCF/EBITDA dip, and the Q1 occupancy decline, which it attributed to new centres and deliberate repricing.
key_quotes: Smartworks compounds.
Tomorrow's campuses are contracted today.
We don't manage for the quarter; we are building for the decade.
Fewer, bigger, longer-duration clients - that is by design.

544449|2026-03.headline: Anthem FY26 consolidated revenue Rs 2,124 crore (+18% incl. other income), with Q4 record revenue Rs 611 crore (+26% YoY) and Q4 EBITDA margin 48.1%.
544449|2026-03.overview: Anthem closed FY26 with its highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q4, up 26% YoY to Rs 611 crore, with CRDMO up 31% and specialty ingredients up 8%. FY26 EBITDA reached Rs 990 crore (43.4% margin, +31%) and PAT Rs 592 crore (+31%), though full-year revenue growth of about 15% fell short of the company's stated 20% aspiration. Management said destocking by customers is largely behind it and refused to give FY27 or FY28 guidance. Capex is shifting to Unit 4, with Phase 1 of about Rs 1,200 crore to finish by March 2028.

financial_highlights.change: Revenue growth about 15% per CFO; total revenue incl. other income Rs 2,280 crore, +18%

+130% YoY; includes Rs 98 lakh exceptional credit from Labour Code impact

segments.name: CRDMO

segments.name: Specialty ingredients
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 352 crore (17%); Q4 Rs 98 crore, +8% YoY, the first revenue growth after flat first three quarters. Management aspires to around 20% growth; products include serratiopeptidase, vitamins, probiotics and enzymes, sold mainly to India and RoW markets.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 or FY28 guidance given; management aspires to around 20% growth in revenue, EBITDA and PAT, citing a 10-year revenue CAGR near 20%.
FY26 revenue growth was about 15% versus a 20% aspiration; management says EBITDA and PAT growth of 30%+ more than compensated.
EBITDA margin: asked whether 38-40% is a fair assumption, CFO said the company has delivered these levels and will continue to deliver, with operating leverage expected to hold margins steady.
Destocking is described as behind the company; management expects restocking to lift FY27 top and bottom line.
Biosimilar project expected to hit P&L next year (FY27) and would be classified under CRDMO.
Unit 3 expected to be EBITDA-positive this year; Unit 4 ready by next financial year per CEO closing remarks.

Phase 1 adds about 365 kilolitres custom synthesis (vs current 425 KL) and 100 KL fermentation (vs current 180 KL), roughly doubling custom synthesis and adding about 50% fermentation capacity.
Capex guidance: about Rs 700 crore in FY27, then about Rs 500 crore per year after that (including maintenance).
Unit 2 expanded from 246 KL to about 376 KL (50% addition); Unit 3 fully operational, and more Unit 2/3 expansion sits in CWIP in H1 FY27.
Unit 4 has two further phases after Phase 1; Phase 1 at least doubles capacity and Phase 2 could triple overall size.
Unit 3 added lab space to handle more projects; management says the company can handle 200 projects versus 100 today.
demand_pricing: Management said destocking happened in FY26 across many customers, and restocking is now under way.
Orders are coming in for both chemistry and biology, with growth in peptides and RNAi (oligonucleotide) work.
Four commercial molecules went live in FY26 (one with big pharma, three with emerging biotechs); they contribute about 8-9% of revenue now, with a 2-3 year ramp expected.

Commercial pipeline rose to 14 molecules; Phase 3 pipeline stands at 10 molecules, all from emerging biotechs (four added in FY26, non-lateral), spanning ADC, peptides, oligonucleotides and biotransformation.

Two new direct big pharma relationships added in FY26; more than 100 early-stage R&D projects. Biotech funding up about 50% YoY through April (per CFO); early-stage requests rising in number though smaller in size.
Management sees tariffs as no impact so far, since commercial big pharma products have separate arrangements with the US administration.

qa_highlights.question: How should FY27 growth for CRDMO research and manufacturing be framed, and are destocking issues resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to about 20%+ growth as per track record but gave no FY27 guidance; it says destocking is largely behind and restocking should benefit FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity a constraint for adding big pharma customers?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Unit 2 expansion (246 to about 376 KL) and Unit 3 give headroom until Unit 4 comes online; capacity is not a constraint now.

qa_highlights.question: Capex outlook for FY27 and the medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about Rs 700 crore in FY27 and about Rs 500 crore thereafter, with Unit 4 Phase 1 at about Rs 1,200 crore over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin improvement and EBITDA margin sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Backward integration into one intermediate was completed, improving material margins in Q3 and Q4 FY26; management expects 38-40% EBITDA margins to be sustained with operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Phase 3 pipeline composition?
qa_highlights.answer: All four Phase 3 additions were non-lateral, from the emerging biotech funnel; the basket of 10 spans ADC, peptides, oligos and biotransformation, with at least one molecule per modality.

qa_highlights.question: Contribution from the four newly commercial molecules?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO estimated about 8-9% of current revenue, with peak sales estimated four to five years after launch and a two-to-three-year ramp.

risks_watch: FY26 revenue growth of about 15% fell short of the 20% aspiration; management declined to commit to FY27 numbers.
Specialty ingredients growth is patchy because its capacity shares space with CRDMO; a dedicated facility in Unit 4 is planned.
Unit 4 capex execution (Rs 1,200 crore over FY27-FY28) and Phase 1 completion by March 2028.
Maintaining 38-40% EBITDA margins at high growth; management acknowledged inflationary pressures and the Middle East war as headwinds.
Ramp-up of the four newly launched commercial molecules; launch timing depends on partner filings and registrations across geographies.
GLP-1 generic opportunity depends on customer formulation approvals, with timing given as six to eight months; the company is in talks with big players to replace China-sourced APIs.
Q4 PAT includes a Labour Code-related exceptional credit of Rs 98 lakh.

key_quotes: Historically, if you look at it last 10 years, our revenue growth has been around 20% level.

So, capacity is not a constraint for us now.
Unit 3 is already turning around and it's going to be in the positive territory this year.

544449|2026-06.headline: Anthem Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to Rs 418 crore with 39.6% EBITDA margin; management guides to H2-weighted recovery, not a number.
544449|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 418 crore, with CRDMO at Rs 341 crore (81.5%) and Specialty Ingredients at Rs 78 crore (18.5%). EBITDA including other income was Rs 176 crore (39.6% margin), PAT Rs 120 crore (27.1% margin), and net cash stood at Rs 1,720 crore at June 30, 2026. Management attributed the soft quarter to customers deferring deliveries into Q2–Q4 rather than to demand weakness, and reiterated full-year growth in line with historical double-digit performance. Analysts pressed on the roughly 25% YoY decline in Q1; management pushed investors to judge the business on a YoY and full-year basis.

segments.name: CRDMO
segments.commentary: Rs 341 crore in Q1 FY27 (81.5% of revenue); management says order book is about 60% of full-year plan after replenishment, with deliveries deferred to Q2–Q4. Analyst cited roughly 25% YoY decline in Q1.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients
segments.commentary: Rs 78 crore in Q1 FY27 (18.5% of revenue); India-focused B2B business with rolling forecasts revised every 3 to 6 months. Management cited raw material and supply chain pressure from the war and expects decent growth by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Management says Q1 FY27 is the softest quarter of the year and expects sequential growth from Q2 onward, with recovery in Q2, Q3 and Q4.

Full-year FY27 growth expected in line with historical performance (double-digit over the last 10 years, per CFO); no specific percentage guided. Analyst's 20% growth figure was not confirmed by the company.
EBITDA and PAT margins expected to be broadly intact for FY27; management sees no margin challenge this year given the order book.
FY27 capex target about Rs 700 crore; capex elevated in FY28 due to Unit 4, then declining.
Tax rate expected to normalise to about 25% to 25.5% for the full year as Neo Anthem moves toward breakeven and profitability.

capex_capacity: Unit 1 utilisation about 78% in Q1 FY27 (about 74% at FY26 end), custom synthesis.

About 14 commercial molecules and 10 late-phase molecules, with 100+ early-stage programmes; commercialisation of late-phase molecules 18 to 24 months away. Two late-phase programmes are ADC-related.
Q1 deferrals attributed to customers rerouting stock between geographies and approval delays for growing molecules; management says confirmed orders remain in place.
Semaglutide: sampled almost all large domestic players; sales not yet started, pending CDSCO approval. Regulatory work started for other markets but none targeted yet.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation at Units 1, 2 and Neo Anthem, and US FDA or EU inspection timing for Unit 3?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 1 about 78%, Unit 2 about 50% (fermentation also about 50%), Unit 3 about 30% to 35%. Unit 3 growth is from new projects rather than shifting volume from existing units. Management did not give an inspection timeline in the answer.

qa_highlights.question: Visibility on the next quarter and the split of the remaining 40% of the year's business across CRDMO, R&D and Specialty Ingredients?
qa_highlights.answer: The 60% order book figure applies to the whole business. The remaining volume is expected from new customers and volume increases from existing ones.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year CRDMO growth after a weak Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said growth prospects remain intact and in line with historical double-digit growth, with recovery expected in Q2 to Q4 and margins mostly intact. CEO asked investors to judge on a YoY basis and not to treat any single quarter as a benchmark.

qa_highlights.question: Semaglutide commercial supply timing and inbound interest from domestic peers facing scale-up issues?
qa_highlights.answer: No commercial supply yet; awaiting CDSCO approval, expected this year. Management said the company is ready to scale, has sampled most large players, and was not responding to a peer's scale-up problem.

qa_highlights.question: Unit 4 capex, timeline and FY27 capex total?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 1,200 crore Phase 1 outlay, about 50:50 across FY27 and FY28, with commissioning by end FY28. FY27 capex target about Rs 700 crore; FY28 stays elevated before declining.

qa_highlights.question: Margin sustainability over 3 to 5 years, and what drives it?
