544450|2026-03.headline: Chembond Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record Rs 101.4 crore, but management flagged a ~3% margin hit from war-driven input cost inflation.
544450|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue of Rs 326.15 crore (up 12%), EBITDA of Rs 51 crore (up 7%) and PBT of Rs 45 crore (up 7%), with H2 revenue of Rs 188 crore, up 35% over H1. Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 101.4 crore and EBITDA of Rs 15.7 crore were the highest of the last nine quarters. Management said margins are under pressure from metal-linked raw material costs that rose after the war declaration, with force majeure invoked and public-sector customers resisting price changes. The call was held after the demerger, which moved the water and construction businesses into the new listed entity.

financial_highlights.change: Highest of last nine quarters; management said above Q4 FY25 and Q4 FY24

financial_highlights.value: Rs 46.3 crore (presentation also cites Rs 51 crore), 14% of sales
financial_highlights.change: Rs 51 crore is +7% YoY per management

segments.name: Water technologies
segments.commentary: About 87% of FY26 revenue and the fastest-growing unit; H2 revenue Rs 162 crore, up 36% over H1, with volume of 4,813 MT vs 3,205 MT... (H1 volume stated as 9,905 MT in transcript, which conflicts with H2 4,813 MT; not reconciled on call). Record single-month revenue of about Rs 32 crore in March.

segments.name: Construction chemicals
segments.commentary: About 7% of revenue; H2 revenue Rs 13 crore vs H1 Rs 11 crore (+18-20%), H2 volume 2,590 MT (+30%). Management claimed PBT margin of about 20%; DSO about 88 days at 31 March 2026.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: About 6% of revenue; H2 revenue Rs 12.5 crore vs H1 Rs 9 crore (+40%), H2 volume 1,049 MT vs 594 MT in H1; DSO about 80 days.

segments.name: Cleaning and hygiene (JV with Calvatis)
segments.commentary: About 1% of revenue; H2 growth of 15%. Management described it as subpar for seven years, with early traction from integration into water channel.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 volume growth expected at about 15-20% in construction chemicals and about 10% in water chemicals.
Management said next four quarters at Rs 100 crore-plus are possible, subject to Q1 seasonality, and sequential quarters should improve on the prior year.
Around 3% margin impact seen in the immediate month from input cost inflation; a couple of quarters expected to pass costs through, with new contracts bid at higher prices.
Rs 1,000 crore revenue within four years described as an aspiration, not a commitment.
Water business entering FY27 with a strong chemicals and equipment order book; chemical contracts run to around mid-year, and FY27 budget already reflects the volume trend.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of about Rs 20-21 crore, mainly PPE transferred on the demerger and office renovation (management).
About Rs 65 crore of cash on books; management said some would go to network growth and geographic expansion, with no new plant planned.
Construction chemicals: de-bottlenecking of production lines; repair mortars outsourced to contract manufacturers.
Limited surplus water chemical inventory was rationed across customers during the force majeure period; volumes were kept below potential.
demand_pricing: Growth was mainly volume-driven, with new customer acquisition as the main driver; price growth contributed very little in FY26.
Construction chemicals realisation fell to about Rs 51,274/MT in H2 from about Rs 55,584/MT in H1, which management attributed to product mix (admixtures vs sealants).
Distribution realisation fell to about Rs 1.19 lakh/MT in H2 from about Rs 1.51 lakh/MT in H1, attributed to product mix.

Water business: about 70% private sector and 28-30% public sector (PSUs such as IOCL, HPCL, BPCL, NTPC, NPCIL). Private customers granted temporary price increases of 5-12% for about three months; public-sector customers refused to amend terms.
Input costs: metal-linked raw materials (zinc, molybdenum) rose from late February/March; management said 15 A-group items are up more than 120%.
Competitors named: Ecolab, Nalco, Solenis, Suez/Veolia, Ion Exchange, Thermax; Vasu Chemicals now owned by Dorf Ketal.
Largest customer under 5-6% of revenue; Nigeria export business exited after the customer refused LC terms.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Rs 100 crore-plus quarterly run-rate continue for the next four quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes is possible, with Q1 seasonally slower than Q4, but quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year comparisons should improve.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure from input costs, and can margins return to last year's levels?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3% margin impact in the immediate month; cost pass-through takes a couple of quarters, and new contracts are being priced at higher baselines. Chemical prices have softened only slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income negative this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Fair-value adjustment on investments: net gain was lower than in the prior quarter and the loss on fair value of investments was higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why are construction and distribution realisations lower in H2 than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Product mix; admixtures lower realisation, sealants higher. Distribution is purely trading, so mix depends on customer demand.

qa_highlights.question: Can water business margins reach construction-level PBT of about 20%, and why are they lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peer margins are at par, within about 0.5 percentage points; employee cost is about 18% of revenue in water versus 14% in other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the public/private split in water and how is force majeure being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Public sector is about 28-30% and private about 70%. Private customers accepted temporary increases; public-sector customers refused, and the company is preparing contingency actions if disruption extends beyond another month.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation in metal-linked raw materials; about 3% immediate margin impact and pass-through lag of a couple of quarters.
Public-sector water customers (28-30% of water revenue) refusing price amendments; force majeure invoked and contingency plans in place if disruption extends beyond about one month.
Working capital: DSO of about 88 days in construction and about 80 days in distribution.
Construction and distribution realisation decline from product mix; water realisation not disclosed on the call.
FY26 capex of about Rs 20-21 crore was largely demerger-related; further capex and cash deployment plans still unclear.
Data inconsistency: H2 water volume of 4,813 MT compared with 9,905 MT in H1 needs reconciliation; FY26 EBITDA quoted as both Rs 46.3 crore and Rs 51 crore.
544450|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on revenue momentum and the order book, but cautious on margins; management repeatedly said near-term profitability is a challenge tied to the war-driven cost spike. Evasive on budgets and on the public-sector price question.
key_quotes: Unfortunately, this story has changed post this war, having started this financial year.
So it's a synergy with our water business that we are now exploiting more efficiently.
So the track remains positive and on the positive growth for all quarters.
Yes, it's possible, but some seasonality comes into this business.

544450|2026-09.headline: Chembond H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% to Rs 182.25 crore, but PBT was flat at Rs 19.79 crore as material cost rose to 56% of sales.
544450|2026-09.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 182.25 crore, up 32% YoY, with Q2 revenue at Rs 95.8 crore (up 11% QoQ and 31% YoY). Operating EBITDA was Rs 22.55 crore (12% of sales vs 16% a year ago) and PBT was Rs 19.79 crore (11% of sales vs 14%), so absolute profit was flat despite higher volumes. Management attributed the squeeze to raw material inflation linked to the Iran war, solvent and China-sourced component costs, and a lag in passing price increases to customers. Q2 EBITDA was Rs 8.4 crore versus Rs 14 crore in Q1, and management said price increases are still being requested and no normalisation timeline can be given.

segments.name: Water technologies
segments.commentary: Revenue up 28% YoY on order book growth; about 82% of group revenue and the main source of margin erosion. Volume rose to 13,343 MT from 9,268 MT.

segments.name: Construction chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 30% YoY, about 8% of group revenue. Volume fell to 1,330 MT from 1,988 MT on product mix (admixtures run-off replaced by sealants); price increases partly offset.

segments.name: Distribution (trading)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 86% YoY, about 9% of group revenue; volume rose to 1,367 MT from 690 MT. Margin erosion is not concentrated here per management.

segments.name: Cleaning and hygiene (JV with Calvatis)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 59% YoY; about 1% of group revenue.

guidance_outlook: No guidance on margin recovery timing; management could not give assurance on when costs normalise, hoping for stability by end of FY27.
If the Iran war effects ease and crude and logistics return to pre-war levels, management expects cost increases to be absorbed in one or two quarters.
Management expects H2 to be stronger than H1, citing a strong order book and Q4 as a historically high-sales quarter.
Raw material cost deflation would give a couple of quarters of tailwind; new higher-priced business acquired in recent months should support margins.
Management said it would consider buybacks or higher payout if cash is not needed; no decision announced.

Management did not commit to returning to the 15-15.5% EBITDA margin cited by an analyst; said the Rs 1,000 crore three-year revenue aspiration is organic plus smaller businesses plus inorganic options.
capex_capacity: Management said capacity is not a constraint: plants are modular and capacity can be added in about two months without disturbing operations.
A production line at the Gujarat plant was repurposed to make additional sealants.
Equipment pipeline (water business) is about Rs 15-20 crore for FY27.
Three manufacturing sites; head office and R&D in Navi Mumbai.
Management said its focus is on profitability and cash flow management rather than capex.
demand_pricing: Management said all end-industries grew in volume, including refining, petchem, chemicals, agrochemicals, fertiliser, power, steel and cement.
Data centres are a growing customer: the top telecom company's data centres are served, plus NTT, Yotta and others, mainly via automated online monitoring plus makeup chemicals.
New-age industries (solar, copper, data centres) are about 7-8% of water revenue, expected to reach 12-15% over three years if the project pipeline executes.
About 80% of business revenue comes from technical-service-driven contracts, 15-16% from pure product sales, and the rest is hybrid.
About 25-30% of water sales are from PSU fixed-price contracts; private sector customers have been passing on part of increases.

Competition: a competitor was acquired by a larger process chemicals company, which management expects to be positive for Chembond over the next few quarters. Management also said customer attrition is very low and some lost accounts have returned at better prices.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins return to 15-15.5% EBITDA and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q1 solvent-driven and Q2 China-import component cost increases, with Q3 similar to Q2. It could not give visibility on normalisation, but hopes costs ease by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin erosion across segments or concentrated in distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Erosion is across segments, mainly water; distribution is only about 8-9% of revenue. Management said margins at Q1 levels would have added about Rs 20 crore to profit (gross profit basis, Q2 at Q1 levels).

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from Rs 11 crore to Rs 16.5 crore QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said technical service labour costs, freight and travel rose as more revenue came from technical service orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the construction chemicals product mix change?
qa_highlights.answer: Admixture projects ended and were replaced by sealants; the Gujarat line was repurposed for sealants. Management described the chemical sealant as a benchmark product in the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the tax rate reach about 35% in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to capital gains on redemption of investments; CFO was to explain further but no detailed figure was given in the transcript.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and pricing with customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Public sector contracts are fixed price and hard to revise; private sector clients pass on part of the increases. New bids reflect current material costs. Management said margin improvement depends on raw material prices falling.

risks_watch: Raw material cost volatility (solvents, China-sourced components, freight), with price increases lagging and sales-team fatigue.
Q3 FY27 margins: management said Q3 is tracking the same as Q2.
PSU fixed-price contracts (25-30% of water sales) limit pass-through.
Effective tax rate of about 35% in H1 FY27, attributed to capital gains on investment redemptions.
Construction chemicals volume decline (1,988 MT to 1,330 MT) despite revenue growth.
Whether the Rs 1,000 crore three-year revenue aspiration and new-age industry share targets are delivered.
Customer concentration was not disclosed.

544452|2026-03.headline: Swastika Castal FY26 total income rose 19.50% to INR36.19 crore, EBITDA INR6.22 crore, PAT INR3.28 crore; operating cash flow turned negative on deliberate working capital build.
544452|2026-03.overview: First earnings call since BSE SME listing, covering H2 and full-year FY26. Management attributed growth mainly to volume rather than price, with pricing impact described as very limited. Operating cash flow turned negative, which management said was a deliberate choice: advance payments to vendors, locked raw material pricing, and higher strategic inventory ahead of commissioning of expansion machinery in March 2026. Management expects FY27 to be a full year of enhanced capacity and says growth should be stronger than FY26, but declined to give a numeric guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue growth (as cited by analyst on call)
financial_highlights.change: YoY, analyst figure, not confirmed by management
Driven by higher working capital; amount not disclosed on call

segments.name: Power transmission and electrical equipment
segments.commentary: Management said power is the largest end-market for the company and has strong potential; named customers include Hitachi, ABB, Siemens, GE and Toshiba.

segments.name: Other industrial end-markets
segments.commentary: Company also serves infra/power capital equipment, railways, oil and gas, and fire-fighting equipment; railways is being expanded and government GeM tenders for defence components have recently been pursued.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management said FY27 has potential for stronger growth than FY26.
FY27 will be the first full year with the benefit of enhanced capacity from the expansion.
Management expects some benefits from the expansion in the near term and a larger financial impact in the medium term.
Margins expected to be sustainable and to improve with scale, operating leverage, fixed-cost absorption and productivity gains; raw material and market conditions noted as influences.
Expects working capital and cash conversion to improve as supply chain stabilises and customer collections normalise, which management said happened in April and May 2026.
capex_capacity: Expansion capex was completed and all machinery was commissioned in March 2026, per management.
Management said the company held higher inventory to feed the newly commissioned machines.
Management cited an order book and improved capacity as drivers of higher volumes, but did not quantify capacity or utilisation.
Capex for the year was described as strategic, though the amount was not disclosed on the call.
demand_pricing: Volume, not price, drove FY26 revenue growth; management said pricing impact was very limited.
Management said current customers are booked for at least the next five years, per what he was told by them.
Two new export customers added in FY26: QAG (Australia-based multinational) and Trench (Europe). Also won orders from another Hitachi factory where the company had not previously supplied.
Export presence cited in Europe, Mexico and the US.
Raw material and fuel costs are passed through to customers monthly under price variation clauses with most customers.

qa_highlights.question: What drove FY26 revenue growth: volume, realisation or new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was volume-led on strong customer demand and better execution; pricing impact was very limited.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow turn negative despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a deliberate choice: faster advance payments to vendors to secure raw material amid geopolitical disruption, locked pricing, higher strategic inventory for the new machines, and March-end customer collection delays that eased in April and May.

qa_highlights.question: When will the capex contribute meaningfully to revenue and returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Some benefits expected in the near term through capacity, order book and operating leverage; the large financial impact is expected in the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes margins are sustainable and can improve with scale, operating leverage, fixed-cost absorption and cost and productivity initiatives; raw material prices and market conditions are influences.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 revenue growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No figure given; management said FY27 is projected to grow faster than FY26, supported by expansion and customer order books.

qa_highlights.question: Are export opportunities growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management is in talks with several customers and said export potential will rise, building on the two new export accounts added in FY26.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow in FY26 from working capital build; watch for cash conversion improvement and collection days in Q1 FY27.
Vendor advance payments and inventory build may tie up capital if demand for the added capacity lags.
Raw material and fuel price volatility linked to geopolitical disruption; pass-through clauses cover most customers but timing gaps can affect margins.
Dependence on a concentrated set of large power and electrical OEM customers.
No quantified FY27 guidance; capacity utilisation and expansion-driven revenue are unquantified.
Recent BSE SME listing, with limited trading history and disclosure track record.

It was more forthcoming in defending the negative operating cash flow as a deliberate, supply-security decision, and it cited a return to normal collections in April and May.

So, in order to ensure uninterrupted production and avoid any impact on our customer commitments, because that is what we are emphasizing on because of our relationships, good relationship with our customer.
While we would prefer not to provide a specific guidance at this stage, we believe FY'27 has the potential to deliver strong growth -- stronger growth in comparison to '26.

544454|2026-03.headline: IndiQube FY26 revenue hit a record INR 1,469 crore (+37% YoY) with EBITDA margin at 21% and PAT at INR 125 crore.
544454|2026-03.overview: FY26 delivered record revenue of INR 1,469 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA above INR 300 crore (+60%) and PAT of INR 125 crore (+145%). Average steady-state occupancy was about 84%, while March 2026 end-of-month occupancy was 81%, which management attributed to newly delivered large properties ramping up. Management guided FY27 to 1.5-2 million sq ft of annual area addition, 25-30% revenue growth, EBITDA margin of 18-21% and PAT margin of 8-10%. Capex per sq ft is rising to about INR 16.5 from INR 15.5, and the company is adding 30-35 MW of solar next year.

financial_highlights.metric: Average revenue per occupied seat per month

financial_highlights.change: Added about 1.6 million sq ft in FY26

segments.name: Flexible workspace (centres)
segments.commentary: Added about 1.6 million sq ft of rent-paying area and launched 15 new centres in FY26; steady-state occupancy 88% per management, versus 87% earlier. Area under management is 9.66 million sq ft, expected to become operational over 18-24 months.

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: Contributed 15% of revenue in FY26 versus 12% a year earlier; management expects 17-18% over the next year. VAS EBITDA margins are about 10-15%, below the 18-20% space business. Around INR 40 crore of the quarter's VAS was one-time, per an analyst's figure.

segments.name: MiQube platform
segments.commentary: Recorded 1.4 million transactions over the year; new space management module and vehicle pooling feature in transport module gaining traction.

guidance_outlook: FY27 area addition of 1.5-2 million sq ft (33,000-44,000 seats), roughly 1-1.25 lakh sq ft per month of rent-yielding area addition.
FY27 revenue growth of 25-30%, EBITDA margin 18-21%, PAT margin 8-10%.
Portfolio occupancy target 80-85%; mature centres 85-90%.
Lease payments expected to grow in line with revenue.
FY27 capex about INR 1,650 per sq ft of added area, with solar capex of INR 125-150 crore for 30-35 MW of new solar.
VAS contribution expected to rise to 17-18% of revenue.
Rental inflation of 5-10% per year on blended revenue per seat expected (contracts carry 5-6% escalation).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex deployed about INR 414 crore: interiors about INR 250 crore, design-and-build about INR 50 crore, solar about INR 73 crore, vendor payments and advances about INR 30 crore; management said this was above the earlier INR 360 crore guidance mainly due to solar.

Solar: 4 MW plant in Latur, Maharashtra now operational; 20 MW Yadgir, Karnataka operational; 2.7 MW Virudhunagar, Tamil Nadu expected operational next quarter. Solar savings estimated at INR 22-23 crore per year.
Plan to add 30-35 MW of solar in FY27 across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra; 40% accelerated depreciation is available on solar.
Capex per sq ft rising to about INR 16.5 from INR 15.5 due to 5-7% material cost increases; not passed to clients.

IPO proceeds of INR 610 crore: INR 462 crore earmarked for capex was reallocated — INR 187 crore to other capital assets (design-and-build interiors INR 55 crore, solar INR 16 crore, security deposits INR 52 crore, real estate/adjacent investments INR 64 crore); general corporate purpose INR 50.4 crore unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did occupancy appear to dip to about 80-81% while area addition was small, and why did capex (about INR 413 crore) exceed the INR 360 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the relevant metric is the FY26 average occupancy of about 84% (a 1% dip), and that quarterly swings are normal. The capex overrun reflected solar investment of about INR 73 crore that generates INR 20-23 crore of annual savings, plus vendor payment timing.

qa_highlights.question: Will lease payments grow in line with revenue next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lease costs will grow in line with revenue, at 25-30%, with EBITDA margin held at 18-21%.

qa_highlights.question: Are IT/ITES tenants reducing footprint, and why do landlords accept 15-year lock-ins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the vertical mix will broadly stay the same with gradual shifts. Landlords accept long lock-ins because the company funds fit-outs, which would be lost on exit, and similar norms exist in hotels and retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook for flex and GCCs over the next 12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strong absorption, no war impact yet, a weaker rupee boosting India work, and GCC-led absorption; AI impact not yet visible. It sees flex taking 20-25% of large occupiers' portfolios.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in one-time VAS revenue, and how will VAS mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one-time items are upfront sales of IT products, design-and-build and furniture, and are hard to predict; VAS share is expected to rise from 15% to 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex per sq ft rising, and what was the IPO fund reallocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said material costs rose 5-7% due to the war, taking capex to INR 16.5 per sq ft from INR 15.5, absorbed by the company. The IPO reallocation moved INR 187 crore of capex to design-and-build, security deposits, solar and adjacent investments.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow faster given available cash and about 50% headroom in area under management?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritises sustainable growth and micro-market defensibility, avoids overbuilding, and values landlord relationships; it said it is trying to push growth faster within those limits.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company disclose quarterly rent-paying area additions in advance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed to consider disclosing expected quarterly rent-paying area; it said it adds about 1-1.5 lakh sq ft per month of RPA, with about 1-1.25 lakh sq ft per month of rent-yielding area.

risks_watch: Quarterly occupancy volatility from large deliveries (Q4 end-March occupancy 81% vs 84% annual average); ramp-up takes 9-12 months to reach 90%.
Capex per sq ft rising (INR 15.5 to 16.5), with war-linked material inflation; management is absorbing it.
Dependence on one-time VAS sales, which management cannot predict; VAS margins of 10-15% are below space EBITDA.
Tier-2 expansion still early; management calls it a 10-year story with supply and landlord-maturity issues.
Data-centre and power-intensive client demand requires further solar and power additions.
Commitment to 1.5-2 million sq ft annual additions and 25-30% growth depends on supply pick-up and demand continuity.
544454|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and detailed on growth, margins and guidance, but defensive when pressed on quarterly occupancy dips and the capex overrun. Management repeatedly stressed annual metrics over quarterly ones. It was candid about the Tier-2 story being early and about cautious growth pacing.
key_quotes: We achieved our highest-ever revenue of INR 1,469 crores, representing a growth of 37% year-on-year.
So, quarter-wise fluctuation in a rent-yielding area or area addition should not be viewed in isolation.
Our belief has always been sustainable growth, because we believe that growth at any cost comes at a huge cost.
So, the right way is you look at a year-on-year, 12-month number, because by that time, the property would have stabilized.
demand_pricing: Calendar 2025 gross office absorption about 82.5 million sq ft; Jan-Mar 2026 absorption 20.7 million sq ft; CY26 absorption expected about 5% above CY25, with Bangalore at about 29-30% share. Flex operators took about 23% of absorption and GCCs about 44%.

Management sees no war impact on demand so far, a weaker rupee favouring India work, and no visible AI impact yet. It expects GCC-led absorption over the next couple of years and sees flex taking 20-25% of large occupiers' portfolios.

Pricing: average revenue per occupied seat about INR 192 for FY26. Contracts carry 5-6% escalation; institutional supply priced higher (cited INR 21-30 versus INR 70-80 earlier). Management expects 5-10% annual growth in blended revenue per seat.

Leasing economics: REIT-to-operator rent differential of 5-10% on long tenures and large blocks; 20-25% difference for single floors versus whole buildings in non-institutional supply. Around 90% of uptake is speculative; single-tenant buildings are about 10% of portfolio.

Competition and micro-markets: about 17 cities, with few additions planned; focus on micro-markets above 90% occupancy (e.g., Guindy, OMR, Outer Ring Road, Golf Course Road), avoiding Manesar, North Bangalore and Navi Mumbai with 15-25% vacancy. Institutional share of portfolio rose from 16% to 18%. Tier-2 described as a 10-year story; Coimbatore cited as a promising city. Management described the rental inflation of 4-5% in key micro-markets as sustainable.

544454|2026-06.headline: Indiqube Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR428 crore (+37% YoY) and PAT rose 91% to INR35 crore, with PAT margin at 8%.
544454|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR428 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA of INR87 crore (+34%), EBIT of INR55 crore (+59%) and PAT of INR35 crore (+91%). Margins expanded, with EBIT margin at 13% (11% a year ago) and PAT margin at 8% (6%). Rent-paying area was flat QoQ, which management attributed to the timing of building handovers, with about 2 million sq ft of annual additions still guided. Q&A centred on VAS revenue (INR39 crore one-time in the quarter), solar capex, a large new Noida centre, and occupancy and margin ranges. Management declined to give quarterly OCF or capex figures ahead of the H1 audit.

Large Noida centre expected to go live around mid-2027 (Q2 or Q3 FY28).

544484|2026-06.headline: BlueStone Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR 733 crore, with pre-Ind AS EBITDA up 135% to INR 55 crore and margin at 7.5%.

544547|2026-03.headline: Jinkushal Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 89% YoY to INR133 crore, a record quarter, but full-year PAT was only INR12.44 crore as logistics and HexL brand costs weighed.

Consolidated net worth rose from INR86 crore to INR194 crore after the IPO, while working capital increased on higher volumes and overseas inventory. Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance, citing the Middle East conflict, and reiterated a medium-term target of INR600-700 crore revenue in 2.5-3 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Mexico about 46%, UAE about 19%, South Africa and Australia about 10% each; management said Mexico Q4 was stronger than Q3.

544547|2026-06.headline: Jinkushal Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 37.4% to INR51.29 crores, but consolidated PAT fell to INR2.2 crores from INR6.51 crores.

Profitability fell sharply on a consolidated basis, with PBT at INR3.04 crores versus INR7.26 crores, as shipping costs and employee expenses rose. Africa contributed about 32% of revenue against about 4.47% a year earlier, partly replacing Middle East business disrupted by geopolitics. segments.commentary: No segment revenue split was disclosed. Management said new customised equipment demand is strongest near term, and that used equipment and HexL should each grow to a larger share over 2 to 3 years.

Management expects healthier profitability in 2 to 3 years once shipping, interest and manpower costs settle; near-term profit is being sacrificed for long-term build-out.

Management said customer collections have generally met commercial timelines, but geopolitical disruptions have led to some customer payment delays.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Africa's growth and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Africa replaced Middle East revenue hit by geopolitics and board capital allocation decisions. Management expects the shipping and business cycle there to be sustainable, and it sees Africa, Latin America and the Middle East as equally important.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR97 crore inventory convert to sales, and how fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business cycle runs at least 2 quarters, so inventory should convert over the next 1.5 to 2 quarters, with inventory levels fluctuating by a few percentage points over the last 2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and debtors rise: what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the debtor rise a planned overseas penetration strategy, with longer shipping times keeping receivables high until machines reach customers. It expects working capital cycles to stay elevated for now.

qa_highlights.question: Will freight costs ease and can they be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is taking a substantial hit on shipping costs, partly passing them to suppliers at purchase and to customers at sale. Management said it cannot forecast oil prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs yield operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it plans to add sales and purchase staff and to move from SME to mid-corporate or large-corporate operations, and will keep investing even at the cost of near-term reported margins.

qa_highlights.question: When will returns on these investments become visible, and what will the business look like in 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects results in 3 to 6 quarters. In 2 to 3 years it targets INR600 crores to INR700 crores revenue with healthier profitability, a dominant international business, and roughly equal revenue from the three verticals.

financial_highlights.change: vs 61% in Q2 FY26 and 65% in Q2 FY25

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail AUM INR97,462 crores, up 30% YoY; mortgages (HL plus LAP) INR64,650 crores, up 27% and 57% of AUM. Unsecured (personal, business, digital, rural micro) AUM INR23,764 crores, up 46% and 21% of AUM. Retail opex to AUM fell 5 bps QoQ to 3.48%.

segments.name: Wholesale
segments.commentary: Wholesale AUM INR13,978 crores, up 24% YoY; real estate to CMML mix 68:32, average ticket INR55 crores, yield 14.1%. Q2 disbursements INR2,615 crores against repayments of INR1,889 crores; about 74% of FY27 contractual repayments already prepaid.

segments.name: Legacy book
segments.commentary: Legacy AUM fell INR780 crores (32%) QoQ to INR1,673 crores, 1.5% of total AUM, with ECL provision of INR459 crores; separate disclosure to be discontinued after the December quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 25% (given at start of year); medium-term AUM target of about INR1.5 lakh crores by FY28 (doubling every 3 years).
FY27 profit growth guidance of about 50% YoY reiterated; management says it is confident of meeting it.
Exit Q4 FY27 Growth RoAUM target of about 2.5% reiterated, even if cost of borrowing does not fall further; management expects further opex reduction of 30-35 bps over the next 6 quarters.
Long-term RoAUM ambition above 3%; FY28 exit target now being recalibrated for the insurance commission headwind, with specific guidance to be given in Q4.
Leverage expected to rise towards 4.5x-5x in the medium term.
Overall cost of borrowing on a stock basis expected at similar or lower levels over the next 12 months despite RBI tightening.
capex_capacity: Branch network 838; no full-service urban branches added in Q2. Rural branches rose from 178 to 203.
Gold loan branches rose from 67 to 100 in Q2; target of 200 by end-March 2027.
Gold loans are a high-yield product that management is growing, partly at the expense of low-yield mortgages.
Non-dilutive regulatory capital release possible over the next 12 to 24 months; management says this plus the QIP gives runway for growth capital for some years.
Capital raise in Q2 structured to limit leverage hit; QIP added ~200 bps to CAR and 5 bps to RoAUM.
demand_pricing: Disbursements up 34% YoY in Q2, with momentum stronger than Q1.
Unsecured AUM mix at 21% (20% two quarters ago); target 25-26% over coming years. Cross-sell share of unsecured disbursements at 30%.
Mass-affluent housing loans and larger-ticket LAP showing higher growth after rating upgrade.

Incremental borrowing cost: 9.36% (H1 FY26), 8.67% (H2 FY26), 8.46% (H1 FY27). Retiring debt about 9.1% vs new borrowing about 8.4%. About INR37,500 crores of long-term borrowings mature in next 18 months (about INR29,000 crores next year per analyst).

Pricing: NBFC lending rates move with PLR; management said it will not pass on rate increases until its own cost of borrowing rises, with roughly a one-year lag and a further three-month lag to customers.
Market-linked borrowings under one-third of total; almost no repo-linked debt. Q2 raised almost nothing from capital markets, shifting mix to MCLR-linked funding.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will pass on higher rates to customers, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through follows PLR changes, which lag cost of borrowing by about one year; management expects no pass-through yet. Around 50% of assets (HL and LAP) are the main repricing book.

qa_highlights.question: Will yields rise as the legacy book runs off?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly. Q2 had one extra day, which cut retail yield by about 11 bps; management called this optical. Growth NIM should converge towards company NIM as legacy runs off.

qa_highlights.question: Is the housing loan vintage uptick real?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, driven largely by one INR4 crore fraud case from Q2 FY26; management expects it to fall in Q3. Concentration in South India IT-sector home loans persists but has not spread.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan exposure and risk strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry data shows 15-23% of gross gold disbursements went to customers 90+ days past due. Piramal's October gold disbursements to such customers are under 1%, and it will not disburse to them.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated provisioning lower than Growth credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy book write-backs (about INR90 crores profit from recovery) offset Growth credit cost, which is used to build other buffers.

qa_highlights.question: Path from 2% to 3% RoAUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex 30-35 bps further reduction over 6 quarters, funding cost reduction and mix shift to unsecured and gold; exit FY27 target 2.5%. FY28 outlook recalibrated for insurance headwind.

qa_highlights.question: How much RoAUM headwind from the insurance commission rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross 18-24 bps FY28 RoAUM impact if the IRDAI draft is implemented from 1 April 2027; partly offset by Pramerica Life profit share and sales-incentive rationalisation. Management says mitigating half would still be meaningful.

qa_highlights.question: Does the rising rate cycle hurt NIM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says rate-cycle positioning is favourable: variable-rate assets INR56,000 crores exceed variable-rate liabilities INR51,000 crores; spreads down 40-45 bps; retiring debt about 60 bps above current borrowing rates.

risks_watch: IRDAI draft on insurance commissions: 18-24 bps FY28 RoAUM gross impact if effective 1 April 2027; formal feedback to regulator planned via FIDC.
RBI tightening in H2 FY27 and rising global yields may raise borrowing costs; management expects offsets from maturing debt and rating-driven spread compression.
Gold loan industry risk: high share of customers with active gold loans (above 35%) and industry disbursements to 90+ DPD customers.
Wholesale growth headwind from high prepayments (72% of disbursements repaid in Q2).
Housing loan 90+ uptick (one fraud case) and IT-sector delinquencies in South India; management expects Q3 improvement.
544597|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, profitability and funding tailwinds, with a notably cautious stance on FY28 RoAUM and the insurance commission draft, which management said it would recalibrate for once rules are final.
key_quotes: Our incremental cost of borrowing at Piramal Finance continues to decline steadily.
We don't take macro calls. We don't take decisions on everyday credit choices because of how the macro looks.
Growth is an outcome of our framework. It is not an input to our framework.
There is a INR4 crores case from Q2 of FY26, which turned out to be fraudulent, which is there in that number.

544599|2026-03.headline: Studds Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR 167.5 crore; FY27 guidance is 17-18% revenue growth with broadly flat EBITDA margin.
544599|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 167.5 crore (up 11.9% YoY), EBITDA INR 31.3 crore (up 11% YoY, margin 18.7%) and PAT INR 21.1 crore (up 6.1% YoY, margin 12.6%). For FY26, revenue was INR 634.2 crore (up 8.6%), EBITDA INR 122.2 crore (up 16.4%, margin 19.3%) and PAT INR 82.7 crore (up 18.7%). Management took 8-9% price increases from 1 April 2026 to offset raw material inflation, but expects Q1 FY27 gross margin pressure before recovery. Management also announced Bharat Goyal's elevation to CFO effective 1 July 2026, an ESOP plan, and a dividend of INR 3 per share.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 two-wheeler helmet and boxes volume

financial_highlights.value: INR 3 per share on INR 5 face value (60% payout)

segments.name: STUDDS (domestic mass/core brand)
segments.commentary: Volume grew from 68.7 lakh units in FY24 to 72.6 lakh units in FY26, about 3% CAGR. Management positions it as the scale and stability base.

segments.name: SMK (premium brand)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew at about 52% CAGR. SMK ASP rose from INR 2,359 in FY25 to INR 2,552 in FY26, and SMK sales grew about 30% YoY. Management says SMK EBITDA margin is about 10 points above STUDDS (STUDDS 17%, SMK 27%).

segments.name: Private label
segments.commentary: Volumes grew at about 22% CAGR. The largest white label, O'Neal, saw ASP rise from INR 1,831 to INR 1,918.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were 20% of FY26 revenue versus 16.75% in FY25, and 22.79% in Q4 versus 17% in Q3. Management guides exports to grow 23-24% in FY27 and reach about 30% of revenue in 2-3 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 17-18%, with EBITDA margins at broadly similar levels to FY26.
Q1 FY27 gross margin expected under pressure from raw material costs; margins to recover in subsequent quarters as material prices ease.

Management does not expect EBITDA margin to reach 22-23% in FY27; it expects that level only after revenue crosses INR 750 crore with operating leverage, and 12 months out margins should be better than FY26.
Advertising and marketing budget for FY27 set at INR 30 crore, across domestic and export, versus about INR 23 crore in FY26.
Normalised inventory days guided at 85-90, versus 91 days currently and 68 days in the prior year.
Expected 2-3 years of 8-9% price increases; a further 2-2.5% or 3-4% increase is possible if raw material costs stay elevated.

Capacity: installed capacity rises from about 9.25 million to over 12 million units (about 33%), with the first 1.5 million units by Q2 FY27 and the second 1.5 million over the following 15-18 months.
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion of 1.5 million units targeted by Q2 FY27, with a second 1.5 million units expected over the following 15-18 months; total installed capacity to rise from about 9.25 million to over 12 million units.
Capacity utilisation FY26: two-wheeler helmets and boxes 89%, EPS 88%, water decals 57%. Q4 FY26 utilisation: helmets and boxes 89%, EPS 91%, water decals 57%.
Capacity figure assumes a 50:50 painted and unpainted mix; unpainted-heavy mix raises effective capacity.
Italy subsidiary being incorporated, with a warehouse in Reggio Emilia via a third-party 3PL. Initial stock of 10,000-15,000 units, about three months' cover, with sales expected from mid-Q2 FY27.
Additional warehouse added in Faridabad in FY26.
Riding jackets and an external Bluetooth communication system for helmets are in advanced prototype; commercial sales expected from H2 FY27.
FY26 capex INR 48 crore.
demand_pricing: Price increases averaging 8-9% across the portfolio and channels from 1 April 2026, with export price increases of about 9-10%. Management says the 8-9% offsets current material costs but not full-year costs if they stay at peak levels.
Raw material prices rose after March and have eased in the last two weeks; management says they remain about 20-25% above the pre-spike level and expects about 2-3 months to return to Nov-Dec levels.
Management reports no volume or demand pressure after the April price increase, and says dealers expected a larger increase.
Unorganised share of the Indian helmet market is estimated at 25-30% (not less than 20%), expected to fall to 10-15% over 2-3 years.
Europe: Italy is the focus market, to be served dealer-direct. Mexico: a 1,200-store retail chain signed; Mexico helmet market about 2.5 million units, with the company below 1% share.
Competition: management says unorganised players may exit under price pressure, and many brands, including Chinese OEM suppliers, have raised prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12 million capacity target conservative if unpainted helmets are produced more?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is fungible. The 12 million figure assumes a 50:50 painted and unpainted mix, and capacity rises if the unpainted share increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material inflation and will 8-9% price increases offset it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 8-9% almost offsets current material prices, but not if costs stay at peak. Q1 FY27 margins will be under pressure, and recovery is expected once material prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin reach 22% as revenue crosses INR 750 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not in FY27 because of Q1 raw material pressure. Operating leverage is expected to lift margins above FY26 levels 12 months out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin gap between SMK and STUDDS, and between export and domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: SMK EBITDA is about 10 points higher than STUDDS (STUDDS 17%, SMK 27%). Export and domestic margins are roughly similar, with exports mostly SMK, and a gap of about 10 points is cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the European subsidiary moved from Spain to Italy?
qa_highlights.answer: The Spanish distributor objected to a direct subsidiary there. Italy has no direct importer, is the largest European market, and is served by a Dutch distributor with small volumes. The warehouse will be in Reggio Emilia.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise from 68 to 91?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the new Faridabad warehouse and higher US inventory with rising US sales. It says 85-90 days is the comfortable range.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: prices spiked to about 150 (index) before easing to 120-125, and Q1 FY27 gross margin is expected to be under pressure.
Working capital: inventory days rose to 91 from 68, and management targets 85-90 days.
Start-up costs and margin drag from the Italy subsidiary and the Europe 3PL warehouse, and new export markets with their own homologation rules (Brazil, Indonesia, Sri Lanka).
Execution on the Decathlon non-motorised helmet supplies from July 2026 and on the 1.5 million unit capacity addition by Q2 FY27.
Marketing spend to rise to INR 30 crore in FY27, which could weigh on operating margins.
Leadership transition: Bharat Goyal becomes CFO from 1 July 2026.
544599|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and the SMK and export story, but candid that Q1 FY27 margins will be pressured by raw material costs. Management was direct on the 22% margin question and on the Spain-to-Italy change, and gave some numbers only as ballparks.
key_quotes: So, export and domestic would be quite similar because most of the exports is with SMK.
I don't think 22 %-23% is what I think will happen this year.
So, I don't see any demand pressures as of now.
We have never reduced our prices.

544599|2026-06.headline: Studds Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.7% to INR169.7 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.5% on a styrene-driven raw material spike; management guides 14-15% in Q2.
544599|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13.7% YoY to INR169.7 crores, with two-wheeler helmet and box volume of 1.95 million units at 81% utilisation. EBITDA was INR19.6 crores (11.5% margin) and PAT INR12.3 crores (7.2% margin), hit by a sharp rise in styrene-based raw material prices (about 600 bps of margin impact) and manpower costs (about 200 bps, from a Haryana minimum wage hike). Management said effective price realisation was about 5% in Q1, with a full ~9% price increase expected from Q2 as older-price orders roll off. Growth initiatives include 1.5 million helmets of new capacity, Decathlon, an Italian subsidiary and new products.

segments.name: Domestic STUDDS (helmets)
segments.commentary: Management cited domestic EBITDA of roughly 16-17% currently, versus about 17-18% in FY26. Q1 price increases were not fully passed through in OEM, CSD/CPC and some export channels.

segments.name: SMK (premium)
segments.commentary: Export EBITDA on SMK was described as about 30-35%. SMK range is INR4,000 to INR15,000 helmets.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About 21% of Q1 revenue; target is closer to 30%. Export orders executed in Q1 were contracted before the price rise; new orders are booked at revised prices.

segments.name: Bicycle helmets (Decathlon)
segments.commentary: Bicycle helmet ASPs are about 15-20% below motorcycle helmets. Commercial production expected from October 2026, with Decathlon working like an OEM relationship.

segments.name: Bluetooth and riding jackets (new)
segments.commentary: Management expects INR15-20 crores of revenue from these two categories in FY27. Some products are made in-house and some by contract manufacturers.

segments.name: Italian subsidiary
segments.commentary: Dealer-direct entry planned in Italy, Germany and France. Expected losses of about INR2-3 crores in FY27 and about INR2 crores in FY28; revenue guidance EUR100-125k in FY27 and about EUR1 million in FY28. Management said profits start from year 3, with 10-12% EBITDA margin cited.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 14-15%; normalised 18-20% run rate by Q4 FY27, subject to stable raw material prices.
FY27 revenue growth of mid-teens guided earlier; volume growth now expected at about 10% with 7-8% blended realisation (management said high-teens revenue growth on last call).
Full ~9% price increase (on FY26 base) expected to be reflected from Q2; Q2 realisation expected at 8-9% for OEM/CSD/CPC channels.
Styrene-based raw material cost impact expected to soften to about 300 bps in Q2 from 600 bps in Q1; management expects Q3 and Q4 to improve further.
FY28 standalone guidance: volume growth 13-14% and price realisation 3-4%, implying mid-to-high teens growth (management said this excludes the Italian subsidiary).
At current styrene levels (~INR185 weighted average), PAT margin expected at about 11.5-12%, versus about 13% earlier; management expects a return to FY26 levels by Q4 FY27.
Export mix rising toward 30% could add 200-300 bps to PAT margin, per management's rough estimate.
Total capex of INR76 crores to 30 June 2026 plus INR10 crores of vendor advances; FY27 capex budget INR58 crores (INR7.5 crores spent in Q1); FY28 plan INR31 crores.

financial_highlights.change: volume growth ~8.5% YoY (1.4 lakh units on 17.56 lakh base)

qa_highlights.question: Share of styrene-based raw materials in bill of materials?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said styrene-based direct raw material is about 36% of consumption, with about 15% more indirect (e.g., paint); analyst confirmed 36% direct.

qa_highlights.question: Italy dealer-direct model: capturing distributor margin or absorbed by costs, and steady-state margin differential?
qa_highlights.answer: Entry planned in Italy, Germany and France where there are no strong distributors; no profit in years 1-2, with profits from year 3 at a surplus EBITDA margin of about 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the 600 bps material and 200 bps other-expense margin hit?
qa_highlights.answer: The 200 bps is entirely manpower cost, up after Haryana minimum wage revision effective 1 April (about 35%, unskilled from INR11,000-12,000 to INR15,000-16,000); expected to soften as 9% realisation flows in, but to persist.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 9% price hike on FY26 base? Q1 vs Q2 realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, 9% on March 2026 base; Q1 realised about 5%, Q2 expected 8-9%, and next quarter about 9%, with CSD/CPC and some exports lagging.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 volume growth and realisation split?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 volume about 8.5%; full-year volume closer to 10% and blended realisation 7-8%, with management referring back to high-teens revenue growth guided on last call.

qa_highlights.question: Italy subsidiary losses and revenue for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses of about INR2-2.5 crores in FY27 and about INR2 crores in FY28 (corrected from earlier figures); revenue EUR100-125k in FY27 and about EUR1 million in FY28, included at consolidated level.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY28 guidance of 13-14% volume and 3-4% price on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified it is standalone only, excluding the Italian subsidiary, whose ASP differs; Italy revenue is incremental on top of that.

qa_highlights.question: PAT margin outlook at current styrene levels, and export mix impact?
qa_highlights.answer: At ~INR185 styrene, PAT margin about 11.5-12% versus ~13% earlier; return to FY26 levels by Q4 FY27 expected. Export mix rising to 30% could add 200-300 bps to PAT margin.

capex_capacity: First-phase addition of 1.5 million helmets annual capacity progressing as planned, expected operational from September/October 2026; existing two-wheeler helmet and box utilisation at ~81% in Q1 FY27.
Total capex of about INR76 crores incurred up to 30 June 2026, plus INR10 crores of advances committed to vendors.
FY27 capex budget INR58 crores (described as the complete FY27 budget); about INR7.5 crores spent in Q1 FY27.
FY28 capex plan INR31 crores, which includes starting a second phase of construction (figure restated on call; analyst had cited INR28 crores).

Italian operations to be fully functional in October 2026; Decathlon commercial production from October 2026; Bluetooth mesh product first commercial production expected Q3 FY27; riding jacket commercial availability around Q2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 effective price realisation about 5%; full ~9% price increase on FY26 base expected to be reflected from Q2, with Q2 realisation of 8-9% in the quarter per management.
Volume growth in Q1 about 8.5% (1.4 lakh units on 17.56 lakh base); management guided FY27 volume growth closer to 10%, with blended realisation of 7-8%.

Styrene-based raw material impact about 600 bps on margin in Q1, expected to ease to about 300 bps in Q2; styrene weighted average ~INR185 currently versus ~INR225 peak and ~INR135 at start of Q4 FY26.

OEM price increases received from all customers except one, with that one expected within a week; manpower cost pass-through expected from OEMs. Management said GT channel price increase was fully passed through without resistance.

Exports about 21% of Q1 revenue, with export orders from before the price rise executed at old prices; new export orders booked at revised prices. Export SMK EBITDA about 30-35%; domestic EBITDA about 16-17% currently vs 17-18% in FY26.
Bicycle helmet (Decathlon) ASPs about 15-20% below motorcycle helmets; Bluetooth and riding jacket revenue expected at INR15-20 crores in FY27.

544600|2026-03.headline: Lenskart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 41% YoY to ₹2,516 crore, with reported EBITDA up 61% and pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at 12.8%.
544600|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter since listing: revenue grew 41% YoY to ₹2,516 crore, PAT reached ₹204 crore, and EBITDA margin expanded 2.7 pp to 21.3%. India and international both grew, with India same-store sales growth at 24% and international revenue up 35.4%. FY26 crossed ₹1,700 crore EBITDA, ₹1,000 crore pre-Ind AS EBITDA and ₹500 crore PAT for the first time. Management kept the steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at about 25% and guided FY27 net store additions to roughly FY26 levels (542 in India plus 61 international in FY26).

financial_highlights.change: Q4 from 8.1% YoY; FY26 from 3.6% in FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash (ex IPO-related payables, largely settled in April)
Return on capital employed (ex undeployed IPO proceeds)

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,475 crore (+44% YoY) with eyewear units up 24.3% to 7.9 million; product margin held at 64%. Store count 2,609 after 170 net adds in Q4 and 542 in FY26; FY26 pre-Ind AS EBITDA ₹753 crore at 14.3% margin.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,054 crore (+35.4% YoY; +25% constant currency) with eyewear units up 29%. Store count 718 after 13 net adds in Q4 and 61 in FY26; FY26 pre-Ind AS EBITDA ₹264 crore at 7% margin. Japan was the strongest market; Middle East had a temporary traffic dip that has recovered to near normal.

guidance_outlook: Net new store additions in FY27 expected to be around FY26 levels (FY26: 542 India, 61 international).
Long-term steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin unchanged at approximately 25% (India currently 14-15%, about 10 pp runway).
Quarterly margins will vary with store-opening phasing, seasonality and long-term bets; management said it will prioritise long-term value over short-term linearity.
Management urged investors to track trailing 12-month volume growth as the cleanest measure of underlying demand.
Step-up in R&D spend in FY27 for automated eye testing, smart eyewear (B by Lenskart) and AI; FY27 priorities include scaling to 100 million customers.
capex_capacity: FY26 store capex funded 603 net new stores (ops cash flow ₹887 crore), alongside manufacturing investment including the new Hyderabad facility.
Factory floors to move toward near full automation from the current 75%; Bhiwadi centralised facility supports next-day delivery across 78 cities (from 7 cities initially, about 30 later).
Hyderabad plant and Thailand JV cited as structural answers to reduce import dependence.
Remote optometry stores rose 3.7x in a year to 623.
India eyewear units reached 29 million in FY26 (18 million two years earlier); long-term store runway of 4,500 stores in India previously articulated, management said more is possible.
demand_pricing: India same-store sales growth 24% in Q4 (broad-based across Metro, Tier 1, Tier 2); same-pincode sales growth 31%. Management declined to split SSSG into value and volume; it rejected an analyst's estimate of ~10% volume SSS as too low.
Eye tests: 6.8 million globally in Q4 (+45% YoY); India eye tests 6 million (+50%); about half of India eye tests were first-time exams. Gold active members 8.8 million (+29.5%).
Product margin in India held at 64% despite rupee depreciation; management said structural margin gains were offset by currency (RMB 11 to 14 cited as an example).
ASP fluctuations are driven by OPP campaigns (New Lens Replacement, Hustlr) and by upgrades to Own days, Meller, progressives.
International ACP reduction ongoing as markets are integrated into central supply chain; operating leverage seen after scale in Singapore, Dubai and now Japan.
Meller sunglasses out of stock in all markets; launched in 1,000+ India stores, Middle East and Southeast Asia, with Japan next.

qa_highlights.question: What geopolitical, raw material, China-sourcing or market risks should investors monitor?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight and raw material have had no meaningful impact so far; currency is the biggest variable. 42% of business is international and vertical integration has offset rupee-import headwinds. No material demand impact seen in India or abroad; Middle East dip was small and brief.

qa_highlights.question: How was the India gross margin held near 64% in a low-ASP quarter, and does SSSG of ~25% with ~15% price imply ~10% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gains came from vertical integration and process changes, not price increases; OPP campaigns are paired with upgrades to offset margin. Management said the 10% volume estimate was not correct and that volume SSS is meaningfully higher; it does not disclose value/volume split.

qa_highlights.question: How will employee productivity and cost leverage trend, especially internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage came mainly from SSG and volume growth on a fixed cost base. HQ and tech costs were flat as headcount was not added; AI and remote optometry are expected to add more output per person.

qa_highlights.question: Does Tier 2 strength expand the 4,500-store runway and allow faster expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than 4,500 stores are possible; 200+ Tier 2 stores have been added and feed GeoIQ. Metros are also growing (eye tests +45%+) and are the main source of SSG.

qa_highlights.question: How should we think about competition in smart glasses (e.g. Google re-entry)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the category is very early with no clear form-factor winner; it sees Lenskart's role in prescription and distribution of smart glasses and its app/data layer as advantages. Launch focus is on learning, not near-term sales.

qa_highlights.question: How will international margins converge to India's level, and what is the KSA breakeven status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a quarter for reaching 15% international margin; it cited falling ACP and operating leverage after scale. KSA is about two years old and ahead of where UAE was at the same stage; no breakeven date was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will store expansion focus on saturating existing pincodes or entering new ones, and what about cannibalisation?

544644|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 21.9% YoY to INR422 crore, with India business up 22.7% against IPM growth of 11.6%, and organic growth of 21.4%. EBITDA rose 33.5% to INR93 crore and PAT rose 30.1% to INR60 crore, with PAT margin at 14.2%. Management kept FY27 guidance of 15% organic revenue growth and 20% PAT growth, but flagged raw material and geopolitical cost risk and said it is premature to extrapolate the Q1 margin. The Europe-GMP hormonal facility was capitalised on 30 June 2026 and export filings are targeted for FY28-29.

financial_highlights.change: +21.9% YoY (vs INR347 crore in Q1 FY26)
+33.5% YoY; margin up ~190 bps (from INR70 crore)
vs INR10 crore in Q1 FY26; mainly amortisation of Wokadine and Bayer brands

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Contributed about 97% of revenue and grew 22.7% YoY, roughly twice the IPM growth of 11.6%.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Contributed about 3% of revenue and did not grow in Q1; management says it will stay in the low-single-digit share for the next few years.

segments.name: Therapy areas (PharmaTrac, per management)
segments.commentary: Women's Healthcare grew about 23.3% vs IPM 9.4%; Urology grew 27.6% vs IPM 14.9%; Cardio-metabolic and Pain Management outperformed IPM by 1.7x and 1.4x respectively.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 15% organic revenue growth plus about 1.5-2% inorganic growth, for about 17% total revenue growth and 20% PAT growth.
Management says it aims to maintain margins 'within a similar range' but will not commit to sustaining Q1 levels given cost volatility.

Raw material: about 70-90 days of stock held at quarter end; new stocks began arriving in June 2026. Management sees possible 100 bps margin hit in coming quarters and is offsetting via other cost cuts.
Hormonal facility asset turnover expected below 1x in FY27, rising to 2-3x over about three years; depreciation on the INR130 crore capex is about INR6.5 crore a year.
Export ramp: dossiers ready by Nov-Dec 2026, then 12-18 months for registration; international launch targeted FY28-29.
Medical representative additions guided at 6-8% per year (about 200-250 MRs), with no MR additions planned in FY27 after about 400 were added in Q4 FY26.
capex_capacity: Europe-GMP hormonal (women's healthcare) facility commercialised on 30 June 2026, after INR130 crore capex; it handles tablets, soft gelatin capsules, ointments and gels.
Ahmedabad oral solid dosage facility Europe-GMP certification renewed.
Manufacturing mix is about 60% in-house and 40% outsourced, expected to stay similar through FY27.
API sourcing: about 60-65% of API needs are met by La Chandra Pharma Lab, in which the company holds a 31% stake (via Remedies Private Limited). La Chandra has EU GMP and a recent US DMF approval.
Hormonal plant to serve the domestic market initially; international dossier filings are in preparation.
demand_pricing: MAT June 2026 PharmaTrac split: volume growth 6.3% vs IPM 1.3%; price-led growth about 8.7% vs IPM 5.6%; new product contribution 3.4% vs IPM 2.9%.
Management says the Q1 India growth split is broadly in line with the MAT split.
Company ranks 26th in IPM (up from 29th a year ago). It is 5th in Women's Healthcare and Pain Management, 9th in Urology, and 20th in Cardio-diabeto (top 10 in new consolidated business).
Two brands now exceed INR100 crore annual revenue (one in MAT June 2023), and more than 40 brands exceed INR10 crore (from 32). Two new INR10 crore entrants are both organic.
Management expects IPM growth of about 9-11%, sustained since December 2025.
Semaglutide: management expects a INR1,500-1,800 crore market and targets a top-10 position, but says focus remains on engine brands.

qa_highlights.question: Is there scope for margin expansion if 20% growth continues, or will incremental growth be reinvested?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited favourable mix and operating leverage in Q1 but would not extrapolate. It said it aims to keep margins in a similar range and cited Southeast Asia and geopolitical cost risk.

qa_highlights.question: Did raw material inflation affect Q1, and will Q2 see more of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was largely unaffected due to 70-90 days of inventory. Management sees a possible 100 bps hit and is trying to offset it with other cost reductions to keep the 20% PAT guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the acquired Bayer-Zydus molecule (Dr. Reddy's-sourced, per the analyst) seem to decline YoY, and what is the path to 25% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: External revenue was INR28-30 crore, plus INR20 crore internal. Management called Q1 the launch quarter and said supply-chain integration took priority; it is targeting INR20-40 crore over the coming years.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth by volume, price and new launches, and IVF traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Split is in line with MAT: volume 6.3%, price 8.7%, new launches 3.4%. The IVF task force started in April 2026; management says it is too early to comment and will update in two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the employee and other expense ratios vs peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is high because about 1,000 MRs (35% of the 3,111 total) were added in three years and productivity per MR is lower; operating leverage should bring it down. Other expenses are mainly UCPMP-governed promotion costs, which are variable.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation and amortisation impact from the Wokadine and Bayer acquisitions, and from the hormonal plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Wokadine (INR97 crore plus GST) and Bayer (INR7 crore) are amortised over 10 years. The hormonal plant is depreciated over 20 years (about INR6.5 crore a year).

risks_watch: Raw material and geopolitical (Southeast Asia) cost pressure could cut gross margin by about 100 bps in coming quarters.
Hormonal facility under-recoveries until asset turnover rises from below 1x in FY27 toward 2-3x.
International revenue was flat in Q1; export ramp depends on dossier approvals (FY28-29).
Wokadine and Bayer-Zydus brand ramp is early; management guides to 25% inorganic growth over 2-3 years.
Dependence on La Chandra for about 60-65% of API needs.
Next quarter: whether margin holds near 22% EBITDA and the India growth rate stays about twice the IPM.
key_quotes: At this stage, it would be premature to comment on the sustainability of current levels, although our endeavor is to maintain margins within a similar range.

While we are encouraged by this performance, we remain cautious about extrapolating the current margin profile into coming quarters given the evolving cost environment due to geopolitical Southeast Asia risk.
We continue to target 15% revenue growth and 20% PAT growth over the FY27.
So, first quarter can't be considered for the future coming quarters numbers perspective, but we are eyeing what we have committed of our 25% growth
544644|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the India growth story, volume and brand momentum, and the FY27 guidance, which was kept unchanged. Noticeably cautious on margins: management declined to extrapolate Q1 profitability, citing geopolitical and Southeast Asia cost volatility, and was evasive on the Bayer-Zydus molecule's YoY decline, attributing it to launch and supply-chain integration.
